key: A Brief History of the Pale Starborn
Brief History of the Pale Starborn
0.comment: A Brief History of the Pale Starborn
0.content:
A Brief History of the Pale Starborn (also: Brief History of the Pale Starborn, Pale Starborn history): Dated by Cycles, a fae calendar, and believed from its details to be written by fae elders, with scholarly footnotes. It covers two stretches: the 428th Cycle and the 799th Cycle.

Appearance: A 3-star book. The text is formal and archaic in cadence ("the Emperor dispatched envoys unto the fiefs of the Vila"), written as year-by-year entries, with bracketed numbers pointing to long explanatory footnotes. Some years are listed but left empty.

Lore: Monomakh's envoys told the Vila to stop paying Miscislav tribute. Miscislav demanded ten years of tribute from the Emperor, who refused. He attacked Kitezh in year seven and lost three battles; the Emperor killed him and two Grand Dukes, and the remaining clans accepted his authority. In the 799th Cycle the Tsaritsa used the Fatui to take the lands of rebellious princes and the Snezhnograd Veche to govern, and many fae gave up their titles and left.

Owners: No character is established as owning it. It is for sale to the Traveler from Dhabit, owner of Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a one-volume Book Collection, bought once from Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books for 1,500 Mora. It has no combat function.

1.comment: A Brief History of the Pale Starborn: Miscislav's war with the Pale Star court
1.content: In the book's account, King Miscislav, ruler of the Volkodlak alliance (the Miscislavli), provoked war in the 428th Cycle by demanding ten years of tribute from Emperor Monomakh, then lost three battles around Kitezh and was killed by the Emperor's thrown spear. Fae chroniclers called him Gorynishche, "Son of the Mountain"; The Volkhov Chronicles call him the Blood-Devourer. Footnotes say he feared the Pale Star court's rise and, in the last battle, tried to use the Shadow Realm to delay it, without success. Grand Dukes Skoldyryt (Nyholmgarthir) and Vodyanoy (Dalegrad) died with him; Seriviiki (Cirnareka) escaped and later joined the court's ministers.

2.comment: A Brief History of the Pale Starborn: Anastasya's consolidation of the north (Pale Starborn account)
2.content: In the 799th Cycle's first seven years, the book says Tsaritsa Anastasya took the north from the fae princes: she crushed the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka holdings with the Fatui, accepted Port Belovodye's surrender on terms, had Glupov built, set up the Snezhnograd Veche under the human Ioanna Ivanovna, and published the Imperial Order Reformation Edict, after which many fae gave up their titles and left Snezhnaya.

3.comment: A Brief History of the Pale Starborn: Mimisbrunnr Books copy of the Pale Starborn history
3.content: The book is sold by Dhabit, owner of Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. The wiki lists it beside other titles in his stock such as The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire.

key: A Day Carved From Rising Winds
4.comment: A Day Carved From Rising Winds
4.content:
A Day Carved From Rising Winds (also: Windborne Flower's Spruchdichtung, Dawn's Brilliant Oath, A Note in Spring's Leich, Heldenepos's Unspoken Tale, Minnesang of Love and Lament, Blessing of Pastoral Winds, Resolve of Pastoral Winds): A Day Carved From Rising Winds is a 4- and 5-star artifact set (added in 6.3) about the old uprising against the storm god Decarabian in ancient Mondstadt and the birth of the wind god who became Barbatos. Its pieces are an oath of the Gunnhildr clan, a guard's laid-down sword, a bard's last song, an archer's final arrow and a huntress's doomed devotion to her king. It is obtained in Moonchild's Treasures in Nod-Krai.

The set's titles borrow German medieval verse terms (Spruchdichtung, Leich, Heldenepos, Minnesang). The pieces are Windborne Flower's Spruchdichtung, Dawn's Brilliant Oath, A Note in Spring's Leich, Heldenepos's Unspoken Tale and Minnesang of Love and Lament.

Lore: Dawn's Brilliant Oath tells of an iron-clad guard who laid down his sword at the song of a young bard and joined the rebels. A Note in Spring's Leich tells of the bard's last song before the crumbling throne, the song that became Mondstadt, and of the wind spirit who kept his name and a strand of time. Heldenepos's Unspoken Tale tells of the archer's last arrow and of a final storm of the dying tyrant that the bard silenced. Minnesang of Love and Lament tells of the huntress who loved the tyrant and was never truly seen by him.

5.content:
A Legend of Sword (also: Legend of Sword): A Legend of Sword is a six-volume light novel sold in Inazuma through Yae Publishing House. It is a space-war epic with a swordsman strategist, and part of it flashes back to a ronin helping a village against bandits.

The wiki credits the pen names Zhenyu (author) and Calx (illustrator), which it identifies as Xingqiu and Albedo. It is a fictional story, not Inazuman history.

Appearance: Each volume carries a short in-game blurb. The cover is written in the Inazuman script. The series is a collectible book collection, with five volumes sold by Kuroda at Yae Publishing House and one placed in the left-hand room of Yashiro Commission Headquarters.

Lore: - Vol. 1: Secretary of Defense Faranges doubts Emperor Sher's long galactic war; his sister Princess Gopatha, scarred by the Intergalactic Anti-Guerrilla War, shuts the doubt down and trusts her brother's vision.
- Vol. 2: Admiral Geldafried trusts the Star Fortress Anusharwan, while the rebel pilot Bastinu slips through its vents to strike the core. Both hope to see Gopatha's face at that moment.
- Vol. 3: Ten years earlier, on a world under the Suruga Shogunate and its Tai-Shogun Imagawa Ujizane, the wandering swordsman Bitchuu Kyuubei, called Shinkurou, a former strategist who was framed, walks the land.

Owners: No in-game owner. Kuroda sells the volumes at Yae Publishing House. The wiki notes that Sangonomiya Kokomi can be seen reading one of the volumes in an idle animation.

Gameplay: Game note: Vol. 6 first became available through Kuroda and Murata during the Hues of the Violet Garden event, after the quest The Five Colors' True Form. The other volumes were part of the Inazuma book set from version 2.0.

6.content: In A Legend of Sword, Shinkurou is the novel's protagonist, a swordsman strategist named Bitchuu Kyuubei. Once a trusted adviser to the Tai-Shogun, he was framed and fled. He wins a battle for Asada Village, is later jailed and blinded, and is eventually freed and given the name Semimaru to serve in a space fleet. He is fiction, not a figure of Inazuman history.

7.comment: A Legend of Sword: Emperor Sher and Princess Gopatha
7.content: In A Legend of Sword, Emperor Sher leads a galactic empire at war, aiming for a realm without fear or rank. His sister Gopatha, who lost an eye and an arm, designed the Star Fortress Anusharwan and defends his vision when Secretary of Defense Faranges doubts it.

8.content:
A Teaspoon of Transcendence (also: Teaspoon of Transcendence): A Teaspoon of Transcendence is a 5-star claymore. Its description calls it an object of fantasy with countless definitions in an endless sea of stories: no real difference between a hero's holy sword and a princess's teaspoon, or between a cold clockspring and the key to the gates of transcendence. Its text is a conversation between Sandrone and Alain. Added in Version 6.7.

The item is built on wordplay: the Chinese name's final character can mean both spoon and key, so the idea of a teaspoon and a key to transcendence are the same object. Sandrone is the weapon's most direct connection, as the wiki records her holding its unascended form in her character trailer.

Appearance: Canon text gives no physical description beyond calling it an object of fantasy. In game it is a claymore with a teaspoon-and-key theme; keep to that and do not invent materials or measurements.

Lore: The text opens with a line that heroes of different stories find different holy swords and face different nemeses, then shows Sandrone closing a storybook and asking Alain why heroes always win.

Alain answers that people prefer easy, happy stories, then offers a different tale: a kingdom ruled by a white dragon, a prophecy that the land would dry up and its princess wither, and a hero named Narzissenkreuz who sought the greatest holy sword and wanted to transcend the weakness of flesh. In it the hero falls into a chasm that dissolves all things, vowing to return as a new universe.

Owners: No in-game text names an owner. The wiki trivia notes that Sandrone is seen wielding the unascended claymore in her Character Trailer, which makes her the closest known association.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star claymore, base ATK 48, CRIT DMG secondary stat. White Fairy's Queening adds an ATK bonus, and each Charged Attack hit grants a short Surmount stack that boosts the wielder's Stellar-Conduct and Stellar Swirl DMG. It was available on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-21).

9.content:
A Thousand Blazing Suns (also: Thousand Blazing Suns, Sunset Reignites the Dawn): A Thousand Blazing Suns is a 5-star claymore from Natlan, a greatsword that dazzles like the rising sun. Its story is a legend of the first human Pyro Archon, who took the Sacred Flame and chose to keep fighting the Abyss.

It belongs to the Pyro Archon weapon series. Its poem closes with a petition to the Lord of the Night to record the first sun and its Ancient Name.

Appearance: Canon gives only the one-line description (a greatsword that dazzles like the rising sun). Keep descriptions to a radiant, sun-like claymore; do not invent engravings or materials.

Lore: When the great dragon bowed its head, the leader of the mortals reached the primal flame, and the god who pronounced death showed him the Abyss devouring all life. He understood that a new war had begun.

The human Archon, whose domain was war, bartered with death for power and bent even the wisest of dragons to his plan, so that hope would burn on through generations.

Owners: No wielder is named in the item text; association with any character is a gameplay convention.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star claymore, base ATK 49 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.3.

10.comment: A Thousand Blazing Suns: Sunset Reignites the Dawn
10.content: Sunset Reignites the Dawn is the passive of the claymore A Thousand Blazing Suns (gameplay): it grants a short CRIT DMG and ATK boost after using a Skill or Burst, amplified in Nightsoul's Blessing. Its name echoes the text's image of a sun that sets and is rekindled.

11.content:
A Thousand Floating Dreams: A Thousand Floating Dreams is a 5-star catalyst from Sumeru, a lamp whose emerald light carries "a song of ancient days". Its item story is a lyrical tale of the girl who had never known "light", who hears the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's whisper in a dream as a palace crumbles and later walks out of the dreams into a real dawn. The wiki reads the girl as the Dendro Archon Nahida.

The short description says the lamp lights the dreams that float up "over a thousand nights". The weapon is a keepsake-like symbol of Sumeru's themes of dreams, stories and the passing of old ages.

Appearance: A lamp-like catalyst. The description gives it an emerald-green light. Canon text gives no further physical detail such as material, size or inscriptions.

Lore: At the moment the palace crumbled, the girl who had never known "light" heard the Greater Lord's whisper inside a dream. A verdant lamp then shows stories: an emerald-eyed dancer kissing nectar-soaked silk, brightly coloured fish in pearly water, a moonlight musician guiding the Jinn's torches, and a sailor seeking a voice from a dream and the blooming gardens of a far shore.

The child leaves the fallen palace on a soft forest breeze that guides lost children away from a place no longer tranquil. As dawn breaks, the lamp fades, and looking back the blind girl realises there is no return. The lamp never flickers again, yet birds still sing its tales, bringing courage, hope and happiness to children who never saw a dream. The closing verses show a traveller reaching the faraway homeland and the rose in the breeze, waiting for a new story.

Owners: No in-world owner is named. Nahida is shown wielding it in her Collected Miscellany video and her Genius Invokation TCG character card.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star catalyst released in Version 3.2 with the Sumeru series. Level 1 base ATK 44 with Elemental Mastery as its secondary stat. Its passive, A Thousand Nights' Dawnsong, gives the wielder Elemental Mastery for each other party member of the same Element and an Elemental DMG Bonus for each party member of a different Element, up to three stacks each, and gives all other nearby party members an Elemental Mastery boost.

12.content:
A Thousand Nights (also: Torn Page: A Thousand Nights): A Thousand Nights is a six-volume collection of torn pages found in Sumeru's deserts. Its stories were gathered by a wandering researcher during the Cataclysm and only a fragment survives.

Each page is a separate tale: shadowless people and a dream-captor, a mage and a faithless scholar, a prince and a sumpter beast, a researcher cursed with fast thoughts, a dreamer in a palace of mirrors, and a man who chases talking birds.

Appearance: Torn Pages, not whole books. The in-game description says a wandering researcher walked through rainforest, desert and city in a time of great catastrophe collecting these stories, and that the original held countless tales.

Lore: - Vol. 1, The Tale of Those Without Shadows: a shadowless people learn from a lost adventurer that shadows hide the secrets of the soul; a young man seeks the dream-captor, learns the taboo of gazing into another's dream, and meets a woman whose shadow is mottled like gemmed drapery.
- Vol. 2, The Tale of the Dastur: a Vahumana scholar is saved in the desert by a mage with amber eyes who teaches him; as he rises to Herbad, sage and Grand Sage he breaks his promises to her, and she returns him to where he began.
- Vol. 3, The Tale of the Prince and the Sumpter Beast: a Port Ormos prince squanders his father's wealth, breaks a witch's rule not to feed or speak to her beast, frees it, and loses a palace that proves to be sand and insects.

13.comment: A Thousand Nights: The Tale of the Dastur
13.content: In A Thousand Nights Vol. 2, a lone Vahumana Dastur is lost in a sandstorm and rescued by a mage with amber eyes who takes him as her disciple in an underground hexagonal library. She asks only that he never deny her. As he becomes Herbad, sage and Grand Sage he refuses her pleas to admit her sister and then her displaced tribe, until she returns him to the desert at Caravan Ribat, where he is a Dastur once more.

key: Tale of the Prince and the Sumpter Beast
14.comment: A Thousand Nights: The Tale of the Prince and the Sumpter Beast
14.content: In A Thousand Nights Vol. 3, a prince of Port Ormos, son of a Dey, spends his inheritance. A priest sends him to a woman who pays ten million Mora if he tends her emaciated sumpter beast for three months without filling it or speaking to it. He speaks, learns the beast was a god cheated by a witch, frees it, and is given a palace and wealth on condition he never asks their source. When he asks, the palace dissolves into sand and scarabs.

15.comment: A Thousand Nights: The Tale of the Bird Chaser
15.content: In A Thousand Nights Vol. 6, a young man goes to war after a priestess says she will send him talking birds. She dies soon after, but the birds she taught keep delivering her words until the war ends. Learning the truth, he spends his life chasing the birds, hoping to catch one that still carries something of her.

16.content:
Absolution (also: Deathly Pact): Absolution is a 5-star rapier once wielded by a deceiver who had forsaken everything. In the past it served mainly as a tool when he had to disguise his identity.

The weapon story belongs to Thompson Reed, a man from the Fleuve Cendre undercity who rose by lying and ended by betraying the people he had joined.

Appearance: Canon calls it a rapier and says nothing further about its looks. When held by a character with an Arkhe alignment it carries a Pneuma or Ousia mark. Do not add guard or blade details.

Lore: Thompson Reed is a young man from the Fleuve Cendre who took his mother's lesson of sincerity and diligence as a lie, after learning she lay buried there. He decided that lying and surviving were what mattered, and used costumes and masks to climb.

He meets a noble girl, Leticia, who has wandered into the Fleuve Cendre in disguise, and spots her at once because her clothes bear no soot, oil or blood. He sees her as a way into House Randolph. The text then follows him through a period in which he courts her and speaks of a world with more sunlight, no segregation and no deception, a place where people could build a home with nothing to trouble them.

Owners: Thompson Reed, per the description. No present-day owner is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword, base ATK 48 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.7. Passive "Deathly Pact": raises CRIT DMG, and whenever the value of a Bond of Life increases the wielder's DMG rises for 6s (up to 3 stacks). Values scale with refinement.

17.content: Thompson Reed is a historical figure from the Fleuve Cendre who appears in the story of the weapon Absolution as a self-serving liar who joined Eduardo Baker's resistance and then betrayed it, with Leticia as his wife. Not enough is known to state what became of him.

18.content:
Aerosiderite (also: Black meteoric iron, Grain of Aerosiderite, Piece of Aerosiderite, Bit of Aerosiderite, Chunk of Aerosiderite): Aerosiderite is a rare black ore used to ascend weapons, sold in Liyue and gathered at the Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula. Its item texts say it came from a black meteor that fell beyond Liyue's Sea of Clouds, dropped to vanquish a monster. The monster's tainted blood stained it, so it no longer holds the pure power of Rex Lapis.

It comes in four grades: Grain, Piece, Bit and Chunk. The name means meteoric iron, and the Chinese name translates the same way.

Appearance: Dark, near-black metal, the colour its item text attributes to the monster's blood. The four grades are shaped like pieces of an interlocking burr puzzle, per wiki trivia.

Lore: The Grain text says a black meteor once fell beyond the Sea of Clouds to vanquish a monster, but powerful tainted blood stained it. The Bit text frames the wider world: coastal nations call the region beyond The Seven's protection the Dark Sea, and defeated gods who fled the new order became evil gods, yet their power shared a source with Rex Lapis, separate from that devouring darkness.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon adds nothing beyond the item texts.

19.content:
Akasha Terminal (also: Neo Akasha Terminal, Akasha earpiece): The Akasha Terminal is a small leaf-shaped device that hovers over the user's left ear and links them to the Akasha, Sumeru's shared information network. Concentrate on a subject and the Akasha supplies what the user's clearance allows. It was a daily tool for most of Sumeru until the system was shut down after the events of Chapter III.

The Akasha began as Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's creation, built from her Gnosis, and the Sumeru Akademiya's sages expanded it after her death. Few users knew that the network ran partly on the dreams of the people connected to it.

Appearance: A leaf-shaped earpiece that floats beside the user's left ear instead of being clipped on. Saying the activation phrase, "May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom", raises a green holographic visor over the eyes. The visor fades when the Akasha is idle and returns when the user calls on it. The visor gives some physical protection and its position can be adjusted, though only people who have read the system manual know how.

Lore: The network lets people look up information, send messages and share documents. A user whose clearance is too low simply gets silence.

Clearance depends on identity, age, demographic and other criteria canon does not list. The Akasha also carries public announcements, partly replacing bulletin boards, and its reach is strongest in large settlements such as Port Ormos and Sumeru City. Devantaka Mountain is a known dead zone. Sages watch private messages and transfers closely. With enough data the system can model a person's likely behaviour; the Akademiya used it to predict Cyno's investigation path until he learned of it and changed his habits.

Owners: Ordinary Sumeru citizens, residents and, later, visitors wore terminals. Alhaitham, as a Scribe, had read the system manual and knew how to alter the visor and the status signal. Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) is described as the First Akasha Terminal: her consciousness has always been able to connect to the network, so she could watch the outside world through other people's terminals while confined. She can also move consciousnesses, her own and the Traveler's, through the Akasha in ways the sages cannot monitor.

Gameplay: Game note, not in-world lore: the terminal is a story device. Players do not equip it.

20.content: A Knowledge Capsule holds a fixed amount of information and can be used by anyone with a terminal, bypassing clearance. It is linked to the user's own terminal. Capsules exist for loading data into the Akasha and were meant to be destroyed after Jnagarbha Day, but many leaked into the market over the last century. The Akademiya banned owning, selling or using them, citing harm to users and fear of losing its monopoly on information, and violators can lose their right to study there. A thriving black market exists anyway. Valuable capsules carry more Dendro energy and shine brighter under Elemental Sight, though this is unreliable.

21.content: Jnana Energy is the name for the dreams the Akasha collects from its users, valued because brain activity is highest during dreams. Few people know about it. It is why Sumeru's people had a reputation for not dreaming. Jnagarbha Day is a separate occasion on which the Akademiya enters new information into the Akasha.

22.content:
Akuoumaru (also: Akuou-maru, Akuou's sword, Akuou's blade): Akuoumaru is a four-star claymore, part of the Watatsumi series, and the beloved sword of the Watatsumi warrior known to his foes as "Akuou". Item text calls the blade huge and majestic yet surprisingly easy to wield. It belonged to a young man whom the people of Watatsumi named Touzannou, a champion of Orobashi's war against the Raiden Shogun's forces.

Appearance: Item text only says the blade is huge and majestic and easy to handle despite its size. It gives no further description of its shape or decoration, so avoid inventing any.

Lore: The item story calls the weapon the blade of a mighty Watatsumi general who knew only the self-taught "Getsumouun" and "Yuushio" styles, yet was never beaten by a mortal in duel or battle. When Orobashi (Omikami) led Watatsumi to war against the gathering storm clouds, this young man stood out; his fearless valour won him great love at home and the name Touzannou. That name was later forgotten and replaced by the epithet his enemies used: Akuou, the wicked fangs and claws of the Great Serpent, the savage invader of Yashiori Island.

Owners: Original owner: the Watatsumi warrior Touzannou, called Akuou (historical.akuou), described by item text as a vassal ruler and vanguard of Watatsumi's forces. No later owner is named; the Traveler may use it as an ordinary player weapon.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star claymore from the Watatsumi series, obtainable from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 42, secondary stat ATK 9%. Passive "Watatsumi Wavewalker": for every point of the party's combined maximum Energy capacity, the wielder's Elemental Burst DMG rises by 0.12% at refinement 1 up to 0.24% at refinement 5, to a cap of 40% at refinement 1 up to 80% at refinement 5. A character's maximum Energy is the cost of their burst. The passive is shared with Mouun's Moon and Wavebreaker's Fin.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the sword suits a story about a loved hero remembered by his enemies as a monster. Few people outside Watatsumi would know the name Touzannou; elsewhere the name "Akuou" carries the Shogunate-side memory of the war.

23.content: Akuou is the epithet by which the Raiden Shogun's side remembered a Watatsumi warrior whom his own people called Touzannou. The item story presents him as a fearless young vassal of Orobashi, whose personal wish was a duel with the Great Tengu of Yougou and bringing the tengu's mask back to the shrine maidens Ayame and Mouun. The text does not say how old he was beyond calling him a young man.

24.content:
Alley Hunter: Alley Hunter is a 4-star bow of the Alley series, an opulent black longbow. Its story belongs to Mondstadt's aristocratic age: a noble house's hunting bow fell into the hands of a gentleman thief who was never caught, and used it to shoot crowns off noble heads without a sound. The tale ends bittersweetly, with a witch he loved branded and vanished and the thief fled across the sea.

It belongs to the same set as the Alley Flash and shares its theme of a thief among the commoners. The Alley series has no shared passive, and the bow's text is a lament more than a boast.

Appearance: An intricate, ornate longbow painted black so that it vanishes into the deepest night. The text says it was once the first choice of an opulent noble house for their hunting games.

Lore: The bow passed from a noble house to a gentleman thief who was never caught. He shot crowns from noble heads in silence, cut through tightened bonds and disarmed pursuing soldiers. He once vowed to bring light to a darkened age and to bring justice, riches and gladness to the oppressed.

The text says he did deliver on this for a time: the powerful lost sleep in impotent rage, rooftops and terraces heard his light footsteps like rain, and bards in the squares gained a song. He pried a sapphire from a noble's regalia and gave it to a blue-eyed witch who hunted the vile with a spear. He never managed to draw a smile from her, and she was as cold as the sapphire. In the end, seeking death, she took a criminal's brand on her flower-like face, and nobody knew where she went. The thief heeded the advice of his brothers, abandoned his vow and sailed into the ocean that belonged to no one.

Owners: An unnamed noble house first; then the gentleman thief. No present-day character is established as owning it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, base ATK 44, secondary stat ATK 6%, obtained from weapon event Wishes (added in Version 1.4). Passive Oppidan Ambush: while the wielder is in the party but not on the field, their DMG increases every second up to a cap; once they have been on the field for more than 4 s, the bonus decays.

25.content:
Amenoma Kageuchi (also: Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma kageuchi, Amenoma shadow forge): Amenoma Kageuchi is a four-star sword forged in Inazuma, described as one of the "kageuchi" copies of the famed blade "Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma". Iwakura Douin, founding patriarch of the Iwakura clan, gave it to the Saimon clan as thanks for caring for him while he lived in seclusion in Konda Village. Its item text is mostly about the Iwakura secret technique Tengu Sweeper.

Appearance: Item text does not describe the blade's look. Its passive is shown in the game as small purple orbs floating above the hilt, a gameplay effect rather than a lore detail.

Lore: The sword is a copy of Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma, a blade Douin had the Amenoma smith of his day craft for the "In" line of Iwakura swordsmen. Douin gave this copy to the Saimon clan in thanks for their care. The text describes the Iwakura secret technique Tengu Sweeper, said to work only when there is no trace of confusion in the heart; for centuries the swordsmen who inherited the name "In" used it against evils across the archipelago.

Owners: Item text names Iwakura Douin as giver and the Saimon clan of Konda Village as recipients; no wielder is named after that. The Traveler can use it as an ordinary player weapon.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star sword, forged from the Saimon Heirloom Blade Diagram (obtained in the World Quest "The Farmer's Treasure"). Base ATK 41, secondary stat ATK 12%. Passive "Iwakura Succession": after an Elemental Skill, gain a Succession Seed (once per 5s, up to 3, lasting 30s); after an Elemental Burst, all seeds are consumed and 2s later the wielder regains Energy per seed (6 at refinement 1, 7.5 at refinement 2, 9 at refinement 3).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a good prop for a village family heirloom, or for a swordsman who prizes a clear mind. Keep Iwakura details to what the text states.

26.content:
Amethyst Lump (also: Violet Crystal): Amethyst Lump is an uncut violet crystal that, by its in-game description, can only be found in Inazuma. It is mined from Violet Crystal ore deposits and treated as a raw forging ore.

The item text hints that some professional craftsmanship is needed to bring out its true value, which fits its role as a smithing material rather than a finished gem.

Appearance: A rough, unpolished lump of violet crystal, harvested by breaking Violet Crystal nodes that stud the Inazuma landscape, including Tsurumi Island.

Lore: The only in-world text is the item description: an uncut crystal found only in Inazuma, whose true value emerges through skilled craftsmanship. No story, owner or legend is attached to it.

Owners: No notable owner. It is an ordinary resource gathered by travellers and used by smiths.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a Forging Material added in Version 2.0. Each Violet Crystal node drops one to three lumps and, like other Geo objects, breaks faster under blunt attacks. It is used, like Crystal Chunks, to forge Mystic Enhancement Ore, and to forge weapons of the Amethyst Series.

27.content:
Amos' Bow (also: Amos's Bow, the bow of Amos): Amos' Bow is an extremely ancient five-star bow from Old Mondstadt, when the land was still a wasteland under the God of Storms Decarabian. It is named for Amos, a huntress who loved Decarabian, then turned against him and fired an arrow at him from the top of his tower. Item text says the bow still holds power although its owner is long gone, and that it draws strength from all things in the world.

Appearance: Item text describes the bow only as extremely ancient and still powerful; it gives no detail of its look, so avoid inventing any.

Lore: The item story is a short tragedy. In a barren age, before the land was green, a barefoot maiden followed the footprints of the Lord of the Tower through the snow. He had been her love and also her enemy, but her hunt was for more than simple vengeance. She told him of her dreams of ocean waves and sand, forests, boars playing in berry bushes and a towering spire, and he did not hear her. She came to see that only she had spoken sincerely: he talked of love but was accompanied only by razor winds, and he read his subjects' bent backs in the howling wind as devotion.

Owners: Original owner: Amos, the huntress (historical.amos), who died in the rebellion. The item text gives no later owners. In promotional art Ganyu holds this bow in her character demo and card, and Fischl is shown with it in her demo; those are presentation, not canon claims that either of them owns it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star bow, obtainable from the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat ATK 10.8%. Passive "Strong-Willed": raises Normal and Charged Attack DMG, and DMG rises again every 0.1 seconds the arrow is in flight, up to five times (12-24% base bonus and 8-16% per step at refinement 1-5). Fittingly for the story, its damage grows with distance from the target.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the bow works as a symbol of unreturned devotion and of seeing someone clearly too late. Characters who know Mondstadt history may associate it with the rebellion; ordinary Mondstadters are unlikely to know its full story.

28.content: Amos was a huntress of Old Mondstadt about 2,600 years ago and the lover or favourite of Decarabian, the God of Storms, before she joined the rebellion against him. The wiki records that she died in the final confrontation, torn apart by his winds as her arrow reached him. Her bow carries her name. The full account of her motives is only in item texts, not in quest dialogue.

29.content:
Anecdota Septentrionalis (also: Anecdota Septentrionalis (scroll), Northern Anecdotes): It reads as a deliberate parody of the tall-tale travelogues that Remurian poets, playwrights and historians wrote and swore were true. It is a rare piece of Remurian humour and shows that Remurians thought of their own writers as liars. It ends abruptly, promising the rest in a next chapter.

Appearance: A 3-star book collection of three scroll volumes found in the Faded Castle: Vol. 1 floating near books on the Lower Level, Vol. 2 floating near books on the Middle Level, and Vol. 3 at the top of the staircase mechanism, also on the Middle Level.

Lore: Vol. 2: The leader of the knights says Remuria does not exist and is a fake history of southern barbarians, and he welcomes the crew into the Empire of Solaris, taking them for traders from Hyperborea. The empire is in civil war: decades earlier a philosopher named Lucilius invented a way to give some people extraordinary powers at the cost of an altered appearance, and one side wants them enslaved or destroyed. The narrator suggests they alter Blubberbeasts instead of humans, then leads imperial legions in a battle in which rebels' one-eyed giants hurl Bulle Fruit that sends people floating into the sun. He skips the war's end.

Vol. 3: After a further 300 days at sea the crew reaches a huge wall in the ocean on which liars are said to be hung after death for judgement, and they flee. They reach an island city called Amoria, meaning love, with walls of twelve gems and a moat of milk, inhabited by welcoming women. The narrator finds human bones in one woman's house, aims a Bulle Fruit at her, and she turns to water. When they flee to the ship the island is gone. It ends with a promise that the next chapter will explain.

Owners: No owner; found as a scroll left in the ruined Faded Castle, once home to Remuria's Harmosts and scholars.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 3-star Book Collection added in 4.6, collected in the Faded Castle.

30.content: The Empire of Solaris appears only in the Anecdota Septentrionalis, an openly fabricated Remurian tale. In it the empire is a technologically advanced realm ruled by knights who ride armoured Blubberbeasts, in a civil war over Lucilius's method of granting extraordinary powers at the cost of one's appearance. It is not a real nation of Teyvat and must not be treated as history.

31.content: Amoria, whose name the inhabitants say means love, is the vanishing island in Vol. 3 of the Anecdota Septentrionalis: a golden city with twelve gemstone walls and a moat of milk, populated by welcoming women, with bones in the houses. When confronted with a Bulle Fruit one woman turns to water, and the island disappears. It is part of the narrator's declared fabrication.

32.content:
Anemo Gnosis (also: Barbatos's Gnosis, Venti's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Anemo Archon): The Anemo Gnosis is the Gnosis of Barbatos (Venti), the Anemo Archon: a gleaming, chess-piece-like divine focus that sat inside his chest and, in his words, resonates directly with Celestia. At the end of the Prologue (1.0) the Fatui Harbinger Signora ambushed Venti in Mondstadt and tore it out. As of 7.1 it is one of six Gnoses held by the Tsaritsa in Snezhnaya.

Losing it did not end Venti's divinity: canon shows that Archons keep their divine thrones and elemental power without a Gnosis. During the limited-time 6.4 event Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind, Venti said it had been of no use to him. Few people know of the theft; he called Gnoses something he was not meant to discuss with ordinary people.

Owners: Chain of possession: Barbatos/Venti (its Archon until 1.0) -> Signora, who took it for the Tsaritsa -> the Tsaritsa (Anastasya), who still holds it. It was the first Gnosis the Fatui seized; the Tsaritsa already had her own Cryo Gnosis. Canon implies the Gnoses went to the seven victors of the Archon War, but never shows how Barbatos, who became Archon after Decarabian's fall about 2,600 years ago, came to hold his. Oddly, after the theft Venti's in-game profile changes from "Vision: Anemo" to "Gnosis: Anemo".

33.comment: Anemo Gnosis: Theft of the Anemo Gnosis
33.content: In Ending Note (Prologue, 1.0), outside the Favonius Cathedral, Signora pinned Venti with ice while her Pyro Agents subdued the Traveler. She tore the Anemo Gnosis from his chest, sneered at the "ugly thing" and left before the Knights of Favonius arrived. Venti, hurt, recovered at Windrise.

34.content:
Angelos' Heptades (also: Angelos Heptades): Angelos' Heptades is a 5-star catalyst in the Hexerei series, described as a golden box as splendid as the light of the heavens that, according to legend, once belonged to a divine envoy of the Eternal Court. Its text tells how the youngest angel was hidden from the angels' rebellion, then chose to cast off divinity and wander among mortals. Added in Version 6.6.

The Hexerei Series is mostly tied to Mondstadt; the wiki points out that this catalyst is the exception.

Appearance: Canon describes only a golden box as splendid as the light of the heavens; the item text does not describe its shape any further.

Lore: The envoy was a newborn girl whose elder sisters protected her; she later gave up her divinity and her old powers, kept human form, and walked the mortal world alone.

Her sisters, including a mother of roses and lilies and a songstress, wrapped her in perfume and warm waters so the music of the world's mundane strings would never touch her. When starlight from beyond ended the paradise beneath the silver-white tree, the eldest daughter who overstepped fell from a mountain peak and armored emissaries perished, while the youngest was hidden far away in a palace in the wilds.

Owners: The weapon "once belonged to" a divine envoy of the Eternal Court. The wiki reads the envoy as Nicole, the youngest angel; Nicole was the featured character on the Version 6.6 banner running with this weapon, but no text declares she holds it now.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 49, ATK secondary stat. Crown of the Final Scion raises ATK. After the wielder creates a Shield they gain Pathfinder's Light, which raises the active character's DMG by ATK scaling, plus Guide's Contentment, which restores Elemental Energy; opening a chest out of combat also triggers it. Under Hexerei: Secret Rite, a Hexerei character off-field gains half the bonus. It was on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2026-05-20 to 2026-06-09).

35.content:
Aqua Simulacra: Aqua Simulacra is a five-star bow of Liyue whose color is unpredictable: under light it takes on a lustrous, watery blue. Its item text says it can summon water and uses water as a lesson, that water has no fixed form and is at once the gentlest and keenest of substances. The story ties the lesson to Yelan, who received it from an elderly senior before she worked for Ningguang of the Jade Chamber.

Yelan is seen with the unascended bow in her Story Quest, in Perilous Trail and in a cameo in The Chasm Delvers, as well as in her promotional material.

Lore: The text opens with the idea that water can serve as blade or bow. A senior taught that water envelops what is impure and washes away filth yet stays pure, takes any form and imitates any life yet never loses itself, and, divided, is uncounted streams or, united, an unstoppable wave. Many secrets hide beneath its azure translucence, and a thousand minds may fail to grasp its shifts.

Owners: Yelan is shown wielding the bow in many quests and cutscenes (her Story Quest, Perilous Trail, a cameo in The Chasm Delvers) and in her art and demo. No earlier owner is given.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star bow from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT DMG 19.2%. Passive "The Cleansing Form": HP rises 16-32% and DMG dealt rises 20-40% while at least one opponent is within 8 metres, whether the wielder is on the field or not (refinements 1 to 5).

36.comment: Aqua Simulacra: Yelan and the bow
36.content: Yelan is the bow's present holder in play; the item story is told partly from her viewpoint, with her own account of preferring tea and dice to ambition and of acting to protect the source of things rather than to serve the powerful. Her full background is in her own file.

37.content:
Aquila Favonia (also: Vennessa's sword): Aquila Favonia is the sword of Vennessa, the enslaved foreign gladiator who led Mondstadt's revolt against its tyrannical old nobles about a thousand years ago and founded the Knights of Favonius and the Church of Favonius. Its item text calls it "the soul of the Knights of Favonius" and says it still calls on the winds of swift justice. Its name means "Eagle of the West Wind", echoing Vennessa's later title, the Falcon of the West.

The sword is a symbol of Mondstadt's founding ideals - justice, freedom and wisdom - rather than an artifact anyone in the present story is shown carrying. In game terms it is a 5-star sword.

Lore: The sword's story says everyone knew "the falcon's" protection was a blessing of Favonius, but few knew that this blessing came from a distant tribe. Under the old nobles, an exiled foreign fighter was enslaved in Mondstadt; she refused to kneel to injustice, overthrew the nobles, founded a chivalric order and the Church, and was eventually blessed to walk with the gods. The sword witnessed all her hardships and deeds.

The text ends with the spirit the wielder is said to feel when swinging it, summarised as a creed: justice for the oppressed, freedom for the shackled, wisdom for the deceived, and to let the wind of justice and freedom lead. The Genius Invokation TCG card adds that the sword was always at the hip of "the warrior from another land" and bore witness to her spreading justice and freedom across Mondstadt.

Owners: Vennessa (the Falcon of the West, first Grand Master and first Dandelion Knight of the Knights of Favonius) is the only named wielder.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword released in Version 1.0, available in the standard Wish (Wanderlust Invocation) and in weapon event and Chronicled Wishes.

38.content:
Archaic Petra (also: Flower of Creviced Cliff, Feather of Jagged Peaks, Sundial of Enduring Jade, Goblet of Chiseled Crag, Mask of Solitude Basalt): Archaic Petra is a 4- and 5-star Geo artifact set (1.0) made of Liyue folk legends about Rex Lapis, the Lord of Geo: flowers from stone, a giant hawk of rock and jade, sundials, wine vessels and a solemn basalt mask. Its Chinese name means roughly 'ancient boulder'.

The pieces are Flower of Creviced Cliff, Feather of Jagged Peaks, Sundial of Enduring Jade, Goblet of Chiseled Crag and Mask of Solitude Basalt. The set drops from the Domain of Guyun in the Guyun Stone Forest.

Appearance: A flower grown in a cliff cleft whose petals seem alive in the wind; a hard seacliff-hawk feather with a black basalt tip; a sundial carved from one large piece of jade; a dignified wine goblet of stone; and a cold basalt mask with hollow eyes.

Lore: Flower: told that barren stone holds no life, the Lord of Geo made golden flowers burst from rock; the text suggests Liyue Harbor, grown out of lifeless mountains, may be that flower. Feather: in the Archon War he uprooted mountains to carve a giant bird of rock and jade, which flattened peaks and dived into the sea, and the stone pillars there still draw birds. Sundial: he made the earth's glittering stars into time-keeping devices to teach early humans the value of every moment. Goblet: he raised bedrock and carved a wine vessel for himself; some say there were seven. Mask: during the Archon War his aspect was one of boundless slaughter and an unchanging stone face, laid down only once the dust settled.

39.comment: Archaic Petra: Rex Lapis legends in Archaic Petra
39.content: The set collects folk legends of the Lord of Geo: golden flowers from stone, a rock-and-jade hawk, star-clock sundials, a carved wine vessel and a mask of unchanging basalt worn during the Archon War. All are told as hearsay.

40.content: Kunwu, then a scholar in training, treasured this jade sundial. After finding no flaw in it he abandoned a dream of studying in Sumeru and apprenticed himself to a master craftsman to rival the creator of such a tool.

41.content:
Ash-Graven Drinking Horn (also: Ash-Graven Horn, Tupac's Grip): The Ash-Graven Drinking Horn is a 4-star catalyst from Natlan: a ritual drinking vessel handed down among the Meztli, said to have been the treasure of the giant hero Tupac. Its story is a banquet song about him.

It belongs to the Meztli series and was given out as an event reward in Version 5.0. The song ends with a moral: unity and promises must never be forsaken.

Appearance: Canon gives only the one-line description: a ritual vessel, a drinking horn. Keep descriptions to a drinking horn; do not invent carvings, inscriptions or colours.

Lore: A minstrel sings of the ancient ancestor Tupac, huge as a mountain. The young hero Tenoch, furious, would have challenged him for the horn; Tupac, laughing, would have answered that it rightfully belonged to him and his homeland's kin.

The song adds tales of Tupac's strength: in a fit of rage he broke mountains with his bare hands and drove rocks into the earth so that hot springs welled up (the singer says those springs in the southwest are still visible), and he once sailed alone to fight a two-tailed whale and tore out its teeth. Years later, remembering the old contest with Tenoch over the horn, he offers the horn before the lord of the blazing flames, the Pyro Archon.

Owners: Legend ties it to Tupac, the giant of the Meztli, who never used it. Later holders are not named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst of the Meztli series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat HP%. Obtained from the Version 5.0 event Traces of Artistry; its refinement material, The Sea's Silent Shade, also came from that event.

42.content: Tupac's Grip is the passive of the catalyst Ash-Graven Drinking Horn (gameplay): an attack that hits an opponent triggers an AoE blow scaled to the wielder's Max HP, on a 15 second cooldown. The name nods to Tupac holding the horn tightly in the song.

43.content:
Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage (also: Crimson Plumage, The Moonring Sighted): Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage is a 5-star bow: an ancient longbow crested with red feathers, a sacred relic of Natlan's Flower-Feather Clan handed down through generations.

Its story is not one tale but several rival songs about a red-eyed young man, banished from the clan, whose pilgrimage ended in divinity.

Appearance: Canon gives only the description: an ancient longbow crested with red feathers. The legend ties the feathers to a red vulture; do not add carvings or colours beyond that.

Lore: The Flower-Feather elder, who only pretended to obey the usurper king, banished a young man to help him escape capture, because he wished to protect the Saurians. His red eyes reflected only the cold aqua moon ring above him.

Poets later sang many versions of the pilgrimage and its hero, and none became the single accepted account. All agree that the red-eyed young man ascended to divinity.

Owners: The Flower-Feather Clan keeps it as a sacred relic; no individual wielder is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star bow, base ATK 46 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.2.

44.comment: Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage: The Moonring Sighted
44.content: The Moonring Sighted is the passive of the bow Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage (gameplay): an ATK boost after a Swirl reaction, with extra Charged Attack and Burst damage when the party's elements are varied. Its name echoes the cold aqua moon ring reflected in the hero's red eyes.

45.content:
Athame Artis: Athame Artis is a 5-star sword in the Hexerei series, described as a precious sword the Day King gave to the brave hero in a little witch's story, only for the witch to take it and defeat the hero herself. Its text is a fairy-tale in which the witch destroys a perpetual motion machine to keep a dying planet alive. Added in Version 6.2.

The weapon is a story object. The wiki's Hexerei Series page notes that its mechanics are tailored to Durin, who also comes from a fairy tale. The name echoes the real-world ceremonial blade called an athame.

Appearance: Canon gives no physical description; it is called a precious sword gifted by the Day King, carried on the hero's back in the story. Do not add decoration or materials.

Lore: A little witch arrives at the Day King's palace as twilight takes the kingdom; the story follows her through the following night.

She had come answering a faint message about a planet feeling unwell, and when night falls the Day King's court dissolves into a black ocean. She flies to a lonely castle where a warrior invites her to see the perpetual motion machine they call the Holy Grail, which burns seawater to keep the dark at bay.

Owners: The item belongs to the story's Day King, who gave it to a hero; no real-world owner is named in canon. The wiki says the weapon is tailored to Durin.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star sword with base ATK 46 and a CRIT Rate secondary stat. Day King's Splendor Solis raises Elemental Burst CRIT DMG and, when a Burst hits, grants an ATK buff to the wielder and nearby party members; having a Hexerei: Secret Rite effect in the party increases it further. It was on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2025-12-03 to 2025-12-23) and again on the Version 6.6 banner (2026-05-20).

46.content:
Aubade of Morningstar and Moon (also: Moonlit Offering's Opulent Dream, Moonlit Offering's Parting Light, Moonlit Offering's Final Hour, Moonlit Offering's Libation, Moonlit Offering's Silver Crown): Aubade of Morningstar and Moon is a 4- and 5-star artifact set dropped in the Moonchild's Treasures domain in Nod-Krai. Its five pieces (Moonlit Offering's ...) carry item text about an ancient age when three moons guided the heavens, how mortals came to worship them, and how two of them fell, ending an age called Eternity. Mechanically it supports Lunar reactions.

Appearance: The pieces are ornaments of ritual devotion to the moons: a carved floral ornament (Flower), a prayer quill (Plume), an hourglass for the final hour (Sands), a wine cup from a rite (Goblet) and a silver circlet worn by hymn poets (Circlet). Item descriptions say they were made in ancient times by artisans, priests, sages, believers and poets honouring the heavenly moons.

Lore: Across the five pieces the legend runs: envoys of the sky, silent at human questions, lose mortals to worship of three moons; a Winged One finishes creation under a false veil and the moons accommodate Order; a primeval dragon had raised the moons and gone into the stars; the long sword at the edge of the world ends Eternity; two moons fall and the New Moon is awaited.

Owners: No character is named as owner. The pieces are described as relics of ancient moon worship, dropped in a domain whose description speaks of Moonchildren priests hiding the remaining sparks of an ancient northern civilisation.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): obtained from Moonchild's Treasures (Nod-Krai), 4- and 5-star. 4-piece: while the wearer is off-field, Lunar reaction DMG is +20%; if the party Moonsign Level is at least Ascendant Gleam, a further +40%. The effect disappears 3s after the wearer is active. Per the wiki it also boosts direct Lunar damage (for example from Ineffa's Overclocking Circuit) and only applies to the equipping character.

47.comment: Aubade of Morningstar and Moon: Aubade of Morningstar and Moon
47.content: Artifact set from the Moonchild's Treasures domain in Nod-Krai, with item text about the age of the three moons, mortal worship of them, and the fall of two moons that ended Eternity. Lunar reaction support for gameplay.

48.comment: Aubade of Morningstar and Moon: The Moon Wheel pact
48.content: In the Opulent Dream text an archpriestess descends from a mountain summit with a small circular talisman, the Moon Wheel, as a new pact between the three moons and humans after the moons hear that mortal hearts also stir with the lunar quakes. It answers human questions with madness and inspiration, something Order could not give.

49.content:
Azurelight: Azurelight is a 5-star sword, once pure white like a dawn star and now tinted deep blue. Its item text is an angel's sermon urging the angels to defy the Heavenly Principles and entrust the world to humanity. Added in Version 5.7.

The sword is a story object rather than a famous artifact in the present-day plot: nobody in the story is shown carrying it, and its text is the only canon voice it has. Its passive is called Whitehill's Bestowal.

Appearance: The in-game description gives only a colour story: the blade was originally white, like a dawn star, and has since been tinted a deep, dark blue. It is a straight sword in the game model; no other physical detail is given in canon text.

Lore: The text is spoken by one who once taught that the heavens' laws must never be questioned, until starlight on a white stone mountain showed them a coming sunrise.

The speaker addresses angels who submitted to the primordial master and says begging, pleading and sacrifice will not loosen their bonds. The call is to cast it all aside, entrust the world to those who live in it and give humanity authority. The speech ends on the promise that once the veil is torn a new day will dawn.

Owners: Canon gives no owner or wielder in the item text. It debuted in Version 5.7 during the same period as Skirk's character banner, but no source cited here says it belongs to her.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star sword with base ATK 48 and a CRIT Rate secondary stat. Whitehill's Bestowal gives an ATK bonus for 12 seconds after an Elemental Skill is used, with a further ATK and CRIT DMG bonus while the wielder has 0 Energy. It was available from weapon event Wishes (Epitome Invocation, 2025-06-18 to 2025-07-08).

50.content:
Ballads of the Squire (also: Squire's Ballads): Both volumes are found in Dawn Winery, and Volume 1 can also be got from Ellin in the City of Mondstadt. The ballads are sympathetic to the poor and hostile to the old aristocracy.

Appearance: A 3-star book collection. The text is free-verse poetry in a first-person voice, in short stanzas with heavy imagery of wind, night streets and chains. The cover title in the Teyvat script reads "Breaking Dawn" (wiki trivia).

Lore: **Volume 1.** The narrator walks every street of Mondstadt and finds both the arrogant rich and the pitiful poor. His peers and superiors proclaim that the starlit knights are the city's true protectors, but he never looks up at the stars or the flag, because he cannot look away from the grimy corners where peddlers weep, old soldiers grimace and a girl rejected by the aristocracy prays to Barbatos for mercy. The wind carries the people's grief against the Cathedral gate and the palace walls, but to those inside it is only the sighing of ants.

**Volume 2.** At dawn a sword-dancer, bound in chains, enters Mondstadt, her silence already a song of freedom. She belongs to the Wanderer's Troupe and is a "dawnlight" to the people but eternal midnight to the aristocracy. The narrator asks why she would overthrow them; she answers by asking why he puts their lives on a pedestal, and whether a man who calls the wind his companion has never known freedom himself. She tells her listeners of the rulers' better ancestors who held divine power, and of angels, gods, dragons and the peoples of the land, turning each legend into song for the wind to carry. In the aristocrats' arena she sings with her sword one last time, her final work stopping short of perfection, and a nameless knight recovers her sword from the blood-soaked battlefield and buries it where the gentle winds meet.

Owners: No character is established as owning it. The Traveler can pick the volumes up in Dawn Winery, and Volume 1 can also come from Ellin in the City of Mondstadt.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a two-volume Book Collection, rarity 3, with no combat function. Both volumes lie inside Dawn Winery; Volume 1 has a second route through a dialogue path with Ellin. Added in version 1.0.

51.comment: Ballads of the Squire: Ragnvindr the Dawn Knight in the ballads
51.content: The ballads are said to come from Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight, and tell of him as a knight's squire in the aristocratic era. The first volume shows him sympathising with the poor and refusing to join his superiors' boasting; the second shows him befriending a Wanderer's Troupe sword-dancer. This is a tradition, not confirmed authorship. His other deeds are covered on his own entry.

52.comment: Ballads of the Squire: The sword-dancer of the Wanderer's Troupe
52.content: Volume 2 centres on a dancer who arrives in chains, speaks of freedom, challenges the aristocrats, and dies in their arena, leaving a sword that a nameless knight buries. She is not named in the ballad. The wiki links her to the Dawnlight Swordswoman and her sword to The Flute.

53.content:
Beacon of the Reed Sea: Beacon of the Reed Sea is a 5-star claymore of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it a large, flat-tipped sword designed as the weapon of an ancient king or some ceremonial instrument. Its story is told through a blind wandering poet who gathers the desert's ballads after the Lord of Sand sank into the desert with dreams in his embrace.

The name echoes the biblical "Reed Sea" (Yam Suph) per the wiki's etymology note; in the text the Reed Sea is the name of a dream that never existed.

Appearance: A large claymore with a flat tip, built like a king's ceremonial weapon. Canon text gives no more detail.

Lore: In an age when kingdoms rose and fell like mushrooms and sandcastles, the blind poet, once of privileged birth, crosses the sea of desert and collects ballads from its scattered people. He hears of the fall of his homeland, of the prince who blinded him finally crushing the overwhelmed throne, of a dancer who helped one man after another become king and then buried them in sandstorms, and of springs replaced by sand and nations shrunk to villages and tribes.

He also hears the tale of the homeless prince's death, the fate of his swords and the killer who went deep into the forest. From the shards of ballads comes a vision, in quotation, of King Deshret's abode on the other side of the dunes: streets like paths of gold converging on one throne, a king who was the destination of all roads until the dreams of gold broke. The kingdom of flowing sands was crushed to golden dust.

Owners: No owner is named. Dehya is shown wielding a claymore of this kind in her Genius Invokation TCG character card and in the Sumeru promotional video (wiki trivia).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star claymore released in Version 3.5 (2023-03-01), level 1 base ATK 46, secondary stat CRIT Rate. Passive Desert Watch raises ATK for 8 s after the wielder's Elemental Skill hits and again after the wielder takes damage, both effects working even off-field, and raises Max HP when the wielder has no shield.

54.content:
Beyond the Chrysalis: Beyond the Chrysalis is a 5-star sword. Its description calls it a longsword brimming with light and color, as weightless as a butterfly when brandished, once used by a certain individual to break bonds. Its text is the story of the eldest daughter of a Vila noble house in Snezhnaya who ended a rebellion against the Tsaritsa and then asked to lose her name. Added in Version 7.1.

Released with Version 7.1 (2026-09-23), the item belongs to Snezhnayan history rather than to a famous present-day wielder; canon does not say who carries it.

Appearance: The only description is of a longsword brimming with light and color, weightless as a butterfly when brandished. The title plays on a chrysalis; the text does not describe any ornament.

Lore: Before she lost her last name, the world knew her as the eldest daughter of the Strivozhas, a Vila noble house.

After Grand Duke Photius died of a sudden stroke, a counselor inherited his title and his planned rebellion with the Druzhna was buried. The Vila house stayed at the top of power, and the Silver Court of Veneter again fell to a Strivozha. Rebels from the fae clans urged the Vila princess to rise against the new Tsaritsa, and she swore to stand at their side.

Owners: Canon does not name an owner. The text tells the story of Gluvasha, a Vila who gave up her house name; a link to the sword is only inferred from the item description about breaking bonds.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star sword, base ATK 48, CRIT DMG secondary stat. Dance of Wings Unbound runs a three-step sequence each time the wielder uses an Elemental Skill or Burst, giving CRIT DMG, then Stellar Swirl DMG, then Energy regeneration, and the sequence resets when the wielder leaves the field. It was on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2026-09-23 to 2026-10-13).

55.content:
Biography of Gunnhildr (also: Gunnhildr's Biography): Biography of Gunnhildr is a Mondstadt history book written by the modern historian Eckhard Gunnhildr. It retells legends of the clan's apical ancestor, Gunnhildr: a chieftain's daughter whose prayer won a wind spirit's protection for her wandering people, and who later honoured Barbatos after the fall of Decarabian's tyranny. It ends by praising the clan's service to Mondstadt today.

The book is a quest item found inside Dawn Winery. Its author calls it a collection of fragmentary stories and legends from the aristocratic period, so it is a clan-friendly, partly legendary account rather than a neutral chronicle.

Appearance: A history book in Mondstadt. Its cover shows the name Gunnhildr in the Teyvat script. The text opens with a blessing to Barbatos and a wish that the wind of freedom prevail in Mondstadt.

Lore: Three thousand years ago (the book's figure), Mondstadt was a frozen wasteland and Decarabian, the Lord of the Tower, fought the North Wind King Andrius. Gunnhildr's father, leader of a nomadic clan, had left Decarabian's service because of his despotism and led his people out into blizzards. Gunnhildr prayed, a wind spirit answered, and she gained the power to protect. She later became clan leader and first priestess, and after Barbatos freed the tyrant's subjects she placed laurels on him.

- The wind spirit gathered the faith formed by the young girl's sincere plea joined to her people's cry, drew its power from it, built a small shelter for the clan and gave her the power to protect.
- After her father's death she became leader and the clan's first priestess, and she led her people to make a stand during the war between Barbatos and the tyrant.
- Later, once Barbatos had departed, aristocrats with divine power rose across the land. The book says they would turn tyrannical a thousand years on, something no one, not even Barbatos, could foresee.
- Her descendants were a prominent aristocratic clan but, unlike the scheming Lawrence Clan, held to the motto "for Mondstadt, as always". In the later struggle against the Aristocracy they sided with the people, and so were spared the exile imposed on the rest of the aristocrats.
- The author closes by noting that the Gunnhildr Clan supplies many knights and clergy of the Knights of Favonius and expects them to keep serving the Anemo Archon.

Owners: No individual owns it; it sits inside Dawn Winery as a quest item.

Gameplay: Game note: a readable quest item with no stats.

56.comment: Biography of Gunnhildr: Gunnhildr's Wind Spirit Shelter
56.content: In the Biography of Gunnhildr, the clan's founder prays in a blizzard and a wind spirit answers. The faith of her people becomes its power, it makes a small shelter for the clan, and it grants her the power to protect. She later becomes the clan's first priestess.

57.comment: Biography of Gunnhildr: Gunnhildr Clan in the Aristocratic Period
57.content: According to Biography of Gunnhildr, the clan's descendants were part of the Aristocracy but kept a motto of protecting Mondstadt, took the people's side in the revolt and avoided exile, unlike the Lawrence Clan. This is the clan's own friendly history, not an independent record.

58.content:
Blackcliff Longsword: Blackcliff Longsword is a 4-star sword of the Blackcliff series, described in game as a sword of blackstone with a dark crimson glow on its black blade. It was wrought by the master craftsman Han Wu from crystallized blackcliff, a rare stone he fetched from the Chasm. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Its item text tells how a cave-in trapped Han Wu's mining crew for four days, how a prototype blade carved them out, and how the sword shattered in the first sunlight and was later remade and named.

Appearance: A black blade with a dark crimson line along its centre. According to the item text the strand is about the length of an outstretched hand and shows on a clear moonlit night, with a faint blood-red flicker in the dark. Do not invent hilt or guard details beyond this.

Lore: Blackcliff is a rare stone; the longsword is cut from its crystallized form and is said to slice through gold and jade easily.

After new prototype designs appeared, Han Wu overhauled his whole catalogue. He believed the right blackcliff would give a superior blade, but final hardness and durability depend on subtle differences in forging temperature and cooling water, a challenge he felt he had to master to rise in his craft. Through a friend in the Yun family he joined a crew to the Chasm to collect the material himself.

Owners: No wielder is named in the item text. Han Wu is its maker. Xingqiu is briefly shown with a Blackcliff Longsword in his Travelers' Tales anecdote (a cameo, not a story claim of ownership).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 44, CRIT DMG secondary stat. Passive Press the Advantage: after defeating an opponent, ATK rises for 30s (12 to 24 per cent by refinement), stacking to 3 with independent durations. It is a Paimon's Bargains item and belongs to the Blackcliff series of weapons.

59.content: Han Wu is the master craftsman named in the item texts of the Blackcliff Longsword and Prototype Archaic. After the great disaster he worked with the Yun family forge on new weapon designs called the prototypes, and later turned to blackcliff for a superior blade. See the entries for the two weapons for details.

60.content:
Blackmarrow Lantern (also: Token of Covenant): Blackmarrow Lantern is a 4-star catalyst of the Rossum series: a lantern with a faint ghostly glow, held in a midnight-black alloy that looks like interlocking bones.

Its description says it was once revered as a precious treasure by a certain secret organization. Its story is a tale of the Godfather of Nod-Krai's black market, who binds three thieves to a creed that theft alone can restore balance, and of the butler who then takes the master thief's black spine bone.

Appearance: A catalyst: a lantern giving off a faint, ghostly glow, contained by a midnight-black alloy resembling interlocking bones. Add no further detail.

Lore: The item story opens with a parable: power is a great edifice, and sheer chance alone decides which brick becomes foundation and which becomes spire. A single brick that refuses the false order can bring the whole building down.

The Godfather's secret treasure is said to lie deep in the black market, and thieves gather to take it in a battle of all against all, where fellow thieves are the deadliest threat. Three get past the guards and into the vault: a fae who reads people like maps and avoids harm, a young lady who cuts every lock with her blade, and a hunter who treats the maze as a harsh hunting ground. All three are defeated by the vault, and a butler in black binds them and brings them before the Godfather.

Owners: No owner is named. The lantern is tied to the Godfather, and the secret organization that revered it is not identified.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst, base ATK 41 at level 1, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 48; part of the Rossum series, introduced in Version 6.0. It is forged, not wished for: the recipe uses a Borderland Catalyst Billet, 50 Rainbowdrop Crystal, 50 White Iron Chunk and 500 Mora, and its diagram is sold by Lyulka at Rossum Workshop in Nod-Krai. Passive "Token of Covenant": increases Bloom DMG (48% at refinement 1, up to 96% at refinement 5) and Lunar-Bloom DMG (12% to 24%), with an additional Lunar-Bloom DMG bonus of the same size under Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam.

61.content: In the Blackmarrow Lantern's story, a fae, a young lady and a hunter fail to beat the Godfather's black-market vault and are bound by oath to the thief's creed after eating a fruit each. His butler then takes the master thief's black spine bone and spares his life. The Godfather is identified as Soini by the Rossum-series lore.

62.content:
Blade of Atonement (also: Repentance and Redemption): Blade of Atonement is a 4-star claymore of Snezhnaya's Kuznets series, described as a greatsword passed down by the Luchkin and said to be fit only for the bravest warrior. Its story is that of Rafalovich, a silent warrior who once served the Burner of Cities and now carries the weight of what he did.

It is a forgeable weapon, with its diagram sold by the blacksmith Kuzmichev at the Kuznets shop in Snezhnograd.

Appearance: Canon calls it a heavy greatsword and gives nothing further about its looks in the text. Do not invent engravings or a hilt.

Lore: Rafalovich is a Volkodlak warrior who once believed the Burner of Cities' promise of a pure, joyful new land. He fought for her without mercy, then abandoned that life and now bears a face wound that never healed and a vow of silence and solitude.

The text tells of a wise one, a fae mentor with an enchanting voice who convinced the warrior that mercy toward foes would only bring ruin. After the warrior defected he followed a guiding one to atone, accepted a new greatsword and swore an oath, but the wise one still visits him in dreams to mock him. Frightened by the kindness of ordinary people who ask him questions, he chooses exile as the price of his sin.

Owners: Rafalovich is the warrior of the story. The description says the greatsword was passed down by the Luchkin. No modern owner is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star claymore from the Kuznets series, base ATK 44 at level 1, second stat ATK 6%; introduced in Version 7.0 and obtained by forging with a Borderland Claymore Billet, Rainbowdrop Crystal, White Iron Chunk and Mora. Passive "Repentance and Redemption": triggering an Elemental Reaction raises Elemental Mastery for 12s, and triggering a Stellar Glimmer reaction also raises ATK for 12s; it works off-field. Values scale with refinement.

63.content: Rafalovich is the silent Volkodlak warrior of the Blade of Atonement's story, who served the Burner of Cities and her wise one, defected to follow a guiding one in atonement, and finally killed a wolf fae of his former comrades. He is not otherwise detailed in canon read here.

64.content:
Blizzard Strayer (also: Snowswept Memory, Icebreaker's Resolve, Frozen Homeland's Demise, Frost-Weaved Dignity, Broken Rime's Echo): Blizzard Strayer is a Cryo artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.2) from Dragonspine. Its pieces tell of the Icebreaker, a quiet hero from a mountain city lost to endless winter, who left with the hopes of its people and was never heard of again. The wiki connects it to Imunlaukr and the fallen nation of Sal Vindagnyr. It drops in the Peak of Vindagnyr domain.

The pieces are Snowswept Memory (flower), Icebreaker's Resolve (feather), Frozen Homeland's Demise (hourglass), Frost-Weaved Dignity (ice cup) and Broken Rime's Echo (crown).

Lore: Snowswept Memory shows a maiden pinning a frost flower on the hero's chest and promising a fourth fresco with his likeness. Icebreaker's Resolve follows him through the storm toward a lost summer palace, carrying the hope of homeless children. Frozen Homeland's Demise says the mountain city believed cold from the sky could freeze time. Frost-Weaved Dignity portrays the silent warrior drinking bitter wine from a cup of ice while the painter begs him to live rather than die forgotten. Broken Rime's Echo has him donning the winter crown and vanishing into the snowstorm.

65.content: The Icebreaker is the unnamed hero of the Blizzard Strayer texts, a silent warrior who left the snow-sealed mountain city to seek hope and was accused of flight when he did not return. The wiki identifies him as Imunlaukr.

66.content:
Bloodsoaked Ruins (also: Mournful Tribute, Requiem of Ruin): A long spear tainted black by unrelenting battle, glowing faintly beneath the ghostly blue light of a lantern-fire. A 5-star polearm from Version 6.0, shown in Flins's hands.

Its item text is a northern tale of two brothers, a snowbound court and a stained spear.

Appearance: A long black spear with a lantern fixed to it. The description speaks of an ethereal glow and ghostly blue lantern-fire; its feathers were once silver-white but the spear now wears the black stain of noble blood. When Flins wields it the lantern shines red in combat (wiki trivia).

Lore: A Snezhnayan folk tale says the King of Midsommar Oak, who brought warmth, was accidentally slain by his elder brother, the King of Winter Icelea, and so the world has known unrelenting winter. The spear's story sets a human tragedy beside it.

The White Emperor, ruler of the fae from the Pale Star throne, fell silent after returning from the ruins of the far north, then opened his doors to humans he had once turned away. A palace rose beside Snezhnograd's furnaces, where the wisest humans and fae gathered and the seeds of a "grand delusion" were sown.

Owners: Flins is shown wielding it in official art and trailers; the item text itself names no owner.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star polearm, CRIT Rate secondary. Passive Mournful Tribute boosts the wielder's Lunar-Charged damage after a Burst and, when Lunar-Charged is triggered, grants CRIT DMG and some Energy (limited to once every 14 seconds).

67.content: Mournful Tribute is the weapon's passive. Its theme, mourning and a vigil, matches the closing image of the Torchforger beginning his watch.

68.content:
Bloodstained Chivalry (also: Bloodstained Flower of Iron, Bloodstained Black Plume, Bloodstained Final Hour, Bloodstained Chevalier's Goblet, Bloodstained Iron Mask, Bloodstained Knight): Bloodstained Chivalry is a Physical artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its five pieces tell the downfall of a righteous knight: he began as a white knight who rescued a maiden, killed so much in the name of justice that he came to see himself as a monster, and finally went to the fallen kingdom to die. The wiki names him as Roland; the texts say only 'the Bloodstained Knight'.

The pieces are Bloodstained Flower of Iron (flower), Bloodstained Black Plume (feather), Bloodstained Final Hour (sands), Bloodstained Chevalier's Goblet (goblet) and Bloodstained Iron Mask (circlet). It is the other half of the story told by the Maiden Beloved set.

Appearance: Black-stained relics of a knight: a dried white flower hardened by blood to the toughness of steel, a raven feather dyed pitch black, a timepiece whose liquid has dried up, a silver goblet engraved with a knight's feats but blackened by smoke and blood, and a luxurious platinum iron mask with permanent dark stains.

Lore: The Flower of Iron tells how the rescued damsel offered a reward and he refused everything but one pure white flower, saying chivalry is its own reward; he wore it over his heart and his bloodshed dried and blackened it. The Black Plume says ravens followed him, he could no longer tell whose blood stained him, and he realised that his path had turned the white knight into a monster. The Goblet shows him returning from a battlefield to find that those awaiting rescue were gone among burning, collapsed houses; he took the smoke-blackened goblet and vowed to rid the world of monsters, poverty and evil. The Iron Mask describes a person he tried to help cowering from him, which made him realise he had become the monster, tainted by the cruelty of a drawn-out war; the mask shields him from the eyes of those he vowed to protect.

Owners: The Bloodstained Knight, whom the wiki identifies as Roland. The goblet and the mask are described as his; the pieces are remnants of his life.

Status as of 7.1: The knight is long dead; the texts say he died in battle in the monsters' lair of the fallen kingdom. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes this set.

69.content: The Bloodstained Knight is the figure of the Bloodstained Chivalry set texts: once a white knight, he became a killer in justice's name and died in the fallen kingdom. The wiki identifies him as Roland. See the set entry for the five piece stories.

70.content:
Breeze Amidst the Forest (also: Breeze in Woods): Breeze Amidst the Forest is a two-volume Mondstadt book. Vol. 1 is an anthology of bard ballads, including the tale of the young Wind Dragon who sought to be understood and became a protector of Mondstadt. Vol. 2 adds excerpts about the Four Winds and the battle between Dvalin and the corrupted dragon Durin. The compiler warns that bards embellish.

Read it as Mondstadt's folk memory of Dvalin, not as an official chronicle. It is also a main in-game text on the faded tradition of Four Winds worship.

Appearance: Cover text reads Breeze in Woods in the Teyvat script. Vol. 1 is introduced as ballads recorded and arranged by scholars centuries ago, the companion to Breeze Upon the Lake; Vol. 2 as a supplement with excerpts from various sources.

Lore: In the ballad, a young dragon graced by Anemo is born in the high heavens, descends and tries to understand humans, but villagers throw stones and farmers curse him. He hears the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the Anemo Archon's lyre, and lands beside the bard. The people panic because dragons and archons never agreed, yet the dragon learns human speech and the bard's songs and stays. Later generations count him among the Four Winds.

- After the Eclipse Dynasty fell and disaster spread, the ballad says the alchemist Gold made an army of shadowy monsters. The black dragon Durin rose from the sea to cast a shadow over Mondstadt.
- At that moment the title of Lionfang Knight had no heir, so the Knights of Favonius could not fly their falcon flag. Prayers called on the Archon, and the Wind Dragon was summoned. He tore open Durin's throat but swallowed its poisonous blood, which was distorted gold, and then fell into a deep slumber.
