- Vol. 2 lists the Four Winds: the Wolf (Knight of Boreas), the Lion (Lionfang or Dandelion Knight), the Falcon (Knights of Favonius) and the Wind Dragon Dvalin. After the Lionfang Knight liberated Mondstadt the Knights of Favonius were established and the Knight of Boreas joined them. The tradition of worship formed gradually, though Dvalin predates all of them.

Owners: No individual owner. Vol. 1 can be obtained from Six-Fingered Jose through a dialogue path; Vol. 2 is Lisa's reward for Sparks Amongst the Pages.

Gameplay: Game note: collectible book collection; lore only.

71.comment: Breeze Amidst the Forest: The Four Winds Tradition
71.content: Breeze Amidst the Forest Vol. 2 explains the Four Winds as Wolf, Lion, Falcon and Wind Dragon, linked to the Knight of Boreas, the Lionfang Knight, the Knights of Favonius and Dvalin. Worship formed over time, the dragon predates them, and temples are now deserted. Who holds the Falcon title is disputed.

72.comment: Breeze Amidst the Forest: The Young Wind Dragon Ballad
72.content: In the Breeze Amidst the Forest ballad, the young Wind Dragon learned human speech and the Windborne Bard's singing. He stayed with the bard hoping to be understood by all souls. This is a bardic, embellished account.

73.comment: Breeze Amidst the Forest: Dvalin and Durin in the Ballad
73.content: The ballad and its supplement say Durin, a corrupted black dragon, attacked Mondstadt and the summoned Wind Dragon killed it, at the cost of ingesting poisonous blood and then sleeping. Durin's remains are said to lie in the snowy peaks to the south.

74.content:
Calamity of Eshu (also: Sanhaj's ritual sword, Eshu's Calamity): The Calamity of Eshu is a 4-star sword from Natlan: the curved ceremonial blade of Sanhaj, the great high priest of the Masters of the Night-Wind. Legend says he used it in rituals that blurred the boundary between the Night Kingdom and the living world.

Its story follows Sanhaj as a silent child who journeyed to find half of his soul and came back knowing the past. The tribe's chief keeps the blade today and lends it for ceremonies.

Appearance: Canon says only that it is a curved ceremonial blade. In its quest uses it carries the power of a Wayob, which the game says can be called on to defend its wielder. Do not invent decoration.

Lore: A child who barely spoke for years was told by a ritual elder that half his soul had been lost in the night flames. On his birthday he walked into the stony wastes to find it, with only the Iktomisaur Mahamba willing to go with him.

Crossing seven curtain layers to reach the Lord of Silence is a journey few return from. In an obsidian hall the boy took in the memories of an ancient era as if he had lived them: the first Pyro Archon swearing a vow before the volcano, and the Sacred Lord Och-Kan, fallen into delirium, beaten down by the crimson-eyed youth on the stairs before an empty throne. The memories gave him every word and its meaning, and let him see far along the threads of time.

Owners: Sanhaj's ritual sword, now kept by the Masters of the Night-Wind's chief.

In The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil (Iktomi Spiritseeking event quests), Citlali brings the chief's ceremonial sword and calls on it during a ritual. In the world quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc she tells the Traveler she borrowed it from the chief and lends it to them for the trip to Mare Jivari, where its Wayob-granted defensive power is used against Bakunawa.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Reward of the Version 5.2 event Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls; its refinement material is Shuttle of Odara.

75.content: Diffusing Boundary is the passive of the sword Calamity of Eshu (gameplay): while a Shield protects the wielder, Normal and Charged Attacks deal more damage and gain CRIT Rate. Its name evokes the blade's story of blurring the boundary between the Night Kingdom and the living world.

76.content:
Calamity Queller: Calamity Queller is a five-star polearm of Liyue, a keenly honed weapon forged from a strange aqua-colored crystal, whose faint blue light seems to whisper of countless past matters. Item text says it was made from materials not of this world, passed through many loyal but unfortunate hands and was lost with the Yaksha who wielded it at the end of the Cataclysm. Shenhe is shown wielding it in official art.

Its owners tend to fight without orders and protect without oaths, and to meet similar fates.

Lore: The story says the long polearm was forged from materials not of this world. It has been through the hands of many loyal yet unfortunate souls, seen slaughters begin and end, and tasted the flesh and blood of foul beasts. An exorcist once came to the great chasm of crystal sands, retrieved an ominous aqua-colored crystal from its depths and hired someone to forge it into a weapon named Calamity Queller.

Owners: Named in the story: a Yaksha lost with it during the Cataclysm (the wiki says Bosacius) and unnamed earlier hands. Shenhe is the character shown wielding it in her official art, which is presentation rather than a story claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star polearm from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 49, secondary stat ATK 3.6%. Passive "Extinguishing Precept": All Elemental DMG +12-24%, and after an Elemental Skill the wielder gains "Consummation" for 20 seconds, raising ATK 3.2-6.4% per second up to 6 stacks, doubled while the wielder is off the field (refinements 1 to 5).

77.content:
Cashflow Supervision (also: Golden Blood-Tide): Cashflow Supervision is a 5-star catalyst: a floating device that can monitor certain phenomena. After being abandoned, it was picked up and modified for other purposes.

Its weapon story is about money. A certain person, linked to Pantalone, wants to prove that currency belongs to humanity and not to a god, and picks the Fortress of Meropide as the place for a test.

Appearance: Canon describes a floating device with a large crystal in its upper part; the crystal glows with Pneuma or Ousia when an Arkhe-aligned character holds it. The text also calls it an overseer made of precision machinery that rumbles as it watches money move. Add nothing else.

Lore: The text argues that the flow of money traces the arteries of the world and that humanity should master currency, not be enslaved by it. A certain person (the wiki links Pantalone) cannot accept that the corner of the world in which money flows was chosen and defined by a god, which the text points at as Liyue and Rex Lapis.

Since the heart of gold has been taken by a god from a distant land, that person decides the system must be overhauled: control of money should be given equally to all, even if mastering the heart of gold is impossible. He proposes to demonstrate it on a small isolated economy, a nation within a nation with minimal divine interference, which the wiki links to the Fortress of Meropide, and to introduce a new currency in place of Mora.

Owners: No owner is named. The device was abandoned, then picked up and modified.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 48 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.1. Passive "Golden Blood-Tide": ATK is raised; when HP increases or decreases, Normal Attack DMG, Charged Attack DMG and Stellar-Conduct DMG rise for 4s (up to 3 stacks, once per 0.3s); at 3 stacks ATK SPD also rises. Values scale with refinement.

78.content: In the weapon story of Cashflow Supervision, a certain person (linked to Pantalone) plans to test a new currency, the Credit Coupon, inside a closed economy, the Fortress of Meropide, to prove money should not be controlled by a god. A machine overseer records every transaction. The text does not state the result.

79.content:
Cecilia (also: Cecilia flower, Cecilias): The Cecilia is a beautiful flower of Mondstadt that grows only where harsh winds blow. It is a Mondstadt local specialty, gathered on Starsnatch Cliff, and is the favourite flower of Venti the bard.

Its item text says the flower has a name that suits its appearance and is as intangible as the true heart of an unbound soul. In the language of flowers it stands for the true feelings of the prodigal son, according to a Paimon questions feature.

Appearance: A delicate wild flower that grows in clusters on windswept ground and appears on Venti's Azure Sky namecard. The Nameless Bard's version had three petals.

Lore: Cecilias grow only in the high, windy places of Mondstadt, and canon ties them to freedom and wind. A vanished civilisation that lived at Cecilia Garden grew them in greenhouses.

Owners: Venti is the character most associated with Cecilias; the Nameless Bard is shown wearing one.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a local specialty found on Starsnatch Cliff, given by a few NPCs after dialogue, sold in shops, and grown via Luxuriant Glebe gardening.

80.content: Cecilias are Venti's favourite flower. He wears one in his hat and has one adorning his lyre, Der Frühling. The Nameless Bard wore a three-petaled Cecilia on his vest.

81.content:
Celestial Gift (also: Heavensent Fragrance, Heavensent Demise, Heavensent Decree, Heavensent Reward, Heavensent Crown): Celestial Gift is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain in Mondstadt. Its Heavensent pieces tell of a star-faring civilisation that watched the cosmos die, a voyager who woke from the void to find a shrouded world, and the eldest angel's rebellion in the frozen north against the heavens. Mechanically it gives Energy Recharge and team Elemental DMG Bonus.

The legend picks up threads also told in Finale of the Deep Galleries and Aubade of Morningstar and Moon, but from the closing days of the northern revolt, not its beginning.

Appearance: Each piece is described as a gift of the high heavens to their envoy, each turned into a temptation: an everlasting flower (greed), a feather of rebirth (forgiveness at fate's end), a sundial of counter-time (a prohibition that fed rage), nectar from an unending feast (desire) and a splendid crown (arrogance).

Lore: Across the five pieces: a star-faring civilisation watches the cosmos die, a chronicler-voyager wakes and finds a shrouded world, and the eldest angel leads a last rebellion in the frozen north against the heavens as a falling nail ends it.

Owners: No owner is named; the pieces are presented as gifts bestowed by the heavens upon their envoys.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; domain Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind (Windrest Peak, Mondstadt). 4-piece: if the wearer has completed Witch's Homework, after using an Elemental Skill they grant nearby party members "Light's Guidance", +20% Elemental DMG Bonus matching the wearer's element, for 20s, even off-field; same-name bonuses do not stack. With the Hexerei: Secret Rite effect it becomes "Mortal Hymn": +40% Elemental DMG Bonus for both the wearer's and the active character's elements (no stacking if the elements match).

82.content: Artifact set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain, with item text about a dying star-faring civilisation, a voyager, and the last war of the first angel against the heavens.

83.comment: Celestial Gift: The voyager of the void
83.content: In the Fragrance and Decree texts a chronicler of a time-transcending race wakes from long contemplation and sees a world missing from the old star map. Bound by law not to interfere, she nonetheless reaches into the world inside the shell, driven by curiosity or the hope for change.

84.content:
Cinnabar Spindle: Cinnabar Spindle is a 4-star sword, in-game description "a sword made from materials that do not belong in this world," whose power might withstand the corruption of a venom that could corrode a mighty dragon. It was the reward weapon of the limited-time event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms in Version 2.3, a Dragonspine event in which Albedo appears; it ran 2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13.

Its item text reads like an alchemist's message handed down to a successor and is tied by the wiki to Albedo and his creator Rhinedottir. Its name is also alchemical: cinnabar is the ore of mercury, and the weapon is refined with an event material called Alkahest.

Appearance: Canon gives no description of the blade beyond the "otherworldly materials". The wiki notes its colors match Albedo's design; avoid inventing other details.

Lore: The text is an exhortation: separate the dust in the flames with joy and extract the exquisite from the crude, for all things in the universe come from a single source and may be derived from a single thought.

It tells the addressee to pursue what the elder brother, "the one-horned white horse," could not accomplish, to reach the far side of philosophy and to create a new destiny for the speaker and the addressee's brothers. The wiki reads this as Rhinedottir speaking to Albedo about the False Horned Steed and the Primordial Human, but the text itself names nobody.

Owners: No owner is named in item text. In the Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event cutscenes, Albedo is seen using a blade matching it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 4-star sword with base ATK 41 and a DEF% secondary stat. Its passive, Spotless Heart, adds a share of DEF to the wielder's Elemental Skill damage (once per 1.5s, cleared shortly after the skill deals damage), and it works even when the wielder is off-field. Instead of duplicate weapons, refinement uses Alkahest, four of which come from the event.

85.comment: Cinnabar Spindle: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event
85.content: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms was a limited-time Version 2.3 Flagship event (2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13) played in Dragonspine, with Albedo appearing in its story. Cinnabar Spindle was its reward weapon, and the event's cutscenes show Albedo using a matching blade. This entry does not cover the event's plot.

86.content:
Clash of Kings: Clash of Kings is a 4-star catalyst: a golden box lavishly inlaid with precious jewels that houses a game much beloved by the kings of the sands. Its story is a legend of three gods who, bored in a formless world, create a new one and play a board game over it.

It is a Battle Pass (Gnostic Hymn) reward from Version 7.0 and belongs to the Gnostic Hymn 3 series. The story is comic in tone: the gods bicker over rules, and nobody wins.

Appearance: A golden box set with precious jewels, holding the game. The description gives no further detail.

Lore: The story is told as a legend. Before anything existed there were only three gods in a world without beginning or end: Valor, with unlimited power; Cunning, with unlimited wisdom and guile; and Nature. Valor and Cunning fought endlessly without result, so Nature proposed making a new world and deciding the winner with dice, since even gods cannot change the dice.

Valor flattened the land into a square chessboard and shaped mountains and rivers after the old world. Cunning carved the pieces: angels, humans, Jinn and monsters, and the dragons and magical beasts that Nature's will drove. Countless days and nights passed over the little world, and only the gods' dice could decide its fate.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, level 1 base ATK 42, secondary stat CRIT Rate 6%. Passive Without Heed for Day nor Night: using an Elemental Skill grants Laws of the Board for 6 s, raising ATK and Elemental Mastery; it can trigger once every 12 s and does not stack. A Charged Attack hit during it extends the duration by up to 6 s.

87.content:
Cloudforged (also: Crag-Chiseled Forge): Cloudforged is a 4-star bow added in Version 4.7. Its in-game description calls it a prototype of a standard-issue weapon that the Yuheng commissioned from Blackcliff Forge, after analysing the ancient mechanisms that guarded the adeptal abode on Mount Tianheng. It was a reward of the limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation.

Its archive text is not about the bow itself but about Blackcliff Forge and the semi-legendary founder of the Yun family of smiths.

Appearance: Canon gives no description of the bow's look. Do not invent materials or decoration.

Lore: The item text says the ancients called Mount Tianheng full of gems and the Chasm rich in jade, and that Liyue's key mining and smelting works are in Blackcliff Forge, carved into Tianheng itself.

The Forge was built by hollowing out the mountain into countless workshops, furnaces and soot-blackened connecting tunnels. In the years of war the ancestors of the mountain tribes took shelter there, and long-forgotten passages are said to lead down to an ancient underground realm. According to the Stone Tablet Compilations, the founder of the famed Yun family first carved the dark paths through the mountains, and the Yun house of smiths has since been honoured by later artisans as their progenitor.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. The description frames it as a prototype of an issue weapon for the Yuheng (the office Keqing holds).

Quests: Obtained through the limited-time Version 4.7 event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation, which also gave the refinement material Cam and Cables of Law.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star bow, base ATK 42, Elemental Mastery secondary stat (36). Passive Crag-Chiseled Forge: after Elemental Energy is decreased, the wearer gains 40 to 80 Elemental Mastery (by refinement) for 18s, up to 2 stacks. Refinement uses Cam and Cables of Law instead of duplicate weapons; four came from the event.

88.comment: Cloudforged: Blackcliff Forge and the Yun founder
88.content: Cloudforged's text portrays Blackcliff Forge as a mountain-carved complex of workshops and tunnels, a refuge in wartime and later Liyue's key mining and smelting centre, begun by the founder of the Yun family of smiths. The legend of adeptal teaching coexists with the claim that the Forge was built by ordinary labour.

89.content:
Conch Echoes (also: Conch Echoes (book)): It is a fable, not a record. No character is named beyond nicknames such as "Shorty", and no real place is identified. Its theme is that a leader's authority fails when he fears being seen as flawed, and that a shared symbol of speech should belong to everyone.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of two volumes. Both are sold by Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town.

Lore: Vol. 2: The young man has become pale, green-tinged and stiff, slumped in a heap-laden chair, with the blade fallen where nobody will pick it up. A girl with glasses finds Shorty. He says he saw this coming from the moment the conch was demanded, and that the tyrant, afraid of showing flaws as the adults had, grew suspicious, sleepless and angry until he undid himself. Shorty picks up the nicked, chipped blade, throws it into the sea, and holds the conch to his ear to hear the waves. He proposes a town where the conch belongs to all, and he accepts that today's children will become tomorrow's adults and others may overthrow them.

Owners: No owner. It is a commercial book sold in Nasha Town.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 6.0, bought from Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books.

90.comment: Conch Echoes: Shorty and the Conch
90.content: In the fable Conch Echoes, "Shorty" is the smallest of the exiled children and keeps the conch that gives its holder the right to speak. He gives it up to a rival with a blade, lets that rival wreck himself, then throws the blade into the sea and makes the conch common property of a new town. Both are fictional figures with no known canon counterpart.

91.content:
Crane's Echoing Call (also: Cranes Echoing Call): Crane's Echoing Call is a five-star catalyst of Liyue, described in game as a fan carved from pure jade with an ancient aura of adeptal energy swirling around it. Its item story tells of a distant time before Liyue Harbor existed, when refugees begged the adepti for shelter while a horde of maddened monsters pursued them, and how the adeptus Cloud Retainer is said to have saved them. Xianyun, who is Cloud Retainer, wields it.

The story gives three competing versions of the rescue, and the speaker at the end teasingly refuses to say which is true.

Lore: In the distant past, before the harbor city existed, even the adepti's abodes were burned by the war of the gods. Survivors who lost everything fled to the mountains and begged the adepti for shelter, hounded by countless monsters that had lost their senses. These monsters came like a flood and were, in truth, mourning the fallen master they had once revered, the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. Only a few yaksha stood between the refugees and catastrophe, fighting for days until white clothes turned scarlet and scarlet turned black.

Owners: Wielder: Xianyun (Cloud Retainer), shown with the ascended version in her character demo and Collected Miscellany. The item text does not name an owner.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star catalyst from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 49, secondary stat ATK 3.6%. Passive "Cloudfall Axiom": after the wielder lands a Plunging Attack, all nearby party members' Plunging Attacks deal 28-80% more DMG for 20 seconds, and their Plunging hits restore the wielder 2.5-3.5 Energy every 0.7 seconds, even off the field (refinements 1 to 5). The wiki lists its base ATK among the highest in the game.

92.comment: Crane's Echoing Call: Cloud Retainer legend
92.content: Cloud Retainer is an adeptus of Mt. Aocang and Jueyun Karst, said in legend to have rescued refugees from a monster tide long before Liyue Harbor. She is also known as Xianyun in the mortal world and can take a crane form. The item story gives three versions of the rescue and does not decide between them.

93.content:
Crimson Agate (also: Crimson Agates): Crimson Agate is a crystal found on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. It forms when concentrated life force combines with an energy unique to Dragonspine, and it is ideal nourishment for the Frostbearing Tree.

The crystals are offered to the Frostbearing Tree, much as Oculi are offered to the Statues of The Seven, to earn rewards. They lie in the open, in chests marked by a dark red glow, and as rewards for Crimson Wishes.

Appearance: A red crystal. Overworld agates show a map icon and sound like Oculi do, and chests holding one are surrounded by a dark red aura.

Lore: The item text frames the agates as the tree's nutrition after it was shattered and frozen by the Skyfrost Nail. The crimson is the blood of a black dragon that fell into Wyrmrest Valley, carried through the ley lines.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: 80 agates can be found in the overworld and chests, enough to raise the Frostbearing Tree from Offering Level 1 to 9 before Crimson Wishes, which unlock at Level 8. Crimson Wishes keep giving agates until the tree reaches Level 12.

94.comment: Crimson Agate: Crimson Agate and the Frostbearing Tree
94.content: Crimson Agates are the offering that makes the Frostbearing Tree of Dragonspine grow. The tree was shattered and frozen when the Skyfrost Nail descended, and later absorbed the blood of a black dragon through the ley lines.

95.content:
Crimson Moon's Semblance (also: Crimson Moon's Semblance polearm): Crimson Moon's Semblance is a 5-star polearm (released in Version 4.6) whose text recalls an ancient Khaenri'ahn dynasty that revered the crimson moon. Its description calls it a keen-edged weapon with a luster as dazzling as the crimson moon, once regarded by that dynasty as a ritual object that could bridge two worlds. Arlecchino is its signature wielder in gameplay.

Nobody in the item text remembers the beliefs and ceremonies tied to the weapon; the dynasty is described as a bygone age. The story is a lament about the fall of the Crimson Moon's followers and the survival of only the epithet "Balemoon."

Appearance: A polearm with a bright, keen edge, its sheen compared to the crimson moon. When Arlecchino wields it, it transforms into a scythe during her Normal Attacks, Charged Attack and Elemental Skill. In her "Masque of the Red Death" state it shows a red aura running down the staff (gameplay presentation).

Lore: The item story is a sombre account of Khaenri'ah's old royal clan and the Crimson Moon, not of the weapon's own forging.

It opens with an invocation to the High Lord of the Nobles of Khaenri'ah: the crimson-red moon has long since fallen into the abyssal firmament, and the blindness of that bloodline has ended the line. A cup of wine is offered to the lord.

Owners: Arlecchino, the Fourth Fatui Harbinger and head of the House of the Hearth, is its signature wielder.

Arlecchino is a descendant of the Crimson Moon Dynasty and is titled "Dire Balemoon," echoing the story's word. The weapon's text does not mention her, and canon does not spell out how the weapon relates to her in story terms.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 5-star Polearm with a base ATK of 48 and a secondary stat of CRIT Rate. Its passive, Ashen Sun's Shadow, grants a Bond of Life equal to 25% of Max HP when a Charged Attack hits an opponent (at most once every 14 seconds). While the wielder has a Bond of Life they gain a DMG Bonus, and a further bonus if the Bond of Life is at least 30% of Max HP. The bonuses rise with refinement, and Bonds of Life from this weapon can stack. It was released on 2024-04-24 through Weapon Event Wishes and is also available in Chronicled Wishes.

96.comment: Crimson Moon's Semblance: Crimson Moon Dynasty and Balemoon
96.content: The weapon's story presents the Crimson Moon Dynasty as an ancient royal clan of Khaenri'ah whose priests tied the throne to the Crimson Moon. Its fall left only the epithet "Balemoon" and a few survivors hiding from the later dark sun.

key: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set
97.content:
Crimson Witch of Flames (also: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set, Witch's Flower of Blaze, Witch's Ever-Burning Plume, Witch's End Time, Witch's Heart Flames, Witch's Scorching Hat): Crimson Witch of Flames is a Pyro artifact set (4 and 5 star) built around the story of a young woman who lost her hopes and loved ones in a calamity and became a witch who burned monsters and demons. Its texts call her 'the Crimson Witch of Flame'. Later canon (Archon Quest, 2.1) identifies her as the Fatui Harbinger Signora, once a maiden of Mondstadt. The set is earned in the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula.

Appearance: Pyro-themed relics: a flower that survives flame, a never-dying feather, a small timepiece holding a hot liquid, a flame-spitting urn holding liquid fire, and a witch's tall hat with a broad brim.

Lore: Per the item texts, a crisis centuries ago took the maiden's loved ones, her past and her promised future. From it the Crimson Witch of Flame was born, dreaming of burning away all the demons in the world. Her fire touched only monsters and demons, yet people shut their windows and tried to drive her off. She wanted no comfort; only the birds beside her understood. Historians were loath to remember her.

98.comment: Crimson Witch of Flames: Crimson Witch of Flame legend
98.content: The 'Crimson Witch of Flame' of the artifact texts is a legendary witch who burned monsters and demons after a calamity cost her everything. The texts do not name her. A student at the Akademiya, she was hated and feared by ordinary people although her fire touched only monsters. Historians were loath to remember her.

99.content:
Cryo Gnosis (also: Tsaritsa's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Cryo Archon): The Cryo Gnosis is the Gnosis of the Cryo Archon. It is held by Anastasya, the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, and is the only one of the seven Gnoses that never had to be collected by the Fatui. Like every Gnosis, it is a divine focus that resembles a chess piece and strengthens its bearer's elemental power. Each Archon's Gnosis also links them to Celestia.

As of Version 7.1, the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses: her own Cryo Gnosis plus the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses her Harbingers gathered. Only the Pyro Gnosis is missing. In 7.1 she revealed that all seven Gnoses were formed from the remains of the Third Descender. She wants them for two reasons: to amplify her power for a confrontation with the Heavenly Principles, and to open a seal the Third Descender left beneath Zapolyarny Palace.

Appearance: Like every Gnosis it resembles a gleaming chess piece and normally rests within its Archon's chest. No canon text describes its individual shape or colour, so do not invent details.

Owners: Current holder: Anastasya, the Tsaritsa and Cryo Archon, at Zapolyarny Palace in Snezhnograd.

Gameplay: Gameplay: the Cryo Gnosis is a story object only. Players cannot obtain or equip it, and it has no stats. It appears only in Archon Quest cutscenes and dialogue.

100.comment: Cryo Gnosis: Third Descender's seal and the Gnoses
100.content: Beneath Zapolyarny Palace lies a large crystalline seal left by the Third Descender before the Heavenly Principles killed him. The Heavenly Principles seem never to have noticed it. The Belyi Tsar guarded it first, and the Tsaritsa inherited the duty. Every attempt to open it has failed, and only a Gnosis draws any response from it. The Tsaritsa believes all seven Gnoses, his reunited remains, are needed. She showed it to the Traveler in Light and Shadow, Intertwined. As of 7.1 it remains sealed because the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

101.content:
Crystal Chunk (also: Crystal Chunks, Crystal Ore): Crystal Chunk is a turquoise crystal, an uncut ore taken from Crystal Ore nodes in caves, mines and mountains across Teyvat. Its item text says only professional craftsmanship can bring out its true value. Smiths use it in forging, chiefly for Mystic Enhancement Ore.

It is found in the wild, including Stormterror's Lair, and can also come from shops and expeditions.

Appearance: Raw, uncut turquoise crystals, grown in clusters inside breakable ore nodes. They are plainer than the blue Magical Crystal Chunk, whose crystals have been altered by the Ley Lines.

Lore: The in-game description calls it an uncut crystal whose real value emerges only through professional craftsmanship. A longer form of the text names this clear rock a precious gift of the land, useful as a valuable weapon-making material. Nothing more is said about its origin.

102.content:
Crystal Core (also: Crystal Cores, crystalfly core): Crystal Core is the core of a crystal butterfly, a crystalfly. Its item text says it absorbs elemental energy that has escaped into the atmosphere. It is obtained by catching a crystalfly, not by fighting it.

Moonglow Fireflies also yield it.

Appearance: A small glowing core taken from a crystalfly, one of the elemental butterflies seen across Teyvat in several types, including Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro, Pyro and Cryo.

Lore: The item description presents it as the core of a crystal butterfly that takes in elemental energy that had escaped into the atmosphere. The wiki describes crystalflies as elemental life-forms. Their cores therefore stand for loose elemental energy gathered into a small body.

103.content:
Customs of Liyue (also: Liyue Customs): Customs of Liyue is a three-volume book about Liyue's traditions, originally compiled by Fadhlan, a scholar from Sumeru living in Liyue, then edited by local scholars and published. It is described as one of Liyue's bestsellers. The volumes cover the wedding flower ball, the Rite of Descension in which the Geo Archon receives his people, and the cultural place of the Silk Flower and its perfumes.

Much of the commentary is the outsider's viewpoint of a Sumeru scholar, who contrasts Liyue's practical, prosperity-minded devotion with Sumeru's ecstatic scholar-sages and who declines in the last lines to guess at the Geo Archon's inner feelings.

Appearance: Three short essays headed Flower Ball, Receiving God and Silk Flowers. The tone is that of a gently wry travel-writer's survey, mixing legend with practical observation, such as Millelith injury logs.

Lore: - Vol. 1, Flower Ball: at Liyue weddings the bride tosses a flower ball to the guests; catching it is said to bring a year of good luck. Wealthier families use silk balls, poorer families paper or cloth.
- Vol. 2, Receiving God: the Rite of Descension is the most iconic Liyue ceremony, at which the Geo Archon descends to deliver his proclamations. In the Qixing era a member of the Qixing hosts it.
- Vol. 3, Silk Flowers: the Silk Flower is used for silk and perfume. Rural legend credits an adeptus on Mt. Aocang with teaching mortals perfume making, and the flower is a symbol of Rex Lapis.

- Vol. 1 notes that the Millelith's security logs attribute roughly as many injuries per year to flower ball tossing as to monster attacks. It gives two possible origins: Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum, or the Salt God Havria, a gentle god ousted in the Archon War and murdered by one of her own followers, said to have handed flowers to her people as comfort. Her remains are thought to lie in the ruins of Sal Terrae, and her followers may have spread the custom across Liyue.
- Vol. 2 says early farmers chose representatives to greet and see off the Geo Archon, who made predictions that set the year's work. After the Archon War, Liyue Harbor's merchants prized his predictions above ore, and travelled home to hear them. Only a Qixing member may host the rite. The author contrasts Liyue's worldly gains from divine guidance with the raving sages of Sumeru's rainforests, and notes that the Seven's paths can diverge.
- Vol. 3 says the Silk Flower is cultivated in a special strain for luxury perfume, offered first to Rex Lapis. An unwritten rule makes it impolite to ask a woman about her perfume, but an admirer who correctly identifies it tactfully may win her favour. Wild Silk Flowers have nearly vanished from rural areas because of mining and geographic change; the remaining few are tended by reclusive adepti.

Owners: No individual owner. Vol. 1 is on a shelf at Wanwen Bookhouse and is a reward from Soraya. Vol. 2 is on Ningguang's desk in the Jade Chamber and appears during Zhongli's story quest Sal Flore. Vol. 3 is sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse in Liyue Harbor.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible book collection read for lore only.

104.comment: Customs of Liyue: Flower Ball Custom
104.content: At Liyue weddings the bride throws a flower ball; the guest who catches it is said to enjoy good luck for a year, whatever their situation. Wealthy families use silk-flower balls and poor families paper or cloth. Origin is disputed between Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum and the followers of the ancient Salt God Havria. Millelith logs count many injuries from it.

105.comment: Customs of Liyue: Silk Flower Perfume
105.content: In Customs of Liyue Vol. 3 the Silk Flower is a Liyue luxury, used for silk and perfume. Perfume is a delicate social topic; guessing a woman's scent tactfully is a courting skill. Legend says an adeptus on Mt. Aocang taught the art, and the flower is one of Rex Lapis' symbols.

106.content:
Dawning Frost (also: Nocturnal Dreams, Dawning Frost catalyst): A silver-forged ritual vessel, pure and without blemish, said to be a sacred relic passed down among the priestesses of the far north. A 4-star catalyst of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.1.

Its text follows a mother's prophetic dream.

Appearance: A catalyst described as a silver-forged ritual vessel, unblemished. The text mentions a silvery-white talisman worn at the chest, but does not say it is this object.

Lore: The item text is a warning and a dream: a mother tells her child, Avrelian, never to set foot in Nod-Krai and not to be taken in by "that fool's dream of Elysium".

She is the woman once worshipped as the Maiden, living far from her homeland (Hiisi Island). She says a thousand-year-old curse runs in his blood and no earthly paradise has been built for mortals under the moon. Pregnant, she is troubled by visions of the fate of her homeland.

Owners: No wielder is named; the description ties it to the priestesses of the far north.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42, CRIT DMG secondary. Passive Nocturnal Dreams gives Elemental Mastery for 10 seconds after a Charged Attack hits, and a separate boost after an Elemental Skill hits. Released in Version 6.1.

107.content: Nocturnal Dreams is the weapon's passive, named for the prophetic dreams in its text. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

108.content:
Deathmatch (also: Deathmatch polearm, the gladiator's spear): Deathmatch is a four-star crimson polearm, part of the Gnostic Hymn series from the Battle Pass. Its item story follows a gladiator who fought for blood, then for the young master he loved, and who died by the blade of a red-haired maiden at his last performance. The wiki identifies that maiden as Vennessa and the master as Eberhart.

Item text calls it a gladiator's priceless treasure, with a point stained by the blood of countless beasts and men. It is a Mondstadt-linked story weapon, tied by the wiki to the Gladiator's Finale artifact set.

Appearance: A sharp crimson polearm with an ice-cold tip. The text mentions nothing else about its shaft or decoration, so do not invent any.

Lore: The story is a duelist's tragedy. The polearm watched the valor of a gladiator whose tip was often wet with the blood of his foes while the crowd applauded. Freedom always seemed near and never came. When his master told him the promised number of victories had been met, he offered the spear as a parting gift and asked him to fight on as a free man, for glory, for the gladiator and for himself. Over many years the beasts and men the spear felled were too many to count, and the weapon was called undefeated, but the gladiator's heart belonged to his young master.

Owners: The gladiator of the item story (historical.unnamed-gladiator), who received it from his master as a parting gift. No later owner is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): obtained through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn. Base ATK 41, secondary stat CRIT Rate 8%. Passive 'Gladiator': with at least two opponents nearby, ATK and DEF each rise by 16-32% across refinements 1-5; with fewer than two, ATK rises by 24-48% instead.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a symbol of loyalty that outlasts freedom, and of a person who stops fighting for himself and starts fighting for someone else. A character holding it can reasonably speak of arena life and of the cost of a master's applause.

109.content: The Deathmatch story's gladiator was freed by promise but chose to keep fighting for his young master Eberhart. He was killed in the arena by a red-haired maiden, whom the wiki identifies as Vennessa. His name is not given in canon.

110.content:
Deepwood Memories (also: Labyrinth Wayfarer, Scholar of Vines, A Time of Insight, Lamp of the Lost, Laurel Coronet): Deepwood Memories is a Sumeru rainforest artifact set (Version 3.0, Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain). Its five pieces are fragments of old forest legends: a labyrinth of roots and water, a lord of the forest and the maiden who inherited his crown, a huntress with a white bow, and friends who fought forgetting.

Nothing in the set is dated. It reads as a mix of oral legend and a few personal confessions, and no piece names its speaker.

Lore: When the lord of the forest was born, the king of trees gave them a crown, which passed to the first maiden to follow in the lord's footsteps. She took in lost children and taught them the hunt, the walk through dreams and love for the forest's plants and creatures. Some became guardians who patrolled the woods and lit bonfires against the dark. One stayed behind, hunting the shadows until she dreamed a great dream of the labyrinth and hunt that covered every other dream of the forest, and then she disappeared with it.

The Laurel Coronet gives the forest's origin: the god of trees made a forest among the sands and first built a device to call rain; moonlight on the water drew a labyrinth, and the labyrinth birthed a tiger named Viaghara, the first lord. Pomegranate seeds became forest spirits, who were allowed to share the labyrinth by a pact. The last lord died defending the nurseries of life and a large whiskered cat took the name. A Time of Insight records the immortal lord melting into the forest and friends who vowed to remind one another of their forms to defeat death, until forgetfulness struck. Lamp of the Lost tells of a desert prince who fled to the rainforest and was accepted by its dream.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a set from the Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain (4 and 5 star) and its strongbox. 2-piece: Dendro DMG Bonus +15%. 4-piece: after Elemental Skills or Bursts hit, the target's Dendro RES is lowered by 30% for 8s, even if the wearer is off-field. Released in 3.0; no later change is listed.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present these as half-remembered rainforest legends, not as history. Treat the forest lords, the maiden and the huntress as unnamed.

111.content: The flower piece of Deepwood Memories: a gold-plated flower from the crown of the lord of the forest. It tells of the first maiden who followed the lord, took in lost children, taught them the hunt and the walk through dreams, and whose lessons produced guardians who patrol the woods. One stayed until she eroded into a vast dream of the labyrinth and hunt.

112.content: The plume piece: an emerald leaf as fluffy as a feather, plucked from a forest scholar's raiment. Two verses: the years of the lord of the labyrinth, with a servant girl who read the poetry of moonlight, and the years of the ominous moon, with a blind swordsman, a white relic and a huntress.

113.comment: Deepwood Memories: A Time of Insight
113.content: The sands piece: a timepiece that holds mustard seeds instead of sand, used by those following the way of the wise. Its verses say the lord of the forest was immortal, melting into the forest at death. Then a speaker whose friend suffers from forgetfulness plans to capture dream spirits to remind them of their shared past.

114.comment: Deepwood Memories: Lamp of the Lost
114.content: The goblet piece: a desert-style oil lamp that has sprouted glowing green leaves. It belonged to a prince of the decaying desert kingdoms. He tells of his father falling from a tower while chasing a falcon, of burying a lover, of becoming a refugee, and of a rainforest that accepted him after a huntress with a white bow hunted him each night.

115.content: The circlet piece: a crown given by the deity of plants, an heirloom of the royal house of the labyrinth, passed at last to the king's attendant. Its verses describe the cycle of life and death, the god of trees creating a forest among the sands, the first rain-calling device, the tiger Viaghara and the labyrinth, and the forest spirits' pact.

116.content:
Dendro Gnosis (also: Gnosis of Sumeru, Dendro Archon's Gnosis, Kusanali's Gnosis, Nahida's Gnosis): The Dendro Gnosis is Sumeru's Gnosis, one of seven chess-piece-like divine foci held by The Seven, carried inside the Archon's chest. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata used it to build and power the Akasha. In 3.2 Nahida (Lesser Lord Kusanali) gave it to the Fatui Harbinger Dottore in exchange for knowledge about the "false sky", and shut the Akasha down. Dottore brought it to the Tsaritsa in Snezhnaya, and as of 7.1 she holds it with five other Gnoses. Nahida is still the Dendro Archon without it.

Lore: Rukkhadevata built the Akasha during the Cataclysm to pool human wisdom against the forbidden knowledge polluting Irminsul, and it ran on the Dendro Gnosis. In 3.2 the Balladeer tried again and again to tear the Gnosis from Nahida's chest. Nahida then combined it with the Electro Gnosis she won from him to reach Rukkhadevata's last memory. Afterwards Dottore asked for it, arguing that Sumeru would have no use for it once the Akasha was shut down, and offered knowledge in return. She accepted, because as God of Wisdom she would not choose ignorance.

Consequences: The Akasha could not run without the Gnosis, so Nahida shut it down for good. Akasha Terminals became useless and dreams came back to Sumeru. Nahida keeps her divine throne and the Dendro Authority. She has also used other Gnoses: the Electro Gnosis briefly in 3.2, and the Pyro Gnosis to burn Irminsul in 6.6.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa (Anastasya) holds it in Snezhnaya, one of her six Gnoses; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

She collects the Gnoses to amplify her power against the Heavenly Principles and to open the Third Descender's seal. In 7.1 the Gnoses turned out to be remains of the Third Descender, Saarelainen.

117.comment: Dendro Gnosis: Dottore's bargain for the Dendro Gnosis
117.content: In 3.2 Dottore (his Omega Build, segment 35) first traded Nahida the destruction of his other segments for the Electro Gnosis. Then he called the Gnosis "another chess piece" and asked for her Dendro Gnosis as a separate deal. Nahida called it arrogant, since people traditionally trade knowledge with the God of Wisdom, not for her property, but admitted she was interested. He told her the rumour that "the skies of Teyvat are fake", the secret Irminsul hides about the world's "truth", and she handed the Gnosis over.

key: The First Days of the City of Kings
118.content:
Desert Pavilion Chronicle (also: The First Days of the City of Kings, End of the Golden Realm, Timepiece of the Lost Path, Defender of the Enchanting Dream, Legacy of the Desert High-Born): Desert Pavilion Chronicle is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain). Its five item texts form one poem, recited by an old blind poet, about Gurabad: the shepherd Ormazd made vassal king with the Jinni Liloupar's help, his slide into tyranny, Liloupar's revenge, the city's fall, and the desert splintering into seven states.

Each piece addresses a different listener. The recurring warning is that love and power left unchecked destroy the city they build.

Lore: Legend says the Lord of the Sands, after his lover's death, made a pact with humanity through the Jinn: only incorruptible mortals could serve as vassal-kings. The Jinni Liloupar chose the shepherd Ormazd, warned him that her blessing carried "sharp retribution", and watched him ignore it. He united the clans, was crowned, and made Gurabad the mortals' capital.

Ormazd then took slaves, tribute and sacrifice and treated her advice as pillow talk, so Liloupar took off the earrings he had given her and swore three generations of ruin on his line. Gurabad fell to a "great plague" of a mob under a brass-masked leader, and her soul was split. The survivors formed seven desert states, with the "city of sapphires", Tulaytullah, among the greatest. Two other pieces step outside Gurabad: Jinn fragments trapped in machines cry out against a "mother who never bore" them, and the Jinni Ferigees seals herself into a crystalline cup to restrain the desert's wrath and protect mortal cities.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a 4- and 5-star set from the City of Gold domain and the Desert Pavilion Chronicle strongbox. 2-piece: Anemo DMG Bonus +15%. 4-piece: when Charged Attacks hit, Normal Attack SPD rises 10% and Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack DMG rise 40% for 15s. Released in 3.3; the wiki lists no later change.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the set as a moral tale told by an elder. A character may quote its warnings but should not claim to know who the unnamed figures were. The Gurabad stories are specialist knowledge, not common in modern Sumeru.

key: The First Days of the City of Kings
119.comment: Desert Pavilion Chronicle: The First Days of the City of Kings
119.content: The flower piece of Desert Pavilion Chronicle: an artificial bloom that shimmers and seems to laugh when held to the ear. Its poem tells of the Lord of the Sands' pact with mortals through the Jinn, of Ormazd and the lily-born Liloupar, and of Gurabad blooming "like a man-made flower in a cliff wall". It ends with Xiphos setting out for the city of sapphires.

120.comment: Desert Pavilion Chronicle: End of the Golden Realm
120.content: The plume piece: a clear artificial feather from an ancient human realm, with eagle cries sealed inside. Its poem records Gurabad's fall to a "great plague" and a brass-masked leader, Liloupar's split soul, the seven desert states with Tulaytullah among the greatest, then unnamed tales of a general, a falcon-killed king, a dancer and a lost prince.

121.comment: Desert Pavilion Chronicle: Timepiece of the Lost Path
121.content: The sands piece: an old mechanical clock with Jinni fragments glowing and trembling at its core. Its voices curse a "mother who never bore us" and swear to return to their birth mother, Shirin. The text does not explain who the speakers are.

122.comment: Desert Pavilion Chronicle: Defender of the Enchanting Dream
122.content: The goblet piece: an ancient gold cup that murmurs from its empty inside. Its poem covers the Lord of Flowers' death, her Jinn passing to King Deshret, the Eternal Oasis, and Ferigees binding herself in frost-like chains as a crystalline cup to hold back the desert's wrath and guard the mortal cities.

123.comment: Desert Pavilion Chronicle: Legacy of the Desert High-Born
123.content: The circlet piece: amber-gold earrings. Its poem shows Ormazd turning a young state into a slave-fed tyranny and his Jinni consort laying aside the earrings he gave her as the sign of her intent to curse his line with three generations of ruin. The wiki notes the earrings are implied to be the ones Ormazd gave Liloupar.

124.content:
Dialogues of the Desert Sages: Dialogues of the Desert Sages is a 4-star polearm: a caduceus symbolising the glory of alchemy, made from special alloys. Its story names the seven sages of King Deshret and tells how the Crocodile King and the Ibis King wagered on a transmutation, with the sage Hermanubis ruling that the two powers must balance.

It was a reward of the Version 4.5 event Alchemical Ascension. The description jokes that it is so rigid and heavy that it would hurt as a cudgel.

Appearance: A caduceus of special alloys, exceedingly rigid and heavy. The description says it symbolises the glory of alchemy.

Lore: King Deshret's seven sages vanished long ago; their deeds are blown away and only their names, carved in stone, remain, now eroded to golden grains of sand. The text lists four: the Goat King (Heryshaf), right hand of the King and head of the sages; the sun-bound bird that was the King's soul, Bennu; the human-headed lioness that was the King's will, Shesepankh; and the dragon Al-Apep, who obtained the King's flesh and blood and never counted himself among the Seven. These four have nothing to do with the story that follows.

The Crocodile King and the Ibis King (Sobek and Thoth) were arguing, as ever, about the changing of things. The Crocodile King produced a man blessed by an Oceanid, through whose hands any liquid became perfect wine. The Ibis King produced a man cursed after touching the tomb of an ancient god, whose touch slowly turned things to pure silver. The text adds that turning things to gold and Mora is the province of Deus Auri alone. They bet on which effect would win and asked Hermanubis, the last of the seven sages, to predict.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star polearm, level 1 base ATK 42, secondary stat HP 9%. Passive Principle of Equilibrium: when the wielder heals, restore Energy, once every 10 s, even when off-field. Refinement uses the material Exalted Earth from Alchemical Ascension instead of duplicate weapons.

125.content:
Diary of Roald the Adventurer (also: Roald's Diary, Roald's diaries, Adventurer Roald's diary): Diary of Roald the Adventurer is an 11-volume book collection of travel diaries by Roald, a seasoned adventurer. He walks through Liyue (Sal Terrae, Qingce Village, Jueyun Karst, Yaoguang Shoal, Guyun Stone Forest), climbs Dragonspine, waits out the Sakoku Decree in Ritou and ends on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. Each entry pairs a travel log with local legends and a note to himself not to lose the diary again, which he keeps doing.

The diaries are a good in-world source for folk legends and how an outsider reads them. Roald is curious, a little accident-prone and wry, wanting above all to find an adeptus and to find out what ancient peoples left behind. The legends are what locals told him, not verified history.

Appearance: A worn travelling notebook with a leather case, left behind at camps. The in-game descriptions mention small salt crystals (Vol. 1), the smell of Mt. Qingce herbs, a fox-paw watermark, sea breeze, moss, ice crystals, sakura and tobacco, and fog and fungus on the pages, matching each place he wrote in.

Lore: Roald records places and the legends told about them, from the God of Salt's fall at Sal Terrae (Vol. 1) and the sea monster Chi at Qingce to Dragonspine, Ritou and Tsurumi Island.

Owners: No individual owns the diaries; they are left at campsites and other spots in the world for the Traveler to find. Their author is Roald, whose fate is not stated in the text beyond Vol. 11.

Gameplay: Game note: a book collection with no stats. Volumes sit at camps in Liyue and Dragonspine and in Ritou; Vol. 11 is on Tsurumi Island and needs the quest The Saga of Mr. Forgetful to be complete.

126.comment: Diary of Roald the Adventurer: Roald
126.content: Roald is the adventurer who wrote the Diary of Roald the Adventurer. He is a seasoned traveller who tracks legends, searches for an adeptus and keeps losing his diaries. In Vol. 11 he thanks a blonde traveler and Paimon for helping him gather Fluorescent Fungus and bring back pictures of ancient murals on Tsurumi Island.

127.comment: Diary of Roald the Adventurer: Salt God's Fall in Roald's Diary
127.content: In Roald's Vol. 1 account, the God of Salt sheltered civilians during the Archon War and built a settlement at Sal Terrae. Her city fell when its first and last king killed her, hoping to turn it into a military power. The king's fate is uncertain in the text. This is folklore Roald collected, and other sources should be used for the canonical history.

128.comment: Diary of Roald the Adventurer: Chi and Qingce Village in Roald's Diary
128.content: Roald reports the elders' story that Morax slew the sea serpent Chi, whose body became Mt. Qingce and the terraced fields. He doubts it, since the rock looks impact-shattered and shows no sign of a Hydro monster. The diary also remarks that Chi was once pronounced Qingce.

129.comment: Diary of Roald the Adventurer: Roald on Tsurumi Island
129.content: In Vol. 11 Roald reaches Tsurumi Island through the fog with the help of a youth named Kama, then meets a small child he suspects may be a hallucination. When he returns without telling Kama he cannot get through the fog; a blonde traveler and Paimon help him collect Fluorescent Fungus. He gives them credit for the discovery of the ancient murals.

130.comment: Diary of Roald the Adventurer: Roald's Diary Volume Summaries
130.content:
- Vol. 1, Sal Terrae: from the ruin's scale Roald suspects it is the refuge temple built by the God of Salt. Folklore calls her the gentlest of the gods. Her followers settled the area, and the city stood several centuries until the king, wanting military strength and thinking gentleness unfit for the times, killed her. Theories on the king's end differ: he ruled alone from the ruins until he turned to dust, or he took his own life from guilt. Survivors scattered across Liyue and, in Liyue Harbor under the Geo Archon, their stories survived. Rumour says her body, turned to salt, remains in the ruins in the pose of her death.
- Vol. 2, Qingce Village: elders say Morax defeated the sea serpent Chi; its body became stone, blood water, scales the terraced fields and its nest Mt. Qingce. Roald thinks the rocks look shattered by impacts and sees no sign of a Hydro monster, so wonders if it is just a tale. He also notes that young people moved to Liyue Harbor for work, which brings prosperity but will eventually empty the village.
- Vol. 3, Aocang Lake: he loses another diary and swims in the mountain lake. A farmer's tale says adepti can turn to mist and roam the sea of clouds. He meets Eduardo, a treasure-hunting Adventurers' Guild member who insists she has no tie to the Treasure Hoarders.
- Vol. 4, Luhua Pool: a herb gatherer says the pond was once a garden where two lovers met; the man went to fight for the Geo Archon and never returned, and the girl's tears gathered into the pond. Roald falls asleep bathing, and a baby fox steals a shoe and his food.
- Vol. 5, Yaoguang Shoal: fisherman's legend says Greenconch Lodge belonged to an adeptus who was the conch itself and sheltered the lost; older fishermen say it housed a family living in a giant shell. The lodge seems empty.
- Vol. 6, Guyun Stone Forest: legend says the Geo Archon carved a huge stone polearm and drove it through a sea monster; wind has worn it into the pillars. Roald dreams he is the impaled monster and decides not to camp there. He sees the Crux setting sail and wonders what Captain Beidou has been assigned.
- Vol. 7, Qingyun Peak: a cold, sleepless night above the clouds before his climb to the adeptus's dwelling.
- Vol. 8, Qingxu Pool: a Sumeru scholar named Soraya told him the Lisha ruins belong to an evil god whose name was erased and its people, flooded during the Archon War and exposed when the tide fell. He meets Eduardo again. Monsters now occupy the ruins since the Chasm mining stopped.
- Vol. 9, Dragonspine: he sets up camp on the southern slope, notes ruins whose style matches other ancient sites, finds old clothing and broken weapons from the aristocratic era that suggest a chase or murder, and discovers unfrozen water in a ruin. He nearly breaks a leg, gets frostbitten toes and decides the trip was a disaster. He hears a gentle yet disturbing song in a dream. Mondstadt tales call the mountain a place abandoned by the Wind of Time.
- Vol. 10, Ritou: delayed by the Kanjou Commission, he is helped by Mr. Kurisu, a reserved commerce chairman from Fontaine. He describes how the Sakoku Decree emptied the port, recalls that Hiroshi of the Hiiragi Clan founded it, notes rumours of a Shogunate attack on a Sangonomiya outpost, and hopes the Crux Fleet can smuggle him out.
- Vol. 11, Tsurumi Island: a youth named Kama helps him reach the fog-shrouded island. He glimpses ancient ruins and dream-like scenes and meets a small child he cannot explain. He is later guided out by a blonde traveler and Paimon, who help him gather Fluorescent Fungus, said to have formed from the memories of the island's dead. He finds it calming and plans to send some to a friend in Sumeru.

131.content:
Disaster and Remorse (also: Dolorous Stroke): Disaster and Remorse is a 5-star Hexerei-series polearm, described as forged from Whitestone and Starsilver, its point always wrapped in a bone-piercing chill. Its text tells how the outlander warrior Imunlaukr hurled this astral-silver lance to protect a maiden of Sal Vindagnyr, and the blow that legend names dolorous destroyed three kingdoms and killed her. Released in Version 6.6.

The Hexerei Series page reads the lance as Imunlaukr's weapon. The item is a record of the Mondstadt-region legend of his throw and its aftermath, and of how it ended his life as a warrior.

Appearance: Canon says it is forged from Whitestone and Starsilver, with a keen point constantly enveloped in a bone-piercing chill; the text calls it an astral silver lance. Do not describe its hilt or length.

Lore: In the moonless city of snow, an outlander warrior mourned a shattered realm and left his old greatsword to the frost.

He wandered the frozen plains believing he could forget his weakness in endless battle, but abandoned that pretense at the first moonfall after leaving the Mural Room. When he saw the maiden of Sal Vindagnyr attacked, instinct made him hurl the lance into a black tide of beasts, to save her.

Owners: Imunlaukr is the warrior of the text; the wiki's Hexerei Series page states that the polearm once belonged to him.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star polearm, base ATK 48, CRIT Rate secondary stat. After an Elemental Skill, the wielder gains Path of Conflict; its Unforgivable effect raises Normal and Charged Attack DMG, Irreparable raises Skill and Burst DMG, and hits of the matching kind extend each other. Hexerei: Secret Rite raises the boosts by 75%. It was on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2026-06-09 to 2026-06-30).

key: Sharpness That Ceased Upon Wondrous Creation
Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams
Pendulum That Ceased Amidst a Great Fall
132.content:
Disenchantment in Deep Shadow (also: Iridescence That Ceased Amidst Glory, Sharpness That Ceased Upon Wondrous Creation, Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams, Ovations That Ceased Upon Festivity, Pendulum That Ceased Amidst a Great Fall): Disenchantment in Deep Shadow is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Superconduct and Stellar-Conduct teams, released in version 6.6. Its five pieces are all about Aksinya, the silver-haired human scholar of the old Snezhnayan court: her friendship with a frost-wielding fae princess, her work among the ruins of the Shadow Realm, a long-haired alchemist who joined her research, and the Tsar who found her as an infant.

Every title begins "...That Ceased...", pointing at the dream of the Belyi Tsar's project that stopped when he fell. The items are keepsakes of Aksinya's life, given to her by friends, colleagues and her master.

Appearance: Keepsakes: a silk flower, a feathered quill, a fleeting moment given as a reminder, a wine goblet, and a delicate piercing trinket.

Lore: All five stories centre on Aksinya, who is not named in some pieces but is addressed by name in the Flower and the Goblet. The Flower is her friendship with the Snegurochka princess in a fae manor; the Quill her teaching of a young Domovoy; the Sands her first meeting with a long-haired alchemist; the Goblet a toast from the old Domovoy lord Alvis; the Pendulum the Tsar's trinket, given in celebration of her birth.

Owners: Aksinya is the recipient of each keepsake. No other owner is named.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain (Windrest Peak, Mondstadt). 4-piece: Superconduct reaction DMG +80% and Stellar-Conduct reaction DMG +40%; when the wearer attacks opponents affected by Superconduct or Stellar-Conduct, that attack's CRIT Rate +16%.

key: Sharpness That Ceased Upon Wondrous Creation
Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams
Pendulum That Ceased Amidst a Great Fall
133.comment: Disenchantment in Deep Shadow: Disenchantment in Deep Shadow
133.content: Artifact set whose item text recounts episodes from the life of Aksinya in the old Snezhnayan court, through gifts from friends, colleagues and her master.

134.comment: Disenchantment in Deep Shadow: The Snegurochka's silk flower
134.content: In the Iridescence That Ceased Amidst Glory text the Snegurochka princess hosts Aksinya in the thousand-year-old mountain manor of the foremost Snegovik. She shows her ice that never melts, warns that magic is fleeting, and gives her a silk flower as a token of friendship. The wiki links the friend to Pavlina.

135.content:
Divine Bridle: The Divine Bridle is a bridle-shaped quest item from Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku). It was the badge of the Sunchild's office, the sign that a child was the nation's puppet ruler. It has no power of its own. The spirit Aberaku hid it and gave it to the Traveler; the Traveler then used it to help the official Clymene release the souls of the seven Sunchildren.

Its journey spans two linked world quests of Enkanomiya: Hyperion's Dirge, where Aberaku hands it over, and The Phaethons' Syrtos, where it becomes the medium that lets Clymene reach the dead children's souls. It is a quiet, sorrowful object, not a weapon or relic of power.

Appearance: Shaped like a bridle; the in-game text gives no further description of materials or markings.

Lore: Byakuyakoku was ruled by a Sunchild, an infant chosen to be the nation's figurehead and said to be a child of the sun. Per the quest accounts, the real power lay with people behind the scenes. The bridle marked the office. Aberaku, who built the Dainichi Mikoshi, calls it proof that a child is a child of the sun, and says he hid it intending to alert the people. Clymene, the official who raised the Sunchildren, believed it lost.

Owners: Made as the Sunchild's badge, so carried by each Sunchild in turn, per Clymene. Aberaku hid it before the events of Hyperion's Dirge and gave it to the Traveler. The Traveler offered it to Clymene, who had it placed in the waters of the Soul Guide's Locus. Its fate after that is not stated.

Gameplay: Quest item received as a reward for Hyperion's Dirge (2.4) and needed for The Phaethons' Syrtos; the hidden exploration objective Sunchildren Hide and Seek opens after that quest. It has no use outside these quests.

136.comment: Divine Bridle: The Rite of Solar Return
136.content: Per Clymene, a Sunchild of a certain age was taken in a ceremony into the Dainichi Mikoshi on their birth date, to return to the "seat of the sun" before the mortal world could taint them. Only shreds of their souls came back to the Soul Guide's Locus. Aberaku ties it to a verse about riding Pegasus to the feast of the sun. The wiki's summary adds that the nobles used it so that no Sunchild would live long enough to see through their manipulation; the quests themselves are less explicit.

137.content:
Dodoco Tales: Dodoco Tales is a 4-star catalyst, a small children's book of cheerful adventure stories about the Dodoco, furry creatures from the Golden Apple Archipelago. Its text is told in a child's voice and says the book was given by the freest mother in the world to the luckiest daughter in the world. It was an event reward from Midsummer Island Adventure (Version 1.6), a limited-time event.

The wiki notes that Klee is shown holding this catalyst in her Genius Invokation TCG card. The book itself is not tied to a named owner.

Appearance: A small, precious picture book. Its description says it is filled with childish short stories that make readers laugh and that even long-grown adults get absorbed in the innocent, naive little adventures.

Lore: The tale says there is a group of islands in a foggy sea called the Golden Apple Archipelago, where the cute, peace-loving Dodo Clan live without troubles. They call each other "Dodoco", which means "the best of friends".

Like dandelion seeds, every Dodoco must one day ride the wind and waves into the wider world to find a red, blazing four-leaf clover. Having lived together so long, the Dodocos have all become alike and cannot tell each other apart, with no "you" or "me". Only the clover, the story says, lets a Dodoco learn what "Dodoco" truly means and tell friends apart. The narrator adds that this is "what my mom says".

Owners: No owner is named in the text. The book is described as given by a mother to a daughter.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst obtained from the Midsummer Island Adventure event (Version 1.6, 2021-06-17 per the wiki infobox), base ATK 41, secondary stat ATK 12%. Passive Dodoventure!: Normal Attack hits raise Charged Attack DMG for 6 s, and Charged Attack hits raise ATK for 6 s. It is refined with the event material Fragments of Innocence rather than duplicate weapons.

138.content:
Dragon's Bane: Dragon's Bane is a 4-star polearm of the Kunwu series, described as a polearm with an entwining golden dragon, light and sharp, that may well kill dragons with ease. It is rumoured to be a legendary polearm of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

The item text says the master craftsman Kunwu forged it with a dragon's spine as the haft and a dragon's claw as the tip.

Appearance: A dragon motif runs from handle to tip. It once had a dragon-shaped wooden sheath, but according to the text it no longer needs to contain its might. Do not invent colours beyond the golden dragon the in-game description mentions.

Lore: It is called a legendary Liyue polearm that pierces anything in its way.

Because of its materials, the body is said to be unbreakable and the tip sharp beyond compare, gleaming with a dragon's malice.

Owners: Only the unnamed dragon slayer of the item text is tied to it in story. Yun Jin, Yaoyao and Xiangling are shown with it in promotional art, demos and trailers, which is a cameo and not an ownership claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star polearm, base ATK 41, Elemental Mastery secondary stat (48). Passive Bane of Flame and Water: increases DMG against opponents affected by Hydro or Pyro by 20 to 36 per cent by refinement. A Kunwu series weapon, shared with the 4-Star Bane series (see Lion's Roar).

139.content: Kunwu is the legendary master craftsman named in the item texts of Dragon's Bane, Lion's Roar and Solar Pearl. He is not described as a character who appears in the game; only these items' stories mention him.

140.content:
Dragonspine Spear: Dragonspine Spear is a 4-star polearm of the Dragonspine series, in-game description "a spear created from the fang of a dragon" that is oddly warm to the touch. It is made from teeth of the shadow dragon Durin and is the reward of the world quest The Festering Fang. Added in Version 1.2.

Its archive entry is Durin's own dying dream. The weapon shares its source dragon with Festering Desire.

Appearance: Canon says only that it is a spear made from a dragon's fang, oddly warm to the touch. Do not invent a colour or length.

Lore: The text narrates a very long dream. He dreamed that he and everyone had journeyed to a land of green grass and soulful songs, where he sang with the gentle people and danced in the skies with a dragon as beautiful as a jewel.

He woke in the sky above a mountain swept by roaring snowstorms. The green land was already painted crimson with fire and blood, the song of a sky-blue bard's lyre almost drowned out, and the jewel-like dragon had pierced his neck with sharp fangs.

Owners: No owner is named. In The Festering Fang the Traveler collects the materials and the craftsman Orban forges the spear; the weapon passes to the Traveler as the quest reward.

Quests: In The Festering Fang (a Version 1.2 Dragonspine world quest), the Traveler picks up a Strange Tooth, asks around the adventurers' camp and learns from Orban that it may be dragon tooth. He asks for three more teeth, 50 Starsilver and a Northlander polearm prototype, then finds that ordinary tools cannot cut the tooth. A tooth must absorb dragon "vitality" first: either from the heart in Wyrmrest Valley (where Fatui skirmishers interrupt) or, if the Traveler has already progressed through The Gardener, via a Runestone that Albedo sent through Sucrose. Orban then forges the spear.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 4-star polearm with base ATK 41 and a Physical DMG Bonus secondary stat. The Dragonspine series passive Frost Burial gives Normal and Charged Attack hits a chance (60 to 100 per cent by refinement, once per 10s) to drop an Everfrost Icicle that deals area ATK damage, much more against Cryo-affected enemies. It is a forgeable polearm obtained as a World Quest reward, with a diagram also given by the quest.

141.content: The Festering Fang is a Version 1.2 world quest in Dragonspine. Orban, an artisan, works with the Traveler to turn a strange dragon tooth into the Dragonspine Spear, after the tooth is first infused with dragon vitality. Festering Desire, a sword, is a related weapon from the same dragon.

142.content:
Dream-Mirror Remnant (also: Skirk's Abyss Crystal): The Dream-Mirror Remnant is an Abyss Crystal that Skirk gave the Traveler, received at the end of the quest Unbounded in Version 5.7. When worn, it can be used during sleep to "dream-mirror" with her; using it again lets the holder revisit certain scenes from what happened during that case.

It is a quest item (listed as 4-star), not equipment. It belongs to the closing stretch of Skirk's Crystallina Chapter, Act I (Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night), after the Traveler and Skirk beat the Khaenri'ahn man Skofnungr in the Abyssal space near the Chasm.

Appearance: Described only as an Abyss Crystal that is worn. No shape, colour or setting is given in canon text read. The item page shows five illustrated scenes, each with a short, poetic caption.

Lore: Skirk, Surtalogi's disciple, is an outsider who visits Teyvat to grow stronger. In Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night she offers to dream-mirror with the Traveler and Paimon so she can experience the Traveler's stolen-soul dream herself. Later, while the Traveler sleeps, they wander through Skirk's inner world and see her memories.

In the quests, those memories include fragments of her childhood on her home planet, training under Surtalogi, and arriving in Teyvat. In Heart and Mind the Traveler reaches Skirk's inner world, a shattered river that stands for her emotions, and helps her accept the emotions she had suppressed. In Unbounded Skirk is restored to full strength and the Traveler and she defeat the culprit, Skofnungr, who stole part of her power.

Owners: The Traveler holds it; Skirk is the giver.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (labelled as mechanics): quest reward in Unbounded alongside Primogems, Mora and other materials. It is a non-equippable quest item.

143.content: The Dream-Mirror Remnant is the Abyss Crystal Skirk gave the Traveler after the events of Unbounded. Worn in sleep, it opens a "dream-mirror" with her and can replay certain scenes from the case in which she and the Traveler tracked down Skofnungr.

144.content:
Dull Golden Bridle (also: Dull Golden Bridle of Byakuyakoku): The Dull Golden Bridle is a quest item found in Enkanomiya's library ruin during the world quest The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. Its description calls it the hereditary national treasure of Byakuyakoku, drained of all power.

The power was removed deliberately, so that thieves who entered by irregular means would not see its value. It is the disguised form of the Golden Bridle that the quest needs.

Appearance: No in-world description of its look is given. Enjou, the guide, says the Golden Bridle is a device smaller than an armful and not a rope; the name comes from a Byakuyakoku legend in which the sun and moon were moved by the chariots of the gods.

Lore: The item text says it is Byakuyakoku's hereditary national treasure and has lost all its own power, a measure meant to stop intruders from recognising its worth. The full Golden Bridle, per its own item text, represents the highest authority in Byakuyakoku and lets its wielder control Evernight and Whitenight.

In the quest Enjou, a self-described researcher, explains that the people of Byakuyakoku, saved by the Great Serpent, left the depths for the surface, and that the library was one of the facilities the people of Watatsumi archived afterwards. To ease later trials the Bridle was moved to the back of the library. Finding it is the first part of the trial and is needed to bring down the barrier around the Dainichi Mikoshi.

Gameplay: Game mechanics only: a quest item with no combat use. The quest skips a step if the Dull Golden Bridle was picked up before the Traveler met Enjou.

145.comment: Dull Golden Bridle: Dull Golden Bridle
145.content: Byakuyakoku's hereditary treasure, found in a drained, unremarkable form in the library of Byakuyakoku so thieves would not value it. It is used in The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent to open the way to the Dainichi Mikoshi, and is tied to control of Evernight and Whitenight.

146.content:
Echoes of an Offering (also: Soulscent Bloom, Jade Leaf, Symbol of Felicitation, Chalice of the Font, Flowing Rings): Echoes of an Offering is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that rewards Normal Attacks. Its five pieces (Soulscent Bloom, Jade Leaf, Symbol of Felicitation, Chalice of the Font, Flowing Rings) carry item text made of Chenyu Vale legends: tea served when the spiritscent flowers bloom at Qiaoying Village, the first tea tree, a jade split into hidden pieces, and the friendship of the vale's adepti.

Added in version 2.6. The pieces are told as tales and rumours, and mostly name no one; the wiki ties the unnamed figures to the Herblord and the carp adeptus Fujin (see uncertainties).

Appearance: Jade ornaments with a water-and-tea theme: a jade carved as a flower, a leaf-shaped jade pendant, a circular jade loop that sounds like running water, a small teacup that holds a spring and the reflected sun and moon, and a pair of jade earrings.

Lore: The pieces recount Qiaoying Village's tea ceremony, the first tea tree planted in Chenyu Vale, a rain-bringing jade split into hidden pieces, and a pair of adepti friends, one bound to water and one to the mountain.

Owners: No owner is named. The pieces speak of a young lady master of a mountain, a priest, and a friend who carries a teacup; the wiki ties these to the Herblord and Fujin.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): obtained from The Lost Valley domain and the Artifact Strongbox. 2-piece: ATK +18%. 4-piece: Normal Attack hits have a 36% chance to trigger Valley Rite, increasing Normal Attack DMG by 70% of ATK until the next Normal Attack deals damage; each failure raises the next chance by 20%; triggers at most once per 0.2s.

147.comment: Echoes of an Offering: Echoes of an Offering
147.content: Artifact set whose item text collects Chenyu Vale legends: Qiaoying Village's tea ceremony, the vale's first tea tree, a sacred jade split and hidden, and the friendship of the adepti.

148.comment: Echoes of an Offering: The first tea tree of Chenyu Vale
148.content: In Jade Leaf, the first tea tree was planted on the Herblord's hillside by someone who promised to brew tea for friends, including Cloud Retainer and Mountain Shaper, once it grew. A jade pendant was tied to its branches. Mortals later grafted its branches across the river, and tea spread from Chenyu Vale to Liyue Harbor. The text says the trees thrive only in Chenyu Vale because they remember an old promise.

149.comment: Echoes of an Offering: The hidden jade of Mt. Laixin
149.content: Symbol of Felicitation and Flowing Rings preserve rumours that Mt. Laixin held a jade able to bring sweet rain; the mountain's master split it into pieces and hid them underwater, in hills and in shrines so that demons could not use its power. Variants say it was carved by Rex Lapis, or was merely a lesser jade or a cup, or that the 'jade' is a figure of speech for a beautiful person. Treat all as legend.

150.content:
Electro Gnosis (also: Inazuma's Gnosis, Ei's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Electro Archon, Electro Archon's Gnosis): The Electro Gnosis is the Gnosis of Inazuma's Electro Archon: a small object shaped like a chess piece that connects an Archon to Celestia. Ei, the Raiden Shogun, gave it up and entrusted it to Yae Miko. Yae traded it to the Fatui Harbinger the Balladeer (Scaramouche) to save the Traveler. In Sumeru, Nahida took it from him, then gave it to the Harbinger Dottore. As of 7.1 it is one of the six Gnoses held by the Tsaritsa.
