Ei had no further use for it once she withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia and left Inazuma to her puppet, the Shogun. She told Yae she had cut her ties with Celestia. Paimon learned only after Signora's death that the Fatui had in fact got Inazuma's Gnosis.

Lore: A Gnosis grants and strengthens elemental power and links its holder to Celestia; Nahida calls the Gnoses symbols of the Heavenly Principles' control over Teyvat and its "laws." Archons keep their thrones and their power without one: Ei is still the Electro Archon after giving hers away.

Ei had first tried to turn the Gnosis into an energy supply device, but none of her techniques had any effect on it. She then gave it to Yae Miko, her old friend, knowing Yae might "sell" it but would only do so for something of equal value. Yae kept it at the Grand Narukami Shrine. When the Traveler fell into the Balladeer's trap at the Fatui's Delusion factory and collapsed, Yae gave him the Gnosis in exchange for the Traveler's safety, judging it useless to Ei and a likely source of conflict.

Owners: Ei (Raiden Shogun) -> Yae Miko -> the Balladeer (Scaramouche, later the Wanderer) -> Nahida -> Dottore -> the Tsaritsa (Anastasya).

Status as of 7.1: Dottore later recalled, in memories recovered from Irminsul's burnt trunk (6.6), presenting the two Gnoses to the Tsaritsa as battle trophies. As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, Electro among them; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: the Electro Gnosis is a story object. It cannot be obtained, equipped or used by the player.

151.comment: Electro Gnosis: Ei entrusts the Gnosis to Yae Miko
151.content: Ei set the Gnosis aside before withdrawing into the Plane of Euthymia, after failing to turn it into an energy supply. She gave it to Yae Miko on the understanding that Yae might trade it, but never at a loss. Yae kept it at the Grand Narukami Shrine. Then the Traveler fell into the Balladeer's trap at the Fatui's Delusion factory, and Yae gave him the Gnosis in exchange for the Traveler's safety. She told the Traveler and Paimon only afterwards, in the Archon Quest "Wishes" (2.1).

152.comment: Electro Gnosis: Shouki no Kami and the Gnosis
152.content: Shouki no Kami was the false god the Balladeer became in Sumeru, built around his puppet body and a giant machine powered by the Electro Gnosis. Nahida defeated him with the Traveler's help and extracted the Gnosis. Losing it left the Balladeer in despair, since it had come to hold his obsessions.

153.content:
Elegy for the End (also: The Parting Refrain, Millennial Movement: Farewell Song): Elegy for the End is a five-star bow released in version 1.4, one of the Millennial Movement weapons, each of which carries a song of Mondstadt's history. Its story tells of the Cataclysm, when a venomous dragon crushed the land, and of a dour knight who could be made to forget his duty only by a girl's song. He fell in the battle; she came home to find the song changed.

Appearance: The item text describes no particular look for the bow beyond comparing it to a bard's lyre: "a bow as lovely as any bard's lyre", whose arrows pierce the heart like a lamenting sigh. Its in-game passive effect is shown as a lyre string lighting up.

Lore: The story opens with a verse about the wind carrying wine's fragrance, news from the mountains and longing. Long ago there was a knight (Rostam) who was always grave, and only one song and one girl who sang it in the square could make him forget his burden. Then the Cataclysm came, and a venomous dragon, Durin, drowned the songs and ripped apart the cries and flames. The Anemo Archon, though he had refused to rule, heard the agony; to protect his old friends' dream he woke and flew into battle beside the sky dragon, Dvalin. The knight and his knights fought as well.

Owners: No canon owner is named. The story concerns Rostam and the girl but does not say the bow was theirs. The bow is a song-weapon in the series sense, not an inherited relic.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star bow from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat Energy Recharge 12%. Passive "The Parting Refrain": raises Elemental Mastery; Elemental Skill or Burst hits give a Sigil of Remembrance, and at four Sigils all are consumed and nearby party members get "Millennial Movement: Farewell Song" for 12 seconds (more Elemental Mastery and ATK), then a 20-second lockout. Buffs of the same Millennial Movement type do not stack.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): suited to scenes about parting, songs that outlive their singers and the cost of the Cataclysm. Do not state the girl is Signora to a character who has no way to know it.

154.content: The knight in the Elegy for the End story is Rostam according to the wiki's link. The text calls him a knight who was ever dour and fought with his knights against the venomous dragon, dying in the valley. No further detail is printed in the item.

key: Emblem of Severed Fate artifact set
155.content:
Emblem of Severed Fate (also: Emblem of Severed Fate artifact set, Magnificent Tsuba, Sundered Feather, Storm Cage, Scarlet Vessel, Ornate Kabuto): Emblem of Severed Fate is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set. Its five item texts tell, in fragments, of the half-oni swordsman Iwakura Michihiro, also called Douin, and of the black-winged tengu Teruyo of Yougou who gave him his new name and fought him in thirteen yearly duels. Mechanically it rewards Energy Recharge with Elemental Burst damage.

The set is dropped by the Momiji-Dyed Court domain on Yashiori Island. The texts read as memory and farewell: a mother lost to a failed bid for glory under the Shogun's banner, a son starting over under a new name, a tengu who cannot keep a promise, and a friend's broken seal cage. Several of the narrated people also appear in the Amethyst Series weapons Amenoma Kageuchi, Katsuragikiri Nagamasa and Hakushin Ring.

Lore: The texts follow Michihiro, the son of an oni mother who lost her standing with the Shogun. After his family's fall he lived in seclusion; a black-winged tengu, Teruyo of Yougou, renamed him "Iwakura" (a seat of rock) to free him from the burden of oni blood and challenged him to yearly duels.

The pieces dwell on a fallen oni house, a renaming and a long rivalry: the mother of the Mikoshi line turned on the Shogun and was ruined; her son withdrew from the clan; the tengu renamed him Iwakura, and after thirteen years of duels he finally touched her, breaking his sword and her shrine. He then became the Kujou Clan's sword instructor, "Douin".

Gameplay: Gameplay, not lore: the 2-piece bonus is Energy Recharge +20%. The 4-piece bonus increases Elemental Burst damage by 25% of the wearer's Energy Recharge, up to 75%. The set drops from the Momiji-Dyed Court domain on Yashiori Island, and a strongbox variant exists. It first appeared in Version 2.0.

156.comment: Emblem of Severed Fate: Iwakura Michihiro (Douin) in the artifact texts
156.content: In the Emblem of Severed Fate texts, Michihiro was born into the Mikoshi line of war-oni, withdrew to a village after his mother's disgrace, and was renamed "Iwakura" by the tengu Teruyo to free him from his oni heritage. After thirteen years of duels he perfected the Tengu Sweeper, became the Kujou Clan's sword instructor with the title Douin, and founded a successful school. The weapon Amenoma Kageuchi, a copy of the sword Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma, descends from his school; the weapon text says he gave a copy to the Saimon Clan for sheltering him in Konda Village.

157.comment: Emblem of Severed Fate: Teruyo of Yougou
157.content: A black-winged tengu who, in the set's texts, gave Michihiro the name Iwakura, fought him in yearly duels at a small branch shrine, and was finally touched by him after thirteen years. She told him tengu names carry blessings and that she had duties to her clan; she said goodbye and asked him to forget her. A line in the Storm Cage mentions "Teruyo of the shrine" inheriting her master's beauty and skill, but the set says no more of her.

158.content:
Engulfing Lightning (also: Kusanagi no Inabikari, Ei's naginata, the Shogun's naginata): Engulfing Lightning is the polearm (a naginata) of Ei, the Electro Archon who rules Inazuma through her puppet, the Raiden Shogun. Its item text calls it a lethal weapon for cutting away "scattered dross" and speaks of Ei's vow to prune mortal obsession and unchecked desire in order to keep an unchanging, eternal world. Its Japanese name means roughly "grass-cutting lightning".

It is a 5-star polearm of the Inazuma weapon series. The Raiden Shogun uses a polearm in ordinary combat and switches to the sword Musou Isshin for her Elemental Burst.

Appearance: A long-hafted naginata, a polearm with a curved blade, charged with Electro. Its in-game model gains a more ornate form at the second ascension phase. Canon text gives no materials or measurements beyond calling it a naginata; the writers have said only that the weapon Ei used to slay Orobashi weighed thousands of tons (see uncertainties).

Lore: The weapon's story is told as Ei's reflection. From high above the storm clouds she looked on the mortal world she loved and saw petty disputes and fleeting obsessions that, to her, were enemies of eternity. Like weeds among crops, they had to be swept away by lightning, so that nothing needed to wither or be lost.

The text recalls a remembered scene under the sakura tree: Yae Miko, drinking wine with Ei, asked what kind of eternity Makoto's eyes would reflect. Ei dismisses it as a pointless question, though the answer she gave was lost to the alcohol. She had already settled the matter countless times in memory: just as fruit trees are thinned for quality, so not one speck of dross could be allowed in an eternal paradise.

Owners: Ei is the wielder the text names. The Raiden Shogun, her puppet, fights with the same style of polearm.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star polearm in the Inazuma series, released in Version 2.1 and obtainable from the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 46 with Energy Recharge as its secondary stat.

159.content:
Envoy's Medal (also: Envoy's Medal of the Tsaritsa, Tsaritsa's special envoy medal): The Envoy's Medal is a medal the Tsaritsa gave the Traveler at Zapolyarny Palace in Version 7.1. It is proof that the Traveler is her special envoy, officially titled "Consultant to the Tsaritsa", and it gives unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace.

The Traveler did not swear fealty to the court, so the Tsaritsa chose the looser title of Consultant rather than a formal court position. The medal is the token of that arrangement.

Lore: The in-game description calls it a medal specially bestowed by the Tsaritsa, bearing the weight of her authority, proof of the holder's status as her envoy, with unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace.

It was awarded in the quest A Letter From Zapolyarny Palace. Vesna sent the Traveler and Paimon a cheerful letter promising a "prize" after some formalities. At the palace they found the Tsaritsa (Anastasya), Vesna, Danica and her secretary Chayka. Vesna proposed the Traveler as the Tsaritsa's new adviser: someone of great skill who belongs to no faction, to carry out decrees that ministers handle poorly and the military would overshadow. Danica doubted anyone who comes and goes freely would carry out orders without hesitation.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a quest item received on completing A Letter From Zapolyarny Palace. It does not itself appear as a usable item in play, and the invitation letter that leads to it is read through quest navigation rather than the inventory.

Status as of 7.1: The Traveler holds the medal as of Version 7.1.

Nothing in the canon read suggests it has been revoked.

160.comment: Envoy's Medal: Consultant to the Tsaritsa
160.content: The title the Tsaritsa gave the Traveler in A Letter From Zapolyarny Palace instead of a court post, because the Traveler would not swear fealty. It comes with the Envoy's Medal as proof, and the authority to carry out the position's duties. Chayka, the Tsaritsa's secretary, is the contact for questions and arrangements.

161.content:
Etherlight Spindlelute (also: Last Singer): Etherlight Spindlelute is a 4-star catalyst: a lute whose golden strings shine like sunlight, which appears to be a relic from the Seelie of old.

It was a reward of the Clink Clank Clash event in Nod-Krai. Its story takes place in the hidden court of the Seelie by Lake Amsvartnir, where a woman's lament recalls a dream and the last Seelie play a final tune.

Appearance: A catalyst: a lute with golden strings as radiant as sunlight, apparently a Seelie relic. Add no further detail.

Lore: Beyond the ruins of an ancient palace, at the edge of the Nod-Krai wasteland, stands the quiet sacred forest of Lake Amsvartnir. Legend says that whoever breaks the golden branch in the forest will find the royal court of the Seelie, hidden from mortal eyes by day.

The court is a kingdom of the past, forgotten by time and space and untouched by heavenly light. Its owner has long departed, leaving a neglected courtyard and a bare hall, yet a young woman's silent lament still echoes through the palace.

Owners: No owner is named. The Seelie are its implied makers or keepers, and the court's owner is described as long departed.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10.0%; introduced in Version 6.0 as a reward from the Clink Clank Clash flagship event (2025-09-12 to 2025-09-29, requiring Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue archon quest), not from Wishes. Refinement uses Golden Strings rather than duplicate weapons, and four can be obtained in the event. Passive "Last Singer": for 20s after using an Elemental Skill, the wielder's Elemental Mastery increases by 100 (refinement 1) up to 200 (refinement 5).

162.comment: Etherlight Spindlelute: The Royal Court of the Seelie
162.content: According to the Etherlight Spindlelute's story, the Seelie court by Lake Amsvartnir can be found by breaking the golden branch in the sacred forest, and is hidden from mortal eyes by day. Its owner has long departed. A woman's lament still echoes there, and the first Seelie played their last tune in its hall.

163.content:
Everlasting Moonglow (also: Fumetsu no Gekka, Byakuya Kougetsu, Pearl and waves catalyst): Everlasting Moonglow is a pearl-strung catalyst from the Sangonomiya and Watatsumi tradition. Its item text is a poetic history of Watatsumi Island: the people who dreamed with their god, the first Divine Priestess, the lightning that struck down their dream, and the memory that survives in the "pearl and waves" emblem.

It is a 5-star catalyst and, unusually, is not part of the Inazuma weapon series. Its description calls it a string of lovely jasper from the deep sea, shining with a pure radiance like the moon and "ever-distant".

Appearance: A string or ring of pearls and jewelled beads, with a pale moonlit glow, set with the Sangonomiya emblem. The description speaks of a string of lovely jasper from the deep sea; canon text says nothing more of its design.

Lore: The text begins with the "pearl and waves" emblem of the Sangonomiya, said to mean the waves that embrace Watatsumi and its bright pearls, though some say it shows the jewelled wheel of Watatsumi Omikami keeping eternal watch over the coral land like the moon. It then recalls how the descendants of their god passed hope from generation to generation.

The first Divine Priestess led her people with wisdom as precious as pearls and chose clergy from those newly introduced to sunlight, who comforted those who feared the day. The text also recalls the Umigozen, who made the navies of Narukami tremble and sang whale-songs with them, and says the emblem was drawn as they danced with the airborne kurage.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon. The weapon is tied to the Sangonomiya clan only by the emblem its text is built around.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst released in Version 2.1 on the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 46 with HP% as secondary stat.

164.comment: Everlasting Moonglow: Pearl and Waves Emblem
164.content: The "pearl and waves" emblem of the Sangonomiya clan is said to stand for the sea around Watatsumi and its pearls, though some say it shows the jewelled wheel of Watatsumi Omikami watching over the coral land like the moon. Everlasting Moonglow's text treats it as a symbol of memory that Watatsumi's people carry through loss.

165.content:
Exaiphanes Blade: The Exaiphanes Blade is a 5-star sword given to the Traveler during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (Chapter VII, Act I), described as a longsword that once shone with the light of the stars and in the voyager's hand becomes a new light unconnected to any past era. It reacts to Statues of The Seven in Snezhnaya and can only be strengthened at them. Added in Version 7.0.

Unlike other weapons it cannot be refined with ordinary materials. After the Traveler uses Cryo on a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya, the blade can be enhanced there once per Statue.

Appearance: Canon describes it as a longsword that once shone with the light of the stars, and in the Traveler's hand as a new light. No further detail is given in the cited text.

Lore: The blade is obtained in a special domain during Great Deeds on the Tundra, and it seems to react whenever the Traveler comes near a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya.

Each Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya can bless the sword once. The in-game Function Details say that the blade can only be enhanced at those Statues, after the Traveler uses Cryo to awaken and connect to them. The quest places the first enhancement at a Statue in Zolnyy.

Owners: The blade is the player's Traveler's weapon, obtained during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest. Its Traveler's Path passive applies only when the Traveler equips it.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star sword, base ATK 46, CRIT Rate secondary stat. The passive, Traveler's Path, grants CRIT DMG, ATK and Energy effects that scale with enhancement, can trigger even when the Traveler is off-field and has a cooldown. It needs no Mora or materials, and the Statue enhancement does not require the Traveler to be in the party. Obtained at step 18 of the quest, which grants the achievement Mystery Play of the Pale Star.

166.content:
Eye of Graeae (also: Graeae, Eye of Graeae gadget): The Eye of Graeae is a palm-sized mechanism that often takes the form of a monocle. The Traveler finds it in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, where it wakes, recognises them as a Descender, and agrees to serve them. In Snezhnaya it lets its user shape Prime Ice, protects against the killing cold by burning Kresnik Energy, calls a train, and speaks as a polite, forgetful voice that is trying to recover its lost power.

It carries a fragmentary mind that was made, by its own account, within the Hvergelmir project. Over the Snezhnaya story it moves from a helpful gadget to a character with its own mission, and the story ends with the device keeping its functions but losing that voice.

Appearance: In the inventory it is a quick-use gadget, described as a strange mechanism from an abandoned station that "often appears in the form of a monocle" and seems to have many convenient functions. On the Traveler's train it also sits on a pedestal at the front of the carriage, where it is used to set a destination.

Lore: The Eye was left in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, untouched through the cataclysm. When it wakes, its memories are broken and its power is scattered across the tundra. It senses the pieces in three places and asks the Traveler for help, as the one it has "signed a contract to serve".

Its message log is also a window onto Snezhnaya. It explains the four cold zones (normal, low, frigid and subzero), which Kresnik's Torches created by warming parts of a land that was once only frigid and subzero. It tells how trains were first conceived for the needs of Hvergelmir's Shadow Realm exploration, and that the technology became public after the Tsaritsa took the throne. It explains that the Shadow Realm firearms were designed for fighting where living beings cannot use elemental power, and that Hvergelmir researchers modelled them on Hyperborean energy-storage devices.

Owners: The Traveler carries the Eye as a standard gadget. Paimon is present for most of its story and helps them search for its power. Aksinya takes the restored Eye in the Court of Eternal Bliss.

key: Messages from the Eye of Graeae
167.comment: Eye of Graeae: Eye of Graeae Messages
167.content: The message feature unlocks after the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands". New texts arrive as "a new message from the Eye of Graeae" and cover quest background and exploration tips. Examples are the cold zones, the train and its history, the Shadow Realm firearms, Snegovik and Aksinya. Most appear only after specific quests. The Eye says its information comes from a database fed by an uploader named Hvergelmir, which it suspects is not a real name.

168.comment: Eye of Graeae: Fab-Vision and Kresnik Energy
168.content: Fab-Vision is the gadget's construction mode: tap to harvest Prime Ice or build and remove constructs from blueprints. Constructing needs Kresnik Energy and Prime Ice Resource. Kresnik Energy also guards against the cold and runs out fast in the harshest zones. The Eye once noted unusual energy fluctuations when constructs are condensed, and speculated, flagged as speculation, that condensing gives form to a possibility that also exists in many other worlds.

169.content:
Fables de Fontaine (also: Fables of Fontaine, Fontaine Animal Fables): The three tales are "The Maiden and the Sun", "The Crow and the Fox" and "The Tale of the Donkey". All are moral fables with talking animals. Vol. 3 follows directly from Vol. 2, since the donkey tries to copy the fox's trick.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of three volumes. Vol. 1 is sold by Hubel in the Court of Fontaine (Quartier Narbonnais). Vol. 2 lies at Romaritime Harbor next to Hermosa. Vol. 3 lies in front of the Beaumont Workshop. The cover title is written in the Fontaine Script.

Lore: Vol. 2, "The Crow and the Fox": a crow on a tree holds stolen cheese. The fox below first warns that the cheese is dangerous, then that it is no delicacy, then claims the crow does not know how to eat it properly and that she has collected recipes from around the world. Curious, the crow opens its beak to ask, drops the cheese, and the fox takes it and runs to her nest. The moral is that those who seek mysteries they should not know will lose even what they had.

Vol. 3, "The Tale of the Donkey": after hearing how the fox won the cheese, a donkey resents that others praise the fox and ignore its own hard work. It copies her, ambushes a cheesemaker's daughter and tells her to throw her cheese away to travel faster. She takes it for mockery, calls for a stick and threatens to drive it back to the mill, and the donkey falls silent. The moral is that imitating someone else and hiding your own identity brings only more suffering.

Owners: No owner. It is a commercial book collection scattered across Fontaine.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 4.0. The wiki notes that the real-world models are fables by Jean de La Fontaine (the first tale resembles "The Mouse Turned into a Maid", the second "The Fox and the Crow"). The Fontaine-Script cover reads "les fables".

170.comment: Fables de Fontaine: Fox in Fables de Fontaine
170.content: In Fables de Fontaine the fox is a clever, deceitful figure: she is mother to the maiden who weds the sun in Vol. 1 and cheats the crow of its cheese in Vol. 2. The donkey of Vol. 3 fails to copy her. These are unnamed fictional animals with no known canon counterpart.

171.content:
Fang of the Mountain King (also: Turquoise Hunt, Kongamato's fang): Fang of the Mountain King is a 5-star claymore, a giant sword forged from pure turquoise. It is named for Kongamato, the Mountain King, because it is far heavier than ordinary weapons.

The item text is less about the blade than about the beast: a Yumkasaur who once protected the tribes and now guards a fire it no longer remembers.

Appearance: A giant sword of pure turquoise, heavier than ordinary weapons. Canon adds nothing about its shape; keep descriptions to a massive blue-green claymore.

Lore: In the heart of Huitztlan sleeps Kongamato, the Mountain King, a creature as vast as the mountains around it. In its half-waking, searing pain it treats everything that approaches as a mortal enemy and attacks without distinction.

Tribespeople say it once protected them and was driven mad by the dark disaster of the Cataclysm, yet no one can explain why it only attacks what comes near.

Owners: No wielder is named. The sword is named after Kongamato rather than owned by anyone.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star claymore, base ATK 49 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.0.

172.comment: Fang of the Mountain King: Turquoise Hunt
172.content: Turquoise Hunt is the passive of the claymore Fang of the Mountain King (gameplay): it builds stacks of Canopy's Favor to raise Elemental Skill and Burst damage, with extra stacks from nearby Burning or Burgeon reactions.

173.content:
Favonius Codex: Favonius Codex is a 4-star catalyst, a secret tome that belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius. It records the logic and power of elements and matter and is inlaid with crystallized elements. Every copy is hand-made, and its text is partly about the order's great library.

It is the one non-standard-issue weapon of the Favonius series, which otherwise holds the knights' swords, spear and bow.

Appearance: A tome set with crystallized elements. The wiki notes that the Teyvat script on the inside reads "Zephyrus", the Greek counterpart of the Roman Favonius.

Lore: The book holds the collective knowledge of the Knights' scholars. Its crystals are precious both in themselves and because each codex is made by hand; the text says only scholars who truly understand the workings of the elements can make such crystals.

When the Knights of Favonius were founded, the Dawn Knight Ragnvindr turned the aristocrats' indoor baths into a library. Contributions from bards, scholars and travelers made it the largest collection of writing in the northern half of the continent. The text reasons that songs are carried off by the wind and wine's pleasure is brief, but what is written down may shine for ever.

Owners: No owner is named. The text says it belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10.0%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

174.content:
Favonius Greatsword: Favonius Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Favonius series, a heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive, and its text tells of the Lion of Light Arundolyn and his childhood friend Rostam the Wolf Pup.

It is usually issued only after approval from both the Grand Master and the Church.

Appearance: A heavy, ceremonial greatsword. The wiki's trivia remarks that the crossguard and pommel resemble a famous fantasy-film sword; this is a design observation, not canon.

Lore: The text calls it an honor given to a Knight of Favonius and the fruit of the work and skills of Mondstadt's craftsmen, who achieved results in elemental affinity by studying the city's ancient artifacts. It reminds the bearer that destruction is only a means; the end is to defend what must be defended.

Only a single-handed form of Rostam's Favonius Bladework survives today. Another form is lost to history: that of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, who could wield a longsword and a greatsword together in battle. It demanded such strength that only the extraordinarily gifted could try it, and it died out.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

175.content:
Favonius Lance: Favonius Lance is a 4-star polearm of the Favonius series, a spear of honor among the Knights of Favonius. It is used in parades and reviews yet is also a keen foe of monsters. Its text recounts how spears came to Mondstadt and how the noble Eberhart took one up.

The shaft is straight and the tip flows lightly like the wind. It is the weapon that tells of spear use in Mondstadt, from commoners' stakes to a noble's secret training.

Appearance: A polearm in the Knights of Favonius' style: a straight shaft and a tip described as flowing lightly like the wind.

Lore: The text calls it a crystallization of the work and artistry of Mondstadt's defenders. By studying the arbor that held firm in the wind, the city's craftsmen and scholars learned much about elemental affinities. In hand, it reminds the Knights to be disciplined and to defend Mondstadt's freedom.

Polearms of a kind have long been the weapon of those who lack martial training: even untrained commoners with sharpened wooden sticks might match trained soldiers' steel. To celebrate the overthrow of the aristocracy, long stakes, flagpoles and pitchforks were stuck all over the greenery around the city. Nobles were once required to study the sword, and the spear was left to foreign gladiators and traitors.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star polearm, base ATK 44, secondary stat Energy Recharge 6.7%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

176.content:
Favonius Sword: Favonius Sword is a 4-star sword of the Favonius series, the standard-issue longsword of the Knights of Favonius. Its text credits Favonius Bladework to Rostam the Wolf Pup, childhood friend of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, and says Rostam's skill has never been matched.

It is usually issued after approval of both the Master of the order and the Church. The Version 6.4 story quest for Varka features a Favonius Sword that speaks in Rostam's name.

Appearance: A light, agile longsword of the Knights of Favonius. Jean is shown with the ascended version in most official artwork, her manga, her TCG card and her Collected Miscellany, per the wiki.

Lore: Mondstadt's craftsmen studied Mondstadt's Anemo to reach elemental affinity, and the sword is both an honor to a knight and the fruit of the defenders' skill. The text warns that its sharp blade is for defending, not attacking.

Favonius Bladework began with Rostam, the childhood friend and spiritual counterpart of Arundolyn. The legend says he could cut every raindrop out of the sky and that the wind from his sword dance could split a rose and put out a torch. The style is light, swift and precise in the defense of Mondstadt.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star sword, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

177.content:
Favonius Warbow: Favonius Warbow is a 4-star bow of the Favonius series, a recurve bow issued only to the Knights of Favonius' best, long-serving archers. Its text tells of the Outriders, the Knights' archer scouts, and how the team declined after their first member left.

It can be obtained as a reward for the A Long Shot quest and from Wishes.

Appearance: An oak-framed recurve bow with metal parts that make it easy to use. The bowstring is described as enchanted with the secrets of alchemy and magic, protecting the archer's fingers.

Lore: The bow is a reward for worthy guardians of Mondstadt and a tool for their continued guardianship. The text says the Knights once had a formidable team of archer scouts called the Outriders, founded by a mercenary leader from Liyue who passed on a lifetime of knowledge.

The Outriders gained tracking skills and a sense for approaching danger that were unique among the Knights and invaluable to the order. This lasted until the first of the Outriders left the order for reasons unknown to the Knights.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner and as a reward for the Archon quest A Long Shot. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

178.content:
Festering Desire (also: Undying Admiration, Durin's sword): Festering Desire is a creepy straight sword that almost seems to yearn for life, dripping with a shrivelling venom that could corrupt even a mighty dragon. Its blade was coated with powder made of the dragon Durin's remains. The Traveler received it as a memento from Albedo after the 1.2 event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon, once the corruption had been drawn out.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a creepy straight sword that seems to yearn for life and drips with a shrivelling venom. No other visual detail is given in text.

Lore: The item text recalls a memory of the dragon Durin, as a child of Rhinedottir. Rhinedottir's words speak of unborn life and unfulfilled wishes at the edge of the universal darkness, asking them to dwell in her body and descend into the world, then go to a lovely place and show their own beauty. Durin answers: "Thank you, Mother, thank you." He says she gave him wings and a mighty form, and that he wishes to go to a land of lovely songs and tell them the place he was born is beautiful.

Owners: No lasting owner except the Traveler, who receives it from Albedo as a memento. Before that it passed from its unnamed maker to Treasure Hoarders and then into Knights of Favonius custody.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star sword obtained from the event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon. Base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10%. Passive "Undying Admiration": raises Elemental Skill DMG and Elemental Skill CRIT Rate (16-32% and 6-12% at refinement 1-5). During the event it also gave Dragonspine boosts.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the sword suits scenes about inherited harm and the line between study and obsession. Albedo handles it with clinical care; do not have ordinary mortals wield it uncorrupted. By 7.1 canon the corruption in the sword itself is gone.

key: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
179.comment: Festering Desire: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
179.content: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon was a limited-time event (version 1.2, Dragonspine) in which Albedo investigates this sword with the Traveler. It gave the sword as a reward and, while it ran, granted bonuses in Dragonspine when the sword was used there.

180.content:
Finale of the Deep: Finale of the Deep is a four-star sword of the Beaumont series, made by forging in Fontaine. Its description calls the longsword as silent as the ocean depths and older than its styling suggests. The item story says it once belonged to a musician whose name is forgotten, a proud figure of Remuria's golden era whose doctrine of music as authority ended in catastrophe.

The sword is covered in ostentatious decoration and gems, which the text takes as proof that its owner was no ordinary instrumentalist. Lynette is shown wielding it in the Version 4.0 trailer and other promotional material.

Appearance: A ceremonial longsword with layer upon layer of decoration and shining gems. When wielded by a character who has Arkhe, the teardrop-shaped gem on the hilt glows with Pneuma or Ousia.

Lore: Legend holds that the sword belonged to a musician, now nameless, who was fiercely proud of an ancient grand symphony he never performed for anyone, believing that no age of chaos would answer it with applause or lament, and that no one would transcribe so complex a work. An opera in Fontaine portrays his life: nobody knows his origins, but everyone understands his tragedy. Like many of humble birth, he decided his fate in the city to which all waterways lead.

Owners: The nameless musician of legend is the only former owner named in the text. In the current game it is associated with Lynette through trailer and promotional appearances.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive An End Sublime: using an Elemental Skill grants a percentage ATK increase for 15 seconds and a Bond of Life worth 25% of Max HP (once per 10 seconds). Clearing the Bond of Life gives extra flat ATK based on the amount cleared, for 15 seconds, and only if the Bond was increased by this weapon at some point. Base ATK is 44 with ATK 6% as its secondary stat.

181.content:
Finale of the Deep Galleries (also: Deep Gallery's Echoing Song, Deep Gallery's Distant Pact, Deep Gallery's Moment of Oblivion, Deep Gallery's Bestowed Banquet, Deep Gallery's Lost Crown): Finale of the Deep Galleries is a 4- and 5-star Cryo artifact set. Its five Deep Gallery pieces carry item text about Skirk, following her master Surtalogi's guidance, walking the frozen north to find relics, with each piece telling part of a legend of the first angel, a stranger from beyond the stars and the Golden City's fall. Mechanically it rewards a character at zero Energy.

The text interleaves two layers: a short frame in which "the girl" (Skirk) searches northern ruins, and a long past in which a youth and the first angel rebel against the heavens. The pieces were released in version 5.5.

Appearance: All pieces are made of northland jade: an icy flower whose petals crumbled, a shimmering feathered accessory, a pocket watch frozen at its moment of destruction, a ceremonial cup, and a helmet with jade ornamentation from an older age. Per the wiki Skirk wears a feather resembling the Distant Pact in her hair.

Lore: Every piece begins with the girl's trek: following her master, she crosses the freezing wastelands and the corridor of fractured mirrors and kills monsters in the ruins before finding a treasure under snow beside a silver tree, Abyssal remnants, the golden tower, the Spiral Abyss ruins or a tattered veil. The legend:
Across the five pieces: a youth asks the first angel about forbidden origins, she breaks her bonds and loves him, the Golden City forges fae and dreams of a world without tears, the heavens destroy it with crystal spikes, and her kin are cursed so that an angel who loves one alone ends as a Seelie.

Owners: No owner is named. The text implies Skirk finds the relics; otherwise they are described as lost objects of an ancient civilisation.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; domain Derelict Masonry Dock in Natlan (5.5) and an Artifact Strongbox. 4-piece: while the wearer has 0 Elemental Energy, Normal Attack DMG +60% and Burst DMG +60%. Dealing Normal Attack DMG pauses the Burst bonus for 6s, and dealing Burst DMG pauses the Normal Attack bonus for 6s. It can trigger off-field.

182.comment: Finale of the Deep Galleries: Finale of the Deep Galleries
182.content: Artifact set whose item text is set during Skirk's northward search and recounts the first angel, a stranger from the stars and the Golden City.

183.comment: Finale of the Deep Galleries: The first angel's curse
183.content: In the Moment of Oblivion text the traitorous envoy is stripped of name and form after the Golden City falls. Her kin are cursed: any angel who singles out one beloved will lose divine beauty and mind until a Seelie rises from the remains, drifting to consume fading memories.

184.content:
Flame-Forged Insight (also: Mind in Bloom): Flame-Forged Insight is a 4-star claymore from Natlan. The People of the Springs are said to have forged a great blade to protect a child who would go on a distant journey, and this weapon is a replica of that legendary sword.

Its story is told through two old adventurers, Akamai and Kau Kau, who melted down the stones of a lifetime of travel to arm a descendant. It was an event reward in Version 5.8.

Appearance: Canon gives only the description of a replica of a legendary great blade. Do not invent engravings. The story only notes that it was forged from crystal and ore gathered on the old friends' travels.

Lore: Akamai and Kau Kau, two youths of the People of the Springs, once swore to explore all of Natlan and see their deeds recorded on woven scrolls. Their treasures turned out to be mostly ordinary ore and crystals, but they treasured them anyway.

Each stone held a memory: one taken from beneath the claws of a giant Tepetlisaurus in crystal mountains, one from the fiend that tripped them by a hot spring when they were drunk, one ash-covered stone that had kept watch on the edge of the burned ancient city of Ochkanatlan before they took it.

Owners: No owner is named. The wiki calls this particular weapon a replica of the legendary sword.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star claymore of the Meztli series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat Elemental Mastery. Reward of the Version 5.8 event Sunspray Summer Resort; refinement material is Drifter's Crystal Marrow.

185.content: Mind in Bloom is the passive of the claymore Flame-Forged Insight (gameplay): it triggers on several reactions (Electro-Charged, Bloom, Crystallize and their Lunar versions), restoring Energy and raising Elemental Mastery for a while, even off-field.

186.content:
Fleuve Cendre Ferryman (also: the Ferryman): Fleuve Cendre Ferryman is a four-star sword from Fontaine that is, plainly, a handy length of abandoned copper pipe once used as a weapon, famous or infamous depending on the circle. Its item story belongs to Eduardo Baker, an outlaw leader of the Fleuve Cendre, who called it the Ferryman for the many who went into the grey river with it. It is obtained from the Fontaine Fishing Association rather than forged.

The story ends with a photograph of Eduardo and others taken in Poisson during a hostage incident, which the Marechaussee Hunters resolved.

Appearance: A discarded copper (the text also says bronze) pipe, kept like a cane in the photograph in which Eduardo leans on it.

Lore: The text says discarded components in the gutters can serve as a weapon in an emergency. This pipe's first opponent was a monster nourished by 'richly nutritious water', and it broke the knees and jaws of countless 'livestock' who threatened Eduardo's countrymen. The Court of Fontaine's bureaucracy could not keep order in the Fleuve Cendre, so the outlaw leader began his rise by beating back crocodiles with it, protecting merchants from gangs, settling disputes and blessing newlyweds, until it was said that the sun's light belonged to them and the Fleuve Cendre to 'us'.

Owners: Eduardo Baker, whose hands gave it the nickname Ferryman.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive Ironbone raises CRIT Rate of Elemental Skill hits and grants Energy Recharge for 5 seconds after using an Elemental Skill. Base ATK 42, Energy Recharge 10% secondary stat. It is sold by Delaroche at the Fontaine Fishing Association for fish.

187.content:
Flower of Paradise Lost (also: Ay-Khanoum's Myriad, Wilting Feast, A Moment Congealed, Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle, Amethyst Crown): Flower of Paradise Lost is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain) about the Lord of Flowers, also known as Nabu Malikata, goddess of the oasis and mother of the Jinn. Its texts tell how she was cast aside by the heavens, how the Jinn were born from her wanderings, and how she bent to her friend King Deshret's ambition at a heavy price.

The set's mood is elegy: gardens, wine, moonlight, and a friendship that ends in the loss of a god.

Lore: Long ago the heavens cast out the Lord of Flowers. She wandered the barren desert for seventy-two nights; her wounds became springs, the springs became gardens, and night-blue water lilies sprouted. The Jinn were born from those lilies. The first Jinn begged her to stay and she remained, and purple moon-like flowers named Padisarah bloomed wherever she walked.

Later King Deshret, the red-crowned king, let two others share his throne, and the three became friends. Deshret rejected the gift the divine throne offered and chose rebellion, knowing it would cost him those closest to him. She saw only ruin ahead for him but admired the rebellion. One night, over pomegranate wine, he told her his deepest wishes; the words are lost. She warned him to remember how the heavens punished the fallen envoys, then used her body as a conduit and gave up the oasis so he could see his desires made real. Sandstorms swept the paradise, King Deshret returned from them, and she was never seen again.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a 4- and 5-star set from the City of Gold domain and the Flower of Paradise Lost strongbox. 2-piece: Elemental Mastery +80. 4-piece: raises Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon reaction DMG by 40%, and Lunar-Bloom DMG by 10%; triggering one grants up to four 10s stacks of a further 25% of that bonus. Lunar-Bloom was added to the effect in Version 6.0 (Luna I).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): do not have a mortal claim to know what King Deshret said that night; the set says nobody knows.

188.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Ay-Khanoum's Myriad
188.content: The flower piece of Flower of Paradise Lost: an amethyst bloom sculpted in the image of an extinct flower. Its poem is the origin of the Jinn: the Lord of Flowers, cast aside by the heavens, wanders seventy-two nights across the wastes; water lilies grow from her wound-fed springs; the first Jinn, born from dreams and loss, beg her to stay as their creator and mistress of the garden.

189.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Wilting Feast
189.content: The plume piece: a feather of a long-extinct bird, inlaid by ancient adherents of the Goddess of Flowers. Its poem makes the Mistress of Oases choose to help King Deshret defy the "absurd shackles" binding the world, even though she saw only ruin for his path. It ends on the question of whether gods were ever needed.

190.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: A Moment Congealed
190.content: The sands piece: an hourglass whose sand will not flow. Its poem tells of the Eternal Oasis built as a cemetery for the Lord of the Desert's beloved. The legend spreads among desert tribes of a green place ruled by a sleeping goddess, guarded by Ferigees. Tribal matriarchs call themselves Daughters of the Flower Goddess.

191.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle
191.content: The goblet piece: a small purple crystal bottle with an emerald cap. It tells of the night King Deshret poured out his ambitions before the Lord of Flowers over pomegranate wine, and she gave in. Her words promise a bridge to higher knowledge, a warning to remember the punishment of the fallen envoys, and a hope that will be found in ordinary mortals. Sandstorms then swallowed the paradise; she never returned.

192.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Amethyst Crown
192.content: The circlet piece: a crown inlaid with amethyst and emerald, seemingly worn by ancient priests of the Goddess of Flowers. It records the three friends sharing a throne of emeralds and rubies, the Lord of Flowers' confession of exile and her warning not to seek the Master of the Four Shades or the mysteries of the sky and abyss, and Deshret's silent vow to transgress.

193.content:
Flower-Wreathed Feathers (also: Inflorescence Unattainable): Flower-Wreathed Feathers is a 4-star longbow from Natlan that burns like a flame, adorned with feathers said to come from the ancient tyrant Ngoubou. It belongs to the Heroes of Natlan series.

Its story is the legend of the Flower-Feather Clan hero Menilek, who refused to kill his dying Saurian companion despite an old sage's warning.

Appearance: Canon describes a longbow that burns like a flame, adorned with feathers. Keep to that; do not invent a colour scheme or carvings.

Lore: A dying old sage tells the hero Menilek, "bearing the name Transcendence", that a calamity older than his name flows in the veins of the injured Saurian whelp in his arms, and that if he pities mortals he should sever its neck and give it freedom. Menilek ignores the oracle and tends the whelp.

Menilek declares that the descendants of the Flower-Feather Clan bow to neither tyrant nor curse, and that he will break the chain just as his glorious ancestors did. With his loyal companion Ngoubou he sets out on a pilgrimage. The Clan still sings of it: the hero tearing mountains apart with thunderous bowstrings, the whelp piercing a wicked python's throat, a forty-day fight with a huge monster won with a single pike, and a contest with Tenoch (before his exile from his tribe) that led to a lasting friendship.

Owners: The feathers are tied to Ngoubou; the bow itself is tied to Menilek by the legend.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star bow of the Heroes of Natlan series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Weapon Event Wishes from Version 5.2.

194.content: Inflorescence Unattainable is the passive of the bow Flower-Wreathed Feathers (gameplay): cheaper gliding and, while aiming, stacking Charged Attack damage. Its name echoes the story's flowers on the high cliffs that Menilek never reaches.

195.content:
Flowing Purity (also: Clockwork Coppelia): Flowing Purity is a four-star catalyst of the Beaumont series, forged in Fontaine. The weapon is a strangely shaped anthology said to record all the scripts written by Coppelius, and the item text presents a reconstruction of fragments from his last opera, Clockwork Coppelia.

The script of Clockwork Coppelia was never publicized or published. The text is a compiled attempt, made with the consent of Coppelius's family and the survivors who recalled it, to reproduce a part of it.

Appearance: A catalyst shaped like an anthology of scripts. For characters with Arkhe, the weapon shows Pneuma or Ousia alignment indicators.

Lore: A preface-style note explains that the opera's script was never released, for reasons 'known to all and sundry'. Survivors of the day at the splendid opera theater wrote down parts and lines performed before the intermission, and a company collated them with the family's consent, hoping to prompt more capable efforts.

Owners: The text names no owner; the scripts belong to the playwright Coppelius.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive Unfinished Masterpiece grants All Elemental DMG Bonus for 15 seconds after an Elemental Skill, with a Bond of Life worth 24% of Max HP (once per 10 seconds). Clearing the Bond adds more bonus per 1,000 HP cleared, up to a maximum, only when the Bond was increased by this weapon. Base ATK 44, ATK 6% secondary stat.

196.content:
Flute of Ezpitzal (also: Ezpitzal, priestly flute): The Flute of Ezpitzal is a 4-star sword from Natlan: a peculiarly shaped jade longsword that the Masters of the Night-Wind have passed down as a "priestly flute". Its story explains how the tribe called Mictlan began.

It is forgeable and belongs to the Salutary series. The story spans two pages, about a Holy Sovereign, her loyal attendant Dinga (later the dragon slayer Maghan) and the dragons' vanished pact.

Appearance: Canon: a jade longsword of strange shape, handed down as a flute. Do not invent holes, engravings or sounds.

Lore: Long ago, when dragons still roamed a deep valley, a girl with mutilated ankles inherited the title of Holy Sovereign. Dragons, frightened into withdrawing into dreams, had made a pact with the mortals: they would shield the village with a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist if the people chose a Sovereign to guide them into their dreams.

The Sovereign's only companions were a flute and her silent attendant. She had foreseen how the dream would end. When the hero passed through the mist and mirrors guided by her flute song, she whispered her last command: when they met again he must pierce her heart, let her name be swallowed by the beacons, break the old pact and make a new one bringing true peace. She names him her most loyal servant Dinga, dragon slayer and fated Sovereign Maghan.

Owners: Handed down among the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its story is tied to the Holy Sovereign and to Maghan.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a forgeable 4-star sword of the Salutary series, base ATK 41 at level 1, secondary stat DEF%. Forging needs a diagram that the Traveler receives from the Hidden Exploration Objective Stoking the Ancient Flames in Ochkanatlan (activate five furnaces, then draw the ancient sword).

197.content: Smoke-and-Mirror Mystery is the passive of the sword Flute of Ezpitzal (gameplay): casting an Elemental Skill raises the wielder's DEF for a while. The name recalls the labyrinth of mirrors and fortress of mist that shielded the valley.

198.content:
Forest Regalia: Forest Regalia is a 4-star claymore of the Aranara series. The description says it has taken the shape of a greatsword that shall cut down the foes of the forest. Its story tells, through an Aranara's memory, of the last king of the forest and the shifting maze of his palace.

It is forged from the diagram Tale of the Forest King, which the Aranara quest line lets a player buy from Aravinay in exchange for Stories of You and the Aranara.

Appearance: A greatsword whose form the description attributes to the forest cutting down its foes. No further detail is given.

Lore: The tale begins "The forest used to be a giant maze many, many moons ago..." The last king of the forest has returned to Sarva, leaving one who once waited upon him to inherit the name "Tiger". Where there was shade, there was the forest king's domain, and birds and beasts bowed as he passed.

Every king had a palace, and as each took the throne the forest reshaped itself to his image. The last king's palace lay behind a fence of trees and vines and a network of water and cliffs, like a disc of pearls made by moonlight through leaves on still water, where he basked alone. Legend says he traced the maze in his dappled stripes; successive palaces piled on one another so that paths wove from tree to tree and streams branched.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat Energy Recharge 6.7%. Passive Forest Sanctuary: after Burning, Quicken, Aggravate, Spread, Bloom, Lunar-Bloom, Hyperbloom or Burgeon, a Leaf of Consciousness appears for up to 10 s; picking it up grants Elemental Mastery for 12 s, once every 20 s, and works off-field. Forged from one Midlander Claymore Billet, 50 Crystal Chunk, 50 White Iron Chunk and 500 Mora.

199.content:
Forged by the Golden Melody: Forged by the Golden Melody is a four-star claymore added in Version 7.0 through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn. The description calls it a greatsword decorated in gold and says legend holds it was the favored weapon of an exalted Harmost of the distant past. Its story is a conversation in the white-stone halls of Remuria between a musician and his golden-haired friend.

The musician is troubled by the burden of attunement and by his friend's contempt for ordinary people; he recalls a female companion who did not believe in gods.

Appearance: A greatsword decorated in gold, as the in-game description puts it.

Lore: In silent corridors of white stone, the golden-haired friend urges the musician to look at the 'benighted slaves' who mistake the labor of the high-ranking for luxury, and laments that a beautiful solo should fall to mortal ground. The musician sighs and does not argue. The duty of attunement, cleansing the bitter sorrow of all waters, was in effect burning one's soul like firewood, so that the God King in his golden palace could fulfil his great and tragic wish to save all souls. He rebukes his friend gently: they were raised up to guide and rescue those people, and one cannot play the Sebastos' perfect melody if one despises them.

Owners: Only an unnamed exalted Harmost of the distant past, according to legend.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive Day and Night in Counterpoint rotates a 10-second Harmonic Movement (ATK, Elemental Mastery, Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG) that works even when the wielder is off-field, and a Stellar Glimmer reaction adds a 12-second Contrapuntal instance. Base ATK 42, CRIT Rate 6% secondary stat.

200.content:
Fractured Halo (also: Purifying Crown, Electrifying Edict): A spinning mechanical blade produced by the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, seeming to hide secrets from a bygone era. A 5-star polearm from Version 5.8, wielded by Ineffa.

Its item text is Ineffa's fragmentary memory of the age of the three moons.

Appearance: A spinning, halo-like mechanical blade with a cyclonic mechanism whose centre holds a hidden remnant of the Moon. In her portrait art and demo Ineffa carries the unascended version.

Lore: After her revival, Ineffa remembers an age even bards forget, but her memories feel hollow, like thoughts flaring and fading in a trance.

She recalls following the Master of Light and Flame to visit the moon-dwelling wills on their three jade thrones, at a time when the king who set the moons aloft had vanished into the fog between the stars. The Master received only three silences in three palace halls.

Owners: Ineffa wields it; the text says Aino forged it for her.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star polearm, CRIT DMG secondary. Passive Purifying Crown raises ATK for 20 seconds after a Skill or Burst, and if the wielder creates a shield the party deals more Lunar-Charged damage.

201.content: Purifying Crown is the weapon's passive; Electrifying Edict is the party buff it grants. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

key: The Grand Jape of the Turning of Fate
202.content:
Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy (also: Harmonious Symphony Prelude, Ancient Sea's Nocturnal Musing, The Grand Jape of the Turning of Fate, Ichor Shower Rhapsody, Whimsical Dance of the Withered): Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.6. Its five pieces are written as one story: Remus, a god who lost his homeland, becomes the God King of Remuria, is told that his glorious empire will drown, and chooses to fight fate with a "Grand Symphony." The set is a Remurian legend, not a family heirloom.

The bonuses reward the Bond of Life mechanic (see gameplay). The five pieces are Harmonious Symphony Prelude (flower), Ancient Sea's Nocturnal Musing (plume), The Grand Jape of the Turning of Fate (sands), Ichor Shower Rhapsody (goblet) and Whimsical Dance of the Withered (circlet).

Appearance: The flower is described as an honorary medal in the shape of a blooming flower, adorned with blue stone and gold, once bestowed upon immortals. The other pieces are known only by their names and lore text.

Lore: The five pieces run in order: a homeless desert god meets the prophet Sybilla and is told he will rule the High Sea; he builds a glorious kingdom yet grieves at its foretold fall; he confronts a vishap prince and the imprisoned Mistress of Many Waters and finds no salvation; as Sebastos he resolves to compose his own symphony against fate; and after the realm sinks, a new nation of Many Waters rises.

Owners: No named owner. The set is narrative item text. Remus and Sybilla are the characters it speaks of.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): 2-piece bonus is ATK +18%. The 4-piece bonus triggers whenever the wearer's Bond of Life value increases or decreases, giving 18% increased DMG for 6s, stacking up to 3 times. It is obtained from the Faded Theater domain (located in Fontaine's Nostoi Region at Petrichor) and from the matching artifact strongbox.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the set as a theatrical, mournful retelling that characters in Fontaine may know as an old opera or legend. Do not present its words as proven history; Remuria's fall is better documented in books and quests than in these verses.

203.content: In the Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy, Remus is the God King of Remuria, once a singer of the oases whose homeland fell to the Lord of the Blazing Sun. He is told by the golden-bee prophet Sybilla that he will rule the High Sea and bring a justice that ruins it, and he spends his reign trying to escape that fate.

204.content: In this set Sybilla is the golden-bee prophet who once guarded the silver tree in a forgotten city below the lightless depths. She foretells Remus's rise and fall, and later agrees to help him with the Grand Symphony even though, in the text's words, her eyes already saw no future.

205.content:
Freedom-Sworn (also: Revolutionary Chorale, Millennial Movement: Song of Resistance): Freedom-Sworn is a five-star sword released in version 1.6, a Millennial Movement weapon whose story is a Mondstadt resistance song. The song says that if someone takes your tongue you can still sing with your eyes, and that stealing your song and your freedom "shall never do". It was sung through Decarabian's reign and the aristocracy's, and when five rebels climbed Decarabian's tower.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a straight sword, "azure as antediluvian song, and as keen as the oaths of freedom taken in the Land of Wind". The text gives no further visual detail.

Lore: The item's story begins with the drinking song itself: even if your tongue is plucked out you can sing with your eyes; even if you are blinded you can see with your ears; and if someone plots to destroy tomorrow, raise them a glass, for the song will live on. It then reflects on whether the Anemo Archon's love of freedom and wine shaped the people or the people shaped him; the text says this can no longer be answered.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. The sword stands for the song rather than a single wielder.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star sword from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 43. Passive "Revolutionary Chorale": raises DMG (10-20%); triggering Elemental Reactions gives a Sigil of Rebellion, and at two Sigils nearby party members get "Millennial Movement: Song of Resistance" for 12 seconds (more Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack DMG and ATK), followed by a 20-second lockout. Buffs of the same type do not stack.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the song works as a toast or defiance chant at taverns. Ordinary Mondstadters can know the song; the identity of the five rebels is more specialist history.

206.content: The resistance drinking song of Mondstadt, quoted in Freedom-Sworn, is said to have been sung whenever the people were oppressed, under Decarabian and under the aristocracy. Its line "even if tomorrow dies, this song shall live on" frames music as the thing tyrants cannot remove.

207.content:
Frostbearer: Frostbearer is a 4-star catalyst of the Dragonspine series. Its in-game description is "a fruit that possesses a strange, frosty will," with a faint sense of agony. It is the one weapon of the series obtained only by forging, using a diagram from the Frostbearing Tree. Added in Version 1.2.

Its text recounts the Frostbearing Tree of Sal Vindagnyr from the princess's birth to the tree's revival by dragon blood, and ends with the tree's own voice offering a bitter fruit to whoever can deliver justice on a poisoned world.

Appearance: Canon text calls it a crimson, icy fruit borne by a silver-white tree. No further physical description is given.

Lore: When the daughter of the priest of Vindagnyr was born beneath the white tree, the verdant mountain kingdom rejoiced at her blessing. Those who wrote the kingdom's annals believed that Sal Vindagnyr's blessing, like the undying silver-white tree, would last forever.

Then the nail that froze the world fell from the sky and shattered the tree. The princess took the most complete branch and tried to graft it to give the tree new life, but the grafted life did not flourish, and the snowstorm covered the moonlight like a curtain of blades.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. It is a crafted weapon, made at the forge from the diagram for Frostbearer.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 4-star catalyst with base ATK 42 and an ATK% secondary stat. The Dragonspine series passive Frost Burial gives Normal and Charged Attack hits a chance (60 to 100 per cent by refinement, once per 10s) of dropping an Everfrost Icicle that deals area damage, more against Cryo-affected enemies. The wiki notes it is the only Dragonspine weapon that can be obtained only by forging; its diagram comes from raising the Frostbearing Tree to level 10.

208.content: The Frostbearing Tree is the silver-white tree of Sal Vindagnyr whose roots pierced the earth. After the Skyfrost Nail shattered it, the princess tried to graft a branch to revive it; in much later times, dragon blood and crimson essence gave it one fruit, the source of Frostbearer. In game it is a Dragonspine tree the player can level up.

209.content:
Frostbreath (also: Frostbreath polearm, A Cast Real Far): Frostbreath is a four-star polearm in the Gnostic Hymn 3 series, added in version 7.0 as a Battle Pass weapon. Its in-game description calls it a spear of solid ice imbued with a chill, said to have belonged to the Belyi Tsar who ruled Snezhnaya long ago. Its story follows the young Monomakh, trained by his master, who asked whether stronger spears exist.

Appearance: The description gives only "a spear of solid ice imbued with an icy chill". The item has a base and a second-ascension look in the game, but the text describes no further detail such as shaft, tip or decoration.

Lore: The story opens with the young Monomakh asking his master whether stronger spears exist, during training so harsh that even a fae could hardly imagine it. He is described as lean as a white-barked birch and gasping on the ice. Looking at him, the crimson princess of the snow, whose eyes had survived the ruin of the golden city, answers that a spear once existed that could shoot down the Lord of the Sky. She tells him he cannot do it, since he cannot yet even defeat her, and that he asked only whether stronger spears exist. He says he would like to learn it so as to protect more people, and she tells him to firm up his stance.

Owners: Per the short description, the Belyi Tsar who ruled Snezhnaya in the distant past once owned it. The story's protagonist, Monomakh, is the only wielder shown, and the item text links him to the same ruler; his teacher is the Knyazhna of Blood (Yalyane Morevna).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star polearm, obtained from the Battle Pass (Gnostic Hymn). Base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10.0%. Passive "A Cast Real Far": triggering a Cryo- or Hydro-related reaction raises the wielder's ATK for 15 seconds and restores Elemental Energy to the other party members, once per 16 seconds.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a northern soldier or scholar might know the polearm as a relic of the old Tsar. The tale's irony, a king who never doubted his teacher and learned too late what she had actually said, makes it a good prop for stories about misunderstood advice or loyalty.

210.content: In Frostbreath's story, Monomakh is a lean, determined youth trained on the ice by the crimson princess of the snow, Yalyane Morevna, called the Knyazhna of Blood. Asked whether stronger spears exist, she tells him of a spear she saw in the lost golden city that could shoot down the Lord of the Sky. He cannot reproduce it, though he later becomes a conquering emperor who unites the northern realms.

211.content:
Fruitful Hook (also: The Weight of Falling Branches): Fruitful Hook is a 4-star claymore from Natlan: a hooked blade made by the courier-hero Burkina of the Scions of the Canopy, with the hero Tenoch's help, to harvest the finest Flamegranates from the great mother tree.

Its story explains why the best Flamegranates are called "Mountain Kings" and how Burkina became companions with the Saurian Kongamato.

Appearance: A hooked blade or sword with a hook, used to cut fruit loose and to block attacks. Do not add decoration.

Lore: A young courier, Burkina, was royally annoyed at a Saurian living on the mountain's other side who mocked his movements, so he swore to climb to the peak and harvest the Flamegranates of the mother tree to show off to the most agile Yumkasaurus of all.

Skill alone did not help: winged Saurians harassed him at the summit and wild beasts waited under the tree. Burkina trained in patience: looking after the Saurians of the Flower-Feather Clan to learn their movements, hardening his body on boulders with the people of the mountain below the volcano, and seeking guidance from the Night-Wind high priests. Tenoch, travelling there, offered to join him; Burkina refused, since the training was the price of the result and he sensed that Tenoch's kindness might one day need to be repaid. Tenoch only said he could still do a small favour.

Owners: Made by Burkina with Tenoch's help. No later wielder is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star claymore of the Heroes of Natlan series, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Weapon Event Wishes from Version 5.1.

212.comment: Fruitful Hook: The Weight of Falling Branches
212.content: The Weight of Falling Branches is the passive of the claymore Fruitful Hook (gameplay): it boosts Plunging Attack CRIT Rate and then Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack damage after a Plunging Attack lands, echoing Burkina's near-fall from the tree.

213.content:
Funerary Mask (also: Signora's mask, mask of La Signora): The Funerary Mask is a quest item the Traveler receives after defeating La Signora, Eighth of the Fatui Harbingers, in a duel before the Raiden Shogun's throne in Tenshukaku, Inazuma (Version 2.1). Its text calls it a trophy and uses it to reflect on why Fatui wear masks.

It is a memento: a keepsake of the duel with no use in play, tied to the end of Signora's story.

Appearance: Canon gives no physical description of the mask. Its name suggests mourning, and its item text speaks of the faceless masks the Fatui present to the world.

Lore: The Archive text first says it is a trophy for defeating Signora. It then says the Fatui often face the world from behind masks, and that this is said to be because everything they were counts for nothing once they become Fatui: they must give up their true names and share one face.

The text adds that giving up everything that makes up an "I", past and bonds included, is hard. It suggests those willing to join a group that rebels against the Heavenly Principles may have an obsession close to or beyond that of a Delusion holder, binding the rest of their days to the Delusion and burning like stars. It also notes that many Fatui are simply drunk on power or sadistic, and that the states are not mutually exclusive.

Origin: Obtained on completing Duel Before the Throne (Archon Quest, Chapter II, Act III), set in Tenshukaku in Inazuma City. After Kujou Sara stormed toward the throne, the Traveler found Signora already there before the Raiden Shogun and accused her of distributing Delusions and of the harm done in Liyue and to Venti's Gnosis. Signora answered as a mere Snezhnayan diplomat, mocking the Traveler's status as a wanted criminal. The Traveler then challenged her to a duel before the throne, which the Shogun allowed.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a quest item with no function in play. The wiki lists it as a memento, so it can be viewed in the inventory but not used.

Status as of 7.1: The Traveler holds it as of Version 7.1; nothing read says otherwise.

Signora died at the end of the duel; the mask is her only keepsake in the Traveler's possession.

214.comment: Funerary Mask: Duel Before the Throne
214.content: The Chapter II Archon Quest in which the Traveler challenged La Signora in Tenshukaku and won. The Raiden Shogun executed her afterward, and the Traveler received the Funerary Mask as the reward.

215.content:
General History of Snezhnaya (also: General History of Snezhnaya (I), General History of Snezhnaya (II)): General History of Snezhnaya is a two-volume book sold by Moes at Torchlight Books in Snezhnograd (added in 7.0). Written by Y. S. Klyucheva and dedicated in fawning terms to Tsaritsa Anastasya, it is Snezhnaya's flattering "official" history: legends of golden Hyperborea, then the youth and campaigns of Tsar Monomakh (the Belyi Tsar) and his fae companions.

Lore: Volume 1 sets out rival legends of Hyperborea, a warm golden realm where Snezhnaya now lies. Volume 2 tells how young Monomakh learned the spear from Yalyane Morevna, beat the shapeshifter Filipov and made him his "Synaimos" (sworn comrade), and spared the human warrior Nepla Korolevitsna's clan.

The in-world work has many volumes: Polar Night legends first, Monomakh's campaigns in the middle, and the Tsaritsa's deeds at the end. The game shows only the preface and excerpts of Volumes I, III and VII. The preface states the thesis: Monomakh conquered by force, but virtue renews the world, and the Tsaritsa's virtue is greater still.

Reliability: This is the court-approved version of history. It passes on a genealogy that makes Monomakh Hyperborea's rightful heir, which other canon contradicts (he was an incomplete Primordial Human born of the Cryo Dragon's remains). Still, the author names competing sources and marks legends as legends.

Appearance: A 3-star Book Collection item in two volumes, (I) and (II). Gaps in the excerpted text are marked by ellipses.

Gameplay: Gameplay: Archive Book Collection (Snezhnaya). Each volume is bought once from Moes at Torchlight Books; the stock does not refresh.

216.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Klyucheva's preface to the Tsaritsa
216.content: In the preface of General History of Snezhnaya, Y. S. Klyucheva addresses Tsaritsa Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya by a long chain of titles. They include Eternal Sovereign Under the Pale Star, Protectress of the Fae Kindreds and of the Lineages of the Peoples of the North, Holy One of All Winters, and Grand Suzerain of the Princes of Snezhnograd, Glupov, Kitezh and Belovodye. The author thanks her for release from "former afflictions" and for being allowed to stand among the immortals, then signs as her loyal subject and child. The preface contrasts Monomakh's conquests, fierce as a winter gale, with the Tsaritsa's greater virtue.

217.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Legends of Hyperborea (General History)
217.content: Volume I of General History of Snezhnaya says many sources agree Snezhnaya was once a warm, fertile plain. Fae poems name the realm there Hyperborea. The author warns that even *The Volkhov Chronicles* was written thousands of years after the age it describes. Grand Duke P. N. Kostomarov pictures virtuous people in golden cities in eternal spring, living on heavenly honey and dew. When their descendants grew idle and lost their nobility, spring left and the long winter came. The author then turns to "true history": before founding Kitezhgrad, Monomakh wandered the blizzard lands for centuries as a young hero, gathering companions and imagining a realm of virtue and mercy.

218.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Songbook of Saint Strivozha
218.content: In-world source quoted in General History of Snezhnaya and attributed to Vaselisa Strivozha. It says the King of Light imprisoned his daughter in darkness. The King of Hyperborea freed her, and from then on night existed; she became the Mother of Night. They had seven Preexistent Gods and twelve Preexistent Men, whose descendants founded Hyperborea of gold and white stone. The King of Light then destroyed it and killed the seven divine bloodlines, except Tsar Monomakh, the last monarch's young son. The book calls this a "strange fable". Its claim about Monomakh's descent conflicts with other canon about his origin.

219.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Yalyane Morevna in the General History
219.content: General History of Snezhnaya (Volume III) says the Snegurochka of Hesperides were closest to Monomakh. He openly called Yalyane Morevna his teacher; she was the grandmother of Hesperides' first Grand Duchess. Real history barely mentions her, and she vanished before Kitezhgrad was founded. Folk accounts make her a Hyperborean survivor called the "Knyazhna of Blood" for savagely raiding other fae kindreds. Yet she never preyed on the destitute human clans of the snowfields; *The Davograd Chronicles* even says she sheltered humans from monsters. She took in young Monomakh and taught him the spear. The author reflects that before courage became a virtue it was a crime, cradled by plunder and nursed by greed.

220.content: "Synaimos" is a word from the fae tongue that General History of Snezhnaya glosses as comrade-in-arms, brother or kinsman. Monomakh offered Filipov Vseslavyevich crystals of the purest kind to become his Synaimos. Filipov first refused and challenged him to a contest.

221.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Filipov's contest with Monomakh
221.content: In General History of Snezhnaya, the young Filipov Vseslavyevich, progenitor of the shapeshifters, scorns Monomakh and demands his submission. He becomes a weasel and destroys Monomakh's weapons, then becomes a falcon, a white wolf, a great bear, a hill-sized bull, a giant the size of a mountain range, and finally Monomakh's own likeness. Each time Monomakh seizes him by the scruff and throws him like a spear over one more mountain, from one up to seven. Moved by Monomakh's purity of heart, Filipov becomes his Synaimos and dearest friend, and later the first Commander of the Druzhna. Legends of the pair sailing into a whale's belly and facing a dragon for seven days are noted as unverifiable. Chronicles always link Filipov with cunning and victory. He lost only three times: to Monomakh, to his wife, and to the pitch-black calamity from beneath the earth.

222.comment: General History of Snezhnaya: Nepla Korolevitsna in the General History
222.content: In General History of Snezhnaya, Nepla Korolevitsna is a human warrior guarding her clan with a huge war hammer and a fire-breathing horse; her shout alone drives Filipov's horse to its knees. Filipov unhorses her at the cost of one eye. Under the law of the age the victors could kill or enslave her clan, but Monomakh spares it, citing the mercy his teacher Yalyane taught him, and settles it at the future Port Belovodye.
