Filipov marries Nepla, saying her arrow took one eye and her valour and beauty the other. She soon dies of sickness, and only friendship and oaths keep him alive.

223.content:
Geo Gnosis (also: Morax's Gnosis, Gnosis of Morax, Geo Archon's Gnosis, Rex Lapis's Gnosis): The Geo Gnosis was the Gnosis of Morax, the Geo Archon, who now lives in Liyue as Zhongli. A Gnosis is a gleaming, chess-piece-like focus that an Archon carries in their chest. Zhongli gave his to the Fatui Harbinger Signora in Liyue Harbor (1.1), fulfilling a secret contract with the Tsaritsa that he called his "contract to end all contracts".

It was the second Gnosis the Fatui obtained, after the Anemo Gnosis, and the first one given up willingly. Canon has not revealed what the Tsaritsa gave in return.

Lore: Zhongli staged his own death at the Rite of Descension to test whether Liyue could thrive without its god. Meanwhile Childe (Tartaglia), kept in the dark, tried to seize the Gnosis and finally freed the ancient god Osial. The Qixing, the adepti and the Traveler stopped Osial together. At the Northland Bank, Signora asked Morax to honour the agreement. Zhongli materialised the Gnosis and gave it to her, saying his promise was "solid as stone" and that the matter lay "solely between the Tsaritsa and I".

Consequences: The Golden House, Teyvat's only Mora mint, stopped working because minting needs the Geo Archon's power; existing Mora did not vanish.

Owners: Morax (Zhongli), then Signora, then the Tsaritsa (Anastasya), who holds it as of 7.1.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, the Geo Gnosis among them; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing. She collects them to amplify her power against the Heavenly Principles and to open a seal the Third Descender left beneath Zapolyarny Palace. In 7.1 she used all six to slow time around Rhinedottir.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a story object only, never an obtainable item. Zhongli's playable Geo powers are not tied to it.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation, not canon): keep the Geo Gnosis with the Tsaritsa after 7.1. Zhongli remains powerful without it, declines to discuss the contract's terms and does not voice regret. Ordinary Liyue citizens believe Rex Lapis died and know nothing of the trade. Never invent the Tsaritsa's side of the bargain.

224.comment: Geo Gnosis: Contract to End All Contracts
224.content: Zhongli's final contract as Geo Archon was made with the Cryo Archon, the Tsaritsa. He would surrender the Geo Gnosis, and Signora would collect it as her emissary. Asked what could be worth a Gnosis, Zhongli said that realistically nothing was. Even so, as God of Contracts he would never agree to a deal that brought him no benefit. One clause forbids him to reveal the contract's terms. He told the Traveler to discover the Tsaritsa's "bargaining chip" on their own journey. As of 7.1 it remains unknown.

225.comment: Geo Gnosis: Childe's search of the Exuvia
225.content: In Heart of Glaze (1.1), Childe used the Traveler's work on the Rite of Parting to learn where the Qixing had hidden the Exuvia, the god's shed body. At the Golden House, where the Millelith guards had been knocked unconscious, he reached into the Exuvia for Morax's Gnosis, but came out empty-handed. He fought the Traveler, believing they had taken it, then realised they had not. He guessed that the Exuvia was a diversion and freed Osial with a swarm of Sigils of Permission to force the god to reveal himself. The handover itself later took place at the Northland Bank, not the Golden House.

226.content:
Gest of the Mighty Wolf (also: Indomitable Chivalry, Four Winds' Hymn): Gest of the Mighty Wolf is a five-star claymore of the Hexerei series, released in version 6.4. Its description says it was forged by Ravenwood, who inherited the name of Boreas, before he became a knight. The item story is a Mondstadt tale of a nameless northern knight and his wolf companion Andrius, and of the blacksmith's son who admired him.

Appearance: No visual description is given in the item text beyond calling it a greatsword. The story speaks of a heavy, fearsome sword, but it is describing the weapon Ravenwood carried at the end, not necessarily this one.

Lore: Mondstadt's tales praise knights' martial feats, and the "wolf" stories are the best loved, as a free-roaming wolf suits a poet more than a stately lion. They often begin with a wandering knight arriving from the north with his companion Andrius, visiting a city freshly freed. Together they killed beasts plaguing the countryside and drove back a great serpent threatening the coast. The homesick wolf eventually left his spirit in the emerald wilds, and the knight quietly followed his companion's steps. No one learned his name.

Owners: Ravenwood, said by the description to have forged it before his ascension to knighthood. The wiki identifies him as the second Knight of Boreas. The wandering knight, the first Knight of Boreas, is an earlier figure from the same story.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star claymore from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat CRIT Rate 7.2%. Passive "Indomitable Chivalry": raises ATK SPD by 10% and builds Four Winds' Hymn stacks (up to four) that raise DMG dealt; with the team bonus "Hexerei: Secret Rite" each stack also raises CRIT DMG.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the story suits scenes about borrowed names and legend outliving the person. Treat the connection between Ravenwood, Andrius and Boreas as something characters know only if they have read the item or Varka's quests.

227.comment: Gest of the Mighty Wolf: Ravenwood
227.content: Ravenwood was the son of Mondstadt's blacksmith, later the second Knight of Boreas (wiki title). He wielded a greatsword in battle, a design later copied and used as a model for Ferrous Shadow. He is dead; he appears in canon only through Varka's quest and item text.

228.content:
Gilded Dreams (also: Dreaming Steelbloom, Feather of Judgment, The Sunken Years, Honeyed Final Feast, Shadow of the Sand King): Gilded Dreams is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.0, Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain). Its five pieces remember a lost golden age: a desert paradise ruled by a "God King" who judged every heart, three inseparable friends, and a law that hardened into chains. The set never names the God King; other lore points to King Deshret.

Its images are gilded: dark gold flowers that never open, molten metal weighing hearts, sundials, wine cups and sand-king crowns. The tone is mournful rather than triumphant.

Lore: Ancient legends tell of three inseparable friends: one withered like a rose in the mud, one made a great hidden oasis, one used all their intellect to build an eternal illusion in the sand. They meant for no one to suffer partings or bitter water, and promised a "golden slumber".

Long ago the heavens fell silent and the land lost its master. A God King then judged all life by law: a feather weighed hearts and molten metal measured wisdom. Tribes who lived by blood-law and the memory of famine imitated his thrones and walls. The priests ruled the oasis cities justly in his name, but later decrees were issued from "illusory madness", and the citizens' fates were chained to their God King's choice. A banquet of the three God Kings, with the moon, sun and green fields as their symbols, ended when time broke the oath between day and night.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a set from the Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain (4 and 5 star) and its strongbox. 2-piece: Elemental Mastery +80. 4-piece: within 8s of triggering an Elemental Reaction, ATK rises 14% for each party member of the wearer's element and Elemental Mastery rises 50 for each of a different element (3 members counted each), once per 8s, even off-field; the triggering reaction itself is not buffed. Released in 3.0; no later change is listed.

229.content: The flower piece of Gilded Dreams: a bud of hammered dark gold with a crimson core and petals that will never open. Its verses tell of three inseparable friends, one who withers in mud, one who builds a hidden oasis, one who builds an eternal illusion, and a promise that in the golden slumber no one need drink bitter water.

230.content: The plume piece: a feather once used to weigh the hearts of the guilty, its original function lost. The verses describe the past of "civilization and ease" abandoned, then the new law: a feather to weigh hearts, molten metal to measure divine wisdom, the God King's blood-rooted law carved into the desert paradise, and sorrow twisting governance into shackles.

231.content: The sands piece: a dark-golden sundial that tells the desert's story. In the beginning tribes lived with the sands, bound by blood-law and the fear of famine, until a God King rose; they copied his walls and thrones into feudal kingdoms, and wise kings received oracles from the heavens.

232.content: The goblet piece: a wine cup from a grand ancient feast that has lost its luster. It recalls the three God Kings as oathbound friends, one for the banquet, one for authority, one for life, whose happiness ended when time broke the contract between day and night. The final lines hint at dreams ground in lifeless machinery.

233.comment: Gilded Dreams: Shadow of the Sand King
233.content: The circlet piece: a gold-inlaid headband once worn by desert priests, modelled on one worn by a legendary desert ruler. Its verses describe a divine pillar from the sky burying forest and meadow, sacred cities on fertile oases, priests ruling justly under the God King, and later absurd decisions that led the people toward a bitter end.

234.content:
Gladiator's Finale (also: Gladiator's Nostalgia, Gladiator's Destiny, Gladiator's Longing, Gladiator's Intoxication, Gladiator's Triumphus): Gladiator's Finale is an ATK artifact set (4 and 5 star, 1.0) about the champion gladiator of aristocracy-era Mondstadt, a slave who nearly won his freedom, was undone by pride and a master's flattery, and fell to a young girl in the arena. The girl is Vennessa, the later founder of the Knights of Favonius. Its weapon companion is the polearm Deathmatch.

The pieces are Gladiator's Nostalgia (flower), Gladiator's Destiny (feather), Gladiator's Longing (hourglass), Gladiator's Intoxication (goblet) and Gladiator's Triumphus (helmet).

Lore: Nostalgia shows the master giving a flower to his silent slave and making it a brooch; years later the master called such gifts whims. Destiny says he was one battle from freedom when a young girl defeated him but refused to execute him, and a bird left a feather on his chest. Longing is the hourglass he flipped before each fight; in his last fight the sand stopped. Intoxication is a gold cup from his master; Triumphus a helmet that made him a symbol of invincibility to the crowd.

235.content: A slave of Eberhart and champion of the aristocracy-era arena, who fought with the polearm Deathmatch and was slain by Vennessa. He is never named.

236.content:
Glaze Lily (also: Glaze Lilies, Liuli Baihe): The Glaze Lily is a very old flower of Liyue, once common across the land and now rare in the wild. Its item text says it turns the land's memories into scent as it blooms. Legend says it opens to pure, beautiful music, and that someone once loved it above all other flowers.

It is a Liyue local specialty grown on the terraces of Qingce Village and in Liyue Harbor's Yujing Terrace, and blooms at night.

Appearance: A lily whose blossoms open at night, between 18:00 and 06:00 in-game. Wild plants smell stronger than the planted ones, per Solitary Fragrance as cited by the wiki.

Lore: The archive text calls it an extremely ancient flower, said to have been a common sight in Liyue, that converts the memories of the land into fragrance during florescence. A legend says it opens at the sound of pure, beautiful music, and that one person loved it more than any other; the wiki identifies that person as Guizhong, though the text does not name her. A full bloom in the wild is now rare.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon still describes the wild flower as rare, with planted lilies in the Harbor and Qingce Village.

237.content:
Golden Frostbound Oath (also: Dawn's Salutation Returned): Golden Frostbound Oath is a five-star bow released in version 6.5 (Luna VI). Its in-game description calls it a longbow carved from ancient whitewood, once wielded by the Jack Frost King of the northern lands. Its story follows the Knight of the Golden Bough, who walks into the frozen north seeking the Golden Bough to save fallen Arcadia and finds the sacred tree already ruined.

Appearance: The description says only "a longbow carved from ancient whitewood". The wiki shows a base and second-ascension look, but the text gives no further detail.

Lore: The story begins in an age when an idyllic land of oakwoods and plenty stood against even the fiercest storms. The Arcadians, exalted by the thousand winds, believed their holy city would last forever, but calamity struck and its spring was laid to rest in a deathly chill. The Knight of the Golden Bough, addressed in a prophecy as Gunnhildr, last light of the people, then walked alone into the endless frost. The prophecy says that only when the pure Golden Bough is severed can the withered wood live again and the sealed paradise endure.

Owners: The short description names the Jack Frost King of the northern lands as the bow's wielder in ages past. The long story features the Knight of the Golden Bough as the traveller who confronts the king but does not give her or him the bow.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star bow from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT DMG 19.2%. Passive "Dawn's Salutation Returned": raises DEF; after the wielder's Elemental Skill or Lunar-Crystallize attack hits, Geo DMG and Lunar-Crystallize Reaction DMG rise for 6 seconds. If Moondrifts are near the wielder, other nearby party members gain a smaller Geo DMG and Lunar-Crystallize bonus, even when the wielder is off-field.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the weapon fits scenes about duty to a lost homeland, hope that has outlived its object, and a guardian loyal to an order whose meaning is gone. Treat the Arcadian tale as ancient history, not common knowledge.

238.comment: Golden Frostbound Oath: The Jack Frost King
238.content: In Golden Frostbound Oath's story, a Jack Frost calls itself king of a sacred northern grove and guards it from the high boughs left by a vanished envoy. It delights in riddles and mockery and gives the knight answers that are not answers, but it is called a warden bound to an old command rather than a rightful lord.

239.content:
Golden Troupe (also: Golden Song's Variation, Golden Bird's Shedding, Golden Era's Prelude, Golden Night's Bustle, Golden Troupe's Reward, Golden Troupe artifact set): Golden Troupe is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.0. Its five pieces tell the story of Boethius: a boy from a conquered island tribe who became a musician and Harmost of Remuria, and, after the empire's fall, the troupe that clung to the dream of its golden age. Its bonuses boost Elemental Skill damage.

The pieces are Golden Song's Variation (flower), Golden Bird's Shedding (plume), Golden Era's Prelude (sands), Golden Night's Bustle (goblet) and Golden Troupe's Reward (circlet). The set and the Golden Troupe faction share a name: this entry is the artifact set, the faction is a separate entry.

Appearance: Only names and lore text describe the pieces. The theatrical, musical and golden imagery (songs, birds, preludes, a golden dome, a theater) is the set's recurring motif.

Lore: The pieces follow Boethius: a conquered child who becomes a musician and Harmost, a rift between two Harmosts over mercy toward the tribes, the God King's failed last orders, the people turned into golems, and the faded-castle troupe waiting for the symphony to return.

Owners: No named owner; the set is narrative item text about Boethius, Cassiodor, Remus and their circle.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus is Elemental Skill DMG +20%. The 4-piece bonus is Elemental Skill DMG +25%, with a further +25% while the wearer is off the field (cleared 2s after taking the field). Obtained from the Denouement of Sin domain in Fontaine's Belleau Region, near Romaritime Harbor, and the artifact strongbox. That domain's Ley Line Disorder gives a CRIT DMG bonus whenever a character's HP rises or falls; its enemies are out-of-control clockwork meka left after an accident at the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present the set as poetic, in-universe artifacts of Remurian memory, with a sadder, more faithful tone than the set's bonuses suggest. Characters should not casually know the Golden Troupe's real methods unless they have read the relevant Faded Castle materials.

240.content: In this set Boethius is the Remurian musician who left his island tribe, gave up his name and became a Harmost. Golden Night's Bustle shows him among the rubble, speaking of treachery, and Golden Troupe's Reward ends in the troupe he is later said to have led.

241.content: The set's last piece pictures the troupe in the faded golden castle beneath the sea, mourning a perfect order and waiting with silent, famished golems to hunt innocents. Wider canon's Golden Troupe faction is covered in its own entry.

242.content:
Great Song of Khvarena (also: Great Songs of Khvarena, Great Khvarena): The Great Songs of Khvarena are five large concentrations of Khvarena, the purifying power left by the divine bird Simurgh. The Pari elder Zurvan says she fused them long ago to cleanse the land of impurity. They hold immense power, but only a Pari who has earned the Khvarena's approval can unleash it, through a special ritual. In Vourukasha Oasis's quest series, Sorush the Pari and the Traveler gather all five, and Nasejuna, leader of the Order of Skeptics, is revealed to have been using them for his own plot.

They are needed to perform the Rite of Chinvat and open a path to the Harvisptokhm, so the Sign of Apaosha in the sky can be extinguished. Whoever holds them can seal or open lands: Zurvan once used them to seal Vourukasha Oasis and the nearby ruins against the Abyss Order.

Appearance: Paimon describes them as much bigger than ordinary Khvarena motes, and "kinda cute" when one rises out of Sunyata Lake; she jokingly calls it "Great Khvarena". The Khvarena's power forms a barrier around each one.

Lore: Zurvan says that after she scattered the monsters that invaded the sea of flowers, she fused the strongest Khvarena gathered into five Great Songs to purify the land. She hid one in Sunyata Lake for a time of need, and the rest were scattered. A Pari needs the Twin-Horned Chaplet, the symbol of the Khvarena's recognition, to touch them. Sorush earns it by being acknowledged as a Bloomguard.

Owners: Fused by Zurvan (or by the first Pari, per the tutorial text), who hid one in Sunyata Lake. In the quests only Sorush, who has the Twin-Horned Chaplet, can pick them up. Nasejuna, with Klingsor and the Abyss Order, tried to take them; the Traveler and Sorush kept them and placed them at the Tunigi Hollow.

Gameplay: Quest items. The tutorial text says the Khvarena's power forms a barrier around each, that only a Pari with the Twin-Horned Chaplet can touch them, and that Sorush, with the Chaplet, may use her power to collect them. The Songs from Samudaya and Dukkha appear in inventory only once those sub-quests are started.

243.comment: Great Song of Khvarena: The Rite of Chinvat
243.content: Nasejuna says the Rite of Chinvat requires collecting the Great Songs so the Sign of Apaosha can be extinguished; Zurvan confirms the rite is real and that she once performed it alongside human heroes to cross the darkness and cleanse the mother-tree. Nasejuna's actual plan is to reverse it with the Songs and release the Abyss. Zurvan says it opens the path into the Harvisptokhm, where the separate Rite of Ab-Zohr then cleanses the tree.

244.content:
Hakushin Ring (also: Hakushin no Wa, Ring of Kitsune Saiguu): The Hakushin Ring is a catalyst that carries the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu, a kitsune of the ancient Hakushin clan who lived in Narukami's mountains and walked among humans. Its short description admits that the device is "but an impoverished vessel" for the full breadth of her thought. Its text is her fond recollection of the friends she made and a final plea.

It is a 4-star catalyst of the Amethyst series that players forge, and it belongs to the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual quest series.

Appearance: A ring-like catalyst; canon text does not describe it further than as a device that stores Saiguu's memory. Its Japanese name, Hakushin no Wa, means "ring of the Hakushin".

Lore: The speaker is the Hakushin Kitsune. She calls her life "simple and ordinary" and says she has lived it to the full, running with her agile and loveable comrades across the mountains and plains of Narukami. She hopes they will be able to run happily again once everything is over.

She remembers an oni maiden with a face as lovely as the moon, with whom she played divine music before the throne, and whose sword dance she applauded. She remembers racing the chieftain of the Yougou Tengu through the spirit mountains and, as a Hakushin, winning the contest, though she suspects the tengu let her off easy. She also remembers outwitting a bake-danuki who challenged her, making him surrender to the Shogun, and then tricking the Shogun into taking that great bake-danuki under her command. A moonlit night in the imperial garden still glows in her memory, and she hopes the Shogun will remember the motto she offered when they parted: do not be blinded, do not waver, keep walking the path you believe in. She hopes the tanuki will not hate her for her final deception.

Owners: The Kitsune Saiguu, the Hakushin of the text, is the originating figure; the physical ring is a memory-bearing device rather than a known heirloom.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst in the Amethyst series, released in Version 2.0. Base ATK 44, Energy Recharge as secondary stat. Forged from a Northlander Catalyst Billet, 50 Amethyst Lump, 50 White Iron Chunk and 500 Mora; the diagram Mask of Memories comes from completing Yougou Cleansing.

245.content: The Hakushin Ring's text is Saiguu's memory: running with her fellow kitsune, racing the tengu chieftain, outwitting a bake-danuki and the Shogun, and befriending people of many kinds, ending with a plea to a dark will to return her memory to Inazuma.

246.content:
Hamayumi (also: the shrine maiden's warbow, evil-banishing bow): Hamayumi is a four-star bow of the Amethyst series. Its text is told from a Seirai shrine maiden's point of view: she watches the bandit Ako Domeki (called Zaemon) refuse to bring her aboard the Seiraimaru, thinks of her late archery teacher, and secretly decides to use "true magic" learned on Mt. Yougou against the Electro Archon's ships. The name nods to the real hama yumi, a sacred evil-banishing bow carried by shrine maidens.

Appearance: Item text calls it a warbow and gives no description of its look.

Lore: Ako Domeki, the thief the shrine maiden knows as Zaemon, tells her to get off the Seiraimaru because women are a hindrance. His tone and the way he turns his back recall the person who taught her archery before going on campaign with the Shogun in the Cataclysm, and she reflects that had he not gone, their son would be Zaemon's age. She resolves not to let this person die. She had once secretly learned real magic on Mt. Yougou, from her Master, the tengu Reizenbou. She plans to undo the great barrier that had held for a thousand years and free the resentment of the dying violet thunderbird against the ships flying the Electro banner.

Owners: The text's speaker is a Seirai shrine maiden, read by the wiki as Asase Hibiki. Promotional material shows Yoimiya and Kujou Sara with this bow; that is presentation, not canon ownership.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star bow. Base ATK 41, secondary stat ATK 12%. Passive "Full Draw" raises Normal and Charged Attack DMG, and the bonus is doubled once the wielder's Energy is at 100%. Forged from a diagram found as a reward from Takashi's Mysterious Conch chests, on the seventh opening.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a keepsake of quiet loyalty and of choosing to protect a stubborn friend despite being told to stay behind.

247.content:
Haran Geppaku Futsu (also: Haran, Rippling Upheaval, Geppaku Futsu blade): Haran Geppaku Futsu is a celebrated sword of the Futsu school of smiths in Inazuma. It is the only surviving blade forged by the great smith Masagomaru (Futsu Masayoshi). Its name pairs "Haran", meaning turmoil or roiling waves, with the Geppaku Futsu series, of which it is the "Rippling Upheaval" blade.

Its item text is drawn from the "Anthology of Inazuman Blades" by Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa of Tatarasuna. Two Geppaku Futsu swords were made by order of the school: Hasui, the Wavespike, and Haran, the Rippling Upheaval.

Appearance: Canon text describes the school's blades rather than this sword's fittings: the Hasui blade was pale blue with a hamon like rippling water, while Haran is said to be formidable as a driving hurricane. The two blades look very similar but differ greatly in quality, in the text's account.

Lore: Two Geppaku Futsu swords were made. Hasui was forged by Futsu Minori, third-generation head of the school; its pale blue blade and water-like hamon were often seen at the waist of the Shogun's valet. It was later broken in a mortal duel to decide the fate of the oni people and sent back for reforging.

By then Minori was worn down by drink, old wounds and the lingering memory of Tatarigami, and her son Futsu Hiroyoshi, fourth-generation head, could not match her skill. The task fell to Hiroyoshi's sworn brother Futsu Masayoshi, called Masagomaru, an orphan taken in by Minori, illiterate and mute from birth. Ordered to revive Hasui's beauty, he inscribed its name as it had been before, and the reforging let the school's masterpiece re-enter the world. He named only one work of his own: Haran.

Owners: Futsu Masayoshi (Masagomaru) is the smith, not an owner. No wielder is named in the item text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword released in Version 2.6 on the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 46 with CRIT Rate as secondary stat.

248.content: The Futsu school of smiths made the Geppaku Futsu pair. Third-generation head Futsu Minori forged Hasui; her foster-son Futsu Masayoshi (Masagomaru), mute from birth, forged Haran and later taught three pupils who made the Isshin Sansaku. Her son Futsu Hiroyoshi became fourth-generation head.

249.content:
Heart of Depth (also: Ocean Conqueror, Gilded Corsage, Gust of Nostalgia, Copper Compass, Goblet of Thundering Deep, Wine-Stained Tricorne): Heart of Depth is a Hydro artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.2), also called Ocean Conqueror in the Adventurer Handbook. Its pieces show the last voyage of the Skipper's Chief Mate: a sardonic, hard-drinking exile from a gray aristocratic land, who joined a Liyue sea captain's hunt for the monster that haunted them both. The wiki names him as Parsifal.

The pieces are Gilded Corsage (flower), Gust of Nostalgia (feather), Copper Compass (sands), Goblet of Thundering Deep (goblet) and Wine-Stained Tricorne (circlet). The set text ties in with the Tales From the Waves books and the Serpent Spine weapon text.

Appearance: Sea-worn keepsakes: a corsage faded by sea-salt wind, a red feather stained by blood and brine, a bronze seaman's compass, a faded finely crafted wine cup ground down by sands in the sea's depths, and a tricorne hat thick with the smell of alcohol.

Lore: The Gilded Corsage shows the warship leaving harbour with the Skipper and the Chief Mate, who hums a shanty of his own that mocks his story: the scoundrel who gave up his family name and the witch who hunted him never reached the sea, and the step-brother who could not be an heir became head at last, 'or did he?'. The Gust of Nostalgia describes his arrival with only a slim sword and a sapphire-blue feather pinned to his mantle, the feather later stained red; at his last moment he remembers his drowned days. The Copper Compass is the Skipper's, guiding the ship over whirlpools and guiding the man whose hatred hid behind laughter; when he tries to leave, the Skipper reminds him he signed a contract aboard.

Owners: The Chief Mate, whom the wiki identifies as Parsifal, and the Skipper (the compass is his). The wiki lists Parsifal as the set's subject.

Status as of 7.1: Both men are dead; the set is background lore about events around a thousand years ago. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes this set.

250.comment: Heart of Depth: The Chief Mate
250.content: The Chief Mate of Heart of Depth is a cynical, hard-drinking exile from a gray land ruled by an aristocracy (the item text's link points to Mondstadt) who sailed under the Skipper. The wiki names him Parsifal. The texts show his drinking, his forgotten past and his blue feather, not his full story.

251.content: The Skipper is the rough, jovial captain of the great warship in the Heart of Depth texts; his real name is unknown. His compass guided the ship through whirlpools and his crew contract bound the Chief Mate. The wiki connects him to Serpent Spine and Tales From the Waves.

252.content:
Heart of the Furnace (also: Foundryman's Conjecture, Foundryman's Observation, Foundryman's Calculus, Foundryman's Magnanimity, Foundryman's Legacy): Heart of the Furnace is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Stellar Glimmer teams, released in version 7.0. Its five pieces, all titled "Foundryman's...", tell the story of a young Domovoy from Kitezhgrad: his rise at the furnace core, his secret assignment, his apprenticeship under the human scholar Aksinya and his later power as president of the Royal Energy Commission.

Each piece starts with the same comparison: something true about the furnace's heart that does not hold for people, such as warmth, the outcome of events, friendship or resolve.

Appearance: No physical appearance is described; the pieces are the personal articles of a furnace worker and later official.

Lore: The Domovoy leaves Kitezhgrad young, with a letter of recommendation, and enters the furnace core where his keen hearing and speed set him apart. Grand Duke Alvis later orders him to join a secret project and watch the others. There, in the research institute Hvergelmir, he becomes the apprentice of the silver-haired human scholar Aksinya, who places a pen in his hand and changes his life. After the old sovereign falls, he takes control of the Energy Commission. In the end he returns the pen to his teacher.

Owners: The set belongs to the Domovoy Izmaylov, who is addressed by that name in the text. No other owner is named.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star set from the Inverted Glacier domain (Everfrozen Earth, Snezhnaya). 4-piece: when the wearer triggers a Stellar Glimmer reaction or deals Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG, ATK +12% for 12s; Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by all nearby party members +50%. It works off-field, and the DMG bonus from several sets with this name does not stack.

253.comment: Heart of the Furnace: Heart of the Furnace
253.content: Artifact set whose item text narrates the life of the Domovoy Izmaylov, from Kitezhgrad's furnace core to the Royal Energy Commission and his devotion to his teacher Aksinya.

254.comment: Heart of the Furnace: Izmaylov and Alvis
254.content: In the Heart of the Furnace text, the Domovoy Alvis, Grand Duke of mining and energy in Kitezhgrad, orders the talented young Izmaylov to join a secret project. After the old court falls, Izmaylov takes the Royal Energy Commission while Alvis oversees the building of Novokitezhgrad, and the two oppose each other in council. The Magnanimity text says some believed it was an act and that only those involved knew the truth.

255.content:
Heretic's Molten Blade (also: Lone Light's Blessing, Och-Kan's blade): Heretic's Molten Blade is a 4-star sword from the Battle Pass, belonging to Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord of Ochkanatlan. A gift from the red-haired Pyro Archon, it was later turned against him.

The item text is a short tragedy: a half-dragon tyrant who was never a swordsman, a gift given at a bonfire, and a death at the hands of the crimson-eyed youth.

Appearance: Canon says only that the blade was made from smelted works of the ancient dragons and kept in a leather scabbard, with an edge that dulled from long disuse yet kept clean of dust. Keep descriptions to a well-kept, unused sword.

Lore: Och-Kan stood alone in his empty royal hall and drew a sword that had gone unused for so long its edge had dulled. He kept it spotless for decades, though he was no swordsman.

The sword had been a gift. At a bonfire after a battle, the heroes asked the red-haired Pyro Archon to judge the best weapon, and he asked Och-Kan what he wanted; the blade was made from smelted dragon works and tuned to his proportions.

Owners: Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord, is the owner. He received the blade from the red-haired Pyro Archon and died by it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Battle Pass (Gnostic Hymn, BP Bounty), Version 7.0; part of the Gnostic Hymn 3 series.

256.comment: Heretic's Molten Blade: Lone Light's Blessing
256.content: Lone Light's Blessing is the passive of the sword Heretic's Molten Blade (gameplay): an ATK bonus after an Elemental Skill that grows with the distance the wielder travels each second.

257.content:
Hilichurl Cultural Customs (also: Hilifolk Study): Hilichurl Cultural Customs is a four-volume study by Jacob Musk, a Mondstadt ecologist whom the books call the 'Poet Laureate of Hilichurlian'. It records how hilichurl tribes organise themselves, what they revere and how three tribes of Dadaupa Gorge differ. It is a field scholar's account, often condescending and incomplete.

The cover and spine carry the title 'Hilifolk Study' in the Teyvat script. The books are useful for what hilichurls are seen to do, less for why, because Musk could not speak to them.

Appearance: Four short volumes in an academic, observational tone, each headed by a topic. Vols. 1, 2 and 4 are kept in Mondstadt's library, and Vol. 3 in the Grand Master's office of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters.

Lore: Vol. 1 (social structure): hilichurl tribes are small and treated like a large family. The oldest member, the shaman, usually leads, wears a horned smiling mask and chants; but in some tribes a larger, stronger hilichurl with a horned mask takes over, which makes the tribe more aggressive. Resources seem to be shared according to need. Vol. 2 (spirituality): they worship elemental power itself rather than an Archon, and masks and body paint show a member's element. Vol. 3: the huge solitary Lawa are called 'king' but do not lead. Vol. 4: the Meaty, Sleeper and Eclipse tribes of Dadaupa Gorge show cultural diversity.

Owners: No individual owner. Copies are in Mondstadt's library and the Grand Master's office of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters. Author: Jacob Musk.

Gameplay: Game note: a four-volume collectible book collection added in version 1.0; reading is purely lore.

258.comment: Hilichurl Cultural Customs: Hilichurl Shamans and Chiefs
258.content: Per Musk, the shaman is normally the oldest member of the tribe and the tribe's parent-figure, but a stronger, larger hilichurl can replace him, after which the tribe grows more aggressive. Shamans wear horned smiling masks, carry a staff, chant to themselves and dye themselves in the colour of their element.

259.content: Lawa are very large and strong hilichurls who use elemental power to defend and strike harder. The tribe addresses them with a respectful word translating to king or chief, yet they do not lead, preferring to avoid the reverent stares of smaller hilichurls.

260.comment: Hilichurl Cultural Customs: The Dadaupa Gorge Tribes
260.content: The Meaty tribe feasts, keeps boars and has a combat arena. The Sleeper tribe sleeps in hide-bedded huts and is the most cunning. The Eclipse tribe is the most occult, worshipping a crude eclipsed-sun symbol and enthroning its strongest shaman. Described in Vol. 4.

key: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
261.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
261.content:
The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria (also: History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria, Decline and Fall of Remuria, Pulteney's history of Remuria): The author is a Fontainian historian under the first Hydro Archon, Egeria. He claims to reconstruct Remuria's true shape with "the universal rationality of history" and distrusts the folklore around it, including the claims of the Golden Troupe, who say they are Remuria's descendants. The tone is pro-Egeria and moralising: Remuria fell because its people abandoned their duties for hedonism and because Remus tried to hand divine authority to humans.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of three volumes. The cover title reads FALL OF REMURIA in the Fontaine script. In the game, Vol. 1 and Vol. 3 are sold by the NPC Hubel in the Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine, and Vol. 2 is found in the Palais Mermonia.

Lore: Vol. 1 opens with the legend that the ocean gave birth to everything and also devoured it. Heaven drowned the early peoples for turning from their fate, and the survivors lived like animals until the great king Remus descended on Meropis in his golden ship Fortuna, taught farming, built cities and temples, and spread music and art.

Heaven's first-era envoys had guided people to peace until people tired of it; Heaven then sent huge waves and a hundred days of rain. With an immortal fleet Remus conquered all the islands on the high waters, and even the great dragon beneath the abyssal depths submitted. Seers prophesied that the greatest empire would meet utter destruction, and that this is Fortuna. In answer Remus composed a symphony of prosperity from the seven-day rotation and the flowing winds, believing that if every city echoed it, they would escape fate's judgment.

Owners: No named owner. In the world it is sold in the Court of Fontaine and kept in the Palais Mermonia, so it reads as a common reference work.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 4.0; its three volumes are collected in the Court of Fontaine (Vol. 1 and Vol. 3 from the NPC Hubel, Vol. 2 in the Palais Mermonia).

262.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria: Pulteney
262.content: Pulteney is the great scholar credited in-game as the author of The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria, written in the early years of Fontaine's founding. Nothing else about him is established. He frames his work as an effort to extract Remuria's true shape with the universal rationality of history, in contrast to the legends and the Golden Troupe's distortions.

263.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria: Remus in Pulteney's history
263.content: In Pulteney's account, Remus is the great king who descended on Meropis in his golden Fortuna, taught farming, building, music and art, conquered the islands of the high waters, and built a symphony of prosperity to escape the prophesied doom. He is called universal Harmost, immortal ruler and God King. The author judges his gravest sin to be the delegating of divine power to humans.

264.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria: The Harmosts of Remuria
264.content: Remus promoted four humans of great capability to be Harmosts, partners in governing every city and removing discordant sounds. Pulteney blames this delegation for the corruption and revolts that ended Remuria. The book does not name them; other sources identify Boethius and Cassiodor among them.

265.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria: The Eternal City's layout
265.content: Vol. 2 describes the approach to the capital: the Ocean Pillars, the royal fairway, the tower with its bell that guided ships between islands, the port where Fortuna lay, the warrior city of Machimos with temples and arenas of carved rock, and finally Capitolium with its theaters and the golden palace of copper pillars. Only the best intellectuals and musicians could live in Capitolium.

266.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria: The Remurian golems in Pulteney's history
266.content: Pulteney admits that the Remurians did build terrifying golems, whose ruins can still be found in the wild. He rejects the folk story that the greatest ancient scholars trapped mortal spirits in them as magisters, and attributes the golems to the moral decay of Remuria's last days.

267.content:
Holy Lyre der Himmel (also: Holy Lyre, Barbatos's lyre, Lyre of the Heavens): The Holy Lyre der Himmel is Mondstadt's sacred lyre, said to be the instrument Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, once played. The Church of Favonius keeps it. In the Prologue the Fatui hide it, the Traveler retrieves it, and Dvalin's purified tears restore enough of its power for Venti to use it against the Stormterror's madness.

Its frame is rosewood carved with a pattern of flowing wind. By the time of the Prologue its Anemo power had run dry; restoring it takes Dvalin's own crystal tears, and it is damaged again in the final confrontation.

Appearance: A lyre with a rosewood frame carved with flowing wind patterns. Venti notes the strings still feel cool to the touch. Its repaired and damaged states are separate quest items; the damaged lyre's description says its once-clear sound has become dull, ear-piercing noise.

Lore: Mondstadt treats the Holy Lyre as Barbatos's relic. It is used in the Ludi Harpastum ceremony, and otherwise borrowing it requires signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a Community Representative. In the Prologue the Fatui hide it in a ruin; the Traveler fights through to retrieve it. Back at Angel's Share, Venti greets it with obvious nostalgia and says that although it is genuine, a thousand years have drained its Anemo power. The Traveler uses a purified teardrop crystal of Dvalin on it, partly restoring it.

Owners: Originally Barbatos's own instrument; held by the Church of Favonius in modern times. The Fatui held it briefly in the Prologue. It ends the Prologue in Barbara's custody.

268.comment: Holy Lyre der Himmel: Holy Lyre der Himmel in the Prologue
268.content: In the Prologue the Fatui take the Holy Lyre to use against Stormterror. The Traveler recovers it, restores its power with Dvalin's purified teardrop crystals, and Venti plays it to reach Dvalin. It is badly damaged in the fight and returned to the Church of Favonius, where Venti covers the damage with an illusion.

269.content:
Hunter's Path: Hunter's Path is a 5-star bow of the Sumeru series, a golden hunting bow made of precious white branches. Its description says it has felled countless wicked beasts trying to infiltrate the woods. The story is about a huntress who pursued a dark herd so long that she forgot the human tongue and became a beast herself.

The bow also appears, as a moon-white bow in the hands of a huntress, in the Light of Foliar Incision's text, tying the two weapons into one tale of the forest.

Appearance: A gilded bow of white branches containing "the blessing of the forest". The text adds that trees with such white branches are now rare and that the bow's blessings were once covered by darkened blood that water has since washed away.

Lore: A hunter pursues a dark herd in a hunt that never seems to end, waiting nights under rotten leaves and sleeping inside carcasses, always moving to the next target after the fatal arrow. She stops caring about the wind revealing her location or about camouflaging her scent with wildflowers, as her smell becomes like that of wild beasts. She forgot the human tongue before she became a hunter, and even the blind youth who first found her and gave her the white-branch bow was forgotten.

She is told that the bloodstained will never find the hunting grounds of endless viridescence, and replies that the world where barbarous beasts roam shall be her hunting grounds. Looking into clear water by moonlight, she sees that she too has turned into a wild beast. A black knight, whose form and sword are reflected in the water, follows the tracks of the beast and finds her at a loss. He says he took her for another beast to destroy, tempted by the illusory moon in the water, though for a moment he thought he saw a maiden lost in the forest, and states that he must continue west to settle the crime of twisting man into a beast's form.

Owners: No owner is named. The huntress is the only wielder in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star bow released in Version 3.0 (2022-08-24), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT Rate. Passive At the End of the Beast-Paths grants All Elemental DMG Bonus and, after the wielder hits with a Charged Attack, the Tireless Hunt effect, which raises Charged Attack DMG by a percentage of Elemental Mastery for 12 Charged Attacks or 10 s; it can be gained once every 12 s.

key: Husk of Opulent Dreams artifact set
270.content:
Husk of Opulent Dreams (also: Husk of Opulent Dreams artifact set, Bloom Times, Plume of Luxury, Song of Life, Calabash of Awakening, Skeletal Hat): Husk of Opulent Dreams is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set that tells, in dream-like fragments, the life of a puppet made to hold a "heart": the figure once known as Scaramouche, Sixth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers (the Balladeer), who now goes by the Wanderer. It is a defence and Geo-damage set.

It is dropped by the Slumbering Court domain on Seirai Island, and came with Version 2.3. The texts follow the puppet from creation and abandonment, through the faces and names he tried on, to the stage name he chose for himself, with the theme that he is still living out a story whose ending is not written.

Lore: The pieces read as snapshots of a wanderer: a vessel made for a heart and left to sleep, a gold ornament of the Shogun's, a young traveller turned away by a rain, and a name taken from the villains of Inazuma's theatre.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not lore: the 2-piece bonus is DEF +30%. The 4-piece bonus grants "Curiosity" stacks: on the field, a stack per Geo attack (once per 0.3s); off the field, a stack every 3s; each of up to 4 stacks gives 6% DEF and 6% Geo DMG Bonus, and a stack drops after 6 seconds without gaining one. It drops from the Slumbering Court domain.

271.comment: Husk of Opulent Dreams: The puppet and the Shogun's gold ornament
271.content: In the Husk of Opulent Dreams texts, the wanderer is never named, but he is a puppet made to hold a "heart", has been a Lord Harbinger, lived at Tatarasuna, and carries a gold ornament that the Shogun gave as proof of identity. The texts describe his name "Kunikuzushi" as one he chose from Inazuman theatre, in which the name belongs to schemers who bring down states. The Raiden Shogun's voice-over line "About Kunikuzushi" and the Wishes quest are the wiki's cited corroboration.

272.comment: Husk of Opulent Dreams: Tatarasuna and the Kabukimono years
272.content: The Plume of Luxury recalls moonlit nights over Tatarasuna and its furnace fires. Wiki summary pages on Mikoshi Nagamasa say a puppet found in the Shakkei Pavilion was introduced to the workers at Tatarasuna and welcomed as one of them under the name "Kabukimono", though the artifact texts do not use that name. Treat the link as wiki-derived rather than stated in the item text.

273.content:
Hydro Gnosis (also: Fontaine's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Hydro Archon, Hydro Archon's Gnosis): Fontaine's Gnosis, the chess-piece-like divine focus of the Hydro Archon. Focalors, the real Archon, hid inside the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale with it while Furina played the god in public for some 500 years. After Focalors's execution (4.2) it passed to Neuvillette, who gave it to the Harbinger Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift".

He let it go because it had "lost all meaning" for Fontaine and because Skirk warned him it was the remains of the Third Descender, an object of "misfortune".

Appearance: A gleaming chess-piece shape like the other Gnoses; its crown resembles an inverted fleur-de-lis.

Lore: In 4.0 Lyney revealed that the Tsaritsa had let Arlecchino use its power first, to try to break the prophecy. In 4.1 Arlecchino recalled ambushing Furina in disguise, sensing no Gnosis on her and only real terror, and concluded the Archon was not what she seemed. In 4.2 Focalors told Neuvillette she had "become one" with the Oratrice, taking Fontaine's Gnosis with her.

Owners: Focalors, then briefly Neuvillette (who says he does not need its power), then Arlecchino, then the Tsaritsa.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is in Snezhnaya, one of the six Gnoses the Tsaritsa holds.

In 7.1 she used all six as nodes of a field that, amplifying her Cryo power, slowed time around Rhinedottir. The Third Descender's seal in Zapolyarny Palace is still unopened.

Gameplay: Gameplay: a story object only; it cannot be obtained or used.

274.content: After the prophecy was averted (Finale, 4.2), Neuvillette gave Fontaine's Gnosis to the Harbinger Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift". Publicly it could pass as gratitude: the Fatui had helped at Poisson and Childe had helped hold back the All-Devouring Narwhal. Privately, Neuvillette judged that the Gnosis was meaningless to Fontaine now that the throne was gone, that the Fatui would otherwise keep pursuing it, and that it was dangerous to keep after Skirk called it the remains of the Third Descender.

275.comment: Hydro Gnosis: Arlecchino's hunt for the Hydro Gnosis
275.content: In Calamitous Tread (4.1), Arlecchino pressed Furina at a tea party about the Oratrice and the Indemnitium it had stored. The quest also shows, in Arlecchino's recollection, how she had earlier approached Furina in disguise while Furina was chasing a stray cat, and struck at her to see whether she carried the Gnosis. She did not, and her terror was genuine, so Arlecchino left.

276.content:
Hymn of the Maelstrom: Hymn of the Maelstrom is a 5-star catalyst, an exquisite lamp of blue chalcedony that looks like a treasure from a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside. Its text is a fairy tale a storyteller tells a young Water Imp about a child born of the waves. Added in Version 7.1.

The tale ends as a warning to the Water Imps to sing only for those who truly understand their song. The lamp's design and name are not tied to a character in canon.

Appearance: Canon describes only an exquisite lamp crafted out of blue chalcedony. The tale mentions silk, golden robes and agate in the prince's gifts and a sacred artifact brought by the sisters, but the text does not say that artifact is this lamp.

Lore: A young Water Imp who sings alone keeps close a fairy tale from her youth: a child born of the breaking waves, nobler than the daughters of the sea, whose voice made mariners sink into whirlpools and thawed frozen seas.

She followed a prince of the land despite her sisters' warnings and her father's call to stay in the sea, sang only for him, and was cherished like a jewel in a jewel-box palace. Her voice grew harsh, she could no longer sing the ancient hymns, and the prince grieved only that she had lost her worth.

Owners: Canon names no owner. The text is about a Water Imp and her tale, not about a possessor.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star catalyst with base ATK 44 and an HP secondary stat. Rondo of Slumber raises Healing Bonus and, after the wielder heals, grants Max HP and a party ATK buff that scales with Max HP above 40,000; Frozen or Stellar Swirl reactions by a nearby party member raise the bonuses further, and the effect works off-field. It was on the weapon event Wish Epitome Invocation (2026-09-23 to 2026-10-13).

key: Prayer Songs of the Frostmoon Scions
277.content:
Hymns of the Far North (also: Hymns of the Far North (I), Prayer Songs of the Frostmoon Scions): The collection preserves the Scions' pre-Aila religion, which prayed to the gods of the far north with offerings and divination, and shows how Aila, five centuries ago, abolished or simplified those rites around the Frost Moon. Its tone is reverent and sorrowful: the singers are exiled heirs of Hyperborea who cannot go home while the moon is imprisoned.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of three volumes with a verse opening, then numbered Prayer Songs. Each song gives the god's name, a parenthetical description of the rite (date, offerings, how many times the Runo is chanted), the hymn, and a note from Priestess Ehrnrooth. Some lines are blacked out.

Lore: The singer of the opening hymn is an exile who cannot return home while the moon is imprisoned. The numbered Prayer Songs address northern gods at solstices, births and funerals, beginning with Pitkamoonen, Lord of the Seven Calamities, then Maadteraahka, Tuonetar and Laimelea; Vol. 2 and 3 include Ianikuinen, Koitar, Saarelainen, Huurrekuutar and the Moon Maiden Kuutar. Ehrnrooth's notes explain how Aila replaced them with short prayers to the Frost Moon.

Owners: No owner. Compiled by Priestess Ehrnrooth of the Frostmoon Scions; the volumes lie near the Meeting Point in the Frostmoon Enclave, where she is found.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a 3-volume Book Collection in Nod-Krai, near the Meeting Point at the Frostmoon Enclave; Vol. 1 appears after the Enclave is upgraded to level 5.

278.comment: Hymns of the Far North: Aila's reform of the Frostmoon rites
278.content: In Ehrnrooth's notes, Aila, the first Moonchanter, abolished the old rites to the Seven Calamities, the Mother of Life and the Mother of the Underworld five centuries ago, replacing them with brief blessings such as "May the new moon illuminate your path". She revised and simplified the prayers to Ianikuinen, Koitar, Saarelainen and Huurrekuutar into short forms addressed to the pale white Frost Moon, which are now the standard recitation.

279.comment: Hymns of the Far North: Prayer Song of the Lord of the Seven Calamities
279.content: The first prayer song, performed at the summer solstice, begs a merciless sky god to turn from the mortal realm. Its offerings include grain, a hen and an ox. Portions of its text are blacked out because the Archpriestess chanted indistinctly so as not to provoke the god. The wiki identifies the god as the Heavenly Principles.

280.comment: Hymns of the Far North: Saarelainen's prayer and the daughter of Pakkaisukko
280.content: Prayer Song XVI honors Saarelainen, a gentle noble who rode across Hiisi Island and Pohjola to court Pakkaisukko's daughter. Pakkaisukko demanded he open the gates of Pohjola. Saarelainen went knowingly, to spare the girl, and the Lord of the Seven Calamities cut him into seven pieces. The wiki links Pakkaisukko to the Belyi Tsar and his daughter to Anastasya; the hymn does not name them.

281.comment: Hymns of the Far North: Frostmoon Scions' prayer to the Frost Moon
281.content: Prayer Song XXI honors Huurrekuutar, goddess of the Frost Moon, "mother of the silver shuttle" who leads lost souls through the cold night, and Song XXII addresses Kuutar, the Moon Maiden, asking her to cleanse sins and the tears of those barred from Elysium. The standard form beseeches the pale white Frost Moon to cast down its gaze from the celestial dome.

282.content:
Jadefall's Splendor (also: Jadefalls Splendor, Bìluò zhī Lóng): Jadefall's Splendor is a five-star catalyst and a ritual vessel carved from jade, reflecting the luster of the skies and clear waters. Its item story says jadeite fell from the sky, was washed clean and was shaped by mortal hands into a splendid instrument awaiting its sacred purpose. The rest of the text is a tea-table debate between a scholar from Sumeru and a consultant in dark robes about whether history bends toward decay or rebirth, framed by the story of Chenyu Vale's ancestors.

It belongs to the Primordial Jade series, though it is the later entry with a different focus. The text ends with the Bishui River flowing eternal and the jade's luster as constant as its former master.

Lore: The story opens with jadeite that fell from the sky, was cleansed by water, freed of dark earth and rotten wood, and shaped by a mortal youth into a ritual instrument. A researcher from the rainforest realm of Sumeru then argues over tea that history bends toward decay: the fall of humanity can only be stopped by the wisdom and mercy of gods, and he points to deserted ruins and hilichurls without speech or spirit as proof that earlier peoples vanished without a ripple.

Owners: Item text names no owner beyond a "former master" (read by the wiki as Morax) and a mortal youth who shaped the jade. No source consulted ties it to a particular playable character.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star catalyst from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat HP 10.8%. Passive "Primordial Jade Regalia": for 3 seconds after an Elemental Burst or creating a shield, the wielder restores 4.5-6.5 Energy every 2.5 seconds and gains an Elemental DMG Bonus of 0.3-1.1% per 1,000 Max HP, up to 12-44%, even off the field (refinements 1 to 5).

283.content:
Kagotsurube Isshin (also: Cursed Blade, Prized Isshin Blade (reforged), Kagotsurube): Kagotsurube Isshin is a long blood-red sword bearing the Isshin name. It was forged by Akame Kanenaga, an Inazuman smith of the fallen Akame school, but made in a snowbound land to the far north rather than in Inazuma, and its journey home was marked by dark deeds. It figures in Kaedehara Kazuha's Story Quest, where the possessed sword is finally reforged and the player receives it.

Its description says it is remarkably sharp and vividly ominous, able to cleave a porous bamboo basket and the water within it before any leaks. The name is taken from Kagotsurube, a haunted sword in a kabuki play whose blade is said to leave no drop of blood on its edge.

Appearance: A long blade the colour of blood. Its hamon, seen in moonlight, appears to flow like the blood and tears of a wayfaring wanderer. In the story it appears first as a menacing blade wreathed in an ominous purple aura (the Prized Isshin Blade), then shattered, and finally as the reforged sword.

Lore: The text says people often think each blade holds a blade-spirit; a sword forged by the Tatarigami would then hold a demon of malice. Akame Kanenaga was a swordsmith who failed to become head smith. He made this blade in a snow-covered northern land, not in the land of thunder and Jade Steel.

The Akame school, in its zealous practice of "Isshin" (the stillness of mind free of distraction), had always sought a killer blade of extreme lethality. Its members grew withdrawn and venomous, and the authorities came to regard the school as undesirable: leadership of the Isshin Art, passed down from Mitsunaga, was rescinded before three generations had passed.

Owners: Akame Kanenaga forged it. After the Story Quest, Kazuha holds the reforged sword.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword obtained from the Story Quest A Strange and Friendless Road in Version 2.8; it has a single refinement rank. Base ATK 42 with ATK% as secondary stat. It was announced under the working name "Cursed Blade", which the game never uses.

284.content: The Akame school pursued the Isshin Art's ideal of a distraction-free mind by forging killer blades of extreme lethality; their works were keen but carried an evil that led the authorities to rescind the school's leadership of the Isshin Art within three generations. Akame Kanenaga, a later member, fled north after the Case of the Eccentric and forged Kagotsurube Isshin there.

285.content:
Kagura's Verity (also: Kagura no Shin'i, Yae Miko's kagura bells, Kagura bells): Kagura's Verity is the set of bells used for the Kagura Dance, blessed by Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, and still carrying the scent of the Sacred Sakura. Its item text is Yae's voice, looking back on her long friendship with Ei and the people and spirits she has met across her life.

The Kagura bells are a short staff with tiered bells used in Shinto kagura dance. In-universe, the text says that where there were once dances before the throne, the sound of the bells still lingers.

Appearance: A staff of tiered bells in the style of a kagura suzu, with the bells glowing in turn as the weapon's passive stacks up (top bells at one stack, top and bottom at two, the full weapon and a particle effect at three). The description adds that the scent of the Sacred Sakura clings to it.

Lore: The text opens with the white silhouette of the past, which never returned and remains an unceasing dream. In Yae's recollection she was a silly little thing, nowhere near as clever as the great matriarch Hakushin. As a whelp foraging through snow she tried to catch Ei's attention; her foolhardy courage earned Ei's pity and she entered her service, warming her hands and feet, a "very great honor".

When Saiguu departed never to return and her seniors were lost for various reasons, the clumsy Yae took up the role of Miko. The unfortunate task of putting a smile on Ei's face fell to her. On the night she first performed the Kagura Dance she felt the weight of the past. The text then says the great silver kitsune, master and friend, vanished into the river of dreams; the daughter of the great kitsune lineage would take up the bells and dance for the vibrant "now".

Owners: Yae Miko is the blesser and voice of the text. The bells are tied to the Guuji's duties at the Grand Narukami Shrine.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst in the Inazuma series released in Version 2.5 on the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 46 with CRIT DMG as secondary stat.

286.content:
Kamera (also: Kamera gadget, Kamera Gadgets, Fontainian Kamera): The Kamera is a photographic device that records a picture at the press of a button and prints it on paper. Canon calls it a special item from Fontaine. In Liyue the Feiyun Commerce Guild imports it as a novelty, and the Traveler receives one as thanks for a small errand.

Xu of the Feiyun Commerce Guild enjoyed it so much that the Guild offered free portraits as a trial, then took small fees for house calls. Several later quests and events use differently equipped Kameras.

Appearance: In the inventory it is a four-star gadget. Its in-game description calls it a convenient tool that records and saves images, and says a Traveler roaming the world will have plenty of people and places worth remembering. Pictures come out printed on paper. The wiki's trivia compares its look to a twin-lens reflex camera, which is an out-of-universe observation.

Lore: Xu, a member of the Feiyun Commerce Guild at Liyue Harbor, says the Guild recently imported a new product from Fontaine, reportedly very popular there. You press a button and an image appears on a piece of paper. He enjoys it a great deal, and the Guild's young master is convinced it will sell well.

Because this would be the first sale of the device in Liyue, the Guild ran a trial in which citizens could have a free photograph taken. It was well received, people offered to pay for the Kamera to be brought to them, and some wanted their pictures framed and delivered. Demand grew daily while the young master was away for several days.

Owners: The Traveler holds a Kamera from the Snapshots quest. Paimon also has her own, which appears in later events. Many variants are loaned or given to the Traveler for specific quests or events (see the variants entry).

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not in-world fact). The Kamera is a reusable Quick Use gadget with no cooldown, obtained from the Liyue world quest Snapshots (Adventure Rank 25 required). Using it takes an instant picture of the current screen that can then be saved or discarded. It works in moments when Photo Mode is unavailable, including while Elemental Sight is active, during combat, gliding, falling and swimming, so it can catch actions such as combat talents. It lacks Photo Mode's camera, expression and pose adjustments and cannot be used in Domains.

287.content: A Liyue world quest, started by talking to Xu at Feiyun Slope near the northern waypoint of Liyue Harbor, for Adventure Rank 25 and above. The Traveler delivers two Kamera Pictures to Granny Shan and Tea Master Liu Su and reports back. The reward is 20,000 Mora, two Hero's Wit and a Kamera.

288.content: The wiki groups many reusable gadgets as Kamera Gadgets. Some are tied to the event that released them and expire with it. Examples from item text: the Kurious Kamera and Special Kamera (1.3, Fontainian models; the former, used for the Five Flushes of Fortune event, was imported by Ji Tong but does not seem to work as expected); the Exquisite Kamera (3.0), which Razi borrowed from Lord Sangemah Bay in the Graven Innocence event; the Windblume Kamera (3.5), borrowed from Fassben; Bresson's Special Kamera (4.0), a custom-built model made from the best materials; the Image Sampling Kamera (4.2), modified by Lepine-Pauline for a "Graph Adversarial Technology" task; Asagiri's Dedicated Fontaine Kamera (4.8), for gathering inspiration on a trip to Fontaine; the Graffiti Kamera (5.0); the Forensic Imaging Device (5.8), which compares past and present data to find clues; and the MAAN-Kamera (7.0), provided by Chichikova for the Mutual Aid Advancement Network.

289.content:
Katsuragikiri Nagamasa (also: Daitatara Nagamasa, Nagamasa's nagamaki): Katsuragikiri Nagamasa is a four-star claymore, a tough, simple nagamaki-style blade designed by Mikoshi Nagamasa, an inspector of Tatarasuna. It was originally named the Daitatara Nagamasa. After he used it to execute his own subordinate Katsuragi, the sword and its owner's title were renamed for that act.

Appearance: Item text calls it a nagamaki sword whose design is as simple and upright as the inspector himself, and a tough, simple sword. There is no further description of its look.

Lore: The item story says the sword was designed by Tatarasuna's inspector, who was for a time obsessed with the grim beauty of steel and consulted the similarly inclined Vice Armory Officer Miyazaki. Nagamasa was only the foster son of the Mikoshi clan. His foster mother had stained the clan's name and the legitimate heir, Michihiro, had abandoned him and disappeared, yet his loyalty made him cherish the Mikoshi name. When his yoriki Katsuragi was connected with a single trace of misconduct, he had him executed without mercy, and from then on the sword's name and his title were changed.

Owners: Mikoshi Nagamasa (historical.mikoshi-nagamasa) designed and used it. No other owner is named in the item text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star claymore. Base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10%. Passive "Samurai Conduct" (shared with Kitain Cross Spear): raises Elemental Skill DMG, and after a skill hits an opponent the wielder loses 3 Energy but regains Energy every 2s for 6s (once per 10s), even off-field. Forged from a diagram found in a chest in Tatarasuna's arsenal.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the blade suits stories about duty against loyalty and the cost of defending a family name.

290.content:
Key of Khaj-Nisut: The Key of Khaj-Nisut is a 5-star sword of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it one of a paired set of scepters fashioned from obsidian, said to work as a key to the gate of a paradise at the end of the ocean of sand. Its story follows a hidden prince, later called Xiphos, and the aged blind poet who served and then freed him.

The name Khaj-Nisut comes from ancient Egyptian words for "the appearance of the king", the coronation of a pharaoh (wiki etymology note). The sword is the partner of the Staff of the Scarlet Sands.

Appearance: Described as a black sword (the poet strokes "the dull blade of the black sword") and as a scepter of obsidian. Canon text gives no further detail.

Lore: The story is set after the Lord of Sand's dreams fell apart and the Grandmaster of Verdure hid away the whispers of the demonic skies. A queen of one of the many kingdoms that arose from the broken realm burned her little prince's gilded robes and crown and sent him away in a servant's sackcloth. He grew up as the son of one who ruled the slave markets and then became a wanderer who had lost everything. His last master was a blind poet.

The poet, who once advised an overlord and blessed the former king's son at birth, is now blind, and takes the prince as an apprentice to be his eyes. The prince recalls his mother's words that they would meet again in the "eternal oasis"; he should use the sword as the key to the paradise's gate. The poet names him Xiphos, the Jinni's favourite, and sends him to wander the failing kingdoms.

Owners: Named in the text: the prince Xiphos, who wields it as his key, and before him his master the blind poet. Legend adds mortal tyrants and kings in between.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star sword released in Version 3.1 (2022-10-14), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat HP%. Passive Sunken Song of the Sands raises HP; hitting with an Elemental Skill grants Grand Hymn stacks (up to 3) that give the wielder Elemental Mastery based on Max HP, and at 3 stacks nearby party members gain Elemental Mastery based on the wielder's Max HP. It works only while the wielder is on the field.

291.content:
Kitain Cross Spear (also: Kitain's cross spear, Kitain Bunsou's spear): Kitain Cross Spear is a four-star polearm: a strangely shaped, very heavy spear made by Kitain Bunsou for his own style of spearmanship. Item text says it is unwieldy for the untrained but destructive in expert hands. The Kitain family had long hunted the Tatarigami and served as the Prefects of Yashiori Island.

Appearance: Item text calls the spear strangely shaped and massive. The wiki's trivia says its design is probably a reference to the cross spears of the Houzouin-ryuu, a real Japanese martial art school; that is a design note, not canon.

Lore: The spear's weight makes it extremely unwieldy for the untrained, but in an expert's hands it can unleash great destructive power. The text says the Kitain family hunted the Tatarigami for many generations and held the office of Prefect of Yashiori Island.

Owners: Maker and user: Kitain Bunsou (historical.kitain-bunsou). The text gives no later owner. Thoma is shown wielding it in official art, which is presentation and not a claim of ownership.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star polearm. Base ATK 44, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 24. Passive "Samurai Conduct" (shared with Katsuragikiri Nagamasa): raises Elemental Skill DMG, and after a skill hits an opponent the wielder loses 3 Energy but regains Energy every 2s for 6s (once per 10s), even off-field. Forged from a diagram given on completing Orobashi's Legacy: Part V.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a fitting prop for an old guardian family whose long duty has left a mark on them.

292.content:
La Chanson d'Erinnyes (also: Chanson d'Erinnyes, The Song of Erinnyes): The text is a fragment of a longer work: it quotes chapters 6 and 20 and refers to earlier episodes such as Otkerus of Rhenanie's battle against a venom-breathing dragon. Remus's emissary is Cassiodor, called Vivarium's heir. The book presents the Lochknights as loyal only to Egeria and the Capitoliani as liars, so it is a partisan, Fontainian legend.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of three volumes. Each volume begins with a chapter and part number and a one-line summary, then verse-like lines with a repeated formal style. Vol. 1 and Vol. 3 are found on the upper floor of Lumidouce Harbor, and Vol. 2 is sold by Hubel.

Lore: Vol. 1: A musician sent by King Remus arrives at Aremori Castle during Erinnyes's victory feast and demands water and earth as tribute and submission to the Sumphonia Capitolii, the eternal harmony. Erinnyes forbids harm to him and answers that her people bend the knee only to the Mistress of Many Waters.

In Vol. 1 Erinnyes has just defeated the princes of Bellouacoi, Atrebatis and Uiromanduoi and accepted their allegiance, hence eight days of feasting. Sir Guillaume of Gellone draws his sword Narbonnais in anger, and Knights Blancandrin and Marsile too. The emissary answers with threats of war, hunger and plague and says Remus acts out of pity.

Vol. 2: Another knight, Drest, Prince of Lyonnais, and his companion Adsiltia, whose name means daughter of ice, call Vivarium's heir a liar and a traitor. Other knights, including Naimes and Tulpin, add their swords. Erinnyes thanks them and tells the emissary that her people are bound to no monarch, because the Mistress of Many Waters has given them all equal honour, and that she will lead the blessed army to destroy the white dragon and the grand city. She orders Sir Fierabras to prepare gifts for him and has him escorted back to Carubdis Castle.

Owners: No named owner. It is a legend preserved in books, with Vol. 2 sold by Hubel in the Court of Fontaine.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 4.2; Vol. 1 and Vol. 3 are collected on the upper floor of Lumidouce Harbor, Vol. 2 is bought from Hubel.

293.comment: La Chanson d'Erinnyes: Erinnyes in the Chanson
293.content: In La Chanson d'Erinnyes she is a wise, merciful leader of the Lochknights who answers Remus with loyalty to Egeria alone, rallies the knights of every region, and at the end gives up her blade Hauteclaire and disappears. Her own entity file has her history; here only the epic's portrayal is recorded.

294.content: Hauteclaire, Sword of Light, is the name Erinnyes gives her blade in Vol. 3. She throws it into the lake three times; twice it returns, and the third time it sinks. The book says Daeira, a maiden of the lake, gave it to the chief of knights and that it won battles at Peiregord and against Aisias.

295.content: In the Chanson the emissary of King Remus is a lone musician with a golden-tipped fasces and a horse, who demands water and earth from Erinnyes and threatens war. The knights name him Vivarium's heir. Other sources identify the Harmost Cassiodor as this figure, but the book does not name him.

296.comment: La Chanson d'Erinnyes: The knights of the Chanson
296.content: Named knights in the epic include Sir Guillaume of Gellone, who wields the sacred blade Narbonnais, Knights Blancandrin and Marsile, Drest Prince of Lyonnais, the lady Adsiltia of the azure sail, Naimes, Tulpin, Fierabras, and Sir Agricane, who speaks before Vol. 2. Otkerus of Rhenanie is recalled as a righteous knight who fought a venom-breathing dragon. Little else is given about any of them.

297.content:
Lavawalker (also: Lavawalker's Resolution, Lavawalker's Salvation, Lavawalker's Torment, Lavawalker's Epiphany, Lavawalker's Wisdom): Lavawalker is a Pyro-resistance artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its five pieces tell of the Lavawalker, a proud sage who wore a flame-flower brooch, a crimson agate circlet and a phoenix feather, walked onto the burning sea of the Mare Jivari and was never seen again. In Natlan, the Abyss Lector Enjou is linked to the name.

The pieces are Lavawalker's Resolution (flower), Salvation (feather), Torment (hourglass), Epiphany (goblet) and Wisdom (circlet). The set is found in the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula.

Lore: Lavawalker's Wisdom says the sage crafted a crimson agate circlet to resist the flames, and that his skill sparked fear and jealousy among peers and seniors, one of whom, his teacher, called it blasphemy and demanded he step into the flaming sea. He walked calmly onto the lava and vanished. Lavawalker's Resolution is his brooch: before the end he told his people they would see the flower's embers shining through dark smoke, and they followed its light to the edge of the Mare Jivari, finding flowers but not the sage. Lavawalker's Salvation is a feather he took from a solitary fire-bird revered as a totem and a sign of nobility; wearing it he withdrew from the world, and since then cries are heard over the Mare Jivari, which no one can tell from the bird's song or his sighs.

Owners: The set texts name only the Lavawalker. The 5.8 world quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc connects the title to Enjou, an Abyss Lector who gives the Traveler a keepsake called Lavawalker's Resolution using the same words as the set text.

298.content: The Lavawalker is the sage of the artifact set's texts, who crossed the burning Mare Jivari, was resented by his teacher and peers, and disappeared leaving a flower, a feather, a circlet and a goblet behind. The set never gives his name.

299.content:
Legend of the Lone Sword (also: Jin the Seventy-Second): Legend of the Lone Sword is a four-volume martial arts novel that sells well in Liyue Harbor. Its blurb stresses that the story takes place in a world without elemental energy or alchemy, so swordsmanship is purely physical skill and nerve.

It follows Jin the Seventy-Second, last survivor of a 72-member sword school, as he hunts the swordsman who destroyed it. It is fiction, not Liyue history.

Appearance: Each volume is a short book with a one-line in-game blurb. Vol. 1 is at Wanwen Bookhouse (and in front of Verr Goldet at Wangshu Inn), Vol. 2 on a table behind a vegetable stand in Qingce Village, Vol. 3 on Su Er'niang's stall in Liyue Harbor, and Vol. 4 is sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse.

Lore: - Vol. 1: Three days after his master and junior were killed in the snow, a starving, wounded man walks home in the rain. He calls himself Jin the Seventy-Second because he is the last of 72. He kills a cart driver who answers him with riddles, and rides the cart to Tupi Village.
- Vol. 2: At Tupi Village, a feared chief with red eyes awaits him. Jin, bound by no school or sect, slaughters the chief's followers, counting exactly 362 men and one gate dog, then enters the mansion.
- Vol. 3: Jin duels the chief. The text says the world has no elements, so the dead leave no lingering memories and swordsmanship cannot be elemental. Jin wins through "heart" and an incense burner held in his empty hand, and learns his enemy is in the barren mountains beyond.
- Vol. 4: Wounded, Jin crosses the barren mountains, which legend says were carved by the Celestial Emperor's blade and made salty by the Earth Mother's tears. Two watchers, an old crone and a stout old man, debate attacking him. He collapses and glimpses azure-blue skirts.

Owners: No in-game owner. It is a sold and displayed collectible.

Gameplay: Game note: a four-volume book collection added in version 1.0 (quality 4 in the wiki infobox).

300.comment: Legend of the Lone Sword: Jin the Seventy-Second
300.content: Jin the Seventy-Second is the protagonist of the Liyue novel Legend of the Lone Sword, the last of 72 members of a sword school destroyed by a rival swordsman. He is a fictional character, not a figure of Liyue history.

301.content:
Light of Foliar Incision: Light of Foliar Incision is a 5-star sword of the Sumeru series, a gilded blade made from precious white branches.
