Its description says it was once used to destroy countless poisons that infested the forest. The story follows an exiled prince from the golden desert who is spared by a huntress in Dharma Forest and told to break off a pale branch.

The sword is the blade counterpart of the bow Hunter's Path: both are made from the pale branches of the forest, and the huntress with the "moon-white bow" appears in this text.

Appearance: A gilded blade of white branches. Canon text gives no other physical detail.

Lore: A wanderer from the land of gold, once a prince, whose body and mind are scarred by battle, is lost in the green maze of the forest. The ancient forest king, tasting the scent of blood stemming from authority, sighs and summons a huntress with a moon-white bow to hunt the beast that has come from beyond the woods.

Death whispers through the maze following the exile; a curse spreads across the desert sands behind him. The huntress finds him by his strange scent, warns him that she has already struck him with one arrow and that the next will find his heart, and tells him the crown he seeks is not here and that he must not disturb the dreams of the children. Yet she lowers her bow and deliberately misses. The Aranara, the dream-hidden children, breathe out as no blood is spilled.

Owners: In the story, the exiled prince Faramarz is the one rumoured to have forged a blade from the pale branch; the wiki calls him its creator and wielder.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star sword released in Version 3.4 (2023-01-18), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT DMG. Passive Whitemoon Bristle increases CRIT Rate and, after Normal Attacks deal Elemental DMG, grants the Foliar Incision effect, increasing Normal Attack and Elemental Skill DMG by a percentage of Elemental Mastery for 28 hits or 12 s; it can be gained once every 12 s.

302.content:
Lightbearing Moonshard (also: Legacy of Lang-Gan): Lightbearing Moonshard is a five-star sword added in Version 6.3 (Luna IV). Its description calls it a legendary blade forged from glimmering moonlight gathered in a well by an adeptus hidden among clear springs, its true form revealed only where dusk meets dawn. The item story is a Liyue legend about a girl of the mining tribes who seeks that adeptus and the sword that could save her people's ancient kingdom.

Appearance: The text gives no physical description of the blade beyond "glimmering moonlight" and a form that only shows at dusk and dawn. The sword is associated with moonlit water, a silvery shadow in a spring and half-formed phantoms behind bamboo curtains. Do not invent a hilt or blade design.

Lore: At dusk a girl in climbing sandals reaches the hidden spring of a forgotten tomb that appears in no chronicle. She has followed a tale told only among the mining tribes, of an adeptus who forged swords from flowing light and then vanished into the watery moon beneath the depths. In the spring a silver shadow answers her with soft laughter.

The legend she carries is the history of Lang-Gan, a western-coast kingdom older than Mt. Tianheng, where people honoured a heavenly being who taught them to farm and weave. A blazing comet then fell from the east and the heavens, sea and earth were ruined, so that the people perished. In her own day, a mighty dragon who once stood with the Lord of Geo has been struck by sudden ruin and tramples human lands; the mountain folk take up their ancestors' weapons and follow the Yaksha under the Lord of Geo's banner.

Owners: No owner is named. The legend says the girl sought the sword, but the text never says she obtained or wielded it, only that she understood its essence.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore. The passive Legacy of Lang-Gan raises DEF and, for a short time after the wielder uses an Elemental Skill, increases damage from Lunar-Crystallize reactions. Base ATK 44; secondary stat CRIT DMG. Obtained from Weapon Event Wishes; featured in Version 6.3's second half.

303.comment: Lightbearing Moonshard: Lang-Gan (kingdom in the sword legend)
303.content: In the Lightbearing Moonshard text, Lang-Gan was an ancient kingdom on the western coast, older than Mt. Tianheng, honoured by a heavenly being and ruined when a comet fell and the sea and earth collapsed. The girl of the mining tribes finds its remnants hidden in caverns. See the location entry for Lang-Gan for other sources.

304.content:
Lion's Roar: Lion's Roar is a 4-star sword of the Kunwu series, a sharp blade with extravagant carvings that does not compromise on durability and sharpness and that roars like a lion as it cuts the air. It is rumoured to be a legendary sword of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Its text tells how the craftsman Kunwu forged it in one day and then carved a sheath for it over a year, and how the sheath was lost.

Appearance: Extravagant carvings. The lost sheath was said to be eaglewood decorated with mica and engraved with war imagery. Do not invent the blade's colour.

Lore: The blade is so sharp that its victims realise they have been struck only an hour later.

Kunwu is said to have forged it in a day, working through the day and night. When his aged master saw the work he clenched his fists, sighed and struck the ground with his staff, calling it a pitiful thing, merciless in all the world.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. Keqing is shown wielding it in cutscenes (the Turning Point and Where the Heart Finds Rest quests, her demo) and in promotional art, which is a cameo and not an ownership claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 42, ATK% secondary stat (9 per cent). Passive Bane of Fire and Thunder: increases DMG against opponents affected by Pyro or Electro by 20 to 36 per cent by refinement. A Kunwu series weapon, shared with the 4-Star Bane series (see Dragon's Bane).

305.content: Kunwu is the legendary master craftsman named in the item texts of Lion's Roar, Dragon's Bane and Solar Pearl. In Lion's Roar he is shown as an apprentice whose master was dismayed by the sword he made, and later as an artisan who spent a year on its sheath.

306.content:
Lithic Blade: Lithic Blade is a 4-star claymore of the Lithic series, a greatsword carved and chiselled from the very bedrock of Liyue. The Millelith of old favoured it, but it is so heavy that no ordinary human can lift it. It was added in Version 1.3.

Its text ties the blade to the Millelith, the armed force first founded at the initiative of Rex Lapis' followers, and to their code about stone and guardians.

Appearance: A plain stone greatsword; canon describes only that it is carved from bedrock. Do not invent decoration.

Lore: It is made of the divine bedrock upon which Liyue Harbor was established, and it is incomparably heavy; records say the Millelith of old wielded it with ease.

The Millelith was founded on the initiative of the followers of Rex Lapis, and its history goes back to when the port city was first completed. They march under Rex Lapis' and Liyue's banner and their code is: while rock stays hard, the mountain shall never fail; while the Millelith stands guard, evil shall never prevail.

Owners: No individual owner is named. The text attributes use to the Millelith of old.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star claymore, base ATK 42, ATK% secondary stat (9 per cent). Passive Lithic Axiom: Unity gives the wearer 7 to 11 per cent ATK and 3 to 7 per cent CRIT Rate (by refinement) for each Liyue character in the party, stacking up to 4 times. It was a Weapon Event Wish (Version 1.3) and has the same passive as Lithic Spear.

307.content: The Millelith's old axiom, quoted in the Lithic Blade and Lithic Spear texts: while rock stays hard, the mountain shall never fail; while the Millelith stands guard, evil shall never prevail.

308.content:
Lithic Spear: Lithic Spear is a 4-star polearm of the Lithic series, a spear forged from the rocks of the Guyun Stone Forest whose hardness knows no equal. It was favoured by the Millelith of old, and its great weight stops today's Millelith from equipping it. It was added in Version 1.3.

Its text says it is said to be able to pierce even dragon scales, and recounts how the Millelith used leftover ancient spears after an earthquake.

Appearance: A spear forged from lith of the Guyun Stone Forest; canon gives no more detail. Do not invent a length or decoration.

Lore: The Millelith conducted themselves in Rex Lapis' name by the axiom: while rock stays hard, the mountain shall never fail; while the Millelith stands guard, evil shall never prevail. In the past they went forth to subdue demons and protect roads and countryside; in peaceful times their duties have shifted to maintaining order.

At a certain point in the past the earth shook and the mountains trembled. The Millelith then gave equipment left over from the ancient wars to those among them of unusually great stature: the very heavy Lithic Spears, which were used like shovels to rescue the injured. The text says the spear pierces rock with ease and that a thousand such spears lined up would be unstoppable.

Owners: No individual owner is named. Yaoyao is seen with the unascended spear in her Thrust and Parry anecdote and Xiangling with the ascended one in the Three to Get Ready, and Here We Go cinematic (cameos, not story claims).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star polearm, base ATK 44, ATK% secondary stat (6 per cent). Passive Lithic Axiom: Unity gives the wearer 7 to 11 per cent ATK and 3 to 7 per cent CRIT Rate (by refinement) for each Liyue character in the party, stacking up to 4 times. It was a Weapon Event Wish (Version 1.3) and has the same passive as Lithic Blade.

309.content: The Lithic Spear text describes the Millelith as the guardians of Rex Lapis' kingdom who once all carried these huge stone spears, and as rescuers who used them to dig out the injured after an earthquake. See the faction entry for the Millelith itself.

310.content:
Long Night's Oath (also: Lightkeeper's Pledge, Nightingale's Tail Feather, A Horn Unwinded, Dyed Tassel): Long Night's Oath is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that rewards Plunging Attacks. Its five pieces (Lightkeeper's Pledge, Nightingale's Tail Feather, Undying One's Mourning Bell, A Horn Unwinded, Dyed Tassel) carry item text that reads as a folk history of Nod-Krai: how the Lightkeepers swore their oath, how the Wild Hunt and the Abyss threatened the borderlands, and how the oath was renewed again and again at great cost.

The pieces were added in version 5.5. The text is told in a storyteller's voice and names almost no one directly; the wiki links the unnamed figures to Solovei, Avrelian, Aila, Sigurd, Rerir and others (see uncertainties).

Appearance: Northern military and ceremonial gear: a metal flower worn by Ratniki ("warriors"), a hat ornament of nightingale feathers, a bronze bell, a horn once used to summon the oath-sworn, and an ancient tasselled helmet.

Lore: The five pieces tell Nod-Krai's story from its founding oath to the cost of keeping it, centring on the Lightkeepers who guard the region.

Across the pieces: after the Cataclysm the borderlands were left without divine protection, a Torchforger from the far north rallied a moonlit defence, and the survivors raised a lighthouse at Piramida and swore an oath of vigilance to the new ruler of Snezhnaya, the Tsaritsa. Centuries later the Wild Hunt returns, the Fatui arrive at Piramida with ulterior motives, an oath-bound legion is lost, and a border officer chooses to save civilians against orders. Each piece frames the oath as a burden that descendants take up knowing what it costs.

Owners: No owner is named; the text speaks of Ratniki and Lightkeepers, and the wiki ties several pieces to Solovei and Sigurd.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): obtained from the Derelict Masonry Dock domain (Natlan) and the Artifact Strongbox. 2-piece: Plunging Attack DMG +25%. 4-piece: a Plunging Attack, Charged Attack or Elemental Skill hit gives 1, 2 or 2 stacks of Radiance Everlasting (each source once per 1s); each stack gives Plunging Attacks +15% DMG for 6s, max 5 stacks, independent timers.

311.comment: Long Night's Oath: Long Night's Oath
311.content: Artifact set whose item text narrates Nod-Krai's history from the Lightkeepers' founding oath to the Fatui's arrival at Piramida and a Warrant Officer's desertion, focused on keeping a sworn duty at great cost.

312.comment: Long Night's Oath: The Nightingale emblem and the first Torchforger
312.content: According to Dyed Tassel and Nightingale's Tail Feather, the first Torchforger came from a family of spies raised to the gentry by the Winter Tsar, with a nightingale as their emblem. After the Cataclysm he rode south from the far north in dark silver armour; with the new-moon maiden's beacon he repelled the black tide and later bound himself to an oath of vigilance. The wiki identifies him as Solovei; the text itself does not name him.

313.comment: Long Night's Oath: The Mourning Bell legend
313.content: Undying One's Mourning Bell tells of a warrior who fought toward the Wild Hunt's source, died without noticing, and continues to walk the abyss to fulfil his oath. His bell's toll became a folk omen that the hunter of the Wild Hunt is near. The wiki links him to Sigurd.

314.comment: Long Night's Oath: Piece text: Lightkeeper's Pledge
314.content: describes a time when the northern Hunting Winds levelled the frontier at the bidding of the tyrannical Knyazes of the fae. A mad monk who spoke strange tongues sought the power left by the heavenly moons and pitched a treacherous plot to the Tsar of all fae; the Moonchildren hiding in their mountain forests were scattered. The monk himself could not escape the celestial shell and was consumed by the sky. Before "paradise" existed it was merely a shared daydream of two children under the moon; years later one was executed as a notorious bandit and the other understood the words left behind. When the long night fell, the royal court ignored the borderlands and a horde of black beasts overran them until the original Torchforger, borrowing the power of the Moonchildren's priestess, raised the first beam of light. The survivors built a lighthouse atop the mountains and the Torchforger defended his friend's childlike dream before the Tsaritsa's court; he won a royal edict but bound himself to an oath of vigilance and sacrifice, and so began the history of "Nod-Krai".

315.comment: Long Night's Oath: Piece text: Nightingale's Tail Feather
315.content: legend of a nightingale carrying an ember on moonless nights. Piramida's high tower stands on the ruins of an age of pioneers, and the Lightkeepers' ancestors had sworn fidelity to the Tsaritsa centuries before. The people of "paradise" believed that so long as the lighthouse burned they could live free of the black beasts. One night the leader of the Wild Hunt rode across the sky and the sun failed to rise; as warriors gathered to march south, the current Starshyna sat silent in the mead hall because a host of the Fatui, the Warriors of the Pale Star, had reached the city gates, claiming to be reinforcements but with their own motives. The Starshyna knew that yielding would end centuries of autonomy. A masked officer's cold voice declared the dark calamity was beginning, that Snezhnaya could not bear the weight of their defeat, and that if none of the Nightingale warriors returned, the Fatui would handle the aftermath.

316.comment: Long Night's Oath: Piece text: Undying One's Mourning Bell
316.content: blood-scented air heralds the return of the great war as an army of spirits flies over the night. Country folk called it a demonic host from another world harvesting souls; others believed it the lingering phantoms of an ancient nightmare. The borderlanders named it the Wild Hunt, and a tempest unseen for a century fell like black-blood rain, proving the legends were born of real terror. A flock of black-feathered crows moved between light and shadow, led by one who stood against the light; the oath-bound legion marched on as moths to a flame. At the path's end only the warrior with the dark blade still stood, aware that the force that summoned the Hunt lay deep in the forest. His body had already been torn apart without his noticing, and his warning bell hissed through the blood and black mire, freezing the carrion-eaters. He was left to walk alone in the abyss to fulfil an unfinished oath. Folklore later held that tolling bells signal the approach of the one sworn to hunt down the Wild Hunt.

317.comment: Long Night's Oath: Piece text: A Horn Unwinded
317.content: when horns proclaimed the northern realm's might, a Fatui contingent sworn to the Tsaritsa and to no single Harbinger vowed to forge a pure new world beneath the stars. The borderlanders, granted autonomy, remained children of the motherland. The Warrant Officer leading a border squad held that conviction until he hovered before the gates of hell and saw souls no one loved. Before any strike was sanctioned he resolved to act, rejecting an order that would let black beasts devour mothers and children. The text skips ahead: the foul miasma is swept away by northern winds at dawn, the war ends, and no triumphant hero returns to the high tower, only a criminal and the children he saved. A renegade doctor ignores the deviation because the goal was met. Desertion and treason against the Tsaritsa are absolved by a newly sworn oath, and new warriors keep watch on a staircase built of bones until the abyssal tides dry up.

318.comment: Long Night's Oath: Piece text: Dyed Tassel
318.content: the first Torchforger came from the furthest northern city, his Nightingale emblem marking a family who began as spies and were raised to the gentry by the Winter Tsar. When the Cataclysm left the frontier without the gods' protection, a single rider in dark silver armour came from the north and the maiden of the new moon lit a beacon. Before departing for the Lempo Isles, warriors feasted in the mead hall, among them a young Ratnik in an archaic dark-tasselled helmet and holding a polearm; such armour marked descent from those who first fought beside the Torchforger against the black tide. Although they held no fief or title, they kept their ancestors' oaths in the belief that the lord of the fae and former protector of Snezhnaya still watched. Later the young warrior kneels among fallen comrades on a blood-soaked tundra and prays to an old god and to the Knyazes his people once ruled. Somewhere, perhaps woken by the horn, a long-dormant phantom stirs, and the ghostly blue wildfire of legend is said to burn again on new battlefields.

key: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
319.comment: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
319.content:
Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds is a 5-star catalyst: an educational tome by anonymous early worshippers of the wind, blessed by the wind for its faithfulness over the millennia. Its text follows the scripture through Mondstadt's ages and ends with a farewell note from a believer who joins the thousand winds. Added in Version 1.0.

Item text calls it scriptures of the ancient winds, passed from generation to generation among observers of ritual who served the Anemo Archon, its yellowing pages touched by countless hands whose prints the wind has carried away.

Appearance: A book with yellowed pages and an elegantly handwritten title page, thicker with every era. Canon gives no cover or size.

Lore: Under the Storm Lord, who reigned from his tower, the scriptures filled with desperate appeals. In the era when the sands of snow thawed, the joy of sprouting greenery flooded the pages.

Under the ruling aristocracy, who pulled puppet strings to control the masses, the scriptures in the hands of slaves told of their envy and their desire for the thousand winds. As the people lived, endured, fought, rejoiced and enjoyed freedom, the scriptures grew thicker and heavier.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. The book is said to have left the Church of Favonius's treasury on its own; no one has been shown holding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 5-star catalyst with base ATK 46 and a CRIT Rate secondary stat. Its passive, Boundless Blessing, raises Movement SPD by 10 per cent and, in battle, adds an Elemental DMG Bonus every 4 seconds (up to four stacks), lasting until the character falls or leaves combat. It is on the Standard Wish and weapon event Wishes.

key: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
320.comment: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds: Thousand winds scripture
320.content: The Lost Prayer is a tome of prayers that tells Mondstadt's history through a worshipper's eyes, from the Storm Lord's tower to the aristocrats' control and the freedom that followed, and notes that the book flew away from the Church. For the phrase "the thousand winds" see the Anemo and Thousand Winds entries.

321.content:
Lumenstone (also: Lumenstone Adjuvant): Lumenstone is a special stone mined from the depths of The Chasm in Liyue. Its item text says it has catalytic properties and nearly blazes with light in the gloomy mines, but loses all such effects once taken out of the Chasm. Entering the Underground Mines requires an adjuvant made from it.

In the quest Chasm Spelunkers it becomes the Lumenstone Adjuvant, a lantern-like gadget for the mines.

Appearance: A stone that glows strongly in the dark of the mines. The Adjuvant is described as a crystal that can be a sun in your palm.

Lore: In Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering, the adventurer Zhiqiong tells the Traveler that to enter The Chasm they must first find an adjuvant made from lumenstone, since only with it can anyone move in the dark below. The Traveler takes the stone from a table, after which Paimon wonders how the cage-shaped objects relate to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing further has been added to canon.

322.content:
Lumidouce Elegy (also: Bright Dawn Overture): Lumidouce Elegy is a 5-star polearm adorned with azure crystal. It is said to have been the treasure of a legendary Champion Duelist, yet never once used.

The weapon story follows that duelist, Marfisa (the wiki's identification), from the undercity Fleuve Cendre to the stage of the opera house, to the court's service as an enforcer, and finally to the pure sourcewaters of Narzissenkreuz.

Appearance: Canon describes a magnificent polearm adorned with azure crystal; the story gives its heroine sapphire eyes, but the text does not link that to the weapon. Arkhe-aligned wielders show a Pneuma or Ousia mark. Add nothing else.

Lore: In the Fleuve Cendre undercity where there is neither rain nor sun, a girl scraped by for scraps and would kill for a slice of mouldy bread, accepting that the weak are prey. Her mother's teaching was ashes to ashes, dust to dust.

Facing death, she is instead shown kindness by a girl in strange attire (the wiki links her to Parsifal the Great), who tucks a Lumidouce Bell flower behind her ear, saying it means hope and matches her hair, and trades it for her heart. She later watches the magician and assistant from a VIP box in the Opera Epiclese and sees hope in the flowers blooming under the spotlight. With no teacher, she steps onto a stage of her own, her lance performing every spear technique she has seen.

Owners: A legendary Champion Duelist, linked by the wiki to Marfisa. The weapon was never used.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star polearm, base ATK 46 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.8. Passive "Bright Dawn Overture": raises ATK; after the wielder triggers Burning, or deals Dendro DMG to Burning enemies, their DMG rises for 8s (up to 2 stacks); at 2 stacks, or when refreshed at 2 stacks, Energy is restored, at most once per 12s. It can trigger off-field. Values scale with refinement.

323.content: Marfisa was a Champion Duelist of the Court of Fontaine who came from the Fleuve Cendre. The wiki links her to the story of Lumidouce Elegy: self-taught lance-fighter, defeated once by a swordsman who convinced her to follow justice, and dissolved in the Narzissenkreuz's waters.

324.content:
Magical Crystal Chunk (also: Magical Crystal Chunks, Magical Crystal Ore): Magical Crystal Chunk is a blue crystal from mines whose rock was eroded by the energy of the Ley Lines. Ordinary methods cannot process it. Only Original Resin can refine it, into Mystic Enhancement Ore for strengthening weapons.

Where the plain Crystal Chunk is ordinary ore, this is its Ley Line-altered counterpart.

Appearance: Blue crystal chunks taken from Magical Crystal Ore nodes, which stand beside regular ore at Mining Outcrops.

Lore: Item text says the crystal was eroded by Ley Line energy and so cannot be handled by ordinary means; Original Resin can, however, refine it into an invaluable material. The description does not say what Original Resin is in-world or how the process works.

325.content:
Maiden Beloved (also: Maiden's Distant Love, Maiden's Heart-Stricken Infatuation, Maiden's Passing Youth, Maiden's Fleeting Leisure, Maiden's Fading Beauty): Maiden Beloved is a healing artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its pieces tell of a sheltered noblewoman rescued by a white knight, who fell in love with him and spent her years waiting for a man devoted to chivalry. She is the counterpart to the knight of the Bloodstained Chivalry set.

The pieces are Maiden's Distant Love (flower), Maiden's Heart-Stricken Infatuation (feather), Maiden's Passing Youth (sands), Maiden's Fleeting Leisure (goblet) and Maiden's Fading Beauty (circlet).

Appearance: A maiden's keepsakes: a fresh, elegant flower of a species the books call extinct, an old delicate feathered ornament under layers of dust, a delicate timepiece, treasured teaware once filled with black tea, and a hat she never took off before her suitors.

Lore: Distant Love recalls the passage she read countless times, of the damsel saved by the white knight and the exchange of flowers as blessings; the flower stays constant because her heart stilled when they met. Heart-Stricken Infatuation says time stopped for her that day; nothing mattered, and she wandered looking for him like a bird without a nest, praying her love would reach him while he pursued chivalry in a distant land where ancient empires crumbled. Passing Youth shows the short hand chasing the long hand like her longing: her time would end, her waiting would not. Fleeting Leisure has her indulging in pastries and tea while recalling the knight saying that the flower would be his medal; her unfinished confession ('my heart is already...') was both her privilege and the chain of courtliness. Fading Beauty has her brush the dust off her hat each night and ignore the flowers of courters whose names and faces were not worth remembering, as fewer and fewer came.

Owners: No named owner; the maiden is anonymous and the pieces are her belongings.

Status as of 7.1: The maiden is long gone and the texts leave her fate and name unstated. The set is background lore, unchanged by 6.x and 7.0-7.1.

326.content: The unnamed maiden of the Maiden Beloved texts fell in love with the white knight who saved her and spent her life waiting for him while courters brought flowers. The wiki ties the knight to Roland.

327.content:
Makhaira Aquamarine: Makhaira Aquamarine is a 4-star claymore of the Tulaytullah series: an ancient greatsword that gleams like water, whose unnaturally sharp edge a thousand years of sand erosion has not dulled. Its legend belongs to the dancer Makhaira, once a tyrant's concubine.

It is one of three Tulaytullah-series weapons that share a story world with the five-star catalyst Tulaytullah's Remembrance, and it was released in Version 3.1 through weapon event Wishes.

Appearance: A greatsword with a blade that gleams like water. The description stresses its unnaturally sharp edge and great age.

Lore: A thousand years ago, when the foolish king (Deshret) was buried beneath the dunes, short-lived city-states were scattered across the gilded land. The sword belonged to the dancer Makhaira, once the tyrant's concubine, who won the king's favor and the prince's attention with a ruthless sword dance.

The noble king of a decaying kingdom was obese and haughty, spending his days on food, wine and hunting, and, like other kings of that decadent age, on conquest and hoarding loot. One night, as water-colored moonlight quieted the kingdom and the Seelie murmured, he fell into a deep sleep. Makhaira, who had seen the signs of destruction, polished her sword for one last dance, and the young prince, who had foreseen the same, came to her.

Owners: The sword belongs to Makhaira in its story. No modern character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, level 1 base ATK 42, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 36. Passive Desert Pavilion: every 10 s the wielder gains a percentage of their Elemental Mastery as ATK for 12 s, with nearby party members gaining 30% of it; it works off-field and stacks across copies.

328.content:
Marechaussee Hunter (also: Hunter's Brooch, Masterpiece's Overture, Moment of Judgment, Forgotten Vessel, Veteran's Visage, Marechaussee Hunter artifact set): Marechaussee Hunter is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.0. Its pieces are mementos of the old Marechaussee Hunters, chiefly Emanuel Guillotin, who directed the Siege of Poisson, retired scarred and drinking, and raised two children he never felt close to. The bonuses boost Normal and Charged Attacks and CRIT Rate when HP changes.

The pieces are Hunter's Brooch (flower), Masterpiece's Overture (plume), Moment of Judgment (sands), Forgotten Vessel (goblet) and Veteran's Visage (circlet). The set shares a name with the Marechaussee Hunters, the older monster-hunting group behind today's Marechaussee Phantom (see its own entry).

Appearance: Each piece is a keepsake: an emblem for feats in Fontaine's defence (the brooch), a small tool for adjusting clockwork torque (the overture), a pocket watch given to Fontaine's enforcers that doubled as a duty badge (the moment of judgment), a wine vessel (the forgotten vessel) and a mask given to a Hunter whose face was wounded in service to the Court (the visage).

Lore: The pieces concern the Hunters' founding under Cassiodor, the Siege of Poisson, Alain Guillotin's clockwork legend, a famous trial by combat, and the retired Hunter (Emanuel Guillotin) who cared for two children he never felt close to.

Owners: Emanuel Guillotin is the set's main figure. The pieces also touch Cassiodor (the brooch's naming), Alain Guillotin (the overture), Karl Ingold and Marfisa (the watch) and Basil Elton, the unnamed friend of the mask.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus is Normal and Charged Attack DMG +15%. The 4-piece bonus gives CRIT Rate +12% for 5s whenever current HP rises or falls, up to 3 stacks. Obtained from the Denouement of Sin domain in Fontaine and the artifact strongbox.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): the pieces suit gentle, melancholic scenes about duty, regret and chosen family. A character who holds one should treat it as a keepsake, not as a weapon or token of rank.

329.content: In this set Emanuel is the scarred, retired Hunter who remembered his childhood games, the Siege of Poisson and his strained fatherhood in his last moments. His own entry holds his full story.

330.comment: Marechaussee Hunter: Siege of Poisson (set lore)
330.content: According to Hunter's Brooch and Veteran's Visage, the Siege of Poisson was an incident whose director was a Marechaussee Hunter; he left the force afterwards, and the bloodshed marked him for life.

331.content:
Memory of Dust (also: the stone dumbbell, Mortal World's Lock): Memory of Dust is a five-star catalyst of the Liyue series, a stone puzzle dumbbell. Its item story recounts Morax remembering Guizhong, who gave him the dumbbell as a token and a challenge: all her wisdom is hidden inside, if he can unlock it. He never could.

Appearance: Item text calls it a stone dumbbell. The wiki notes its design is based on a Kongming/Luban lock burr puzzle, and its Chinese name means Mortal World's Lock.

Lore: The story is told from Morax's memory. He recalls meeting a young woman with billowing sleeves among blooming Glaze Lilies; she acted solemn but seemed joyful as she handed him the dumbbell, calling it the mark of their pledge and her challenge to him. He insists there was no formal contract between them, just two people on the same path for their own reasons, yet he remembers the scene anyway.

At their end she said that the little people are as small and fragile as dust, and fear because they cannot know when disaster will take them, and so they work hard to grow clever. Since she and he differed so greatly in strength, she chose technique and wisdom, and with his brawn and her brains the city would become great. Her final smile was lonely as her form dissolved into fine dust. She told him to forget about the dumbbell.

Owners: Guizhong forged it by unknown methods and gave it to Morax (Zhongli). The wiki says he presumably still has it; the text never confirms this.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore. The passive Golden Majesty raises Shield Strength and stacks ATK on hits, with a larger bonus while shielded. It shares this passive with the Liyue-series claymore The Unforged. Obtained from Weapon Event Wishes; added in Version 1.1.

332.content:
Mistsplitter Reforged (also: Kirigiri no Kaikou, Mistsplitter, Takamine's sword): Mistsplitter Reforged is a sword from Inazuma's past, one of the blades the Shogun bestowed on her Hatamoto. It was carried by the samurai Takamine the Mistsplitter, who used it against demons and Tatarigami, and who fought the dark army of the Cataclysm at the end of his life. The sword broke and was reforged from its fragments, so the "Reforged" in the name marks it as a successor bearing the old name.

Its item text says it can call on lightning to cut through mountain mist and night fog. The reforged blade has a hamon like flowing clouds. The original line of users ended with Takamine; the sword now survives mainly in stories.

Appearance: A sword that blazes with a fierce violet light (the item description). The reforging left a hamon, the temper line on the blade, that resembles flowing clouds. In play, a purple aura surrounds the weapon while its passive is active and brightens with more stacks.

Lore: The text says the sword was shattered into a thousand pieces and reforged. Its user, Takamine the Mistsplitter, appears in a children's rhyme listing famous martial artists, after Arataki of the Front Gate, Iwakura the Successor and Kitain the Serpent.

Takamine once accompanied a member of the clergy and used the blade to slay demons and Tatarigami. He learned archery from the Yougou Tengu and passed it on to a person he loved, Asase Hibiki. At the end of his life he became one of the Shogun's yoriki and fought a dark army.

Owners: Takamine the Mistsplitter is the only named user. The Shogun is named as the one who gave such swords to her Hatamoto.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword in the Inazuma series, released in Version 2.0 on the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 48 with CRIT DMG as its secondary stat.

333.content: Takamine the Mistsplitter was a samurai of Inazuma's past, listed in a children's rhyme of famous martial artists. He used the sword Mistsplitter against demons and Tatarigami, learned archery from the Yougou Tengu, and made a wager with Asase Hibiki that involved leaving his bow with her. He died or vanished fighting the dark army of the Cataclysm; his own entry carries the rest.

334.content:
Mitternachts Waltz: Mitternachts Waltz is a 4-star bow described as painted in the color of transgression and nights of illusion. Its text is a dramatic, German-flavored tale: the Prinzessin der Verurteilung and her Night-Severing Raven, Ozvaldo Hrafnavins, recount a long journey across space and time. The wiki notes Fischl is shown with this bow in her TCG card.

The name is German for "midnight waltz". The text never says in plain words who the Prinzessin is, but it addresses her as "mein Fräulein" and the wiki links the address to Fischl.

Appearance: A bow painted in a transgressive, dream-like night color. Beyond that short description, canon gives no visual detail.

Lore: The tale opens with Oz telling the Prinzessin that not one of her tears was shed in vain on her pilgrimage. The Prinzessin and her raven, in their journey across space and time, witnessed countless stories and their endings.

In the text, every young man's rage at injustice must turn to calm, and everything must pass through the doorway of its destruction into the Prinzessin's future kingdom, where it finds sleep in her pitch-dark Nachtgarten. When Droctulf fell to the Beast of the World, having fought for a young man's dreams, the Prinzessin began to tear up, and she declared that the Sovereign of the Immernachtreich weeps not.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. The wiki notes Fischl is seen wielding this bow in her TCG character card.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, base ATK 42, secondary stat Physical DMG Bonus 11.3%, obtained from weapon event Wishes (added in Version 1.6). Passive Evernight Duet: Normal Attack hits raise Elemental Skill DMG for 5 s, and Elemental Skill hits raise Normal Attack DMG for 5 s, by 20% at refinement 1 up to 40% at refinement 5.

335.content:
Moonfall Silver (also: Moonfall Silver crystal): Moonfall Silver is a silver crystal as pure and pristine as moonlight, a local specialty of Nod-Krai. Canon says it has almost perfect elemental affinity, which is why Nod-Krai craftspeople treat it as an excellent elemental conductor. It is found on Hiisi Island.

Its name comes from Frostmoon Scions tradition, which held that the crystals were a gift from the moon. Older Snezhnayan chronicles tell a different, much older story about silver woven by the Frostmoon.

Appearance: A silvery crystal with an iridescent white sheen. Dorota, a collector in Nasha Town, praises its flawless form, smooth rounded texture and unrivaled elemental affinity. Even good samples can hide tiny flaws that only a careful eye notices.

Lore: The item text gives two traditions. In the legacy of the Frostmoon Scions, the crystals were born five hundred years ago alongside the Moon Maiden, and the Moonchanter of that time believed them a gift from the moon, hence the name. Yet older documents by Snezhnayan chroniclers say the descendants of the golden realm (Hyperborea) were already using secret silver woven by the Frostmoon thousands of years earlier. The text says plainly that how these two tales connect is unclear.

Owners: No notable owner. Collectors such as Dorota in Nasha Town keep prized samples, and Nod-Krai craftspeople use it as an elemental conductor.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a Nod-Krai local specialty added in Version 6.0 (Luna I). It is gathered on Hiisi Island, especially between Frostmoon Enclave and the Light-Bathed Platform, and in Silvermoon Hall, and is used for crafting and character ascension.

336.content:
Moongazer's Engraving (also: Moongazer Engraving, Stellar Blackbody message): Vol. 1 is the dragon researcher Lusalim's digest; Vol. 2 is Nin-Kiggia's annotated translation of the first message, the lament of the immortal Ysna'qurel. The script is unreadable, yet readers understand it in their own tongue.

Appearance: Both volumes are described as an ancient stone tablet found on the moon, with writing that is completely indecipherable but understood by anyone who reads it. Vol. 1 reads as a plain, hopeful letter; Vol. 2 as a long epic poem in the third person, with repeated formulae and untranslatable words in brackets.

Lore: Vol. 1 is addressed to a friend from a distant world and urges them to beware. Vol. 2 tells of Ysna'qurel, ruler of Throgg, who learns of a Dark Destroyer and sends a last messenger to warn other worlds, despite the cost.

Owners: No owner. Vol. 1 is credited to Lusalim and Vol. 2 to Nin-Kiggia; both are long dead as of the cutoff (the wiki lists both as deceased).

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a 2-volume Book Collection on the Frost Moon. Vol. 1 is obtained during the quest Project Moongazer (Part 1); Vol. 2 is picked up from an Edict Module in Lusalim's Laboratory.

337.comment: Moongazer's Engraving: The Stellar Blackbody's message
337.content: A warning carried across space and recorded on stone tablets found on the Frost Moon: pitch-black annihilation is crossing the universe, other worlds should be watchful, and a light kindled by one civilization can embolden another. Lusalim's digest and Nin-Kiggia's verbatim translation survive. Whether the original senders survived is unknown.

338.content: In Vol. 2 of Moongazer's Engraving, Ysna'qurel is an immortal, "child of Ghel'vur" and ruler of Throgg, who united the world under an empire after defeating seven monsters or compatriots. When they learn of the coming "Dark Destroyer", they choose to send a final messenger to warn other worlds, against the assembly's objection, and weep for what they will lose. Their sex, if any, is unknown.

339.content: Nin-Kiggia ("Ninnin") annotates Vol. 2 as an artificial, draconic Moongazer raised by Lusalim as his daughter. Her notes stay careful: she marks unreadable words, summarizes omitted line ranges, and declines to say whether the message's authors were Ysna'qurel's own empire.

340.content:
Moonweaver's Dawn (also: Secret Silver's Testament): An immaculate silver sword that slices armour like moonlight through an empty night; legend says it was blessed by the first Moonchanter, Aila. A 4-star sword of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.0.

Its text shows Aila obeying, then ending, the last Archpriestess.

Appearance: An immaculate, sharp silver sword; canon text gives no hilt or decorative detail.

Lore: A guardian addresses her ward Aila as her heart's child and tells her the pure silver blood of their line alone is worthy of the Frost Moon's grace.

Aila is told she will bear the heir to Elysium and must not wed an outlander's son. The text says Lovia, the Archpriestess of the far north, repeated blasphemous deeds, and Aila obediently carried out her commands, including severing silver threads of fate with the blade and silencing singing voices, to purify the holy blood.

Owners: No wielder is named; the blade is attributed to Aila's blessing.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star sword, base ATK 44, ATK% secondary. Passive Secret Silver's Testament increases Elemental Burst DMG, with an extra bonus when the wielder's Energy Capacity is low (60 or 40 or less, depending on the tier of the effect). One copy is awarded by the quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past.

341.content: Secret Silver's Testament is the weapon's passive; its name echoes the scene where Aila's silver blade reveals a crimson truth. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

342.content:
Mora (also: Mora coins, Mora currency): Mora is the common currency of Teyvat, accepted in every nation. It takes its name from Morax, the Geo Archon, whom Liyue calls Rex Lapis. All of it is minted at the Golden House in Liyue. Loading-screen text calls it the one language everybody speaks.

Mora is also described as a kind of catalyst: a medium of physical transformation, which is why so many tasks, such as crafting and strengthening equipment, can only be done by spending it.

Appearance: Mora comes as small coins stamped with a triquetra, a triangular symbol. Both faces are identical, so a coin cannot be flipped without marking one side. People in Teyvat still settle disputes by flipping a coin and still say "heads" and "tails", even though neither side has a head. Larger sums are carried in bags; a huge bag of gold coins appears as a quest item, and Childe's high-value coins could be redeemed for smaller change at the Northland Bank.

Lore: In-game text calls Mora the currency accepted worldwide, whose value and standing nobody disputes. All of Teyvat's Mora is minted at the Golden House on Mt. Tianheng in Liyue, and the currency is named after the Geo Archon Morax. In Liyue he is called Rex Lapis, and Paimon notes it is considered impolite for outsiders to use the name Morax there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mora remains the universal currency. The Geo Archon has given up his Gnosis, and the Golden House no longer mints new Mora, though the existing supply stays valid.

343.content:
Mouun's Moon (also: Mouun's longbow, the Watatsumi shrine maiden's bow): Mouun's Moon is a four-star bow of the Watatsumi series, the longbow of the Watatsumi shrine maiden Mouun. Item text says it shines pure white like seafoam at the tip of a moonlit wave. She befriended the monsters of the distant seas and fought with them against the thundering clouds in the war of Orobashi (Watatsumi Omikami), a path of no return that ended in tragic obliteration.

Appearance: Item text describes a longbow shining as pure white as seafoam at the tip of a moonlit wave. No further detail is given.

Lore: The text says the shrine maiden was friends with the monsters of the distant seas, and together they fought the thundering clouds for the sake of Watatsumi's "transient dream", riding the waves in the spray at ships' bows. She is quoted as accepting that Orobashi's war may have been doomed from the start, but hoping that leaving memories and "seeds of sacrifice" would make it worthwhile. Songs eulogise her unspoken bond with her twin Ayame, "Umigozen", depicting them with bow drawn and spear raised in the wave-spray of a ship.

Owners: The shrine maiden Mouun (historical.mouun). No later owner is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star bow. Base ATK 44, secondary stat ATK 6%. Passive "Watatsumi Wavewalker" is shared with Akuoumaru and Wavebreaker's Fin: for every point of the party's combined maximum Energy capacity, the wielder's Elemental Burst DMG rises, up to a cap. Obtained from weapon event wishes.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a bow of lost friends and a lost cause. Within Watatsumi, Mouun is remembered with affection; elsewhere she is mostly an unknown name.

344.content: Mouun was a Watatsumi shrine maiden, twin of Ayame ("Umigozen"). She befriended sea monsters and fought with them in Orobashi's war; her bow is Mouun's Moon. The item texts leave her fate to inference: she was consumed by a dark storm of crow feathers in the war's final defeat.

345.content:
Musou Isshin (also: Musou no Isshin, Makoto's blade, the Shogun's sword): Musou Isshin is the legendary sword of the Raiden twins. It was created from Makoto's divine might and kept unsharpened and unused while she lived, as a symbol of true peace. When Makoto died in the Cataclysm it passed to her sister Ei, who began to use it in battle. It is the blade the Raiden Shogun draws from her heart during her Elemental Burst.

The name means roughly "a dream of one heart". Makoto gave the sword its name and wished it to witness an Inazuma as lovely as a dream, and the noble hearts of the people in it. Ei kept the name.

Appearance: A tachi, a samurai sword with a slightly longer hilt and blade than the more familiar katana, according to the Burst's talent text. The Raiden Shogun produces it from her chest rather than from a sheath at her hip. Canon gives no further description of its fittings.

Lore: The character story calls it a sword that has accompanied Ei to this day and has "witnessed both time and eternity". It was born from Makoto's divine might but never sharpened, because Makoto was not one for battle; it was a symbol, a sign of true peace.

On the day Makoto passed on, the sword was given to Ei. It was already stained with blood and, as the blade drew its first crimson, the ichor was blown aside by wild winds and blazing thunder. Ei did not change its name, because she too had looked out over the vast scene of Inazuma's beauty and it had given her a stronger, purer dream of her own. The text ends on the aesthetic of lightning: to capture what is precious amid fleeting transience.

Owners: First Makoto, who never used it to fight, then Ei, who has used it in battle since Makoto's death. The Raiden Shogun, Ei's puppet, wields it in her Burst.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): the sword is not an obtainable weapon. The Raiden Shogun's Elemental Burst, Secret Art: Musou Shinsetsu, changes her stance from a polearm to the Musou Isshin, which uses sword animations. In the Inazuma Archon Quest boss fight, the playable Raiden Shogun stays permanently in her Musou Isshin state.

346.content: Makoto made Musou Isshin from her divine might as a symbol of peace and never sharpened it. After her death it passed to Ei, who used it in battle. Makoto left a fragment of her will in the blade, released when Ei embraced its full power; Ei says the sword seems to guide her toward understanding her sister.

key: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
347.comment: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
347.content:
New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune (also: Chronicles of the Six Kitsune, Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune, Black Fox Itaru): New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune is a six-volume Inazuman novel sold at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. It adapts "Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune", a hit about 500 years ago, and follows the tales of Itaru, eldest of the six apprentices of the Great Kitsune Hakushin. Its last volume adds the author's commentary on the Kitsune Saiguu and why she left.

The author is unnamed: a writer who, in the Prologue, is talked back into writing for the publishing house by the chief editor (Yae Miko, as the linked text indicates) over drinks at the Uyuu Restaurant.

Appearance: A set of novels with a cover lettered in the Inazuman script. The wiki reads it as an abbreviation of the Japanese title, which is its own reading and not stated in-game. The volumes are numbered one way in the Archive and another in shops and the overworld.

Lore: The Prologue frames the book. An aging writer meets Yae Miko at the Uyuu Restaurant and is persuaded to write again; she notes she was not yet born when "she" (the Kitsune Saiguu) left, and that he is the only one still able to recite the stories she told.

Volume 2 explains the title: "new" implies an "old". Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune was popular five hundred years ago. The story begins on Mt. Yougou, where the Great Kitsune Hakushin had six skilled apprentices.

Owners: Not a unique item. It is a published book, printed by the Yae Publishing House for general readers.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a collectible book collection. Vol. 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 are sold by Kuroda at the Yae Publishing House; one volume is in the left-hand room of the Yashiro Commission Headquarters. Added in Version 2.0.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's suggestion): an Inazuman may know the book as a popular novel with a fox heroine; only readers of the last volume or Yae's close circle know the commentary on the Saiguu. Do not present Itaru, Dozaemon or the Twin Oni as historical figures, and do not add detail to what the Saiguu or Urakusai did.

348.comment: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune: Itaru the Black Fox
348.content: Itaru the Black Fox is the heroine of the novel: the eldest of Hakushin's six kitsune apprentices, huge, strong and unruly, banished from Mt. Yougou after destroying the Shogun's shintai while drunk. She travels as a self-described masterless youkai, takes the Twin Oni of Tokaku into her company and rights wrongs such as the Lavender Melon swindle in Konda Village. She is a character in an adaptation; the book does not say she was a real person.

349.comment: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune: Urakusai
349.content: Urakusai is the kitsune writer of the original Chronicles of the Six Kitsune, popular about 500 years ago. Once prized by the Kitsune Saiguu for his writing and tea expertise, he made a grave mistake and was driven out; why is not recorded, though the new author says it may have been linked to the later incursion of the Abyss. Vol. 5 is said to have been written after Urakusai's return from Liyue.

key: Night Murmurs From the Far Border
Night Murmurs From the Far Border: Varcolac
350.comment: Night Murmurs From the Far Border
350.content:
Night Murmurs From the Far Border (also: Night Murmurs From the Far Border: Varcolac, Varcolac folktale): The item description calls it a collection of folktales circulating in Snezhnaya that records lesser-known fae tales; this volume covers the dangerous fae called the Varcolac. The tale is told as a legend and ends on a deliberately open note.

Appearance: A 3-star Book Collection with one volume, credited to an author named Viliana. The prose is a short horror-tinged narrative in the style of a winter tale, closing with a brief narrator's coda that steps outside the story.

Lore: Czcibor, a seasoned hunter, keeps watch in a hunting lodge after a village girl is found with her throat torn open. A monster of coarse black fur passes; he wounds its right shoulder and follows the blood to a gloomy estate deep in the forest. A pale elderly butler denies seeing it, and the master, a strikingly handsome man in his early twenties with waist-length black hair, invites the hunter to dine and stay out of the blizzard. Czcibor, raised in the Frostmoon Scions' encampment, recalls an old priestess's warning that Varcolac are the trickiest of the fae: they have two hearts, take a human and a fae form, and keep the same fur colour in both. He tests his host with pepper, garlic and his amulet, and nothing bothers the man.

Owners: No character is established as owning it. It is sold to the Traveler by Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a one-volume Book Collection bought from Dhabit. It has no combat function.

351.comment: Night Murmurs From the Far Border: The Varcolac
351.content: In this folktale a Varcolac is a fae with two hearts that can take a human or a wolf-like form, with the same hair or fur colour in both. A hunter's priestess warns that they are the trickiest fae. A Varcolac heals wounds by drawing on the glow of Frostlamp Flowers, and the story claims that piercing one heart does not kill it. The book says they are now nearly extinct and often written off as myth.

352.comment: Night Murmurs From the Far Border: Czcibor the hunter (folktale)
352.content: The protagonist of the tale, a veteran hunter who grew up in the Frostmoon Scions' camp and carries an amulet that shimmers in moonlight. His dagger sneak attack fails to kill the Varcolac, and the story ends as the beast lunges at his throat. He is a story character who happens to share a name with a modern NPC.

353.content:
Night of the Sky's Unveiling (also: Bloom of the Mind's Desire, Feather of Indelible Sin, Revelation's Toll, Vessel of Plenty, Crown of the Befallen): Night of the Sky's Unveiling is a 4- and 5-star artifact set added in version 6.0 that strengthens Lunar reactions. Its item text tells of Rauthvangi, a young stargazer of subterranean Khaenri'ah who glimpsed a "pitch-black Elysium" beyond the sky. For this he was exiled, survived the surface, wandered the nations, and as Rotwang, the Tsar's "mad monk", travelled to Nod-Krai to claim a hidden treasure and break out of the celestial shell.

The set links Khaenri'ah's astrology, the forbidden knowledge of the great sin, the court of the Snowland fae and the Cataclysm-era Nod-Krai. It never states his later fate; that comes from Nod-Krai quests.

Appearance: Item text only names the pieces: a flower, a feather, a bell or clock-like piece, a vessel and a crown. It gives no physical description of the set.

Lore: Rauthvangi, a novice monk in subterranean Khaenri'ah, glimpses a forbidden "pitch-black Elysium" in a star mirror, is exiled from the Universitas Magistrorum and survives the surface unharmed. He later wanders the nations, becomes the Tsar's favourite as Professor Rotwang, the "mad monk" of Zapolyarny Palace, and goes to Nod-Krai as envoy to seize a treasure and break through the celestial shell.

Owners: No owner is named. The text follows Rauthvangi (Rotwang); none of the pieces says who owned the objects.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; domain Frostladen Machinery in Nod-Krai (6.0) and an Artifact Strongbox. 2-piece: Elemental Mastery +80. 4-piece: when nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions, if the wearer is on the field they gain Gleaming Moon: Intent for 4s (CRIT Rate +15% with Nascent Gleam, +30% with Ascendant Gleam). Party Lunar reaction DMG is increased by 10% for each different Gleaming Moon effect among party members, and these effects do not stack. Per the wiki, Silken Moon's Serenade's 4-piece and this one together give a total of 20%, and extra copies of either do not add more.

354.comment: Night of the Sky's Unveiling: Night of the Sky's Unveiling
354.content: Artifact set whose item text follows Rauthvangi, a Khaenri'ahn astrologer and later the Tsar's mad monk, from his glimpse of a forbidden "Elysium" through exile to his mission in Nod-Krai.

355.comment: Night of the Sky's Unveiling: Signs of Truth
355.content: Per the Bloom of the Mind's Desire text, Khaenri'ahn astrologers recorded unusual phenomena in their star charts as "Signs of Truth" and decided the mirror's illusions must be pierced to reach truth. Rauthvangi's glimpse of the light around the horizon, through the dust-covered mirror of Apaosha, is the origin of his obsession with the "pitch-black Elysium".

key: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods
356.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods
356.content:
Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods (also: Selfless Floral Accessory, Honest Quill, Faithful Hourglass, Magnanimous Ink Bottle, Compassionate Ladies' Hat): Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods is a Geo artifact set from Version 4.3. Its five pieces tell a bedtime-style fairy tale, read aloud in fragments by a little girl in an attic with her dog Pie: a witch in the Echoing Woods grants a youth's wish, and the girl he loves is given endless good luck that turns out to be a curse.

The tale is framed twice. The outer story is the attic scene (the girl, her dog Pie and her mother, who likes to tell stories); the inner story is the book. Each piece holds a page of the book and a short return to the attic.

Lore: A girl follows her dog Pie into the attic and finds a storybook with golden-winged butterflies on its cover. It says a witch in the Echoing Woods grants any wish but hides her hut in fog and echoes, so few reach her. A youth, led by a golden-winged butterfly, finds the hut and asks that the girl he loves, who loves another, have all the happiness in the world. The witch agrees; the price will come later and need not be his soul.

The witch's magic is a pen, ink bottle and other items: whatever the dipped pen writes becomes real and the girl becomes fate's favourite. Everything goes her way, everyone adores her, and she grows spoiled.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): 4 and 5 star set from the Waterfall Wen domain and its strongbox. 2-piece: ATK +18%. 4-piece: after an Elemental Skill, +20% Geo DMG Bonus for 10s; increased by 150% under a Crystallize shield or near Moondrifts formed by Lunar-Crystallize, with the extra ending 1s after the condition lapses. Introduced in 4.3.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the story as a fairy tale told through a storybook rather than as a historical event; do not assign it a nation, and do not decide the witch's or youth's fate beyond what the text says.

357.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods: Selfless Floral Accessory
357.content: The flower piece: a butterfly-shaped brooch worn by the witch. Its text opens the frame story (the girl, Pie, the attic, the butterfly-covered book) and the legend of the Echoing Woods witch whose fog confuses visitors with echoes.

358.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods: Honest Quill
358.content: The plume piece: the witch's dip pen. The girl wonders why souls are sold so easily in stories; the youth asks what could fulfil a higher happiness, and the witch says words written with the pen dipped in her ink come true and the girl will be fate's favourite.

359.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods: Faithful Hourglass
359.content: The sands piece: the witch's sand timepiece, said to run very fast if the wrong incantation is spoken. In the tale, the girl scorns blue ribbons given by guests, tells her mother she does not need a mother who does not love her like the others, and leaves home.

360.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods: Magnanimous Ink Bottle
360.content: The goblet piece: the witch's ink bottle. Its text has the girl return home to find her mother long dead, call her luck a curse and set out for the Echoing Woods; the youth shows her the witch's magic mirror.

361.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods: Compassionate Ladies' Hat
361.content: The circlet piece: the witch's lady's hat. The girl chooses the harder path, the witch's appointed time arrives, the girl is trapped in the ink bottle, and the frame story ends with the girl leaving the storybook behind on the attic floor.

362.content:
Nightweaver's Looking Glass (also: Looking Glass of the Nightweaver, Millennial Hymn): A flawless silver mirror said to have witnessed the Moon Maiden's birth; the Frostmoon Scions hold it a relic of unrivalled provenance. A 5-star catalyst from Version 6.0.

Its item text is a Scion-side history of Hyperborea's Archpriestesses, the first Moonchanter Aila and the hoped-for new moon.

Appearance: A mirror of flawless silver used as a catalyst; canon gives no further description.

Lore: Its story opens with a prophecy-verse: the Eternal Moon fell, the Iridescent Moon shattered, the Frost Moon ceased to turn, and the world marches toward its end until Elysium dawns.

Descendants of the Golden City of Hyperborea built a lonely temple on the tundra, forged pale crowns of secret silver and chose Archpriestesses, though their gods had departed. The first Moonchanter, Aila, was a mortal who witnessed the birth of a god.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon; the description ties the mirror to the Frostmoon Scions as a whole.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star catalyst with Elemental Mastery as secondary stat. Passive Millennial Hymn gives Elemental Mastery after the wielder's Hydro or Dendro Skill damage and when party members trigger Lunar-Bloom; with both active, the party gains Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon and Lunar-Bloom bonuses, even off-field.

363.content: Millennial Hymn is the weapon's passive. Its two named effects, Prayer of the Far North and New Moon Verse, echo the text's themes of the northern faith and the coming new moon. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

364.content:
Noblesse Oblige (also: Royal Flora, Royal Plume, Royal Pocket Watch, Royal Silver Urn, Royal Masque): Noblesse Oblige is a 4- and 5-star artifact set (1.0) about the old aristocracy of Mondstadt: nobles who began as heroes and guides of the people and decayed into idle, grasping rulers. Its name is French for 'nobility obliges'. It drops in the Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain.

The pieces are Royal Flora, Royal Plume, Royal Pocket Watch, Royal Silver Urn and Royal Masque.

Lore: Each piece pairs a virtue with its decay. Royal Flora: nobles guided subjects by conduct and wisdom. Royal Plume: hunts shared with common folk. Royal Pocket Watch: punctuality as self-discipline, a worthy noble more vigilant than his people. Royal Silver Urn: treasures that stood for the people's prosperity. Royal Masque: chieftains of humble origin who welcomed the people to banquets. Each ends with later nobles abandoning that virtue.

365.comment: Noblesse Oblige: The old nobles of Mondstadt
365.content: The set remembers early Mondstadt nobles as guides and hosts of the people who later fell into self-indulgence. The same class eventually became the tyrants overthrown by Vennessa's rebellion.

366.content:
Noctilucous Jade (also: Night-Staying Stone, Yepo Stone): Noctilucous Jade is a rare mineral from Liyue that glimmers in the dark. Its item text says it is a mutated gemstone condensed from the world's flourishing elements. It is found in caves and mines across Liyue, especially near Mingyun Village.

The Chinese name means Night-Staying Stone.

Appearance: A gemstone that shines faintly in dark places, which is the sense of the word noctilucous.

Lore: Beyond the item description, canon gives it no story. It is called a mutated gemstone, condensed from the flourishing elements of the world, and only said to be so. Chang the Ninth in Qingce Village gives four to the Traveler on a first dialogue branch.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon adds nothing beyond the item text.

367.content:
Nocturne's Curtain Call (also: Ballad of the Crossroads, Bountiful Sea's Sacred Wine): A jade pearl wrapped in moonlight whose gentle warmth lingers like a song even on the coldest winter night. A 5-star catalyst from Version 6.3, its text a lullaby and a vision of the Moon Maiden.

It frames Columbina's memories of the three moons.

Appearance: A jade pearl shrouded in moonlight. Canon text describes only the pearl and its warmth.

Lore: The text is framed by a lullaby to a little dove, child of the moon: may the moon be with you in your slumber. Between its verses is Columbina's vision of the Moon Maiden drifting through the night.

A shattered husk falls toward Nod-Krai, the misty land that never became a moon. In a prison beyond the reach of Time and Wind, Columbina, called the one who traverses backward, watches the eternal slumber of three sisters.

Owners: No wielder is named; the text concerns Columbina but does not make her the owner.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star catalyst, CRIT DMG secondary. Passive Ballad of the Crossroads raises Max HP and, on triggering Lunar reactions, restores Energy and grants Bountiful Sea's Sacred Wine, a Max HP and Lunar CRIT DMG bonus.

368.comment: Nocturne's Curtain Call: Ballad of the Crossroads
368.content: Ballad of the Crossroads is the weapon's passive, named for the three-way fork in its text. Bountiful Sea's Sacred Wine is the buff it grants. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

369.content:
Nymph's Dream (also: Odyssean Flower, Wicked Mage's Plumule, Nymph's Constancy, Heroes' Tea Party, Fell Dragon's Monocle, Nymphs Dream): Nymph's Dream is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that boosts Hydro damage and ATK. It was released in Version 3.6, long before Fontaine opened, and its lore tells a quiet story: orphans playing heroes, wicked mages and fell dragons, a tea party that pauses the adventure, and the later scattering of the "Narzissen champions" after a catastrophe.

The pieces are Odyssean Flower (flower), Wicked Mage's Plumule (plume), Nymph's Constancy (sands), Heroes' Tea Party (goblet) and Fell Dragon's Monocle (circlet). It is the one set here that is obtained in Sumeru but belongs to Fontaine's story.

Appearance: A pocket watch (Nymph's Constancy) pieced from rejected parts of other devices, a dark green feather from a hat (Wicked Mage's Plumule) and a monocle are described, but no piece has an owner who is shown on-screen.

Lore: Told as children's play, the pieces move from a tea party that pauses the adventure, through stories of heroes, mages and fell dragons, to the Director's departure and the scattering of the champions after a catastrophe.

Owners: No named owner. The pieces speak of anonymous children and of the Director and Vice Director.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus is Hydro DMG +15%. The 4-piece bonus grants a Mirrored Nymph stack (8s) after attacks, skills and bursts hit opponents; 1, 2 and 3+ stacks give ATK +7%/16%/25% and Hydro DMG +4%/9%/15%, and stacks from each attack type are independent. Obtained from Molten Iron Fortress (Gavireh Lajavard, Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru), whose Ley Line Disorder gives Elemental Mastery for Dendro-related reactions, and from the artifact strongbox. Added in 3.6.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the set as nostalgic and wistful, a childhood game remembered after loss. Do not name the children or confirm which Fontainian figures they became unless a canon source for that scene is cited.

370.content: In these pieces the "Narzissen champions" are children playing heroes, mages, knights and fell dragons at a home without sun or moon, tended by a Director and a Vice Director. The Institute itself is covered in its own entry.

371.content:
Oathsworn Eye (also: Oath Eye, serpent's eye jewel): Oathsworn Eye is a jewel-like catalyst that glimmers like a snake's eye. Its description calls it a national treasure of Byakuyakoku, stored in the Dainichi Mikoshi, and says that when the Serpent God came, it was used to notarize great oaths and wishes. Its item text is a short fable of the oath a lonely serpent swore with a child and with his people in the depths.

It is a 4-star catalyst that players could obtain only as a reward in the Three Realms Gateway Offering event (Version 2.5), so its in-world material is tied to Enkanomiya.

Appearance: A jewel that glimmers like snake-eyes, shown in the text as held out by the giant white serpent. Canon text describes it no further than a glittering jewel used as a witness to oaths.

Lore: The text imagines the giant white snake looking down at a child who asks him to become their deity. The snake says he fled into waters unknown because he could best neither Deus Auri nor Narukami, and warns that anyone who keeps seeking the light will suffer loss. Yet he shows a snake-eyed jewel and says: swear it upon this eye, as he did when he made a pact with his coral servants.

A speaker quotes Master Spartacus's teaching that they must never worship a god and can rely only on themselves. The white serpent says nothing, since he respects the will of the people dwelling in the depths: if vain worship were replaced by new belief, would that not dishonour those who fought? The child swears before the eye anyway, declaring that all is as it was when everything was lost.

Owners: No individual is named. The eye belongs to Byakuyakoku as a national treasure, and its home was the Dainichi Mikoshi.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst, an event weapon of the Three Realms Gateway Offering (Version 2.5, limited-time event). Base ATK 44 with ATK% as secondary stat.

372.content:
Obsidian Codex (also: Obsidian Codex artifact set, Reckoning of the Xenogenic, Root of the Spirit-Marrow, Myths of the Night Realm, Pre-Banquet of the Contenders, Crown of the Saints): Obsidian Codex is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Natlan, added in Version 5.0. Its five pieces are mythic fragments, each opening with the line that many stories "were never recorded or eulogized in any human history": a dragon's gift of fire to humans, the first tribe, a contest of heroes and the crowning of a king who ended the tribes' wars. It boosts characters in Nightsoul's Blessing.

The pieces are Reckoning of the Xenogenic (flower), Root of the Spirit-Marrow (plume), Myths of the Night Realm (sands), Pre-Banquet of the Contenders (goblet) and Crown of the Saints (circlet). Together they read as one long legend told in epithets, not names.

Lore: Every piece opens with the same refrain, that many stories passed which no human history recorded. In order:
- Reckoning of the Xenogenic: a dispossessed divine envoy fell into lightless realms.
- Root of the Spirit-Marrow: the wisest of dragons carried a seed of the primal fire across a burning land and, finding no creation worthy of it, chose the weakest and most cherished of species, humans living in the shadow of ancient wings.
- Myths of the Night Realm: brave Chaac took the ever-bright kindling from the Sage of the Stolen Flame, shared it.
- Pre-Banquet of the Contenders: priests of smoke.
- Crown of the Saints: as a dark tide rose, warriors carried the Wayob's blessings into forbidden realms, the dragons were gone from the fields.
Each piece has its own entry with its full text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus gives +15% DMG while the wearer is in Nightsoul's Blessing and on the field. The 4-piece bonus gives +40% CRIT Rate for 6s after the wearer consumes 1 Nightsoul point while on the field, at most once per second.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present the pieces as relics whose texts are half-understood. Ordinary Natlanians know the tribal legends of Chaac and the Wayob but not the dragons' side of the story; no one has a ready key to the epithets. Do not let a character confidently name every figure in the set.

373.content: In Myths of the Night Realm Chaac is the brave, wise hero who received the ever-bright kindling from the Sage of the Stolen Flame, shared it with fellow tribespeople, defeated a raging dragon, founded the first tribe, and called on the night realm's god on the last night of his life.

374.comment: Obsidian Codex: Sage of the Stolen Flame
374.content: In Root of the Spirit-Marrow and its sister pieces, the wisest of dragons carries a seed of primal fire to a rugged land, grants humans the kindling of wisdom and foretells a savior of two worlds. The wiki's lore transcription links this figure to Kukulkan, Waxaklahun Ubah Kan. The pieces call his path "evolution" and note it will order human destinies as the price of civilising them.

375.comment: Obsidian Codex: Reckoning of the Xenogenic
375.content: a dispossessed divine envoy fell into lightless realms, and the newly returned ruler destroyed a blasphemous citadel. The vishap kingdom survived the collapse of heaven and earth, isolated by a sea of red soil, but its fire-wisdom had been seized by foul darkness and only a gray corpse shambled on, while its blind heirs mistook violence for law. One "human" among them foresaw the ruler's deathbed and the fall of a great civilization, and carried off unextinguished primordial kindling from the palace beneath the magma.

376.comment: Obsidian Codex: Root of the Spirit-Marrow
376.content: the wisest of dragons carried a seed of the primal fire across a burning land and, finding no creation worthy of it, chose the weakest and most cherished of species, humans living in the shadow of ancient wings. The gift would civilise them but also order their destinies, since it was the profane path of "evolution" rather than the first divine plan. The dragon told the first barbarian who climbed the floating landmass that from his heirs would come a savior of two worlds who would slay the overlord of fire and take the oldest throne.

377.comment: Obsidian Codex: Myths of the Night Realm
377.content: brave Chaac took the ever-bright kindling from the Sage of the Stolen Flame, shared it, and with his companions defeated a raging dragon and founded the first tribe. The Sage knew every answer but two: the end of the living and the homeward path of the dead. When his companions were gone, Chaac climbed a mountain on his last night, lit the first flame, and the god of the night realm answered; people heard what seemed a mother's song, the birth-cry of the first Wayob.

378.comment: Obsidian Codex: Pre-Banquet of the Contenders
378.content: priests of smoke and mist fed bonfires with the blood of other species, a hero rode a tamed beast to a fortress of huge stones with the Wayob's guidance, and reptiles feared an ancient city. The wisest dragon watched, planning that the strongest tribal hero should rule all humans, make a covenant, raise the banner of the blazing sun and take the primal fire from the living corpse on the throne. It knew foes waited in the deepest night, and that neither the gods in their heavens nor the high king among dragons would be enough.

379.comment: Obsidian Codex: Crown of the Saints
379.content: as a dark tide rose, warriors carried the Wayob's blessings into forbidden realms, the dragons were gone from the fields, and the dragon temples stood waiting for judgment. The tribes' war chiefs abandoned dragon-slaying to fight over supremacy. A hero no plan had accounted for, wearing a crown of golden flowers and carrying a great obsidian blade, visited tribe after tribe; the tribes made a pact of armistice and the sacred ones of the night realm offered him the crown. The dragon that thought itself master of evolution had not foreseen that strength would answer with something other than conquest.

380.content:
Ocean-Hued Clam (also: Ocean-Hued Clam artifact set, Sea-Dyed Blossom, Deep Palace's Plume, Cowry of Parting, Pearl Cage, Crown of Watatsumi, Sea-Dyed Foam): Ocean-Hued Clam is a 4 and 5 star artifact set from Watatsumi Island's songs. Its texts recall Omikami, the sea god the islanders worshipped; the first Divine Priestess and her twin sisters; shells and pearls given as tokens of family; and the sacrifice that ended that age. It is a healing set whose 4-piece turns healing into burst damage.

It drops from the Slumbering Court domain on Seirai Island, and came with Version 2.3. The texts are legend rather than record: they say what the islanders sing, and the Pearl Cage admits that the tale may be an ancient story that can no longer be verified.

Lore: Watatsumi's people say they came out of the dark depths, and took a single shell each as a keepsake of their clan; those who had none were welcomed into another family. Omikami chose a Divine Priestess and rulers from among them, and the age ended in sacrifice.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not lore: the 2-piece bonus is Healing Bonus +15%. The 4-piece bonus makes each heal create a Sea-Dyed Foam that collects the healing for 3 seconds (up to 30,000 HP, overflow included) and bursts as Physical-type damage of 90% of the total, with one foam every 3.5 seconds and one at a time; it works off-field. The damage ignores Elemental Mastery, level and reaction bonuses, and counts healing absorbed by Bond of Life.

381.comment: Ocean-Hued Clam: Omikami and Watatsumi's faith
381.content: The Ocean-Hued Clam texts speak of Omikami as a deity who chose priestesses and rulers from the sea people, rejoiced in their love and gave pearls. Wiki summaries identify Omikami with Orobashi no Mikoto, the coral serpent once worshipped in Enkanomiya and on Watatsumi Island, who met its end near the close of the Archon War; the artifact texts themselves allude only to sacrifice and martyrdom, not to the war.

382.content: The Cowry of Parting says that in the old tongue the keepsake seashells of the Watatsumi people were called Parcels of Reunion; each person took one for their clan, and those without one were welcomed into a new family. The shell symbolises leaving the depths for daylight.

383.comment: Ocean-Hued Clam: Divine Priestess and the twin sisters
383.content: The Divine Priestess of Watatsumi is, in these texts, the first of the shrine maidens, a pearl-gathering sea-daughter whose songs gave her people hope. She and her twin sisters were favoured by Omikami and, at the moment of defeat, swapped clothes and hid in the waves. A note names the Yuna twins as Mouun and Ayame, but it is not stated whether the Priestess is one of them.

384.content:
