Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale (also: Oratrice, Oratrice Mecanique, Mechanical Oratress of Cardinal Analysis): The Oratrice is a huge mechanical scale in the Opera Epiclese, Fontaine's court-theatre. At trials it weighed the arguments, returned the verdict the Iudex had to honour, and turned judgment into Indemnitium, the energy that powered the Court of Fontaine. Fontaine believed it was Furina's creation; in truth Focalors, the real Hydro Archon, built it and hid inside it. In 4.2 it sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death and executed Focalors. It has not functioned since.

Its name is French, roughly "Mechanical Oratress of Cardinal Analysis".

Appearance: A towering set of scales at the back of the stage, below the judge's seat, with four lights that come on as a trial progresses. Its core sits in a chamber in the opera house basement.

Lore: Navia explains a trial (4.0): the arguments of both sides, testimony and even the audience's emotions are projected onto the Oratrice, whose scales tip toward whoever is winning. The Iudex's decision is fed in as a reference, and the result is treated as the will of "justice" itself.

True purpose: Focalors revealed (4.2) that the Oratrice was no enactor of justice but a device built to kill the God of Justice and her divine throne. For 500 years she stored almost all its Indemnitium inside it; only a small fraction ever powered Fontaine.

Status as of 7.1: Since Focalors's execution (4.2) the Oratrice no longer works. Neuvillette hears cases and passes verdicts himself.

The opera house no longer produces Indemnitium; Neuvillette's full command of Pneumousia replaces it.

Gameplay: Gameplay: a fixed object in the Opera Epiclese. In the Archon Quest courtroom sections its scales and lights track the arguments.

385.content: Indemnitium is the energy the Oratrice produced from trials, drawn from people's belief in justice. It powered lamps and transport in the Court of Fontaine and the island of Erinnyes. Large doses are harmful: getting close to the Oratrice's core contaminated Lyney with a great deal of it.

386.comment: Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale: The Oratrice's verdict on the Hydro Archon
386.content: At Furina's trial in Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2), the Oratrice found her guilty as Neuvillette had, then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death, a shock because the trial had just proved Furina was not an Archon. The All-Devouring Narwhal attacked the courtroom. Inside the Oratrice, Focalors explained her plan to Neuvillette and was executed by its blade, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne and returning its authority to the Hydro Dragon.

387.content:
Padisarah (also: Padisarahs, Padisarah flower): The Padisarah is a holy, noble flower of Sumeru. It is very demanding about where it grows, and its buds are processed into valuable spices. Its archive text says it is a cultivar restored to the land by the Anahitian Blessing, after the original flower vanished.

It is a Sumeru local specialty and a cooking ingredient, seen around Sumeru City, Pardis Dhyai, the Palace of Alcazarzaray and the real Vanarana.

Appearance: Item text gives no description of the blossom beyond calling it holy and noble. The wiki's wild-growth image is the only visual reference; do not invent colours or scent.

Lore: The item text calls it a holy and noble plant with demanding growing conditions, whose flower buds become valuable spices. Its archive text adds that the name is said to come from an ancient deity. It tells of a time when three gods were on excellent terms and a great plain of lovely flowers lay in the land; people gathered the blossoms as incense to offer to their gods.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon changes its description; it remains a cultivated local specialty of Sumeru.

388.content:
Pale Flame (also: Stainless Bloom, Wise Doctor's Pinion, Moment of Cessation, Surpassing Cup, Mocking Mask): Pale Flame is a 4- and 5-star artifact set added in version 1.5. Its five pieces read like origin stories of the Fatui: the first Fatuus (Pierro) approaches a woman consumed by fire, a heretical scholar, a moneyman and a discarded constructed being, and each takes a role in the Tsaritsa's cause. The last piece, the Mocking Mask, is Pierro's own declaration. In it he says the blood of his Khaenri'ahn compatriots cannot be washed away and that he will become a jester who mocks fate.

The set is an early long-form hint that the Fatui's founders each carry a grievance against the heavens or the old order. The first four figures are not named in the item text; the wiki reads them as Harbingers.

Appearance: The five pieces are a flower (Stainless Bloom), a feather (Wise Doctor's Pinion), a clock-like sands piece (Moment of Cessation), a cup (Surpassing Cup) and a mask (Mocking Mask). Item text gives no further physical description.

Lore: The five pieces dramatise how the first Fatuus, Pierro, recruited early Fatui: a woman consumed by fire (read as Signora), a heretical scholar (Dottore), a man seeking worldly power (Pantalone) and a discarded divine creation (the Balladeer). The Mocking Mask is Pierro's own vow: because his Khaenri'ah compatriots' blood cannot be cleansed, he will become a jester who mocks fate and serve the Tsaritsa.

Owners: No owner is named. The text is narrated from the perspective of the first Fatuus about his recruits and himself.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; obtained from the Ridge Watch domain (Liyue) and an Artifact Strongbox. 4-piece: when an Elemental Skill hits an opponent, ATK +9% for 7s, up to 2 stacks, once per 0.3s. At 2 stacks the 2-piece Physical DMG Bonus increases by 100%. The wiki notes the effect applies only to the wearer, only for an on-field hit, and persists after swapping characters.

389.content: Artifact set whose five pieces of item text dramatise how Pierro, the first Fatuus, recruited early Fatui members, and state his own vow of mockery.

390.content: Pierro's own piece. He says the stain of his Khaenri'ah compatriots' blood cannot be cleansed and that he will become The Jester who laughs at fate, a Fatuus devoted to Her Majesty (the Tsaritsa), who understands his pain. He addresses his Fatui comrades, saying they carry both the fire of rage and the cold of eternal winter, have seen the callousness of the world's foundational principles, and should wear masks in mockery to rewrite destiny.

391.content:
Parametric Transformer (also: Parametric Transformer gadget, transmutation device): The Parametric Transformer is a gadget the Traveler wins in Liyue by solving an Adventurers' Guild treasure riddle. It is a mysterious device from the ruins that can "transmute" material objects: a heap of ordinary materials goes in, and different materials come out after elemental energy has charged it.

It is a placeable device, usable again after about a week. Its Archive text frames transmutation as accelerating the natural cycles of the world, and no maker or origin is given.

Appearance: In the inventory it is a four-star gadget. It is set down on a flat surface, where it shows a charge gauge. The wiki lists a "Deployed" state and a "Loaded" state. Canon does not describe its build beyond calling it a device.

Lore: Lan, who works at the Liyue Harbor Adventurers' Guild, posts a rumour about treasure near Tianqiu Valley. Nobody has found it. The Traveler follows a treasure map to Dunyu Ruins, reads a rhyming note about a giant tree, a road and a flight of stairs, opens three chests, and finds a strange box. Lan has never seen anything like it.

Lan says that, by the adventurers' code, whatever is found belongs to the finder, and that the Guild only wanted the experience of solving the riddle. Puzzled that the box was at Dunyu Ruins, a place searched many times, Lan arranges a closer search there.

Owners: The Traveler holds the only copy shown in canon. Lan hands it over as the finder's reward.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not in-world fact). The device is placed on a valid surface and loaded with non-event materials worth a total quality of 150 or more. It must be charged with Elemental damage, either from the player or from an environmental source such as an Electro Crystal. It cannot be used while in combat and is dismissed if the player wanders off or draws enemies, keeping the loaded materials for the next try. After use it has a cooldown of about 7 days. The first use grants the achievement "Transmutation Nuclide".

392.content: A Liyue Harbor world quest that gives the Parametric Transformer. Lan of the Adventurers' Guild passes on a treasure riddle near Tianqiu Valley. After fighting hilichurls the Traveler gets a treasure map to Dunyu Ruins, finds the Strange Note, opens three chests and returns with a Strange Box. Lan lets the Traveler keep it, with the reward.

393.content:
Peak Patrol Song (also: Halcyon Years Unending, Ode to Flowers): Peak Patrol Song is a 5-star sword: an obsidian blade of unparalleled sharpness and light as a song, modified by an artisan (linked to Xilonen) with a detachable Phlogiston device that plays records.

Its story is not about the blade but about Sakkuk, an old hero of the mines, and the songs of the Nanatzcayan.

Appearance: Canon says an obsidian blade of unparalleled sharpness, with a detachable record-playing Phlogiston device. Add no further details such as pattern or colour.

Lore: Every year, before the Embercore Flowers bloom, the mistress of the mountain mines comes alone to Tequemecan Valley to lay dew-kissed flowers for friends who never saw the dawn. Her once-hard heart has softened with age.

The sound of the mines and the artisans' songs shakes her from her bitter memories: the echoes of the Nanatzcayan have reached even this place, and she laughs.

Owners: No wielder is named. The description's only person is the artisan who modified the blade, linked to Xilonen.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat DEF; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.1.

394.comment: Peak Patrol Song: Halcyon Years Unending
394.content: Halcyon Years Unending is the passive of the sword Peak Patrol Song (gameplay): it builds Ode to Flowers stacks that raise the wielder's DEF and Elemental DMG Bonus, then gives nearby party members an Elemental DMG Bonus that scales with the wielder's DEF.

key: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon
395.comment: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon
395.content:
Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon (also: Clustered Storage Array): The Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon is a flawless piece of jade, the heart of the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L (nicknamed Ixlel), who ruled Chichen Uctokah, the original city of Ochkanatlan, before human civilisation was kindled. The Traveler receives it at the end of the Natlan World Quest "Open Your Heart to Me". Its energy is exhausted, so it can no longer command anything.

Its alternate name is Clustered Storage Array. The Traveler gathers the three Ancient Jadestone Fragments of Ixlel's broken heart, and she pours her last energy into them to restore it. Item text calls it a quest item and a memento.

Appearance: Item text describes only "a flawless piece of jade." Canon gives no size, shape or glow.

Lore: The item text says the heart once let its owner command every device in Ochkanatlan, "the ineffable city". It is now spent. The text also remarks that, like the half-humans who chased it, the Dragonlord's quest for perfection ended in something as cold and lifeless as jade.

In "Open Your Heart to Me", Ixlel speaks through a great dragon statue in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, deep under Ochkanatlan. She says a traitor tore her heart apart, hid the pieces in devices and used her memories to hold her there, forcing her to "sing" for his empire because he did not know how to run the city. She would not die enslaved, so she asked the Traveler, the "Chosen of Dragons", to gather the fragments, let her restore the heart with her remaining energy, and then take it out.

Owners: Original owner: Ixlel, the Dragonlord of Chichen Uctokah. It was taken from her and hidden in pieces by Och-Kan. Current holder as of 7.1: the Traveler, who keeps it as a memento after freeing her.

Gameplay: Gameplay: a quest item and memento from the 5.2 World Quest "Open Your Heart to Me".

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the heart as a solemn keepsake of a proud ruler's chosen end, not a weapon or power source.

396.comment: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon: Ixlel
396.content: Ixlel, the Ninth of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords and ruler of Chichen Uctokah, was a proud dragon who insisted on her full name, and her nickname came from Paimon. Trapped for thousands of years in a statue, she asked the Traveler for a dignified release and died after the Traveler cut the chains that bound her consciousness. Her heart is the Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon.

397.comment: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon: Ancient Jadestone Fragment
397.content: Three strange fragments scattered through the Old Core of Chu'ulel, which feel warm to the touch and are made of a material hard to identify. They are the pieces of Ixlel's torn heart. Once she restores them with her remaining life energy, they become the Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon.

398.content:
Perinheri (also: Hleobranto Innamorato): Sold by Hubel in the Court of Fontaine. Its author claims a Khaenri'ahn origin that nobody alive can verify, and it has grown over generations as an anthology with footnotes by later editors.

Appearance: A 3-star Book Collection (2 volumes). Vol. 2 carries two scholar's notes and a list of thanks naming contributors across 15 editions, which gives it the feel of a long-edited text.

Lore: Vol. 1: things from outside the world leak into the Kingdom, and its weapons destroy calamities that slip in. A sage tells the ruler a tale of sea people who honor shipwrecked strangers as possible gods. The Kingdom then founds an orphanage in case a being who transcends the gods arrives; orphans and outside wanderers are accepted too. Perinheri's first memory is being sent through a pitch-dark soot-filled corridor and asked 'Are you dead?', then seeing the crimson moon turn into a horrified eye. The adults tell him he is reborn. The awaited being never came, but many orphans became great knights, and Perinheri led them unless he competed with his best friend Hleobrant, whose rivalry turned deadly.
Vol. 2: Angelica arrives, claiming her priestly line's nation fell to Deus Auri. She will wed only the mightiest knight. Hleobrant is smitten and picks duels; she lists Njord, Alf, Alberich and Perinheri as the strongest. Convinced that killing Angelica would cure Hleobrant's madness, Perinheri hunts her. Outside the borders Hleobrant becomes beast-like; Angelica says it is the curse of forebears who forsook their god, while Perinheri, who drifted in, is free of it. At sunrise she reveals herself as freedom and tells Perinheri it is his to take, and he faces empty land.

Owners: No named owner; sold by the bookseller Hubel in the Quartier Narbonnais, Court of Fontaine.

Gameplay: Both volumes are bought from Hubel; this is a collectible lore text.

399.content: In the tale, Hleobrant is Perinheri's best friend and rival. Out of love for Angelica he grows reckless, and outside the Kingdom's borders his speech degrades into howls. Angelica attributes this to a curse on descendants of those who abandoned their god and came to the Kingdom, which she links to the pure-blooded aristocracy. The book does not say what became of him.

400.content:
Polestar Ballet Anthology (also: Black Snow Swan, The Seabird, The Envoy, The Firebird): Each volume is an excerpted script with cast, act headings, stage directions and spoken lines, in the manner of a printed libretto. The four ballets are separate stories. Black Snow Swan is the one the game connects to other content, including the character Odette and the sword Whitelake Frostfeather.

Appearance: A 4-star Book Collection of 4 volumes. The text uses stage directions in parentheses, tempo markings (adagio, presto), named variations and curtain calls, and some acts are skipped with ellipses.

Lore: **Black Snow Swan.** Odile, a black swan among white sisters, believes her colour is a shame. Queen Myrtha says it comes from human emotion, love and passion, a poison that fate uses as a snare, and promises three spirits across three nights. Bathilde de Petrichor (Spring), a Fontainian noble betrayed in love, Hamsatti (Summer), a princess of Pragjyotishpura who destroyed the man she loved and the dancer he loved, and Tatiana (Autumn), a snow swan, each warn that love is sorrow, cruelty and weakness. In Act III Odile answers that love and passion belong to the heart, not to Fate, dances thirty-two fouettes, and refuses eternal purity. Myrtha lets her go. At dawn the black swan sets out to fly higher than any snow swan.

Owners: No character is established as owning it. Vols. 2 to 4 are sold by Moes at Torchlight Books; Vol. 1 is obtained through the quest Variations on Belyi and Chernyi per the wiki.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a four-volume 4-star Book Collection. It has no combat function.

401.comment: Polestar Ballet Anthology: Black Snow Swan ballet
401.content: The Korolevskiy Troupe ballet in Vol. 1 of the Polestar Ballet Anthology. Odile, a black swan, is taught by Queen Myrtha and three spirits (Bathilde, Hamsatti, Tatiana) that love is a poison, then chooses love and flight over purity.

402.comment: Polestar Ballet Anthology: The Seabird, The Envoy and The Firebird
402.content: Vols. 2 to 4 of the anthology. The Seabird is about a composer and a singer who part. The Envoy is a comedy of mistaken identity in the reign of Emperor Monomakh. The Firebird has Khramov, Vaselisa and the Firebird Sirin overthrow the Demon King Berstuk.

403.content:
Primogem (also: Primogems): Primogems are the premium currency of Genshin Impact. Their item text calls them a primordial crystalline gem beyond the mundane world, shining with the condensed hopes and dreams of universes that once were. In play they are spent mainly on wishes.

Primogems are different from Mora, the ordinary currency of Teyvat. Canon never shows characters trading in them.

Appearance: A crystalline gem. The in-game description stresses that it is primordial and not of the ordinary world.

Lore: The only in-world text is the item description: a primordial gem, beyond the mundane world, containing the condensed hopes and dreams of universes that once were. Its wording echoes Genesis Crystals, whose text describes an energy crystal formed from pure potential and hope, with enough energy to create a newborn star. Neither is explained by a quest.

404.content:
Primordial Jade Cutter (also: Primordial Jade sword, Pányán Jiélǜ): Primordial Jade Cutter is a five-star sword of Liyue, a ceremonial blade masterfully carved from pure jade. Item text says that when Liyue first arose, Rex Lapis once walked the land with a sword hewn from jade. It was cut as a costly gift for peace and luxury, then bathed in blood in war. It is a legend rather than a quest object: no scene shows the sword.

It belongs to the Primordial Jade weapon series, the Liyue weapons tied to the Archon War era. The wiki's reading of the series is that the sword is the weapon Morax wielded after the gift never reached its recipient.

Lore: The item story is a lament. The jade edge, soaked in blood long ago, still looks new; rain washed the blood away over a thousand years, but the thoughts and grudges gathered around it linger. A friend, now long forgotten, once said that nephrite has the soul of the Bishui River's gentle heart and will in time cleanse itself of old grudges, and then asked who would ease the agony the jade feels at having become an instrument of slaughter.

Owners: Item text names no owner beyond the legendary Rex Lapis (Morax, the Geo Archon, who as Zhongli appears in the game). It does not say the sword ever left his hands, and no playable character is attached to it by canon.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star sword from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT Rate 9.6%. Passive "Protector's Virtue": HP rises 20-40% and the wielder gains ATK equal to 1.2-2.4% of Max HP, at refinements 1 to 5. The bonus does not apply if the wielder has fallen or is not in the party.

405.content:
Primordial Jade Winged-Spear (also: Primordial Jade Winged Spear, Hépú Yuān): Primordial Jade Winged-Spear is a five-star polearm of Liyue. Its item story is a creation legend: at Liyue's foundation a sea behemoth called Baqiu, which the Geo Archon's own Geo Whale could not beat, drowned settlements with its waves. The Geo Archon hand-forged a black kite from jade and stone, it dove into the sea, and Baqiu sank for good.

It is part of the Primordial Jade series, the Liyue weapons of the Archon War era. Despite its polearm form the text describes the origin object as a kite (a bird), not a spear.

Appearance: Item text says only that the Geo Archon fashioned a black kite by hand from jade and stones, and that the stone bird took flight once forged. Nothing is said of the polearm's own look; the name's "Winged" and the kite are the only visual hints.

Lore: Item story: when Liyue was founded, monsters and gods still ruled the seas and the forebears lived in fear, fighting the sea with all they could. Over many ages a behemoth rose that dominated the waters; even the Geo Archon's Geo Whale could not triumph. Liyue's people called it Baqiu, a beast without rival in the ocean's deepest abyss, whose enormous waves washed away whole settlements.

Owners: The item text names no later owner. In promotional art Xiao wields the ascended version in his official art and character demo; that is presentation, not a canon statement that Xiao owns this exact weapon.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star polearm in the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 48, secondary stat CRIT Rate 4.8%. Passive "Eagle Spear of Justice": on hit, ATK rises 3.2-6.0% for 6 seconds, up to 7 stacks, once every 0.3 seconds; at max stacks DMG dealt rises 12-24% (refinements 1 to 5). The wielder must be on the field to gain stacks.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): an old Liyue sailors' and coast-dwellers' legend of the time before the harbour, useful for themes of the sea as an enemy and of a god's ingenuity. Keep it a tale; no character in canon can confirm it.

406.content: Baqiu is the sea behemoth named in the Primordial Jade Winged-Spear item text, a beast that dominated the seas around early Liyue, washed away settlements with its waves and defeated the Geo Whale of the Geo Archon. It was finally sunk by a black jade-and-stone kite the Geo Archon made. It appears only in that item text.

key: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation
407.comment: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation
407.content:
Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation (also: Mina of the Fallen Nation): Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation is a six-volume Inazuman adventure novel series, sold by Kuroda at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. A wandering samurai in luxurious robes, accompanied by a small girl in an oversized haori, takes a princess prophesied to bring destruction on a journey to the Sky Tower at the centre of the world. The blurbs sell it as a hugely popular romantic adventure.

It is an in-world work of fiction, so nothing in it is evidence about Teyvat's real history. It is notable in Inazuma for its ironic, genre-aware voice: the narrator jokes about plot conventions.

Appearance: Six paperback-style instalments. Each volume has a short blurb of the kind used to advertise serialised fiction. The narration is chatty and self-aware. Vol. 6 includes an appendix on the setting, with the wicked overlords and monsters who did not appear in the story.

Lore: Vol. 1: after thirteen years of peace, a century-scale age of warring states begins; a wandering samurai and a girl stop at a checkpoint where the samurai quickly disposes of three ashigaru. Vol. 2: the princess asks what the samurai thinks about her prophesied destruction; he calls the prophecy an excuse for war. Vol. 3: they see the devastation the war has caused. Vol. 4: a flashback. Vol. 5: at the Sky Tower the onmyouji reveal their plan. Vol. 6: the samurai walks the desert and leaves for another world.

Owners: No individual owner. Kuroda at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City sells Vols. 1 to 4 and 6; Vol. 5 is in the left-hand room of the Yashiro Commission Headquarters.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible six-volume book collection added in version 2.1; reading is purely lore.

408.comment: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation: Nakura's Hex
408.content: In the novel, Nakura's Hex is a sorcery created by the Onmyouji of the Sky Tower that drains life from living things and the land, passing it to powerful samurai and feeding a war that has lasted over a century. The samurai who exploit it are the Nakura Daimyo.

409.comment: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation: The Princess Who Brings Destruction
409.content: The titular princess is prophesied to destroy the world. The samurai says the prophecy is an excuse for war; the princess wants to save the world anyway. By Vol. 6 the story ends with the samurai travelling on to another world.

410.content:
Prized Isshin Blade (also: Accursed Isshin blade, the cursed Isshin sword): The Prized Isshin Blade is a four-star sword that exists only inside Kaedehara Kazuha's Acer Palmatum Chapter, Act I ("A Strange and Friendless Road", Version 2.8). It is a blade full of Tatarigami malice that possesses a samurai and goes hunting for Kazuha, wanting to prove that the Isshin Art can beat even the Shogun. Kazuha defeats it, the curse drains out of it, and at the end of the quest it is remade into the ordinary, obtainable Kagotsurube Isshin.

It appears in two quest forms: an Awakened form while it is still dangerous, and a Shattered form once the curse has been worn down. It cannot be kept as a weapon; the lasting result of the quest is the Kagotsurube Isshin.

Appearance: The Awakened description speaks of an ominous purple aura clinging to a bizarre blade, with the power to control its wielder's heart and mind. After the curse weakens, the text says the aura's wickedness and hostility have decreased greatly. The Shattered form is described as a battered cursed blade showing its true form, its innate endowment ground to dust by its journey.

Lore: In the quest the Traveler and Paimon are attacked on Byakko Plain by a samurai who is really looking for Kazuha. Investigation leads through Ritou, the Tenryou Commission and the Amenoma Smithy to a small island off Inazuma City, where they find Amenoma Yuuya, a samurai of the Amenoma Clan, possessed by the sword. The sword speaks for itself. It says it was the prized weapon of an Isshin smith who failed the Shogun's tasks and exiled himself to Snezhnaya, and that after the smith died it began possessing people to make its way back to Inazuma and show that it was the ultimate weapon the Shogun had carelessly lost.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a four-star sword, base ATK 42, secondary stat ATK. Passive "Wandering Striker": Normal, Charged or Plunging Attacks that hit an opponent release an Accursed Spirit for AoE Physical DMG equal to 180% of ATK, once every 8s, and the wielder's DMG is reduced by 50%. The Awakened form also restores HP equal to 100% of ATK; the Shattered form does not. In the Awakened form the secondary stat is about 41.3% at Level 90 on entering the Occupied Hold and drops to about 20.7% after the second fight, making it the first weapon with different secondary-stat values at the same level.

411.content: The Kagotsurube Isshin is the four-star sword the cursed blade becomes at the end of "A Strange and Friendless Road". Its own item text credits the swordsmith Akame Kanenaga of the Akame School, which pursued the killer-blade ideal of the Isshin Art, and says it was forged in a snow-covered northern land rather than in Inazuma. The quest presents the rebirth as the sword giving up its consciousness so that it can serve as reference material for the Isshin Art.

412.content:
Prototype Archaic (also: Prototype Gǔhuá): Prototype Archaic is a forgeable 4-star claymore of the Prototype series. Its description calls it an ancient greatsword discovered in Blackcliff Forge that swings with such force it seems to cut through reality. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

The item text credits the master craftsman Han Wu and the Yun family forge with building it as the first greatsword of a new line of designs called the prototypes.

Appearance: Understated: dull, blotchy gold that hid its true strength. Its hilt is made from a rare ore and the blade from fine steel, and it weighs close to forty pounds according to the text. Swung, it shows blinding flashes of light.

Lore: It is an ancient prototype greatsword from Liyue's arsenal. The batch number has faded and no records confirm the date of production.

After the great disaster, the Yun family forge joined forces with Han Wu to push past the limits of contemporary blade design. The result was a new series of weapon models simply called the prototypes, and this greatsword was the first built to the new design. It was weighty but not unwieldy.

Owners: Han Wu is its maker. The martial artist who named it is unnamed in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star claymore, base ATK 44, ATK% secondary stat (6 per cent). Passive Crush: Normal or Charged Attacks have a 50 per cent chance on hit to deal extra AoE Physical damage of 240 to 480 per cent ATK (by refinement), at most once every 15s. It is obtained by forging (Northlander Claymore Billet, 50 Crystal Chunk, 50 White Iron Chunk, 500 Mora). It is the claymore of the Prototype series, whose other weapons include Prototype Rancour (sword), Prototype Crescent (bow), Prototype Starglitter (polearm) and Prototype Amber (catalyst).

413.content: In the game's story texts the prototypes are the new weapon models born when the Yun family forge and Han Wu revolutionised their craft after the great disaster. Prototype Archaic is described as the first greatsword of the line, later copied thousands of times in Liyue.

414.content:
Pyro Gnosis (also: Natlan's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Pyro Archon, Pyro Archon's Gnosis): The Pyro Gnosis is the Gnosis of Natlan's Pyro Archon, Mavuika, and the only one of the seven the Fatui never obtained. Capitano fought Mavuika for it and failed. In 6.6 she gave it away so Nahida could burn the corrupted Irminsul, and it vanished in the fire. As of 7.1 nobody knows where it is.

It also holds a terrible emergency function: it could drain every soul and memory in Natlan's Night Kingdom into a net shielding the Ley Lines from the Abyss, erasing Natlan's history. Mavuika always refused to use it.

Appearance: Like every Gnosis, a small, gleaming chess-piece-like object carried inside its Archon's chest. Holding it, the Traveler found it strangely ordinary and not heavy. Canon gives no description of its specific design.

Lore: Mavuika revealed the secret in 5.1: the Pyro Archons kept it as a worst-case contingency against the Abyss. The net would cost the Night Kingdom's dead, memories and legends, and could still corrode if the Ley Lines were not repaired.

Owners: Mavuika until 6.6; then briefly the Traveler and Nahida. No known holder since. Capitano sought it for the Tsaritsa but never held it.

Status as of 7.1: Missing as of 7.1; the Tsaritsa holds the other six. In 7.1 the Traveler told her it burned with Irminsul and, per Mavuika, returned to the Ley Lines. She replied that remains of the Third Descender cannot coexist with the Ley Lines for long and expects it to resurface.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a story object in Archon Quest cutscenes and dialogue only; not an obtainable item.

415.comment: Pyro Gnosis: The Night Kingdom soul-net
415.content: Natlan's secret last resort, revealed by Mavuika in The Flickering Light Splits in Twain (5.1): the Pyro Gnosis can drain every soul, memory and legend in the Night Kingdom and weave them into a giant net around Natlan's Ley Lines to hold back Abyssal corrosion. The cost is the erasure of Natlan's history and culture, and the net can still corrode unless the damaged Ley Lines are repaired in time. Mavuika said the Pyro Archons had to plan for the worst case given the Abyss, but she cared about how Natlan won and refused to use it except as a last resort.

416.comment: Pyro Gnosis: Capitano's duel for the Gnosis
416.content: In Chapter V Act II (5.0), Capitano led the Fatui into the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to seize the Gnosis and fought Mavuika, who wounded him with one full-power strike before Night-Wind smoke carried him off. When a subordinate later suggested taking it from the weakened Archon, he refused, counting the duel as his defeat. He later said Mavuika had held back to protect the spectators, and she called them evenly matched. He said he wanted the Gnosis chiefly to save Natlan and would only have taken it to Snezhnaya afterwards. After their duel he asked the Tsaritsa to release him from the mission and she agreed (Mavuika reported this in 5.3 from a letter he left behind); Mavuika doubted the Tsaritsa would let the matter rest, since it was the last Gnosis the Fatui lacked.

key: Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne
417.content:
Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow (also: Rain Bow, Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne): Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow is a 4-star bow, an ancient ceremonial weapon passed down by the Masters of the Night-Wind, dark and forever wreathed in an unshakable chill. Its story tells of a covenant between a young priest and a rainbow-winged dragon.

It was an event reward in Version 6.2 (Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey). The story picks up after Cinder City's fall and Maghan's death, and ends with the first Iktomisaurus appearing.

Appearance: Canon description: a dark bow forever wreathed in chill. Keep to that; no added carvings or colours.

Lore: Cinder City and its usurper's dream collapsed in a blaze when the scarlet-eyed hero called down the god's fiery wrath and burned the corrupt throne to ash. Decades earlier Maghan the dragon slayer had driven the old ruler from the deep valleys.

The young priest Wagadu laid Maghan to rest in a nameless grave as he had wished, took up his bow and walked into the mist-shrouded mountains. He did not understand what "renew the covenant" and "restore peace" meant; he thought he was returning the cherished bow to the Night Realm to soothe spirits abandoned since ancient sacrifices.

Owners: Used by Maghan in the story; carried into the Night Realm by Wagadu. No modern bearer is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star bow, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat Energy Recharge (10%). Event reward of Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (Version 6.2); refinement material is Refined Heart.

key: Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne
418.comment: Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow: Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne
418.content: Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne is the passive of the bow Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow (gameplay): hitting enemies while off-field grants a temporary ATK boost.

key: Records of Hanan Pacha book collection
419.content:
Records of Hanan Pacha (also: Records of Hanan Pacha book collection): Records of Hanan Pacha is a three-volume collection of Natlan folk tales about the Sage of the Stolen Flame, Waxaklahun Ubah Kan. Vol. 1 tells how he and a companion, Chaac, tricked a vain winged dragon and took the power of phlogiston. Vol. 2 tells how they raised the land of Hanan Pacha and taught people to use it. Vol. 3 tells how the people broke a taboo and were driven out. The game itself labels it a fable with no basis in historical fact.

The narrator is an unnamed storyteller who speaks to listeners and jokes with them about the plot. The books give Natlan's popular account of how humans first gained phlogiston and how the first permanent tribe came to be.

Appearance: A readable book collection in Natlan, in three volumes. Vol. 1 and 2 are found at the Scions of the Canopy (on crates near the patrolling guard Yawar, and next to Amauta); vol. 3 is in front of Battuta at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. No author or publisher is listed.

Lore: Told in the age of dragons, when the Lord of the Night ruled the night realm and no Pyro Archon yet existed. Humans had no Visions and were at the mercy of the elements until the Sage brought phlogiston from the "red and black land".

The sage tricks a vain dragon and takes its phlogiston, raises Hanan Pacha with Chaac to teach people, then expels them after the Lord of the Night gets them drunk. Chaac goes on to found settled tribes.

Owners: No individual owns it; the volumes lie at fixed locations in Natlan.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible book collection with no stats. Volumes are found in Natlan at the Scions of the Canopy and the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

420.comment: Records of Hanan Pacha: Sage of the Stolen Flame
420.content: In the Records of Hanan Pacha, the Sage is the cleverest figure in history, who took phlogiston from a dragon, taught it to humans and raised Hanan Pacha, then left Natlan after the people broke his taboo. The text says his homeland is not named and implies he will one day return. The book is a fable; do not use it as proof of what he actually did.

421.comment: Records of Hanan Pacha: Hanan Pacha (legend)
421.content: In the tale, Hanan Pacha was once a whole stretch of land floating above the clouds, visible from anywhere in Natlan. People came up through the power of phlogiston to learn from the Sage and settled there. Today the Upper Sanctum is a ring of islands, accessible only via Spiritways.

422.comment: Records of Hanan Pacha: The Winged Dragon and Pyrophosphorite
422.content: The fable's dragon is a vain winged creature in the red and black lands that took the treasures of the sleeping volcano lord Xiuhcoatl. Its pride rested on Pyrophosphorite, a rainbow crystal of primal fire. The Sage and Chaac blinded and tricked it with disguises and grainfruit replacements, and the Sage broke the crystal to gain phlogiston.

423.content:
Records of Jueyun (also: Jueyun Records): Records of Jueyun is a six-volume book collection of folk stories, myths and legends of Liyue by an author named Wuyuan. Each volume handles one tale: living stone beasts, a Sea God who takes brides, the haunted ruins of Wuwang Hill, the lonely seelie of the mountains, the gentle qilin, and the ancient Dunyu Ruins. The in-game blurb calls it quite a page turner.

The collection shows how ordinary Liyue people explain their landscape, and what local belief says about adepti and illuminated beasts. It is hearsay, not history: the compilers repeatedly hedge.

Appearance: Six short prose pieces in a storyteller's voice, each under a single-title heading (Stone Beasts, Palace Beneath the Sea, Wuwang, Mountain Spirits, Qilin, Hidden Jade). The narrator mixes local rumour with dry asides, such as noting that nobody has actually seen a stone beast move.

Lore: - Vol. 1, Stone Beasts: Liyue's animal statues are said to wake on cool autumn nights and wander. Qingce elders say they are illuminated beasts who fought beside Rex Lapis in the Archon War and asked him to turn their mortal flesh to lasting stone.
- Vol. 2, Palace Beneath the Sea: a Sea God collects a village bride each festival in return for calm seas. One bride is released, keeps his sea-snail shell, and years later blows it when her own daughter is to be given up; the village is drowned.
- Vol. 3, Wuwang: Wuwang Hill, north of Mt. Qingce, is haunted by spirits that lure travellers off the path.
- Vol. 4, Mountain Spirits: seelie are held to be good omens that guide travellers and Vision-bearers to treasure.
- Vol. 5, Qilin: gentle illuminated beasts of the mountains who sometimes take human form and live among mortals.
- Vol. 6, Hidden Jade: the Dunyu Ruins, north of Nantianmen and northwest of Liyue Harbor, were a walled city whose people sealed it and left.

- Vol. 1 says locals who know the land have long noted that animal statues change place and posture overnight, and that campers hear a deep sound like flowing water. Bishui River fishermen, Silvergrass harvesters of Dihua Marsh and old miners share the story. The narrator admits nobody has witnessed a stone beast moving.
- Vol. 2 ends cruelly: the Sea God's tidal embrace swallows the sleeping village and its elders, and mother and daughter ride his clam carriage into the sea. The Sea God had earlier said his palace sheltered women who were driven from their villages.
- Vol. 3 explains the name: Wuwang means prudence, so the hill is where the prudent are punished. A village lies abandoned at its foot. A Qingce children's fable says its young people threw themselves into the Bishui River, enchanted by a distant sea monster's song, and drifted to the Sea of Clouds. The text then offers an explanation for the haunting: the ley lines remember what people forget, and unconsciously recreate the dead village's past as spirits.
- Vol. 4 gives two readings of the seelie: auspicious souls of departed adepti or old benevolent gods, or echoes of friendless strangers who guide the lost home. A mountain legend adds that seelie once had beautiful bodies and great wisdom, long before the adepti, and links their ancestor to a traveller from the Sea of Stars, an oath witnessed by the three sisters of the Lunar Palace, and a catastrophe thirty days later that separated them and wiped their memories. The narrator dismisses all this as incoherent folk tale.
- Vol. 5 says that after the Archon War many adepti withdrew from society at Rex Lapis' direction, but some illuminated beasts chose to stay and help mortals, leaving unusual bloodlines in Liyue Harbor. A tale of a young qilin who ate a herb gatherer's lotus-leaf clothes at a mountain pool and took human form has two endings: she leaves a child in a basket at his door, or she stays and raises children with him.
- Vol. 6 says Dunyu means the land to which beauteous jade flees. The legend tells of a star that fell onto the plains west of Liyue and made the chasm, from which jade emerged and supported a thousand years of mining. A fragment fell in northern Lisha and later leapt back to the sky, leaving a pit where humans built fortresses. These kept good relations with Liyue Harbor until about 500 years ago, when the black calamity and the rise of the Abyss led the residents to seal the city and leave. The text says even the old adepti and yaksha are silent about why.

Owners: No individual owner. Vol. 1: Granny Ruoxin's home in Qingce Village; Jifang gives it as a dialogue reward. Vol. 2: Wuyuan gives it as a dialogue reward; Jifang also sells it. Vol. 3: a restaurant table at Wangshu Inn where Huangshan sits. Vols. 4-6: sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse in Liyue Harbor.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible book collection read for lore only.

424.comment: Records of Jueyun: The Sea God's Bride
424.content: A Liyue folk tale in Records of Jueyun Vol. 2. Each festival a village sends a bride to a Sea God in exchange for a year without storms. One bride is freed and given a conch to sound when she regrets leaving; she does so when the elders come for her daughter, and the Sea God drowns the village. The god is not identified.

key: hill where the prudent are punished
425.comment: Records of Jueyun: Wuwang Hill Legend
425.content: Per Records of Jueyun Vol. 3, Wuwang Hill is haunted by lingering spirits that imitate the voices of the dead and lead travellers astray. The book gives a Qingce children's fable and an explanation that the ley lines unconsciously replay the abandoned village's past.

426.comment: Records of Jueyun: Dunyu Ruins Legend
426.content: Records of Jueyun Vol. 6 says Dunyu is the land to which beauteous jade flees. A star fell on the plains west of Liyue, making the chasm; a fragment fell in northern Lisha, and the Dunyu fortresses were built in the pit it left. Their people sealed the city and left about 500 years ago, at the time of the black calamity; the reason is not known, even to old adepti and yaksha.

key: Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord
427.content:
Redhorn Stonethresher (also: Redhorn Pestle, Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord): Redhorn Stonethresher is a five-star claymore whose item story is a folk tale. Its full name is the "Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord", and it was the beloved blade of an eccentric known as the "Otogi Kongou Lion King". Because both names were too long, the village children called the weapon the Redhorn Pestle and its wielder the Otogi King.

The tale is told partly in affectionate mockery: the Otogi King was a boaster with real strength, and the weapon's legendary reputation outlived the man who never returned.

Appearance: The item story describes the Redhorn Pestle as a weapon made from an enchanted monster's horn. It does not describe colour or shape beyond that; the in-game model is a very large blade. Avoid inventing further detail.

Lore: In the children's telling, the weapon's bite made bake-kitsune, bake-danuki and evil demons beg for mercy, and even the Great Tengu Reizenbou of Mt. Yougou feared it. The children did not believe this. The text says the Otogi King really was strong, so strong that seven men together could not push him out of a sumo ring, and that he would kick a tree to bring down fruit for children who could not reach it. He also once kicked down a whole tree, a Lavender Melon tree, and was chased into the mountains by an old man.

Owners: Former owner: the Otogi Kongou Lion King, called the Otogi King by children. No other owner is named. The same figure is the recipient of Uraku Misugiri in that sword's text. The weapon is an ordinary player weapon in-game.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star claymore from the Otogi King series, base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT DMG 19.2%. Passive "Gokadaiou Otogibanashi": increases DEF by 28-56% and adds bonus damage to Normal and Charged Attacks equal to 40-80% of DEF at refinement 1-5. It was the event-exclusive weapon of the Version 2.3 Epitome Invocation, alongside Skyward Harp.

428.content: The Otogi King is the nickname given by village children to the Otogi Kongou Lion King, a loud, eccentric Inazuma warrior who carried the Redhorn Pestle and bragged that he would send monsters packing. The Redhorn Stonethresher text portrays him as a boastful prankster; Uraku Misugiri's text adds that he loved plays, toys and clothes and went into battle in gold brocade with painted features. It also describes him as an oni who earned the villagers' nickname "The Great Idiot" and did not dislike it. His name remains unconfirmed beyond those titles.

429.content:
Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes (also: Proof of the Cognoscenti, Proofs of the Cognoscenti, Cognoscenti keepsakes, Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest, Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather, Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow, Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication, Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask): The Proofs of the Cognoscenti are five quest-item relics in Nod-Krai, each "said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller", founder of the Treasure Hoarders: a silver mask, a black feather, a stopped timepiece, a goblet and a rusted flower. Legend says they point to his Great Treasure. The Traveler collects all five in East of the Moon, West of the Sun.

"Reed Miller" was an alias worn by at least three people, so the legend the keepsakes carry is deliberately tangled. The collective name used here is this archive's label, not an in-game title.

Appearance: - Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask: a cold, plain silver mask with no decoration but the frosty moonlight on its surface.
- Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather: a feather as dark as night.
- Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow: a timepiece that stopped long ago.
- Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication: a lavishly decorated goblet.
- Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest: an artificial flower stained with rust.

Lore: Folk retellings of the master thief, mixing legend and rumour, not eyewitness history.

Owners and finding: All five end up with the Traveler, one per quest in East of the Moon, West of the Sun. The first four can be done in any order; the Flower unlocks only after the other four.

Gameplay: Gameplay (labelled): the five are quest items with no combat or stat use; the wiki styles them as flower, plume, sands, goblet and circlet pieces only for presentation.

430.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Proof of the Cognoscenti
430.content: Five relics said to be keepsakes of Reed Miller, the Treasure Hoarders' founder, that legend claims point toward Reed Miller's Great Treasure: Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest (flower), Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather (plume), Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow (sands), Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication (goblet) and Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask (circlet). The Traveler gathers them in East of the Moon, West of the Sun. Their texts retell the Reed Miller legend, which canon shows was shaped by several people using one alias, and one text calls the tokens counterfeits.

key: silver mask of the master thief
431.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask
431.content: A plain silver mask under frost-pale light. Its item text says the master thief wore it after surviving a failed execution, then removed it for good after the Cataclysm; rumours say he wore it to hide from the searches in Snezhnaya, to cover executioner's marks, or from weariness of the crowd. The thief scorned both gods and nobles. The last line, which switches to "her" and moonlight from a high tower, suggests the wearer at the end was a woman (the wiki reads this as Alia), but the text does not say so directly. Obtained in The Tale-Telling Heart.

432.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather
432.content: A night-black feather whose text recalls Snezhnaya before the Cataclysm: nobles ruled for the Tsar, the poor were told the nobles bore "the sin of fullness" on their behalf, and the master thief raised a black raven emblem to gather the despised and promise an Elysium built on the wealth of the haughty. It is found beneath the Eye of Kratti in Whisper Beneath the Waves.

433.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow
433.content: A timepiece that stopped long ago, left by Miller for Grazina in the bunker in Wavechaser Plain. Its text mourns the failed dreams of a prophesied ruler, a would-be heir, a maid and an adopted son, and admits the tokens are counterfeit work that can nevertheless guide a finder to the great treasure. Obtained in Return to Sender (listed as added in 6.3).

434.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication
434.content: A lavishly adorned goblet. Its text describes the master thief after the mask: no longer chasing fallen nobles' wealth, taking many identities and spreading song and wine among both nobles and commoners until the thief and the legend blurred. The Fatui held it first; the Traveler gets it in The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot.

435.comment: Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes: Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest
435.content: A rusty artificial flower. Its text collects legendary tricks played on the powerful, notes that the first master thief "never lied" and promised his partner Alia he would not take risks, and ends with the execution and the woman who then took his name. It is the last Proof, given by Hiljetta in The Raven's Legacy.

436.content:
Reliquary of Truth: Reliquary of Truth is a 5-star catalyst added in Version 6.1. The in-game description calls it an angular box carved from gold and jade that legend says was once enshrined in a temple deep within Tulaytullah, the Sapphire City. Its story is about a young noble named Goudarz, who is given a power by a holy sage in exchange for an honest answer, and who rises as the king Saleb Dowleh, a king whose reign is built on lies.

The weapon connects to the Sapphire City and its Tighnarian people, a part of the Great Red Sand's history after King Deshret. It also links to the Lunar-Bloom reaction in its gameplay passive.

Appearance: An angular box of gold and jade. Canon text gives no more detail than that.

Lore: After the great tower of Shah Ramshahr fell, the royal power passed among states as fleeting as dew. The nobles of Tulaytullah, free of the tyrant, followed false sages into new carnage. By the time the brutal Khagans arrived on horseback, no warriors guarded the Garden of Endless Pillars, and foreign soldiers and tax collectors preyed on the weary people. People then looked back to the brief reign of King Humayun.

The young noble Goudarz enters a sacred hall beneath the sands, the palace of the Ibis King, wisest of the seven sage monks and keeper of records. The wise men of Tighnar had long fled and the sanctuary lay buried. From a dried-up spring a voice answers him and says it can grant a power never seen by prophet or proselyte, but only if he answers the riddles that the lord of flowers and oases left for the sage's master, King Deshret, who fell into a poisonous dream before answering. Goudarz asks to hear them and promises honest, mortal answers.

Owners: No owner is named. Goudarz, later King Saleb Dowleh, receives the Staff of Falsehoods in the story; the reliquary itself is only said to have been enshrined in a temple of Tulaytullah.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star catalyst released in Version 6.1 (2025-10-22), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT DMG. Passive Essence of Falsity raises CRIT Rate; casting an Elemental Skill grants Secret of Lies (Elemental Mastery for 12 s), dealing Lunar-Bloom DMG grants Moon of Truth (CRIT DMG for 4 s), and when both are active their results are increased by 50%.

437.content:
Retracing Bolide (also: Summer Night's Bloom, Summer Night's Finale, Summer Night's Moment, Summer Night's Waterballoon, Summer Night's Mask): Retracing Bolide is an Inazuma artifact set from launch (Domain of Guyun). Its five "Summer Night's" pieces record, in a man's voice, meetings with a fox-eyed woman at summer festivals near Mt. Yougou: lost as a child, nursing a sprained ankle as a teenager, and as an adult hoping to see her again. The wiki links her to Kitsune Saiguu.

The set is framed as an Inazuma ghost story about meetings between the human and the inhuman. It is a memory of kindness and parting, not a monster tale.

Lore: At a summer festival a lost child, separated from his parents by the crowd carrying the divine palanquin, cries by the torii gates on the road to the shrine. A beautiful woman with fox-like eyes takes his hand and offers to see fireworks, throw darts and play fusen. Years later, on a festival night, the same woman sits beside him on a rock by the wayside, unchanged after ten years, and invites him to watch the fireworks with wine.

The woman never ages: in the pocket-watch piece, the teenager (hurt, with a broken watch while the girl he admired fetched ointment) meets her after ten years and she has not changed. Later, in the dart piece, he is a man whose wife is pregnant; he climbs the mountain carrying the water balloon from age seven, the fox mask from seventeen and a flower that would not wilt, and thinks he sees her in white on the same rock, but it is only a sunbathing fox that flees, leaving an old throwing dart.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): 4 and 5 star set from the Domain of Guyun and its strongbox. 2-piece: Shield Strength +35% (affects only the wearer). 4-piece: while shielded, +40% Normal and Charged Attack DMG. Introduced in 1.0.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present it as a wistful Inazuma festival memory. The fox-eyed woman is kind, teasing and unexplained; do not state definitively that the fox on the rock was her.

438.content: The goblet piece: a finely made water balloon. The narrator as a child is separated from his parents at the summer festival, cries by the torii gates and is found by a fox-eyed lady who offers fireworks, darts and fusen.

439.content: The sands piece: a stopped pocket watch. On a festival night, a young man walking to the shrine with a girl he admired hears a lost child crying, falls and breaks the watch. A masked woman sits by him on a rock and offers to watch the fireworks.

440.content: The plume piece: a wooden throwing dart. The man, whose wife is expecting, climbs Mt. Yougou with the water balloon, mask and flower; he sees what looks like the woman in white but finds only a fox that flees, leaving a dart.

441.content: The flower piece: an artificial summer festival flower that never wilts. It is the final thing left to remember the foxy-eyed woman who disappeared without a trace.

442.content: The circlet piece: a mask in the image of a legendary fox deity. People wear such masks hoping to gain her transformation ability. A note on the back apologises for leaving under the fireworks and wishes the finder well.

443.content:
Revelations of Divine Love: Its theme, per the in-game description, is the distinction between the love of the gods and human love. It concludes that compassion, friendship and romantic affection are all imbued with the sacred, since they arise from the same longing for freedom.

Appearance: A quest item with an icon and description only. No text of the poems can be read in game.

Lore: The Anemo Archon is the god of freedom in Mondstadt, so the book's conclusion ties human warmth to the divine and to freedom alike. The authorship claim is hedged ("said to have been composed"), and no priest is named.

Owners: Hannelore gives it to the Traveler. No other owner is established.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a Quest Item with no combat function, obtained through Hannelore's perfume dialogue branch (wiki: Luna VI, taken as 6.5), together with 2 Hero's Wit and 21,500 Mora.

444.comment: Revelations of Divine Love: Hannelore and Dornman Port
444.content: Hannelore is an open-world nun of the Church of Favonius at roofless Dornman Port, where she listens to the confessions of merchants and sailors. In the perfume branch she declines to keep the Traveler's gift and gives Revelations of Divine Love in return. The wiki has no further profile for her.

445.content:
Rex Incognito (also: Rex Incognito novel): Rex Incognito is a four-volume Liyue fantasy novel telling of Rex Lapis' incognito excursions among mortals. A framing story set in the antique shop Xigu Antiques, run by Min'gui, surrounds tales of a jade craftsman and a harsh fishing-boat owner. Its running theme is that rules matter less than a person's own judgement, and that a relic is worth its story.

The in-game blurbs say fact merges with fiction. Treat it as popular Liyue literature about the Geo Archon, not as history; its closing twist deliberately undermines its own claims.

Appearance: Four unillustrated chapters in alternating voices: a shop-set frame, then nested stories-within-stories. The mood is wry and playful, with an unnamed visitor who is a pedantic young expert with amber or golden eyes and dark long robes.

Lore: - Vol. 1: At night, Xigu Antiques of Feiyun Slope is visited by a black-robed young man who calls a damaged jade plaque in her shop a modern counterfeit. He argues that ancient tribes of Rex Lapis' followers carved such plaques as stand-in currency before Mora existed. The owner, Min'gui, says she can disprove his verdict with a story.
- Vol. 2: A prankish jade carver in Mingyun Village is asked by an amber-eyed woman to carve the true likeness of the Lord of Geo from what he has seen, or go unpaid. He delivers a plaque showing a woman and explains his three-day process of learning, observing and carving by heart.
- Vol. 3: A harsh fishing-boat owner in Liyue Harbor docks the pay of a new hand, a bashful youth from Qingce Village, who tells him a story about a jade plaque while someone takes the docked wages from the owner's pocket and returns them to the labourers.
- Vol. 4: Back in the shop, Min'gui argues that antiques are valued for their stories. The young noble buys the plaque, and admits his jade-currency theory was invented.

- Vol. 1 lists the shop's curios: a Fontaine timepiece, Sumeru incense, a Mondstadt aristocrat's goblet, a stool an adeptus once sat on, a teacup the Lord of Geo sipped from and a vase the Anemo Archon accidentally broke. The plaque, bought from an adventurer who brought it out of an abandoned palace deep in the abyss, cost Min'gui much of her fortune.
- The young man notes that this plaque carries a woman's image, unusual for the period, and that there is no historical record or physical evidence of Rex Lapis ever taking female form.
- Vol. 2's carver was known for contrary commissions, such as a fleeing boar for a hunter statue and an empty throne for a ruler. The Lord of Geo was rumoured to be cold and unfeeling, but trusted because his laws made trade fair.
- Vol. 3's youth asks why a person should do the work they hate most; the owner says that is how the world works, and the youth replies that perhaps that was not what Rex Lapis meant by his rules.
- Vol. 4 draws the moral that Rex Lapis never forced mortals to live by contracts as a perfect template, since the rules are a means rather than the end, and that a balance lies in people's awareness and choices.

Owners: No individual owner. Vol. 1 is on a table in Qingce Village's main plaza, Vol. 2 is at the bottom layer of the north boat docks in Liyue Harbor near the flower shop, Vol. 3 is at Wangshu Inn, and Vol. 4 is sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible book collection read for lore only. A separate soundtrack piece of the same name exists and is not part of this item.

446.comment: Rex Incognito: Min'gui and Xigu Antiques
446.content: In Rex Incognito, Min'gui is the first owner of Xigu Antiques on Feiyun Slope, an antique shop open after moonrise for wealthy customers. She is a skilled storyteller who sells relics by their legends and spars with a pedantic young visitor over a jade plaque.

447.content: The central object of Rex Incognito: a damaged jade plaque showing a woman's likeness. The visitor calls it a recent counterfeit and says ancient plaques were a form of tribal currency. In the finale he admits that currency theory was his own invention.

448.comment: Rex Incognito: The Mingyun Jade Carver
448.content: In Rex Incognito Vol. 2, a prankish jade carver in Mingyun Village makes a plaque of the Lord of Geo as a woman after a three-day process of learning, observing and carving blind. He cannot explain why it came out that way.

449.content:
Rhinedottir's "Gift" (also: Rhinedottir's Gift, Rhinedottir's "Gift" quest item): Rhinedottir's "Gift" is a quest item from the world quest Old Friends and New Knowledge (Version 6.2). It is the present that Rhinedottir sent to her creation Albedo through her cat Sebas, and it carries a short riddle about a tree, its perfect fruit and a seed of dreams. Albedo's only response is that he needs to think.

It follows the completion of the final task Rhinedottir set Albedo, and it works as the start of a new problem rather than a reward in the usual sense: the item's own description calls it a new gift and a new quest.

Appearance: Canon does not describe the object. Sebas only says the gift is on the table at Albedo's campsite. What the item shows is its text: two lines in the voice of Rhinedottir.

Lore: Albedo's master Rhinedottir sends the gift via Sebas, her old cat-butler, together with a spoken message. The message says that once a problem is solved, dwelling on it loses its point, and urges Albedo to pose questions of his own instead of resting on answers. The gift's text then compares a tree proud of its most perfect fruit with a "seed of dreams" that refuses to be only the king of a universe confined to its flesh.

Rhinedottir also teases that Albedo may be bored, asks him to bring questions she has never considered, and warns him not to build a "self" whose only purpose is asking questions, since she tried it and it failed. She adds that the gift should be kept well and that Sebas need not be fed.

Owners: Albedo, to whom it is addressed and delivered. The Traveler receives it as a quest reward in the game's mechanics, but within the story it is Albedo's.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a 4-star Quest Item received on completing Old Friends and New Knowledge. The quest also unlocks Albedo's Book of Blinding Light talent. It has no combat use.

450.content: Rhinedottir's "Gift" is a quest item from Old Friends and New Knowledge (6.2): a present sent to Albedo by Rhinedottir through Sebas. Its text contrasts a tree's perfect fruit with a "seed of dreams" that will not settle for being king of a universe confined to its flesh. Albedo takes it as a prompt to think and the riddle is never explained. The object itself is not described.

451.content:
Ring of Yaxche (also: Yaxche Ring, Echoes of the Plentiful Land): Ring of Yaxche is a 4-star catalyst you forge: a jade vessel made by a hero of yesteryear, said to have shot down the giant dragon of the volcano. Its story belongs to the twin heroes Ahpub and Ixquieh.

Page 1 is their triumph and vow; page 2, unlocked later, is how the same bond ended.

Appearance: Canon says only that it is a jade vessel. Do not add shapes or inscriptions beyond that.

Lore: In the age of myth, when great dragons roamed Natlan, the lost twin heroes reunited before an evil dragon's corpse and swore, upon sacred Yaxche, to end death, destruction and pain, and to ensure the strong never again bully the weak.

Their father had died through a Dragonlord's whim and their mother sacrificed herself to protect them, and without the Collective of Plenty and the clans of the mines they could never have reunited.

Owners: No wielder is named. The ring is a jade vessel attributed to the heroes of the legend.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a forgeable 4-star catalyst of the Salutary series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat HP; introduced in Version 5.0.

452.comment: Ring of Yaxche: Echoes of the Plentiful Land
452.content: Echoes of the Plentiful Land is the passive of the catalyst Ring of Yaxche (gameplay): after an Elemental Skill it grants Jade-Forged Crown, which turns the wielder's Max HP into Normal Attack DMG.

453.content:
Royal Bow: Royal Bow is a 4-star bow of the Royal series, an old royal longbow of the erstwhile rulers of Mondstadt. Countless generations later its string is still tight and fires with great force. Its text is about the fall of the ruling Lawrence Clan and the Knights of Favonius exiling them.

It is the Royal series' bow, made of premium materials with master craftsmanship, which the text gives as the reason it is still as powerful as ever.

Appearance: A longbow of fine, long-lasting materials whose string is still taut after generations.

Lore: Hunting was once a pastime of the nobles. They showed their strength in the natural world and shared the spoils with the people in benevolence. Benevolence was lost, and with it their reign.

After the uprising, the Lawrence Clan that had long ruled Mondstadt was overthrown. The newly established Knights of Favonius judged long investigations unnecessary in the name of benevolent governance, and the clan was promptly cast out, never to return.

Owners: No owner is named; the text says only a noble who ruled Mondstadt.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, base ATK 42, secondary stat ATK 9%, sold in Paimon's Bargains. Passive Focus: dealing damage increases CRIT Rate by 8% to 16% by refinement per stack, up to 5 stacks, and a CRIT hit removes all stacks.

454.content:
Royal Greatsword: Royal Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Royal series, an old greatsword once used by the nobles who ruled Mondstadt, made of the finest materials and described as a weapon for royals only. Its text covers the noble duty to fight monsters and the history of gladiatorial combat.

Even after being passed down for generations it is described as good as new.

Appearance: A large, finely made greatsword that has aged without losing its condition. The wiki notes Eula is shown with it in a character teaser and a Collected Miscellany video.

Lore: Combat was once a responsibility of the nobles, who protected their people from monsters. They all but forgot that duty, which turned them into the very monsters they once sought to destroy.

The text says research suggests gladiatorial combat began in a religious context during the aristocracy's rule, as a sacrificial ceremony held jointly with prayers to the gods. It was later turned into a perverted sport for the Lawrence Clan's pleasure and abolished by the Knights of Favonius, who now outlaw it.

Owners: No owner is named; the text says only that nobles used such greatswords.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, base ATK 44, secondary stat ATK 6%, sold in Paimon's Bargains. Passive Focus: dealing damage increases CRIT Rate by 8% to 16% by refinement per stack, up to 5 stacks, and a CRIT hit removes all stacks.

455.content:
Royal Grimoire (also: royal mage's grimoire): The Royal Grimoire is a four-star catalyst of the Royal series. It is a wax-treated scroll that once belonged to a royal mage of Mondstadt, holding both historical accounts and spells. Its item story is mainly a bitter note on how the nobility and their mage tutors failed Mondstadt, and on an oath whose wording was lost.

Appearance: Item text describes a delicate scroll treated with wax against decay and moth damage; the catalyst is a scroll, not a bound volume. Nothing further about its look is stated, so avoid inventing detail.

Lore: The text says royal mages were charged with nourishing the water and soil, fighting monsters and tutoring the nobles, so their research covers history, governance, management and culture, and is still described as forward-looking. When the people overthrew the royals, the mages were exiled too, because they had abandoned their duty to instil virtue in the nobles and become birds of a feather with them.

Owners: Item text names no individual owner, only a royal mage of Mondstadt.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Royal-series passive 'Focus' stacks CRIT Rate on damaging hits (up to 5 stacks, reset by a CRIT). Four-star catalyst, base ATK 44, ATK 6% secondary. Obtained from Paimon's Bargains. This is gameplay, not in-world lore.

456.content:
Royal Longsword (also: longsword of the old nobles): The Royal Longsword is a four-star sword of the Royal series. It was the sword of a noble who ruled Mondstadt, made of premium materials and still as sharp as ever. Its item story laments that noble swordsmanship, once meant to refine wisdom and elegance, decayed into formality, and recalls an oath of protection sworn 2,600 years ago.

Appearance: Item text calls it exquisitely crafted, with carvings and embellishments that testify to its owner's stature. No specific design is described.

Lore: Swordsmanship was once a required skill for nobles, but as a discipline for wisdom and elegance rather than for combat. Both qualities were eventually all but forgotten and the skill became a formality, even though the sword itself stayed sharp through generations.

Owners: Item text names only a noble who ruled over Mondstadt.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Royal-series passive 'Focus' (stacking CRIT Rate, max 5 stacks, cleared by a CRIT). Four-star sword, base ATK 42, ATK 9% secondary. Obtained from Paimon's Bargains.

457.content:
Royal Spear (also: noble's hunting spear): The Royal Spear is a four-star polearm of the Royal series. It was kept in the collection of a Mondstadt noble, remains as sharp as the day it was forged, and in the aristocracy's own time never left the dark. Its story contrasts noble sword-fighting with the spear as a commoner's weapon.

Appearance: The text mentions only that the spear is premium work and that the legendary one was emblazoned with a noble house's crest. It bathed only in pale moonlight in the old days.

Lore: The old nobles held that people of high blood fought with swords and that clashing blades were the chorus of lofty souls, whereas spears and bows were for plebeian gladiators and commoners. Commoners with pitchforks and sharpened poles could still threaten sword-wielding scions, which the rulers of Old Mondstadt found hard to accept, so the spear was kept out of sight.

Owners: No named owner. The legend refers only to a noble youth.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Royal-series passive 'Focus'. Four-star polearm, base ATK 44, ATK 6% secondary. Obtained from Paimon's Bargains; released in Version 1.1.

458.content:
Sacrificer's Staff (also: Untainted Desire, Archpriestess's staff): A silver-white polearm, pure and without blemish, which legend says the Archpriestesses of Hyperborea used to guide their flock of Frostmoon Scions. A 4-star polearm of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.1.

Its text is Lovia's turn from compassion to authority.

Appearance: A silver-white staff-like polearm. The text mentions an antlered crown worn by Lovia later, but that is separate from the staff.

Lore: A fading Archpriestess hands the staff to her kind adopted daughter Lovia, telling her only her mercy can open the eyes of the lost.

Lovia was an orphan from another land, unaware of it, and never blessed with the moon's light. The pale Frost Moon no longer gazed down and the faithful were turning away, so the frail Archpriestess put her adopted daughter on the fragile throne, hoping kindness would unite her followers.

Owners: The text passes the staff to Lovia, the last Archpriestess; no current wielder is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star polearm, base ATK 45, CRIT Rate secondary. Passive Untainted Desire grants ATK and Energy Recharge for 6 seconds after Skill hits, up to 3 stacks, even off-field.

459.content: Untainted Desire is the weapon's passive; its name fits Lovia's turn toward absolute devotion. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

460.content:
Sacrificial Bow: Sacrificial Bow is a 4-star bow of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text calls it a ceremonial hunting bow petrified by time, once the property of the proud Lawrence clan of old Mondstadt, who used it in ritual reenactments of their victory over the frozen wilderness.

The Sacrificial weapons are linked to ceremonies honouring Time and Anemo together; the Bow's story is the one in which a clan's self-image decays from conquerors to overlords to kings.

Appearance: A hunting bow with trinkets still visible on it, which the in-game description says has been petrified over time. The text adds that it was once a prop with an immobile bowstring, but the string became flexible and sturdier with the passage of time. Do not invent further decoration.

Lore: The Lawrence clan used the bow to act out their ancestors' conquest of the frozen wilderness in sacrificial ceremonies, and the bow itself was said to tell the story of the pioneers and their hardships.

On the cliff facing the eastern sea, the ancestors are said to have worshipped the masters of Time and Anemo together; the item text quotes a saying that Anemo brings stories while Time nurtures them. The ceremony's first act told how the forebears took the land through wisdom and strength. The ceremony was eventually lost, but the clan kept playing the same role.

Owners: The item text names the Lawrence clan as the bow's former owners. No individual wielder is named.

Further details: Diona is briefly seen holding a Sacrificial Bow in her anecdote in the Travelers' Tales: Anthology Chapter event (a limited-time event). It is a cameo, not a story claim of ownership.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star bow, base ATK 44, Energy Recharge secondary stat. Passive Composed: after an Elemental Skill deals damage, it has a 40 to 80 per cent chance (by refinement) to end its own cooldown, at most once every 30 to 16 seconds. Obtainable from the Standard Wanderlust Invocation and from character and weapon event wishes; part of the Sacrificial series.

461.content: The Lawrence clan is the former owner of the Sacrificial Bow per its item text: a proud clan that reenacted its ancestors' victory over the frozen wilderness in ritual, and whose self-image corrupted over time from conquerors to overlords to kings, costing it the affection of Mondstadt's winds. See the clan's own entry for its history.

462.content:
Sacrificial Fragments: Sacrificial Fragments is a 4-star catalyst in the Sacrificial series from Mondstadt. Its description calls it a weathered script whose text is no longer legible, a cursed item eroded by the winds of time. Present since Version 1.0.

The Sacrificial series are props from early Mondstadt's wind-worship rituals; the wiki notes this script is the only one described as cursed and with no clan named.

Appearance: Canon describes only a weathered script whose text is illegible. As a catalyst it is shown as a book or script; no further detail is given.

Lore: Early Mondstadt built theaters atop windy cliffs and performed rituals as stories and ballads, because they believed the gods enjoyed stories.

The script is millennia old and now illegible. A long-ago war between the Lord of Storm and the Great Wolf King of the North buried Mondstadt in blizzards; a group who could not bear the cold built a clifftop shrine in the east to pray for mercy. Later generations presumed the shrine had always been for the wind alone.

Owners: No owner or clan is named in the item text.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 4-star catalyst, base ATK 41, Elemental Mastery secondary stat (48). Composed gives a chance for an Elemental Skill that damages an opponent to end its own cooldown, with a cooldown on the effect. It can be obtained from Wishes, including the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event Wishes.

463.content:
Sacrificial Greatsword: Sacrificial Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text describes a ceremonial greatsword that began as a prop and was hardened by time, once belonging to the Imunlaukr clan, brave and gifted warriors who fought hard and died young.

It tells a story of war and was used to enact war tales in sacrificial ceremonies dedicated to Time and Anemo.

Appearance: A greatsword with trinkets still visible on it, described in game as petrified over time. The text says its blade, originally only a prop, was hardened by the passage of time. No other detail is given.

Lore: The Imunlaukr clan used it in sacrificial ceremonies to enact duels between brave warriors stained black with blood.

On the cliff facing the eastern sea, the ancestors are said to have worshipped the masters of Time and Anemo together; the item text quotes a saying that Anemo brings stories while Time nurtures them. In the clan's eyes, combat existed neither for protection, glory nor territory but for the amusement of the gods high in the heavens. They fought monsters and outlaws alike with no regard for whether they would return to their loved ones, and the point was to roar loud and clear in the heat of battle.

Owners: The item text names the Imunlaukr clan as former owners. No individual wielder is named.
