Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star claymore, base ATK 44, Energy Recharge secondary stat. Passive Composed: after an Elemental Skill deals damage, it has a 40 to 80 per cent chance (by refinement) to end its own cooldown, at most once every 30 to 16 seconds. Obtainable from the Standard Wanderlust Invocation and from character and weapon event wishes; part of the Sacrificial series.

464.content: The Imunlaukr clan is the former owner of the Sacrificial Greatsword per its item text: warriors who treated battle as entertainment for the gods and died young, until they found something to fight for as Mondstadt took shape. See the clan's own entry for its history.

465.content:
Sacrificial Sword: Sacrificial Sword is a 4-star sword of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text describes a ceremonial sword, originally a prop and sharpened by time, that belonged to the kindly Gunnhildr clan, who enacted the defense of Mondstadt in rituals for the winds of time.

Its story is one of protection, meant to show the courage to protect.

Appearance: A sword with trinkets still visible, described in game as petrified over time. The text says its blade, originally just a prop, was sharpened by the passage of time. No other detail is given.

Lore: The Gunnhildr clan used it in sacrificial ceremonies that enacted the defense of Mondstadt.

On the cliff facing the eastern sea, the ancestors are said to have worshipped the masters of Time and Anemo together; the item text quotes a saying that Anemo brings stories while Time nurtures them. The ceremony dedicated to the winds of time had three acts, and the final act told a tale of the protection of Mondstadt, of life, and of freedom.

Owners: The item text names the Gunnhildr clan as former owners. No individual wielder is named.

Further details: Albedo is seen wielding a Sacrificial Sword in his official art. This is an art detail, not a statement of ownership in the story.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 41, Energy Recharge secondary stat. Passive Composed: after an Elemental Skill deals damage, it has a 40 to 80 per cent chance (by refinement) to end its own cooldown, at most once every 30 to 16 seconds. Obtainable from the Standard Wanderlust Invocation and from character and weapon event wishes; part of the Sacrificial series.

466.content: The Gunnhildr clan is the former owner of the Sacrificial Sword per its item text: a kindly clan who enacted the defense of Mondstadt, of life and of freedom in ceremony, and who still act as guardians of the city today. See the clan's own entry for its history.

467.content:
Sakura Bloom (also: Sakura Blooms, Hiou-kyuu): Sakura Bloom is a petal that has fallen from the Sacred Sakura of the Grand Narukami Shrine, and a local specialty of Inazuma found on Narukami Island. Electro energy keeps the petals floating in mid-air.

Item text says the blossoms are filled with a fondness for Inazuma, and attaches to them local legends about the Thunder Sakura.

Appearance: Clusters of pale petals drifting in the air rather than lying on the ground, found around Narukami Island and especially near Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine. They only come together into a collectable bloom when touched by Electro.

Lore: The description calls them petals from the Sacred Sakura at the Grand Narukami Shrine, suspended by Electro. It adds that, according to legend, the roots of every Thunder Sakura join deep underground, and that following them always leads back to this sacred tree standing guard over Inazuma.

Owners: No notable owner. It belongs to the shrine's sacred tree and is gathered freely by travellers.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: an Inazuma local specialty added in Version 2.0, found on Narukami Island and used for cooking and character ascension. To harvest a floating cluster, a player must use an Electro ability, touch it while Electro-affected, or carry an Electrograna. In Japanese the name is written with an older character form for sakura, a detail noted by the wiki.

key: Chalice of Your Blood and Sorrow
468.content:
Scarlet Proof (also: Honor to Your Devotion, Glory to Your Legacy, Time Gifted Unto You, Chalice of Your Blood and Sorrow, Testament to Your Faith): Scarlet Proof is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Stellar Swirl teams, released in version 7.0. Its five pieces are bright red Fatui keepsakes (a flower medal, a quill, a pocket watch, a wine bottle, a helmet), and each carries a short vignette about a Fatui member in the Tsaritsa's Snezhnaya: Sandrone, Pulcinella, Capitano, Dottore and Pantalone.

The tone is dry and personal: how members joined, what they quietly carry and how the organisation treats talent as fuel for its "grand ideal".

Appearance: All five items are described as bright red: a flower ornament symbolising blazing glory, a quill, a pocket watch, a wine bottle and a helmet. The Fatui recruitment poster in the Flower bears a scarlet flower, which is the medal promised to those who devote themselves to the cause.

Lore: - Honor to Your Devotion: Miss Guillotin, who had come from Fontaine after Duke Alain Guillotin's death, sits in a Snezhnograd square. In Fontaine she had talked with a branch president who praised a foreign bank; in Snezhnaya she met the Director of the Fatui, who spoke of saving the world by destroying the old. She later became Marionette, or Sandrone, and took on a Harbinger's duties.
- Glory to Your Legacy: a fae named Mirko joined the Fatui, studied under Mayor Ioanna Ivanovna and as Pulcinella watched a young man, Ajax, grow into a Fatui officer who showed him an old recruitment quill.

Owners: No single owner. The items are linked with the Harbingers named in each vignette; the Sands says a retiring soldier left five red items with Capitano to give to those who come after.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star set from the Inverted Glacier domain (Everfrozen Earth, Snezhnaya). 4-piece: for 10s after the wearer triggers a Stellar Swirl reaction, their CRIT Rate +16% and their Stellar Swirl reaction DMG +40%.

key: Chalice of Your Blood and Sorrow
469.content: Artifact set of red Fatui keepsakes whose item text offers short portraits of Sandrone, Pulcinella, Capitano, Dottore and Pantalone.

470.content: According to the Time Gifted Unto You text, Pulcinella arranged quiet rooms for Fatui members to talk with a companion they trust. Capitano is described as a kind of walking counselling room because colleagues confide in him. The text says Lohefalter, Dottore and Pantalone each used the rooms, or did not, in small anecdotes. Treat these as item text.

471.content:
Scion of the Blazing Sun: Scion of the Blazing Sun is a 4-star bow: an ancient longbow from King Deshret's era, carved with indecipherable ancient text and solemn patterns. Its story traces the priests of King Deshret's kingdom, their archery, and the descendants who still keep the old ceremonies in secret.

It is a Battle Pass (Gnostic Hymn) reward from Version 4.0 and belongs to the Gnostic Hymn 2 series.

Appearance: An ancient longbow carved with indecipherable text and solemn patterns.

Lore: In the era when the desert king ruled the land, authority covered it like sunlight over the dunes. The nomads' surviving songs sing of that golden age, and say the red lord once contended against the bright sun and fell to the earth like a meteorite. Some priests were not slain by the kings and princes who followed and passed down King Deshret's art of archery.

The priests' descendants call themselves the "Heirs of the Burning Sun" and continue the ceremonies of the old kingdom without ceasing. Few have the right to inherit the priests' legacy, few can read the ancient texts, and fewer still master the combat arts the priests prized: cudgel, spear and, above all, archery. The Eremites call such people "ascetics".

Owners: No in-world owner is named. The wiki notes Sethos wields the ascended bow in his character introduction, which is promotional use only.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT Rate 4%. Passive The Way of Sunfire: after a Charged Attack hit, a Sunfire Arrow descends on the opponent hit, deals ATK-based damage and applies Heartsearer for 10 s, increasing Charged Attack DMG the opponent takes from the wielder; once every 10 s.

472.content:
Scroll of Streaming Song (also: Streaming Song): Scroll of Streaming Song is a three-volume set of torn pages from desert ruins, kept in the House of Daena. It tells how the Mistress of Pushpavatika visits a wise princess and tests her with three riddles. Scholars have added notes on its translation and gaps.

The pages were retrieved by Vahumana researchers, and Haravatat and Vahumana herbads argue in the margins about what the text means. In the end the two rulers ally. The in-game description says the author is unconfirmed.

Appearance: Torn pages in verse-like lines, interrupted by the scholars' bracketed remarks. Missing words appear as (...) and some guesses are marked with question marks.

Lore: Vol. 1: the Mistress of Pushpavatika, who calls herself a spirit created at the beginning, goes to the princess's land to test her wisdom. The princess is surrounded by attendants in a cloth no one has seen before, like stars around one moon. The Mistress offers spices, gold and gems if the princess can answer three riddles; the princess replies that knowledge is worth more.

Vol. 2: the first riddle (cold as the dead while alive, warm in death) is answered with the rose; the second (rises from earth, descends from the sky, unseen yet sees all, runs only top to bottom) with the universal law made in heaven, which only worship and not imitation may meet. Her warning is that forbidden arts bring calamity at the edge of divine knowledge.

key: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
473.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
473.content:
Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (also: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City artifact set, Beast Tamer's Talisman, Mountain Ranger's Marker, Mystic's Gold Dial, Wandering Scholar's Claw Cup, Demon-Warrior's Feather Mask): Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Natlan, added in Version 5.0. Its five pieces belong to members of one band of adventurers: a beast tamer, a mountain ranger, a young mystic, a scholar and a warrior who set out in the Cataclysm for a legendary Abyss-repelling treasure in a ruined ancient city. It boosts Nightsoul Burst and elemental-reaction team play.

The pieces are Beast Tamer's Talisman (flower), Mountain Ranger's Marker (plume), Mystic's Gold Dial (sands), Wandering Scholar's Claw Cup (goblet) and Demon-Warrior's Feather Mask (circlet).

Lore: The five pieces, each with its own entry:
- Beast Tamer's Talisman: passed down among beast tamers of the Scions of the Canopy.
- Mountain Ranger's Marker: rangers from the spring's source left feather-shaped markers on their paths for future travellers.
- Mystic's Gold Dial: mystics from the canyon of night smoke normally train for decades to speak with the Wayob.
- Wandering Scholar's Claw Cup: a scholar who claimed to be President of the Saurian Relics Association spent his days with scrolls and strange mechanisms until war burned his work.
- Demon-Warrior's Feather Mask: Taika, once the mightiest warrior of the Flower-Feather Clan, said goodbye to his wife and unborn child to fight monsters, becoming as ferocious as a demon.
Each piece has its own entry with its full text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus restores 6 Elemental Energy when a nearby party member triggers a Nightsoul Burst. The 4-piece bonus gives nearby party members a 12% Elemental DMG Bonus for the elements in a reaction triggered by the wearer, for 15s; if the wearer is in Nightsoul's Blessing, they gain a further 28% for 20s.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): these are the humble effects of ordinary tribespeople who walked into a lost cause; treat them with respect rather than as treasure. A Natlanian who finds one can plausibly recognise the tribe by its crafted style.

474.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Liriwu
474.content: In the set's text, Liriwu is a young mystic of the canyon of night smoke whose dial needle points home. The wiki says she belonged to the Masters of the Night-Wind and was the only member of the party to return alive; she was left in a safe tower, and found only shattered corpses at the camp.

475.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Taika and Bona
475.content: Taika was the mightiest warrior of the Flower-Feather Clan. He left his wife and unborn child to fight the demons and monsters, and died at the apex of Cinder City. If the child was a girl, he said, her name should be Bona. The wiki's Bona entry says she grew up to follow his path.

476.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Cinder City
476.content: In the set, Cinder City is the burned ancient city where the legendary treasure was said to lie; the beast tamer's and mountain ranger's notes call it filth-ridden and ash-laden. The wiki ties it to Ochkanatlan, which later canon shows as Och-Kan's domain.

477.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Beast tamers and Saurians
477.content: Beast tamers of the Scions of the Canopy focus on building friendships with Saurians and try to settle disputes peacefully, even with violent Saurians that have hurt a human, sometimes before the Saurian Hunters can act. Their ideals are sometimes incomprehensible even to their tribe.

478.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Beast Tamer's Talisman
478.content: a talisman passed down among beast tamers of the Scions of the Canopy, carved with the paw print said to be that of the first Yumkasaurus to bond with a human. Beast tamers befriend Saurians, even violent ones, and believe in patience. The young tamer who learned this believed beasts share human hearts until the black tide came, bringing monsters who could never be understood. He settled the survivors of his hometown and set out on a journey of no return, hoping to find a secret Abyss-repelling treasure the ancient Python King was said to have forged in the burned city.

479.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Mountain Ranger's Marker
479.content: rangers from the spring's source left feather-shaped markers on their paths for future travellers. When the black tide swept over their homeland, the last ranger, who knew every inch of Natlan, set out again to retake it, hoping for a golden wheel in the city of the foul dragon that could reverse time, even if it was another trap laid by a heartless spectator.

480.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Mystic's Gold Dial
480.content: mystics from the canyon of night smoke normally train for decades to speak with the Wayob, but in this chaotic time even fresh disciples had to guide fallen warriors' spirits home. The dial belonged to a young mystic named Liriwu. Joining a team of veterans bound for the city above the clouds, she was left behind in a safe tower; when she reached their camp she found only shattered corpses and the remains of a dragon's meal. Resolved to take word of their end to waiting families, she set out on the road home.

481.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Wandering Scholar's Claw Cup
481.content: a scholar who claimed to be President of the Saurian Relics Association spent his days with scrolls and strange mechanisms until war burned his work. Having read that ancient dragon ruins held weapons against demons, he rebuilt machines from the secret source to aid warriors, then found a secret in a forsaken city, hidden for thousands of years. Believing the legend that the Python King of Ochkanatlan built a sky-faring treasure ship holding a prize that could drive the Abyss out of the world, he joined an adventurers' team bound for the city in the clouds, despite public scorn after earlier expeditions never returned.

482.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City: Demon-Warrior's Feather Mask
482.content: Taika, once the mightiest warrior of the Flower-Feather Clan, said goodbye to his wife and unborn child to fight monsters, becoming as ferocious as a demon. He fell at the apex of Cinder City and, as he died, remembered telling his wife that if the child was a girl she should be called Bona.

483.content:
Serenitea Pot (also: Realm Within, The Realm Within, Teapot realm, Ode-of-Dust Teapot, Chen'ge Hu, Serenitea Pot realm): The Serenitea Pot is a small teapot the adeptus Madame Ping gives the Traveler in Liyue Harbor as thanks for helping save the city. Inside is a private pocket world made with the adeptal art of Sub-Space Creation, where the Traveler can build a house, garden and grounds and rest from the road. It is kept by a courteous finch-like teapot spirit named Tubby, who calls herself a butler.

The teapot is placed on the ground like a gadget and entered by interacting with it. The realm cannot become a full world: Tubby says it is only a moment of respite from the mortal realm, not a way of escaping it. Over time it becomes a home that the Traveler can fill with furniture, buildings and animals, share with visiting friends, and, later, with the characters they have met on their travels.

Appearance: Seen from outside, it is a teapot carried in the inventory and set down on a surface. Its item text calls it a teapot from Madame Ping with "a whole realm within". Inside, the Traveler first finds a large house at the centre of otherwise empty floating ground, which the player then builds out.

Lore: Madame Ping used Sub-Space Creation, an adeptal ability she says was a blessing from Rex Lapis, to make a small autonomous world. The Traveler first walked through one such teapot in the Archon Quest, when she tested them while they collected the Cleansing Bell. After the Osial crisis she learned the Traveler camped outdoors and prepared a gift, with Yanfei running errands for the materials. Tubby, the teapot spirit, introduces the realm.

Ping says a teapot is a small trick compared with Rex Lapis, who moved mountains and seas; an adeptus of her sort must leave the real world to make a world of their own. Tubby explains that adepti create such realms but seldom have time to maintain them, so teapot spirits were created to guard realms and run their affairs. Anything built inside comes from blueprints and materials, shaped by thought, and the Traveler can refashion the realm as they please.

Gameplay: Gameplay description, not story. The Serenitea Pot is the player-housing system.
- It unlocks at Adventure Rank 28 after "A New Star Approaches", through the world quest "A Teapot to Call Home" (Part I in Liyue Harbor, Part II inside the realm).
- The Traveler builds from furnishings made with blueprints and materials, limited by a Load meter.

484.content: Tubby is the Teapot Spirit who runs the Realm Within: a small floating blue finch with an orange and white beak, who speaks politely and calls herself a butler to the realm. She gives access to Trust Rank, furnishing creation, realm style and the Realm Depot. She mentions Tianheng Bohea, Yunlai white tea and Bishui green tea among her centuries-old stock, enjoys dozing in the sun, and says she has an adeptus name, "Rain Calmer", which she struggles to recall. She remembers a golden-eyed adeptus but not his name.

485.content: Chubby, the Teapot Traveling Salesman, is a second teapot spirit with the adeptus name "Jade Seeker". He appears in the realm from Friday to Sunday and sells furnishings (animals, Sub-Space Boulders and Radiant Spincrystals) for Realm Currency; how many goods depend on Trust Rank. Tubby says he travels widely for rare treasures and sometimes gives her rare flower teas.

486.content: Sub-Space Creation is the adeptal ability to create a small autonomous pocket world through imagination. Ping says it was part of the illumination adepti received as a blessing from Rex Lapis. It can make teapot realms like this one and larger abodes. Its limit is that such a world is not true: it offers respite, not escape.

487.comment: Serenitea Pot: Realm Dispatch and companions
487.content: After "Idle Teapot Talk", Tubby gives the Traveler a Realm Dispatch, modified so that a light tap on a friend's palm invites them. Invited playable characters live in the realm and produce Companionship EXP (Realm Bounty). Up to 8 can live there at the highest Trust Rank.

488.content: In the Archon Quest, Zhongli sends the Traveler to Madame Ping for the Cleansing Bell used in the Rite of Parting. Ping transports them into her magic teapot as a test, revealing herself as an adeptus. After Osial's defeat she prepares the Serenitea Pot as a gift.

489.content:
Serpent Spine: Serpent Spine is a 4-star claymore from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn, in the game since Version 1.0. The in-game short description calls it a rare weapon from the ancient ocean whose swings carry the sound of ageless waves. The full text says it is a greatsword made from the spine of a great sea monster and tells of a singing sea captain who never returned from the deep.

The Skipper is the greatsword-wielding captain of the story, and the wiki notes that the book series Tales From the Waves covers the same character.

Appearance: A greatsword made of a sea monster's spine, each eerie segment of bone described as a tale unto itself. Brilliant white bone is mentioned in the story of the beached monster. No hilt or other design details are given in text.

Lore: In the stormy seas of the ancient past, those who set out often never returned. A greatsword-wielding captain, fond of drinking and merriment before voyages, sailed off on the day sea and wind aligned and neither he nor his ship came back.

The text says sailors once used the bones of sea monsters as figureheads to frighten the beasts of the deep sea, who envied land-dwellers. Carefree sea shanties of today were once farewell songs that left people silent. When questioned about his revelry the captain would laugh, say he knew himself, tell people not to worry and that once the sea and winds were right he would go, but never finish the thought, instead raising his mug.

Owners: The previous owner is the Skipper, the greatsword-wielding captain of the item text. His relationship with his Chief Mate, Parsifal, is covered in the Heart of Depth artifact set.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star claymore, base ATK 42, CRIT Rate secondary stat. Passive Wavesplitter: every 4s the wielder is on the field they deal 6 to 10 per cent more DMG and take 3 to 2 per cent more DMG (by refinement), up to 5 stacks. Stacks persist when leaving the field and drop by one when the wielder takes DMG. Obtained through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn bundle.

490.content: The Skipper is the greatsword-wielding captain linked to the Serpent Spine and the Heart of Depth artifact set: a carefree, hard-drinking sailor of the ancient stormy seas who sailed into the misty ocean and never returned. Parsifal was his Chief Mate. See their own entries.

491.content:
Severed Fragment of Ikhor (also: Fragment of Ikhor, Ikhor's Fragment, Ikhor's power): The Severed Fragment of Ikhor is a quest item found in Snezhnaya (added in 7.0). Its description calls it a piece of Ikhor's power, split off by Aksinya when a "ritual" was interrupted, and notes it has taken the form of a glowing doll.

Two copies are earned at Fellfrost Peak, one in the House of Hesperides cellar and one in the garden's great tree, while the Traveler gathers fragments to restore the Eye of Graeae's power.

Appearance: A glowing doll. The item text suggests the doll form is not natural to the power: it speculates that Ikhor's wish to fulfil the wishes of others became the strings that once controlled him, leaving him a puppet carrying transcendent power.

Lore: The description is the main lore. It credits Aksinya with splitting the fragment away when the ritual was cut short, and offers a sad reading of Ikhor as a being reduced to a puppet by a desire to grant others' wishes. It speaks of it as a reflection by the writer, not a statement from Ikhor himself.

492.comment: Severed Fragment of Ikhor: Severed Fragment of Ikhor
492.content: A glowing doll-shaped fragment of Ikhor's power, said to have been split from him by Aksinya when a "ritual" was interrupted. Two are recovered at the House of Hesperides in Snezhnaya during the search for the Eye of Graeae's scattered power. Its text is melancholy, calling Ikhor a puppet held by a wish to fulfil others' wishes. Nothing beyond that is established.

493.content:
Shimenawa's Reminiscence (also: Shimenawa's Reminiscence artifact set, Entangling Bloom, Shaft of Remembrance, Morning Dew's Moment, Hopeful Heart, Capricious Visage): Shimenawa's Reminiscence is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set. Its five item texts are the first-person memories of the shrine maiden Hibiki of her teacher the Kitsune Saiguu at the Grand Narukami Shrine, of fortune slips and paper-cord charms, and of the friends who were lost. It boosts ATK and trades Energy for Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack damage.

It drops from the Momiji-Dyed Court domain on Yashiori Island and has existed since Version 2.0. The theme is love of someone after they are gone: the texts return again and again to the idea that moments cannot be held, but time spent with someone is not lost.

Lore: The narrator came to Narukami as a country shrine maiden and was trained by the Kitsune Saiguu, who spoke in riddles about entanglement, memory and loss. Years later Saiguu is gone, and the narrator holds the empty pipe and keeps a promise to someone who is not at her side.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not lore: the 2-piece bonus is ATK +18%. The 4-piece bonus: when casting an Elemental Skill with 15 or more Energy, the wearer loses 15 Energy and gains +50% Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack DMG for 10 seconds; it does not retrigger during that time and does not trigger on characters that do not use Energy (such as Mavuika). It drops from the Momiji-Dyed Court.

494.comment: Shimenawa's Reminiscence: Hibiki's memories of the Kitsune Saiguu
494.content: In Shimenawa's Reminiscence the narrator, Hibiki, remembers the Kitsune Saiguu as a teacher who spoke in paradoxes, drank sakura wine, and tapped heads with a tobacco pipe. The texts show Saiguu worrying about memory and loss, giving Hibiki a Great Fortune, and warning that she herself has "already passed away like the morning dew". The Hakushin Ring catalyst is narrated from Saiguu's side.

495.content: "The idiot Konbumaru" is Hibiki's teasing name in the set for a wandering, gambling man who becomes a Hatamoto of the Shogun, marries a samurai's daughter and taught her archery. The wiki names him Takamine, a servant of the tengu Reizenbou, and says he disappeared in the cataclysm; the item texts use only the nickname. His connection to the Storm Cage text of Emblem of Severed Fate is inferred from the shared setting.

496.content: The Shaft of Remembrance lists the aftermath for Hibiki's fellow trainees: the Great Tengu in exile, Harunosuke leaving Inazuma, Nagamasa joining the Shogunate to clear the Mikoshi name. Wiki summaries call Hibiki, Harunosuke and Nagamasa "the Yougou Three" for training under the Yougou Tengu; the set itself does not use that term.

497.content:
Silken Moon's Serenade (also: Crystal Tear of the Wanderer, Pristine Plume of the Blessed, Frost Devotee's Delirium, Joyous Glory of the Pure, Holy Crown of the Believer): Silken Moon's Serenade is a 4- and 5-star artifact set tied to Lunar reactions and the Moonsign. Its five pieces carry one narrator's account of the far north: the night Hyperborea's golden realm was destroyed by dark blue crystal nails, the pity of the Frost Moon's mistress, and the later suffering of the Frostmoon Scions, down to the Moonchanter Aila and her sister. It was released in version 6.0.

Four pieces open in a time before the new moon (Columbina) rose; only the Flower is set earlier, at the disaster itself. The stories are the Scions' own memory and myth.

Appearance: Immaculate northern relics: an everlasting flower, a feathered accessory said to have been forged by the first Moonchanter, a long-stopped timepiece, a silver cup from old Frostmoon Scion rituals, and a circlet imitating the antlers of the grove's envoy.

Lore: The set text has five stories, one per piece.
- Crystal Tear of the Wanderer: in a single night the golden tower fell, and dark blue crystal nails wiped out every city with any sign of life; the apostle and the gods' first messenger (wiki-linked to Anacharsis and Koitar) vanished. The gods stayed silent. Only the mistress of the Frost Moon wept for mortals; legend says she spun silver threads to guide survivors, and her tears became lilies. Hence the descendants of Hyperborea call themselves the Frostmoon Scions.
- The other four pieces follow the Scions' later decline, from the twin sisters Aila and Alia to the Archpriestess Lovia's long project of a "pure" bloodline and a manufactured faith.

Owners: No owner is named. The pieces are relics of the Frostmoon Scions' heritage and are collected by the player as artifacts.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star set from the Frostladen Machinery domain (Paha Isle, Nod-Krai). 4-piece: when the wearer deals Elemental DMG they gain Gleaming Moon: Devotion for 8s, giving all party members +60 Elemental Mastery under a Nascent Gleam Moonsign or +120 under an Ascendant Gleam Moonsign (off-field works). All party members' Lunar Reaction DMG rises 10% for each different Gleaming Moon effect present; they do not stack.

498.comment: Silken Moon's Serenade: Silken Moon's Serenade
498.content: Artifact set whose item text tells of Hyperborea's fall, the Frost Moon's mercy and the later history of the Frostmoon Scions and the Moonchanter Aila.

499.comment: Silken Moon's Serenade: The mistress of the Frost Moon's mercy
499.content: In the Crystal Tear of the Wanderer text, when the golden realm fell and the gods stayed silent, one celestial ruler alone shed tears for mortals. She was the mistress of the Frost Moon, queen of the celestial chariot and of light. According to legend she wove threads from the silver glow to lead survivors across the frozen plains, and her tears became everlasting lilies. The text adds that she acted from pity and a deeper, unspoken wish, "whatever her original intent".

500.content:
Silver Light (also: Radiance on the Water): Silver Light is a four-star sword obtained from the limited-time Version 7.1 event Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (part of the Moonchase Festival). Its description says it is a longsword left by Wind Reader, one of the Three Hermits of Guizang. The item story shows him as a reckless young thaumaturge humbled and gently taken in by the swallow adeptus.

Appearance: The text describes only a longsword, said to be forged from sacred silver from the heavens, that once cleaved sea water into two. Do not invent more detail.

Lore: The story begins in the youth of the man later revered as founder of Qimen Divination, before the name Wind Reader was known. He wandered as a vagabond, plucking talismans from the air, laying formations with poured wine, proud of his genius and answering to nothing but his whims. He once stole the bronze mirror of the Two Sages of Lianshan and struck down bandits. One night he burned shadow phantoms terrorising a mountain village, then mocked the villagers he had saved.

A flash of silver light followed, and the swallow adeptus (later one of the Three Beasts of Tao Dou) appeared, lamenting that he treated his foresight as a toy. He drew his sword and boasted with a rude verse, but was beaten and pinned under her foot. She did not rage. She lifted him up and invited him to walk the wanderer's path with her, since the world was bigger than the outlaws' squalor.

Owners: Left behind by Wind Reader, according to the description. No later owner is named.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore. Obtained from the event Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (Version 7.1, from 2026-09-24). Passive Radiance on the Water grants Elemental Mastery after an Elemental Skill. Refinement material is Tea-Scented Tassel.

501.content:
Silvershower Heartstrings (also: Dryas's Nocturne): Silvershower Heartstrings is a 5-star bow, the legendary bow of the fairies, said to touch the hearts of listeners whether on stage or on the battlefield.

Its story is not about a person but about a very old Fontainian play, Dryas, and the many versions of its ending.

Appearance: Canon calls it a bow, fairy-made and later modified as a theatrical prop. It carries a Pneuma or Ousia mark for Arkhe-aligned wielders. Add no other detail.

Lore: Fontainian playwrights liken strings to hearts, and the word heartstring appears in one of the oldest plays, Dryas, though the string there was a bowstring.

The hero is Aurelius, glorious as gold, who conquered countless traitorous nations for Fontaine. He is the forerunner of the Aurelius in Coppelius's The Saga of Aurelius, yet no such figure exists in recorded history, so he is often regarded as fiction, like Ajax. In the story he falls into a foe's trap and is lost with his army in a pine forest.

Owners: No owner is named. The bow is attributed to the fairies in legend.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star bow, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat HP; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.7. Passive "Dryas's Nocturne": the wielder can gain Remedy stacks, one for using an Elemental Skill (25s), one when a Bond of Life value increases (25s), and one for performing healing (20s); each stack count adds Max HP, and with 3 stacks Elemental Burst CRIT Rate rises, ending 4s after falling below 3. Works off-field. Values scale with refinement.

502.content: Dryas is an ancient Fontainian play in which the fairy maiden Dryastis saves the hero Aurelius with silver arrows and begs him to end the war on her land. Its many endings are the story of the weapon Silvershower Heartstrings. No historical Aurelius is recorded.

503.content:
Skyward Atlas (also: Cloud Atlas, Wandering Clouds): Skyward Atlas is a five-star catalyst of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It is a cloud atlas that symbolises Dvalin and his former master, the Anemo Archon, details the winds and clouds of the northern regions and holds the power of sky and wind. In its story it is a copy of a far older atlas of 100,000 odes, each naming one cloud or wind.

Appearance: The item text describes an atlas presented as poems and images. It gives no cover or binding detail.

Lore: The atlas pairs images with 100,000 odes, each dedicated to a single cloud or wind and calling it by name. The atlas gave the winds form and the odes gave them personality, so the formless winds became friends and family in Barbatos' eyes. Legend says that in ancient times Barbatos used the original to summon the four winds, thaw the snow, drive away vicious beasts, call rain and create Mondstadt.

Owners: Original author or keeper: Barbatos. Copies passed among the people of Mondstadt. The item names no current holder. Mona is shown holding the catalyst in her 2022 birthday artwork, which is presentation rather than a canon statement of ownership.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star catalyst from the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 48, secondary stat ATK 7.2%. Passive "Wandering Clouds": raises Elemental DMG Bonus (12-24%); Normal Attack hits have a 50% chance to summon clouds that seek out nearby opponents for 15 seconds, dealing 160-320% ATK DMG, at most once every 30 seconds.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): treat it as lore-rich rather than as a god's personal spellbook. Weather-lore, names and odes suit scenes with scholars and bards.

504.content: Cloud Atlas is the popular name for copies of the atlas of winds that Barbatos allowed people to share. They preserve poems and images describing northern weather and are incomplete.

505.content:
Skyward Blade (also: Sky-Piercing Fang): Skyward Blade is a five-star sword of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It is the sword of a knight and symbolises the restored honour of Dvalin, with the Anemo Archon's blessing on its fuller. Its story is Dvalin's fight with the shadow dragon Durin and the poison that followed.

Appearance: The text puts the Archon's blessing on the fuller of the blade and calls it "the sky-piercing fang". No other visual detail is given.

Lore: The story opens with a fang that pierced the black-gold scales of the abyssal kingdom and cut the throats of the sons of ancient sinners. Mondstadt was threatened by the shadow dragon Durin, whose jealousy of the city's prosperity bred evil and poisoned the land. Hearing the people cry, the Anemo Archon descended and woke Dvalin, who rose into the sky to fight for all life.

Owners: No wielder is named; the sword stands for Dvalin's honour. The Traveler is shown wielding it in the cinematic of the limited-time event Moonlight Merriment Part II, per the wiki's trivia.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star sword from the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat Energy Recharge 12%. Passive "Sky-Piercing Fang": raises CRIT Rate (4-8%); after an Elemental Burst you gain Skypiercing Might for 12 seconds (Movement SPD +10%, ATK SPD +10%, Normal and Charged hits deal extra damage of 20-40% ATK).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a symbol of redeemed reputation. Do not say the blade is Dvalin's own fang; the text says it symbolises him.

506.comment: Skyward Blade: Dvalin and Durin's battle
506.content: The Skyward weapons retell the Cataclysm-era battle from different angles. In the Blade's version Dvalin, blessed by the Archon, pierces Durin's throat, is poisoned by the blood, falls unconscious and is forgotten.

507.content:
Skyward Harp (also: Echoing Ballad, Sky-Piercing Lyre): Skyward Harp is a five-star bow of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. The item calls it the sky-piercing lyre: its story is how Barbatos' lyre drew Dvalin to him, held back the shadow dragon, and then went unheard by a poisoned Dvalin.

Appearance: Described as a greatbow whose sound when fired is music to the Anemo Archon's ears. The text gives no further look.

Lore: The clear tune of the lyre still echoes in the hearts of the people and in the winds, and it is said the ancient evil dragon from the abyss was drawn there by it. In ancient times Barbatos softly strummed his lyre and summoned the pure thousand winds and songs. Charmed by the free winds and songs, the high dragon Dvalin descended and swore loyalty. Barbatos, glad of a new friend, entrusted the people of Mondstadt to Dvalin, and the Archon and the Wind Dragon together forged Mondstadt's dawn.

Owners: The item names no wielder. Per the wiki's trivia, Venti wields the bow in his Character Demo and a Collected Miscellany video, and in the Dvalin fight of the Prologue (A Long Shot) he uses it to help the Traveler free Dvalin from the Abyss Order's control. Tartaglia used it as a trial character in an early Story Quest, since replaced by the Polar Star.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star bow from the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 48, secondary stat CRIT Rate 4.8%. Passive "Echoing Ballad": raises CRIT DMG (20-40%); hits have a 60-100% chance of a small AoE dealing 125% Physical ATK DMG, at most once every 4 seconds at refinement 1, down to every 2 seconds at refinement 5.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a weapon about friends who misunderstand each other. The text only says Dvalin will soon hear the songs again; it does not show the reconciliation.

508.comment: Skyward Harp: Holy Lyre der Himmel
508.content: Barbatos' lyre, named in the Harp's text as the memory that survived Dvalin's anguish. It has its own entry.

509.content:
Skyward Pride (also: Sky-Ripping Dragon Spine): Skyward Pride is a five-star claymore of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It symbolises the pride of Dvalin soaring through the skies and hums deeply when swung, with the force of his command of sky and wind. Its story tells of the battle with Durin, the poison, and Dvalin's fall to become Stormterror.

Appearance: Only its sound is described, a deep hum when swung. The text says nothing of its look.

Lore: A tale of sky-shaking valour: even the vile dragon Durin, brought into the world by a sinner of an ancient abyssal nation, lost its dark, metallic wings to "Anemo's pride and joy". Durin, jealous of Mondstadt's glory, terrorised it. The Anemo Archon, woken from his sylvan slumber by the victims' cries, summoned his faithful servant, and the two rode the wind to fight.

Owners: The item names no wielder. The claymore stands for Dvalin's pride rather than being something he held.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): five-star claymore from the standard Wanderlust Invocation and weapon event wishes. Base ATK 48, secondary stat Energy Recharge 8%. Passive "Sky-ripping Dragon Spine": raises all DMG (8-16%); after an Elemental Burst, Normal and Charged Attack hits create vacuum blades dealing 80-160% ATK DMG along their path, lasting 20 seconds or 8 blades.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): suits a retelling of Dvalin as hero first and Stormterror second. Mention the poison honestly; the text insists he was a hero.

510.comment: Skyward Pride: Dvalin's battle with Durin
510.content: The Pride's version has Dvalin fight with six wings, claws and teeth, swallow Durin's poisoned blood, be deceived by the Abyss into becoming Stormterror and later be calmed by Barbatos. Dvalin has his own entry.

511.content:
Skyward Spine: Skyward Spine is a 5-star polearm, part of the Mondstadt series of weapons. Its item text is a short legend of the dragon Dvalin: he fought and killed the shadow dragon Durin in the skies over Mondstadt, but swallowed Durin's venom and spent the following centuries wounded in an ancient ruin. Added in Version 1.0.

The weapon is described as a polearm that symbolizes Dvalin's resolve, its shaft pointing at the heavens and clad in the might of sky and wind. It sits with Skyward Blade, Skyward Pride, Skyward Harp and Skyward Atlas in a set of Mondstadt weapons, but this entry covers only the spear.

Appearance: Canon text gives only the symbolic picture: an upright shaft that points toward the heavens, wrapped in the power of sky and wind. Do not invent materials, a maker or measurements.

Lore: In olden times the shadow dragon Durin envied Mondstadt's peace and came to defile it. His black wings darkened the sky and released toxic fumes that even the thousand winds could not hold back, so poisoned black rain fell on the people. The Anemo Archon heard their agony and called Dvalin to his side.

Cloaked in storm, Dvalin tore through the poisoned clouds and a whirlwind in his wake destroyed them. He seized Durin in his claws and carried him above the clouds, where the battle continued. In the end Dvalin's fangs pierced Durin's throat and his claws tore out its corrupted heart. The text calls Durin the sinners' creation and says it fell, full of regret, onto a snowy peak.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon. The weapon is not tied to any playable character or to Venti, and no story shows Dvalin giving it to anyone.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 5-star polearm with base ATK 48 and an Energy Recharge secondary stat. Its passive, Black Wing, raises CRIT Rate and Normal ATK SPD and gives Normal and Charged Attacks a chance of a vacuum blade that deals area damage (roughly once per two seconds). It is on the Standard Wish and weapon event Wishes.

512.comment: Skyward Spine: Dvalin and Durin's battle
512.content: Skyward Spine's text recounts Dvalin's victory over the shadow dragon Durin in the poisoned skies and the venom he swallowed afterward. Treat it as legend told with sympathy for Dvalin. For the aftermath, the Abyss Order's exploitation of his pain and his freeing in the Prologue, see Dvalin's own entry.

513.content:
Snow-Tombed Starsilver (also: Snow Tombed Starsilver): Snow-Tombed Starsilver is a 4-star claymore of the Dragonspine series, in-game description "an ancient greatsword stored between frescoes" and forged from Starsilver. Its text tells of the princess of the snow-entombed mountain city of Sal Vindagnyr, who gave it to a hero from another land. Added in Version 1.2.

In game, one copy and its diagram lie in the Mural Room unlocked by the Hidden Exploration Objective Dragonspine's Glacial Secret; the weapon can also be forged.

Appearance: Canon calls it an ancient greatsword of Starsilver that can cleave ice and snow. In the text it lies between frescoes in a great hall, with black blood once dripping from its blade.

Lore: When the verdant city was sealed by cloud and mist and unending snowstorms blotted out the moonlight, a nail that fell from the azure skies pierced all life and every interrupted story. The priest's daughter gave the Starsilver greatsword to the hero from another land, Imunlaukr.

In the howling storm her words could not reach him. She told him a fourth fresco was prepared for him, where his likeness would remain, and promised to wait and pray for his return. She withered together with the grafted, barren silver branches while he was far away chasing answers.

Owners: Owner: the hero Imunlaukr, who was given it by the princess and left it in the mural hall. Nobody is shown wielding it afterward.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 4-star claymore with base ATK 44 and a Physical DMG Bonus secondary stat. The Dragonspine series passive Frost Burial gives Normal and Charged Attack hits a chance (60 to 100 per cent by refinement, once per 10s) to drop an Everfrost Icicle for area damage, with much higher damage against Cryo-affected enemies. Obtainable by forging or from the Mural Room.

514.content: Imunlaukr is the hero from another land who received the Snow-Tombed Starsilver from the Sal Vindagnyr princess. He arrived too late, found the city silent and left to find a land at war. See his own entry for more.

515.content:
Solar Pearl: Solar Pearl is a 4-star catalyst of the Kunwu series, a dull golden pearl of unknown substance that harbours the light of the sun and moon and pulses with warm strength. It is rumoured to be a legendary orb of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Its text gives Liyue's jewelers' tale of how the craftsman Kunwu made it, and Kunwu's own, more modest, account.

Appearance: A dull, golden pearl. Its substance is unknown and it pulses with a warm strength. Do not invent a size or setting.

Lore: The text says it once absorbed all the light in the world and was then kept in a wooden box for millennia, yet its power has not dissipated. Released from its container, it shines on, and a truly knowledgeable sage might unleash its power after so long.

A story long popular with Liyue's jewelers says Kunwu took the light of the heavenly bodies and sealed it in a wooden box, which he buried in a dark rocky chamber. After forty-nine days and twenty hours in pitch blackness, the pearl within had absorbed the shine of the sun and moon.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. Ningguang is shown with the ascended version in artwork of the Turning Point battle and Shikanoin Heizou in his character demo, which are cameos and not story claims.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42, CRIT Rate secondary stat (6 per cent). Passive Solar Shine: Normal Attack hits increase Elemental Skill and Elemental Burst DMG by 20 to 40 per cent (by refinement) for 6s, and Skill or Burst hits likewise increase Normal Attack DMG. Kunwu and Gnostic Hymn 1 series; it comes from the Battle Pass bounty.

516.content: Kunwu is the legendary master craftsman named in the item texts of Solar Pearl, Dragon's Bane and Lion's Roar. In Solar Pearl's story he is an eccentric old man who credits polishing and not magic.

517.content:
Song of Broken Pines: Song of Broken Pines is a 5-star claymore, part of the Millennial Movement series. Its item text is a history of Mondstadt's rebel songs: how bards and a split Church of Favonius stood against the tyrant Decarabian and the ruling aristocracy, and how a folk song gained a second, defiant half when the rebellion rose. Added in Version 1.5.

The Chinese name means roughly "when the pine-sound echoes", a phrase from the song's last line; this is wiki etymology, not an in-world title.

Appearance: Canon text describes it as a greatsword as light as the sigh of grass in the breeze, yet as merciless to the corrupt as a typhoon. Nothing more is said of its look.

Lore: The text opens with a folk song urging people to toss coins to the bard, give a bouquet to a fair maiden, drink bitter wine and sing for tomorrow. Mondstadt, the text says, is a land where songs travel on the wind, so tyrants such as Decarabian and the ruling aristocrats sometimes banned certain chords and tunes, sensing resistance in the bards' music.

Songs and hymns were also used by rebels to communicate. Under the aristocracy the Church that revered the Anemo Archon split in a schism: clergy who dined at the lords' table, wrote hymns of praise and even helped overturn the archon's statues, against saints without office who walked the streets and wine cellars, blessed slaves and commoners with the original holy manuscripts and wrote forbidden songs.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. Eula carries it in promotional art only; do not treat it as an heirloom of the Lawrence Clan or of Vennessa.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 5-star claymore with base ATK 49 and a Physical DMG Bonus secondary stat. Its passive, Rebel's Banner-Hymn, raises ATK and gives the wielder a Sigil of Whispers when Normal or Charged Attacks hit (at most once per 0.3s). With four Sigils, all are consumed and all nearby party members gain the Millennial Movement: Banner-Hymn effect for 12s (higher ATK and Normal ATK SPD), after which Sigils stop accruing for 20s. Different Millennial Movement buffs do not stack. Obtained from weapon event Wishes.

518.comment: Song of Broken Pines: Nameless Shepherd
518.content: The Nameless Shepherd is an aged saint of the Church of Favonius mentioned only in Song of Broken Pines. When Vennessa raised the banner of rebellion, the Shepherd mobilized the Church's true adherents, and many of them died on the fields singing the rebel half of an old folk song. Nothing else is known, including the Shepherd's real name or fate.

519.content:
Song of Days Past (also: Forgotten Oath of Days Past, Recollection of Days Past, Echoing Sound From Days Past, Promised Dream of Days Past, Poetry of Days Past): Song of Days Past is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.3. Its bonuses reward healing: it records healing as a Yearning effect and turns it into extra damage. Its pieces tell of the people the Remurians called the "people of bygone times": the rebellion of a songstress against the golden authority, her search for a wish-granting Pure Grail, and the verses that later turned her into legend.

The pieces are Forgotten Oath of Days Past (flower), Recollection of Days Past (plume), Echoing Sound From Days Past (sands), Promised Dream of Days Past (goblet) and Poetry of Days Past (circlet). Many details are told through unnamed figures.

Appearance: Only a few images are given: a butterfly wing worn in the ear (Recollection), the tolling night bell (Echoing Sound), a golden grail brimming with primordial water (Promised Dream) and a silver flower and silver armor (Forgotten Oath and Poetry).

Lore: The pieces follow a northern songstress who unites the tribes against Remuria's golden authority as the first Lochknight, a doomed love between a musician and a woman of his tribe, a desperate search for the wish-granting Pure Grail, and later poems that turn her into legend.

Owners: No named owner; narrative item text only.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus is Healing Bonus +15%. The 4-piece effect creates a Yearning effect for 6s when the wearer heals a party member, recording total healing including overflow (up to 15,000), then converts it to Waves of Days Past, adding 8% of the recorded total to the active character's DMG for the next 5 hits or 10s. Standby wearers still trigger it. Obtained from the Waterfall Wen domain in Fontaine and the artifact strongbox. Added in Version 4.3.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): lean into the set's elegy: memorial verse, bells, silver and gold. Remind characters that stories of Lochknights are partly legend, as the circlet itself says.

520.comment: Song of Days Past: Lochknight (set lore)
520.content: In Forgotten Oath of Days Past, the first Lochknight is the unnamed oracle-songstress who united northern tribes against Remuria and swore to Egeria, with two vows: never draw the sword on those who pledge faith in Egeria, and never tolerate evil. Poetry of Days Past shows how later poems retold her, and the Lochknights have their own entry.

521.comment: Song of Days Past: Pure Grail
521.content: In this set the Pure Grail is a legendary vessel of primordial water said to heal, restore youth, revive the dead and grant any wish. No one in the pieces has seen it, the belief came from an Oceanid's words, and it is called a heterodoxy. Poetry of Days Past retells the quest as myth.

key: Dawn and Dusk by the Lake
522.content:
Splendor of Tranquil Waters (also: Hauteclaire, Dawn and Dusk by the Lake): Splendor of Tranquil Waters is a 5-star sword: a scepter around which pure water swirls, once a symbol of the highest authority over the seas. Its story belongs to Erinnyes, a figure of the age of Remuria.

The description exists in two versions that disagree about what Erinnyes was and what she achieved, which makes the sword a good example of how Fontaine's legends are told in more than one way.

Appearance: Canon gives only: a scepter wrapped in swirling pure water, water-blue in colour, with a pommel tip that glows with Pneuma or Ousia light when held by a character who has an Arkhe alignment. Add no further detail.

Lore: A scepter that once symbolised supreme authority over the seas. It belonged to Erinnyes, who in the time of the great symphony united the people of the high waters against the gods.

The legend says her home was destroyed early by the God King, Remus, whose army from the Golden City enslaved or killed her family. Only two escaped. One met the proud Harmost during the war and rose to inherit his authority (the wiki links this person to Cassiodor and the Harmost to Boethius). The other was taken in by the Prince (page 1) or chieftain (page 2) of Aremorica to guard the waters the God King had not yet seized. The text frames them as two survivors of one home drifting apart, one toward good and one toward evil.

Owners: Erinnyes, per the description. No present-day wielder is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.2. Passive "Dawn and Dusk by the Lake": when the wielder's current HP increases or decreases, their Elemental Skill DMG rises for a few seconds (stacking up to 3 times); when other party members' HP changes, the wielder's Max HP rises (stacking up to 2 times). Both can trigger off-field. Values scale with refinement.

523.comment: Splendor of Tranquil Waters: Erinnyes and Hauteclaire
523.content: The scepter Splendor of Tranquil Waters is tied to the legend of Erinnyes: a figure of Remurian times who united rebellious people of the high waters, with two conflicting tellings of her quest for the Pure Grail and her plea to Egeria. The wiki says it was once called Hauteclaire, citing the book La Chanson d'Erinnyes.

524.content:
Staff of Homa (also: Homa Staff, Hùmó zhī Zhàng): The Staff of Homa is a five-star polearm of Liyue: a "devilishly red" ritual staff from the Archon War era, when fire rites were used to cleanse the miasmas of dead gods. Item text says a merciful doctor was given it by a whispering flame and used it to burn away impurity and release the dead from their ill karma. Today it is carried by Hu Tao, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's director, who inherited it through the Hu family.

Its name echoes homa, a fire-offering ritual. The wiki also notes the winged top of the staff, possibly a nod to the Homa bird of Persian myth. Nothing in the item text states the staff is a weapon first: Hu Tao's friend Xiangling does not know much about it beyond what Hu Tao has told her.

Lore: The item story: rites that cleanse by fire let impurity rise with the flames to the heavens. Fresh cinders were lit in rainy seasons and wolf smoke rose as prayers for blessings and the defeat of evil. These rites were common in the ancient period of strife, since the dreams and delusions of the silent corpses of gods bred evil miasmas that snatched away citizens.

Owners: Current owner: Hu Tao, director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, per the wiki's reading of the Lantern Rite event Springtime Charms (5.3, limited-time) as showing it passed down through the Hu family. The doctor of the legend is unnamed; the wiki treats the first wielder as heavily implied to be a Hu family ancestor.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star polearm from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat CRIT DMG 14.4%. Passive "Reckless Cinnabar": HP rises 20-40% and the wielder gains ATK equal to 0.8-1.6% of Max HP, plus a further 1-1.8% of Max HP while HP is under 50% (refinements 1 to 5).

525.comment: Staff of Homa: Hu Tao and the staff
525.content: The Lantern Rite event Springtime Charms (5.3) is cited by the wiki for showing Hu Tao as the staff's current owner, passed down through the Hu family. Xiangling, her best friend, does not know much about the staff beyond what Hu Tao has told her.

526.content:
Staff of the Scarlet Sands: The Staff of the Scarlet Sands is a 5-star polearm of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it one of a paired set of obsidian scepters that grant the right to lead the people of the desert, though no retainer now lives who can verify the proper appearance of these regalia. Its story is a monologue by King Deshret about how the world should be ordered, ending in his longing for a perfect world.

The staff is the polearm partner of the Key of Khaj-Nisut. Together the wiki treats them as keys to the Orchard of Pairidaeza, the eternal oasis made as Nabu Malikata's resting place.

Appearance: An obsidian scepter or staff. Canon text gives no more detail. The in-game description stresses that no one is left alive who can confirm what the genuine regalia looked like, so depictions are uncertain.

Lore: The narrator, speaking as a creator, lists how the world was made: the sun and three moons (as a woman once described them to him), weight so that sand sank into earth, and seven sage monks to rule the paths of earth, water and stars. After the original world's barriers fell and dark poison seeped in, spikes pierced the earth to heal it.

He then lists what must be removed for his ideal: the cycle of seven, the barrier between life and death, the sun, moons and weight, the original rules and verdicts, and all creatures, so that none steal wisdom. He pictures the Sand King sleeping alone, drawing up new theorems, and "our paradise" regained; that oasis was never a paradise for the many.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. Cyno appears with the ascended staff in his official art and character demo, and Candace with the unascended one in her wish art and TCG card (wiki trivia).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star polearm released in Version 3.1 (2022-09-28), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT Rate. Passive Heat Haze at Horizon's End gives bonus ATK equal to a percentage of the wielder's Elemental Mastery; when an Elemental Skill hits opponents, the Dream of the Scarlet Sands effect adds more for 10 s, up to 3 stacks. Multiple targets hit give multiple stacks, and the effect is not gained off-field.

527.content:
Starcaller's Watch (also: Offering Unto Wind and Sun, Mirror of Night): Starcaller's Watch is a 5-star catalyst: a statue carved in the shape of an eagle, a sacred relic of the Masters of the Night-Wind passed down from generation to generation.

Its story is about the girl chosen to guide the people into night's slumber, and about the man who believed he could manipulate her.

Appearance: A statue carved in the shape of an eagle; the story calls it a statuette and associates eagle feathers with the star-caller's crown. Add no other details.

Lore: In an ancient, exalted contract the messenger of night chose a child with a star-bright soul, set a crown of eagle feathers on her brow, and charged her to guide a formless ancient people into night's slumber.

The text pictures her as a young woman, once kneeling before dragons, who later turned and led an outlander through a wall of fumes with flute and song.

Owners: The Masters of the Night-Wind keep it as a sacred relic. The wiki names its first wielder as the Holy Sovereign who was Maghan's master.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat Elemental Mastery; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.3. The passive only triggers while the wielder is on-field.

528.comment: Starcaller's Watch: Offering Unto Wind and Sun
528.content: Offering Unto Wind and Sun is the passive of the catalyst Starcaller's Watch (gameplay): an Elemental Mastery boost, plus the Mirror of Night damage bonus for the active character after the wielder creates a shield.

529.content:
Starsilver (also: Starsilver ore, Starsilver Ore): Starsilver is a rare, precious ore found only on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. Its item text says it is formed by the mountain's unique geography and its ley lines. It is silvery, is worked in forges, and is also prized by artists as a pigment source.

Smiths use it to forge Fine Enhancement Ore and several weapons, notably the Dragonspine series. In the mountain's old lore a Starsilver greatsword was handed by the princess of Sal Vindagnyr to the outlander Imunlaukr.

Appearance: A silver-coloured ore. Albedo notes that even impure Starsilver contains fine silver-coloured particles, but that lower grades lack luster, while good specimens have great luster and a lovely colour. Escoffier reports that it tastes like snow and ice mixed with limewash paint.

Lore: Its item text calls it a rare and precious ore formed by Dragonspine's unique geographical conditions and ley lines. In the Snow-Tombed Starsilver text, the greatsword is forged from Starsilver and able to cleave ice and snow. The weapon lore has the princess of Sal Vindagnyr give it to Imunlaukr as he left to search for a way to end the frost; he later returned it, and it came to rest between the frescoes of the mural room.

Owners: No notable owner. Albedo uses it for paint, smiths for forging, and in old Dragonspine legend its metal was carried as a greatsword by Imunlaukr and as a lance in the Disaster and Remorse tale.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a forging material added in Version 1.2, mined only on Dragonspine from destructible ore nodes that drop 1-3 each and respawn after 48 hours. Blunt attacks and Geo abilities break the nodes fastest, and Anemo cannot move the drops.

530.content: During the Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event, Albedo says Starsilver makes high-quality silver paint and that he has run out of his last batch. Only luminous, low-impurity ore is suitable: dull specimens give a paint seen as a fake or defective product. He collects the ore himself on Dragonspine, which he also finds a quiet place to gather his thoughts.

531.content:
String of Pearls (also: String of Pearls play, Lian Xin Zhu): String of Pearls is a five-act Liyue opera script by Yun Jin, split into five volumes. It follows Zixin, a young fisherwoman, and Fan Jie, a dock worker who returns her lost string of pearls. A misunderstanding, a false reward notice, a local bully named Wu Wang and a rescue in a dark stronghold bring them together.

The script is written as stage directions, role lists and sung lines in the "Dongtang" and "Ganging" styles. It uses stock roles of opera: a male lead, a female lead, a comic role and a villain. A comic character, Grandma Zhang, speaks to the audience and mentions Yun Jin's plays directly.

Appearance: Printed script pages with an act title, a cast list and numbered scenes. Delivery notes in brackets (aside, aloud, and musical directions like lento or appassionato) mix with stage movements.

Lore: Act I, Of Fish and Water: Zixin, sixteen by her own line, sells fish to support her ageing parents. She loses her string of pearls and Fan Jie, who found it, checks her wrist for wear marks. She takes this as an insult and scolds him before learning he meant well. He leaves before telling his full name, and she regrets it.

Owners: No owner; the volumes are spread through Liyue Harbor. Yun Jin is the credited author.

Gameplay: Game note: a book collection with no stats. Vol. 1 is at Third-Round Knockout on the table Jiangzhou sits at during the night; Vols. 2 and 3 are sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse; Vol. 4 is on the bookhouse roof; Vol. 5 is next to Geri.

532.comment: String of Pearls: Zixin and Fan Jie
532.content: Zixin and Fan Jie are the leads of the opera String of Pearls. Zixin is a fisherwoman who sells fish in Liyue Harbor. Fan Jie is a dock worker chosen by fellow workers as leader. He returns her pearls, and after misunderstandings and a rescue from Wu Wang they plan to marry. They are stage characters from Yun Jin's script.

533.comment: String of Pearls: String of Pearls Act Summaries
533.content:
- Act II, The Search for the Gentleman: on Grandma Zhang's advice Zixin posts a Mora reward notice to find him. Three tricksters, Zhang San, Li Si and Wang Er'ma, try to claim it with false goods. Grandma Zhang drives them off with a trap, Fan Jie is brought in by mistake, and the two realise the misunderstanding and apologise to one another.
- Act III, The Pearls, Lost Again: the two meet daily. The local bully Wu Wang, with companions Wu Yi and Wu Er, seizes Zixin. Grandma Zhang gives Fan Jie the pearls, and he rides to rescue her.
- Act IV, Trial by Candlelight: Fan Jie scouts Wu Wang's stronghold. Zixin hits the drunk Wu Wang with a candlestick and flees in the dark without relighting it.
- Act V, Twin Pearls Returned: in the dark, Fan Jie and Zixin find each other, Wu Wang mistakes Fan Jie for someone else and is stabbed, and the couple leave together with a promise.

534.content:
Sturdy Bone (also: Trapper's Pride, Wanjiru's bone sword): Sturdy Bone is a 4-star longsword from Natlan, made of bone that has only grown harder with use. Legend says it was the hero Wanjiru's reliable weapon.

Its story shows Wanjiru, famous for strength, slipping into the great dragon's tomb for a weapon and coming back with a bone in her palm.

Appearance: A longsword made of bleached bone, the spit of a giant beast's tail in the story. Do not invent engravings or a handle design beyond a hilt.

Lore: The great dragon that once ruled the land of flame had a tomb of bleached bone ridges like giant claws, patrolled by secret machines. Hearing of it around the tribe's fire, Wanjiru leaps for joy: nothing in the world was more fearsome, and surely she could find there the weapon she wanted most.

The text lists her feats: shattering century-old ironwood with a swing, crushing raw ore to powder, bending boulders and toughest metal in her fingers. She jumps into the volcano from Tollan's peak, avoids the serpent-like guardian constructs and enters the ruins, following scars left by the heroes who once fought the dragon. She wishes she had been born in those days. The boneyard seems only a place of lonely corpses until a huge winged golden shadow throws itself at her.

Owners: Wanjiru, by the text's legend. No later wielder is named.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword of the Heroes of Natlan series, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Weapon Event Wishes from Version 5.1.

535.content: Trapper's Pride is the passive of the sword Sturdy Bone (gameplay): sprinting costs less Stamina and the next Normal Attacks hit harder for a short time.

536.content:
Summit Shaper (also: Zhuófēng zhī Rèn, Blade of Mountain Cut): Summit Shaper is a five-star sword of Liyue and one of the Liyue series weapons tied to Rex Lapis in the Archon War. Item text says that in an age of turmoil, when people cried out for lost loved ones, the ruler of Geo carved a long blade from a slab of golden Cor Lapis, cut a corner off a mountain with one stroke, and on it swore a solemn oath: to gather the scattered and punish those who broke contracts.

The text says the oath still works in Liyue: to break a contract is to make an enemy of the land, and the mountain Rex Lapis cut will sooner or later fall on contract-breakers. A legend adds that the sword's true owner will one day return among mortals.

Lore: The story begins with ordinary people asking where their lovers and children had gone, when the departed would return and how long the horrors would last. Even hearts hewn from bedrock cracked, and the eyes of those who kept faithful silence began to smolder.

Owners: The text credits the sword to the ruler of Geo, Morax or Rex Lapis. It records no later holder, and canon does not show Zhongli carrying it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star sword from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat ATK 10.8%. Passive "Golden Majesty", shared by the Liyue series: Shield Strength +20-40% and scoring hits raises ATK 4-8% for 8 seconds, up to 5 stacks, doubled while under a shield (refinements 1 to 5).

537.content:
Sunny Morning Sleep-In (also: Bathhouses, Hawks, and Narukami): Sunny Morning Sleep-In is a five-star catalyst, a bell lantern forged from purple jade. The game description says that placed beside a pillow it brings sweet dreams. Its item story is a sad, quiet one about a shrine maiden who had the three auspicious "first dreams" of the new year before the Cataclysm, and whose dreams of bathhouses, hawks and the Narukami banner came to mean loss.

The story is told in fragments, each ending with a dream she would never have again, then closes on a warm bathhouse day that may have been only a lazy nap after the rain.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a bell lantern forged from purple jade. The text does not describe it further.

Lore: The item story opens on a half-asleep shrine maiden explaining to her companions that she was late because she dreamed of a bathhouse and thought she had already reached the meeting place. In truth, on the first day of the new year she had simply overslept. A frivolous young man teases her and a young woman of Seirai glares at him; an apprentice who is the oni's foster son says nothing. The text explains the Inazuman saying "First, bathhouses, second, hawks, third, Narukami": the sights of the first dream of the year, standing for health and longevity, high achievement and wishes fulfilled.

Owners: No owner is named in the item text. The wiki notes only the dreaming maiden and her companions as the story's characters.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star catalyst, base ATK 44, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 58. Passive "Bathhouses, Hawks, and Narukami": Elemental Mastery increases by 120-240 for 6s after triggering Swirl, by 96-192 for 9s after the wielder's Elemental Skill hits an opponent, and by 32-64 for 30s after the Elemental Burst hits an opponent, at refinement 1-5. It was the event-exclusive weapon of the Version 5.4 Epitome Invocation (2025-02-12), alongside Silvershower Heartstrings. The three effects echo the three dreams in the saying.

538.comment: Sunny Morning Sleep-In: First dreams of the year
538.content: The Inazuman saying in the item story lists the good omens of a first dream of the new year: bathhouses for health and longevity, hawks for high achievements, and Narukami for wishes fulfilled. In the story each fades from the shrine maiden's dreams as the Cataclysm approaches and arrives.

539.content:
Surf's Up (also: Aqua Remembrance, Scorching Summer): Surf's Up is a 5-star catalyst: a commemorative prize reserved for the champion of the First All-Tribe Surfing Championship, kept at the Leisurely Puffer while the tournament is being prepared.

Its story is a comic legend about the Pyro Archon Cochanina, a surfing champion, driving the Volcano Lord away from the People of the Springs.

Appearance: Canon gives no physical description of the item beyond calling it a commemorative piece. Keep descriptions simple and festive; do not add decorations.

Lore: A huge black Volcano Lord fouled the springs of the People of the Springs by dumping his filth into them. The Pyro Archon Cochanina, a surfing champion, left her famous blade at home, took only a surfboard, and tricked him out to sea.

She told him the tribe's treasure, the Iridescent Chalice left by the hero Uenuku, lay in the deep sea and that only he deserved it. When the clumsy Volcano Lord was dizzy, she tossed out a Drifting Pufferfish as the supposed key; he charged it, was struck, and fell off his board.

Owners: No wielder is named. Mualani is the custodian of the prize, not its holder.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.0.

540.content: Aqua Remembrance is the passive of the catalyst Surf's Up (gameplay): a Max HP boost and Scorching Summer stacks that raise Normal Attack damage after an Elemental Skill and are refreshed by Vaporize.

541.content:
Sword of Descension: Sword of Descension is a 4-star sword in the game since Version 1.0 and given by mail to players who start on PS4 or PS5. Its description says it does not appear to belong to this world, and the item text calls it proof that the Traveler came to Teyvat by special means.

It can be wielded only by one who has challenged the "world", and it is addressed in second person to the Traveler as a weapon forged for one who challenges and pursues.

Appearance: A sword of unique craftsmanship. The wiki notes that the PlayStation triangle, circle, square and cross symbols appear on the handle, a real-world platform reference rather than an in-world detail.

Lore: The item text says only one who has challenged the "world" may wield such a sword, and that the Traveler wields it while searching for the answers hidden in this world.

It recalls the last time the sword was drawn: humankind tried to preserve a doomed world that was their last and only home, drawing steel against the law that all who exist must one day perish. Against the star-devouring darkness, the text says, the only fitting weapon is a sword, bearing the memory of those who faced their ends without fear.

Owners: Addressed to the Traveler only. The text says only one who has challenged the "world" may wield it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 39, ATK secondary stat, fixed at refinement 1 with one copy given. Its Descension passive is effective only on PlayStation: Normal and Charged Attack hits have a 50% chance to deal 200% ATK as DMG in a small area (once every 10s), and if the Traveler equips it their ATK rises by 66. Players on other platforms can obtain the weapon through cross-save, but the effect applies only when playing on PlayStation.

542.content:
Sword of Narzissenkreuz (also: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, Hero's Blade): The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is a 4-star sword received after the Rowboat's Wake quest in Fontaine. In the story it is the holy blade of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, its power faded when that story ended.

Its description calls it a sword that will now begin a new journey with the power remaining in it, commemorating a certain great dream. The Arkhe it carries, Pneuma or Ousia, can be switched at Annapausis.

Appearance: The only canon visuals are two forms, a Pneuma-aligned and an Ousia-aligned blade. The wiki gives no further description; avoid inventing engraving or hilt details.

Lore: A ceremonial sword of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. It was used in a ritual to separate mind from body and, in the Ordo's story, held reason itself.

Narzissenkreuz himself used it in that ritual, for example to grant a certain hilichurl intelligence, per the wiki lore summary. The quest-exclusive version, shown during Waking from the Great Dream, is described as a sacred blade with enough reason and will to create and destroy a universe, or a dream. After Rowboat's Wake it is replaced by the ordinary weapon.

Owners: Ann carries the blade in the story; the player receives the weapon at the end of the quest.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat ATK; obtained after Rowboat's Wake, version 4.2. Passive "Hero's Blade": for a wielder with no Arkhe of their own, Normal, Charged or Plunging Attacks that hit release a Pneuma or Ousia energy blast for a percentage of ATK, at most once every 12s. Refinement uses the material Surging Sacred Chalice, made from Drained Conch Cup at the Little Fountain.

543.comment: Sword of Narzissenkreuz: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz
543.content: The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's ceremonial blade, used in a ritual separating mind from body and carried by Ann in the In the Wake of Narcissus quests. The player's weapon form (4-star) comes after the Rowboat's Wake quest.

544.content:
Symphonist of Scents (also: Seasoned Symphony): Symphonist of Scents is a 5-star polearm: an elegantly built baton said to have been wielded by a great musician, Euergetia, to bridge tune and taste.

Its story is a quiet one about the Remurian Harmost Euergetia and her use of authority to comfort homesick conquered people.

Appearance: Canon describes only an elegantly built polearm shaped like a conductor's baton. Arkhe-aligned wielders show a Pneuma or Ousia mark. Add nothing else.

Lore: During the long conquest of the tribes and kingdoms of the High Sea by the Legion Athanatoi, the Harmost Euergetia listened to the pleas of the conquered. The homesick people, though awed by the golden capital, missed the cuisines they had once enjoyed.

Stone golems need neither food nor drink, but the people were frail flesh and would grow dejected at poor fare. The God King's directives were the supreme rule, yet Euergetia reasoned that fulfilling a tiny wish was no offence in a symphony meant to embrace all living things. Her golden-haired colleague (the wiki links Boethius) grumbled behind her back but never stopped her.

Owners: Euergetia, per the description (she is called the benefactrix on Remurian engravings).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star polearm, base ATK 46 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.6. Passive "Seasoned Symphony": raises ATK, with an extra boost while the wielder is off-field; after the wielder initiates healing, they and those healed gain "Sweet Echoes" (ATK up for 3s), also while off-field. Values scale with refinement.
